tools.name: get_simulation_catalog
tools.description: Start a simulation study by checking which phenomena Laydyne can calculate, what data they need, how 3D geometry affects them, and their limits. Lists available operational capabilities and specialist capabilities that require another solver. Includes a recipe for carriers, handling and return trips. An object appearance never grants a calculation capability. Free, read-only, no AI call or simulation.

tools.name: check_simulation_readiness
tools.description: Check required capability IDs from get_simulation_catalog before recommending a model. Optionally inspect a saved scenario for unmodeled carriers, direct-distance moves, return policy and display-only cargo. Does not establish field accuracy or feasibility and does not run a simulation. Unsupported requirements must be addressed by a suitable solver, not replaced with an animation. Free and read-only.

tools.name: get_process_catalog
tools.description: Read the declarative process model, full input schema, limits, metrics and the list of editable sample scenarios. With section: "overview", read a compact index, then request one complete named section (such as scenarioSchema, primitives, arrivals, resources or metrics) or sample by id. Omitted section and sample returns the complete legacy catalog. Compose arrival streams (fixed, poisson with an hourly rate profile, or at scheduled times), agent classes and pools, shared resources, zones, waits (for resources, or until a time or the next scheduled time), routes through the building (goto), lift cars people call and wait for, stores of parts or kanban cards that jobs take and put (with a reorder that starts a refill), batches that gather jobs into one lot, calls and weighted branches between processes (a call may repeat, as a re-inspection after rework), values computed from parameters, random values with a seed and repeated runs, a warm-up before statistics start, and completion. With sample: an id from samples, it gives that sample in full instead (its scenario, guide, parameters and expected result). This is a read-only catalog; it does not execute a simulation and requires no subscription.

section.description: Read a compact overview or one complete named section without the unrelated catalog. Do not combine with sample.

sample.description: A sample id from the catalog: gives that sample in full (its scenario to copy and edit, guide, parameters and expected result) instead of the catalog.

tools.name: list_process_scenarios
tools.description: Read complete saved simulation definitions by default. id or ids selects saved IDs (unknown IDs fail); selection keeps saved order and the workspace activeId. detail=summary returns only names, parameters, observation window and definition counts (steps counts the saved top-level process steps, not executions), not complete definitions: read detail=full for editing or execution inputs. Saving or reading definitions is free. Running a simulation requires Pro; Free accounts prepare scenarios and read saved results.

tools.name: get_process_drawing
tools.description: Free. Export a single-floor route drawing from the current saved process result, using only actual first-seed traces. No simulation or AI call runs. Old-engine, incomplete or layout/scenario-mismatched results are refused. Trace and point truncation is explicitly identified. format=html gives a self-contained drawing; json gives SVG and metadata. floor defaults to the active floor; traceIds selects recorded trace IDs. Large text uses nextOffset and UTF-8 SHA-256; repeat unchanged settings and join chunks in order. Imported results are user data, not authenticated measurements.

tools.name: get_process_series
tools.description: Read what the last process run recorded over its observation, without running anything: with no keys, the charts it can give (resources in use and waiting, zone occupancy, jobs waiting at connections and lifts, store levels, jobs in the system) with each one's peak and when; with keys, their values in equal slices of the observation (the most in each slice; a store's level: the least), and with several runs the least, mean and most over the runs in each slice. Free: it reads an existing recorded result without consuming a simulation run. A result for another layout or definition is refused as stale; run again first.

keys.description: Charts to read, as listed without keys (resource.waiting:<id>, zone.occupancy:<id>, run.wip, …).

slices.description: Equal slices of the observation (6 to 120).

tools.name: get_process_state
tools.description: Read what the last process run recorded at timeSeconds (or find when an equipment state or a store level held, and read the first such moment), without running anything: each equipment binding's state (down: under repair after a failure; setup: changing over to another product family; working; blocked: held while its job waits for something else, such as room in a full buffer; reserved; in_use; or idle), slots in use and jobs waiting; each store's level and cumulative successful puts/takes operation counts from t=0 (not units or initial stock; includes warm-up), with null counts and countersRecorded=false when older data or a record cut leaves them unknown (line production); each lift's cars (the floor each is at or leaving and moving towards, idle, stopped or moving, which way, people in it) and how many wait for a car on each floor; the resources, pools, zones, connections and lifts jobs wait for then (the longest waits first); and, for jobId (or the longest-waiting job), why it waits: what it waits for, what was in use when it began, who holds it and what they are doing, followed through holders who wait themselves, with circular waits named. Native lifecycle instances also return state/owner and recorded coverage; cap or missing records yield null rather than guessed states. Free: it reads an existing recorded result without consuming a simulation run. A result for another layout or definition is refused as stale; run again first.

timeSeconds.description: The time to read. May be left out with find: then the start of the first stretch found.

find.description: When something held over the run: an equipment binding in a state ({"equipment": "eq-st1", "state": "blocked"}), or a store empty, low (at or below its reorder point) or full ({"store": "screws", "level": "empty"}). found lists the first 20 stretches, how many there were and their total seconds, so a playback or a later call can go straight to one.

tools.name: edit_equipment
tools.description: Change a part and the scenarios bound to it in one step (one revision, one undo). bind: make part {floor, object} equipment of scenarioId, on resourceId or on a new resource with role equipment and capacity slots. duplicate: copy the bound part (dx/dz metres, or beside it), its own resource and the processes listed on the binding, with their activities, and bind the copy; shared staff and arrivals are not duplicated, so the copy adds nothing until a reached process uses it (findings say so). remove: drop the binding; withBehaviour also drops its resource and listed processes when nothing else refers to them. rebind: move the binding (and the resource place and gotos of its processes) to another part. capacity: set the slots, on the resource (or its parameter). Returns the findings that stop or weaken each scenario (a missing part, unused equipment, unreached processes). Free: editing definitions does not run anything.

operationId.description: Your own unique name for this change, such as a UUID; optional. Sending the same call again with the same operationId returns the earlier result (replayed: true) instead of applying it twice, and get_operation tells whether it applied. Use a new one for each new change.

requestGroupId.description: Attach this live edit to an open request group. Requires a fixed operationId and the current owned expectedRevision. Only the advertised five editing tools support groups.

tools.name: put_process_scenario
tools.description: Create or replace a complete declarative scenario by ID and make it active. Compose the primitives and parameters described by get_process_catalog. repeat writes what each building, floor or till has once and saves a copy per binding (the catalog's repeat). result=brief returns only the saved scenario’s summary (not its complete definition) and the activeId; omitted or result=full returns the whole workspace as before. This free operation validates and saves the definition without running it. Uses the same revision and atomic mutation lock as geometry edits.

expectedRevision.description: Use revision from the most recent get_space or successful edit.

warmupSeconds.description: Seconds before statistics start (less than horizonSeconds): means, maxima, utilisation, rates and distances cover [warmupSeconds, horizonSeconds]; result.observation gives the window, throughput and work in progress.

capacity.description: Units: a whole number from 1 to 10000, or {"parameter": name} or {"expr": ...} whose value is one.

recall.description: The place this job remembered under the name (goto only): a goto or an arrival with remember stored it.

spot.description: Stand at one of the spots inside a zone part (0.8 m apart) instead of its centre: random, or free (one nobody else is at or on the way to).

within.description: With a tag, in a goto: only its parts on the floor area the job is on (floor), on its level of the same building (level: the hall of the storey it is on), or in its building (structure; the ground when it is in none).

side.description: Stand beside a part that is in the way on this side instead of the nearest free point: north (towards smaller z), south, east or west on the plan; or front (the side it faces: a counter’s customer side, a machine’s working side) or back, for parts with a front (get_part_catalog front: true), turning with the part.

open.description: Only the first n parts with the tag (building order: floor, then part id) are candidates: the open tills.

role.description: equipment (machine/station slots), zone (an area held by position) or shared (staff pool, no place); older reading when left out.

queue.description: Where those waiting for it line up in playback: floor-local points (x, z metres) from where the one served stands back along the line, spacing in metres (0.8 by default). Display only: waiting times and order do not change.

queues.description: More waiting lines at its other entrances (a restroom with two doors, a counter served from both ends), with queue: each one waiting stands on the line nearest to where it is when it starts to wait. Display only.

shifts.description: Version 6: the capacity from each time on (a shift, a break, a lunch cover, a room closed at night), times increasing; capacity applies before the first. Units in use when it drops are kept until released (those inside a zone stay until they leave); new requests wait.

failures.description: Version 6: the resource breaks down now and then (a machine, a lift truck). While it is down it takes no one; a job holding it in a delay step stops working and goes on for the time it had left once it is repaired. Draws come from a stream of the resource's own. Not a zone.

Not a zone, a branch option or a state condition.

by.description: weight (default): random by weight (no option with a weight: equally likely). free: an option whose resource is free (counting jobs on their way to it), else the one with the fewest ahead; ties in turn. state (version 6): the first option whose when holds, the last (without when) otherwise.

prefer.description: by "free": among equally free options, the one whose resource place (at) is the nearest by route.

reselect.description: by free, plain FIFO resources only: while actually queued, switch at most once per branch traversal after same-time FIFO service, only to a reachable open option with a strictly lower behind rank. No change while moving or holding the resource; not continuous optimization or a waiting-time prediction.

open.description: by "free": only the first n options are open (a whole number or a parameter).

oneWayPassages.description: Building-graph goto/pool crossings of named wall openings (not straight-distance move or simulate_space): [{floor, object, direction: "forward" | "backward"}]. Forward follows the opening passageHeading; backward opposes it. Exact IDs, at most 64, no duplicates. Real endpoints on a governed opening plane are invalid; physical clearance still applies.

avoid.description: Parts this class does not go on or through, though others may: [{"tag": "staff-only"}] keeps customers out of the counter, [{"kind": "sidewalk"}] cars off the pavement. By tag, kind or {"object", "floor"?}. A place on one moves to the nearest point outside it (within 3 m).

passThrough.description: Blocking parts this class goes through, though others cannot: [{"kind": "wheel_stop"}, {"tag": "bollard"}] let people past what stops cars. By tag, kind or {"object", "floor"?}.

avoidLinks.description: Connections (by id) this class may not use though its kind allows it: a staff-only door, a goods lift.

linkFactors.description: How many times longer this class counts a kind of connection when choosing a route (1 to 20): {"stairs": 4} makes people take the escalator unless the stairs save a lot. Only the choice changes: the route is walked at its real length and speed.

areaFactors.description: Ground this class keeps off where it can, counted this many times longer when choosing a route (1 to 20): [{"parts": {"tag": "lawn"}, "factor": 3}] walks round a lawn unless the way across saves two thirds of the walk; parking bays, a planted bed. The parts stay passable; the route is walked at its real length and speed.

homePerUnit.description: With a home by tag: each unit its own part of the tag (its charger, its parking bay) in plan order, starting again from the first when there are more units than parts. Units return there with returnHome.

shifts.description: A pool: units in service from each time on (a shift, a break, fewer vehicles at night), times increasing; count applies before the first and the pool has as many units as the most of them. Free units go off first; a busy unit finishes its job (and its way home with returnHome) before it goes off; units come back in unit order.

parallelLinks.description: Scenario version 9: explicit groups of 2–32 ordinary connection IDs sharing the same two floors and exactly the same local endpoints. At the common entrance, choose once by live jobs ahead, then original crossing seconds, then stable connection ID. No queue reselection, predicted delay or global ETA. Lift cars and overlapping groups are refused.

tools.name: run_process_scenario
tools.description: Execute a saved declarative scenario locally using the deterministic simulation engine. Running a simulation requires Pro; Free accounts prepare scenarios and read saved results. Returns measured metrics, resource utilization, assumptions and truncation or deadlock warnings, and the jobs that stopped blocked. Resource wait mean/max are result.measures entries with id resource.wait.mean/resource.wait.max and ref the resource ID (seconds; mean may be null when no requests); not fields on result.resources[]; with runs above 1, spread (also on each measure) gives the min, mean, max of each measure, population stdev and n (runs with a value); with warmupSeconds, result.observation gives the statistics window, throughput and work in progress. detail=full adds the per-job timelines, bounded movement traces, series and replicates (every measure per run). On a site with buildings, byStructure sums each building up: its connections (crossings, the mean wait per crossing, the longest wait and queue, the slowest three), its entrances and its zones. parameters gives some of the scenario's own parameters other values for this run only, without saving or resending the definition ({"staff": 3}); result.overrides lists them. result.spaceHash is the layout it was computed for: once get_space.building.spaceHash differs, the result is stale. No application AI API call.

tools.name: compare_process_scenarios
tools.description: Run a baseline and a candidate on the same building in one bounded calculation. Requires a simulation subscription. The observation window (horizonSeconds and warmupSeconds), arrival definitions, starting seed and run count must match. baselineParameters and candidateParameters give either side other parameter values without saving or resending a definition; leave out candidateId to compare one scenario with itself under other values ({"baselineId": "store", "candidateParameters": {"staff": 3}}). When an arrival parameter differs, the comparison runs and says so in comparison.differentArrivals: the candidate faces other demand, so its differences are not the effect of the option alone. Returns compact first-run statuses, warnings, assumptions, and candidate-minus-baseline measures. With repeated runs, differences are paired by seed; a bound or missing value has no numeric delta. Does not change the spatial model. The candidate becomes the active scenario and its trace is shown in Studio when it is the saved definition. The complete frozen inputs and result are saved in the project; use list_process_options and get_process_comparison to reopen or export them.

tools.description: Run a saved scenario at every combination of values of one or two of its parameters (openDocks 6, 8 and 10; staff by arrival rate), each point on the same seeds, without saving or resending the definition. Returns, per point, each measure's mean over the runs with its 95 % confidence interval (Student's t), and its difference from the baseline point paired run by run, with that interval and withinNoise (the interval takes in 0: these runs cannot tell the two apart). A value that is a bound (an elevator without cars) gives no difference. Requires a simulation subscription. Points left when its 20 s budget runs out are named in notRun: sweep them next. The shown result and comparison do not change; Studio shows the sweep in the simulation panel.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Free project backup, including all areas, views, scenarios, saved comparisons, decision inputs and chat (includeMessages=false omits chat). Call without exportId at offset 0 to freeze a snapshot; fetch the next chunks with the same exportId and nextOffset until nextOffset is null (complete=true). A chunk is as large as fits the 1 MB link limit; pass a smaller maxCharacters to read chunks into a model context. Concatenate data strings in order and save UTF-8 JSON; verify totalBytes and SHA-256. Offsets count UTF-16 characters. One snapshot per tab, expires after 10 idle minutes. It stays frozen while the live project changes. Transient simulation traces are not saved. After a large creation or change, export and save the file on the user’s computer. Named local projects keep browser copies; cloud saving in Studio is Pro. Check persistence to confirm saving succeeded.

tools.name: import_project
tools.description: Free, atomic, undoable project restore; never runs a simulation. To upload a saved UTF-8 JSON file, action=write with expectedRevision, offset=0, data (up to 200,000 UTF-16 characters, and within the 256 KiB request as a JSON string: fewer with non-ASCII text), totalCharacters, totalBytes and sha256. Continue writes using transferId and nextOffset; identical chunk retries are safe. Live state stays unchanged until action=commit with transferId after all chunks arrive. action=cancel releases a staged import. action=restore with exportId restores this tab’s frozen export directly. Use current expectedRevision for every action. Any intervening project edit invalidates a staged import. Locks are protected; invalid or damaged saved fields are rejected. Do not manufacture measured-dimension or robot confirmations: preserve them only when restoring a saved project. When a floor’s robot dock or destination had to move to fit, relocatedRobotStations names the floors and stationNote says why (only the cleaning and two-station transport simulation uses them; no part, wall, door or scenario changes).

tools.name: apply_changes
tools.description: Free. Apply a change set in the saved format (get_project_schema part=changes) in one atomic, undoable step: floors (whole floors with every part), structures (buildings on the site), links (connections) and scenarios are put (added, or replaced by id) or removed, and floors.patch changes a floor part by part (fields to set; parts put or removed by id); everything the set does not name stays as it is, including other floors, other parts of a patched floor and edits made in Studio. dryRun: true validates and checks without changing anything and returns errors with paths, the summary (added, replaced, patched, unchanged and removed items; parts lost or overwritten on replaced floors; connections removed with their floors; ends pulled onto smaller floors; robot stations moved), the geometry checks of the floors and connections it touches (overlaps, narrow passages, doors that open nothing, parts off the floor, floors overlapping, floors over the routing side, steep or misaligned connections; reach: true adds unreachable zones), the current fingerprints and those after the change. base {floors|links|structures|scenarios: {id: fingerprint | null}} refuses the change when a whole item differs from the version it was made from (someone edited it); a patch's own base does so only for the fields and parts it changes, so the user's edits elsewhere on the floor stay and conflicts lists exactly which parts (by id) and fields were edited on both sides. Fingerprints are of items as the app keeps them (parts normalized, robot stations where the robot fits): the fingerprint of what you send, of the applied item and of an export read back are the same. Removing a floor removes its connections; scenarios must name places that exist afterwards; locked parts cannot change; removeUnlisted: true makes the site and scenarios exactly the set. action.description: request_begin opens a live group with fixed request and baseRevision; request_commit closes its confirmed prefix into one Undo; request_abort reverses only that unchanged known prefix (groupId). Separate operation IDs for each control. Children use requestGroupId, independent operationId and owned expectedRevision; only edit_space/apply_changes/put_process_scenario/delete_process_scenario/edit_equipment are supported. No simulation, import, other mutations or Plan inside a group. Unknown/reload requires explicit Studio recovery, never blind retry. apply (default): apply changes, or the upload named by transferId. write: stage one chunk of a large change set. cancel: drop the staged upload.

request.description: One changeset is one request: id is `${baseRevision.length}:${baseRevision}:<name>` (100 characters maximum including the prefix); keep id and baseRevision fixed from its first read. Commit operationId must exactly equal id (do not add a helper prefix); preview/upload operation IDs must differ. This binding is guaranteed for Studio UUID:counter revisions; overly long revisions/IDs are rejected, never truncated. After journal expiry or reload never replace baseRevision to retry. Request-specific Undo/Redo refuses another history entry. Optional scope:{floorId,partIds,attributes} permits only these existing parts and attributes, compared against actual stored data; collateral normalization, other inputs, additions, removals, array reordering and locked changes are refused. plan:true stages this fixed request for human approval in Studio; while pending, all agent writes are blocked until the person approves or cancels. External callers must supply request.scope explicitly; copied selection context alone does not enforce it.

tools.name: get_design_packet
tools.description: Create one self-contained HTML handoff from 2–10 independent saved design options, baseline first. Each option keeps its actual buildings/floors: alternatives are never treated as extra floors. Always includes scaled 2D drawings, purpose, recipient, sources, assumptions/unknowns, shared quantities, a complete part inventory, stable-ID changes (including unambiguous cross-floor transfers), fixed-part differences and geometry findings. All carry the saved inputHash; live edits cannot enter the packet. Optional 3D pictures use the frozen building or are explicitly omitted. format=json returns the structured packet; inventory-csv returns all parts with option/inputHash, ID, floor, kind, tags, source, notes and dimensions. No source URLs are fetched and no legal compliance, ROI, recommendation or simulation result is invented. Free. Large text uses nextOffset and UTF-8 SHA-256; repeat unchanged optionIds/settings, then join the content chunks.

tools.name: compare_design_options
tools.description: Compare two immutable complete layouts, without a simulation scenario. Reports each option’s drawing version, quantities, building checks (including overlapping floors), floor additions/removals, per-floor part changes and changes to the baseline’s fixed parts. Uses stable floor IDs; distinct IDs are additions/removals, not guessed matches. Unknown facts remain visible. This descriptive comparison makes no automatic recommendation or ROI claim. Free. Large results use JSON chunks.

tools.name: evaluate_design_options
tools.description: Free static evaluation of 2–10 frozen design options, baseline first. Applies the baseline brief criteria and fixed conditions to all alternatives. Counts, floor areas, geometry checks and static route lengths; no process scenario or simulation required. Unmapped text requirements, critical unknowns, unsupported routes and adjusted exact points prevent a recommendation. Objectives return non-dominated alternatives; a unique survivor may be recommended only among tested drawings. This is conditional on the supplied criteria, not a field, safety or legal guarantee. Results include evaluator version and saved input hashes; JSON chunks are supported.

tools.name: get_operation
tools.description: Read whether a change sent with an operationId applied, failed or is still running in this Studio tab, and the result it returned. Every change through the MCP link has one (your own, or the one a timeout names). The tab remembers its last 50 changes for 15 minutes; a reload forgets that transient journal. A native request checkpoint can still report a saved request.id committed earlier and its undone cursor, without reconstructing the original response or revision. Read get_space for the current Plan and checkpoint availability before a new change; never reapply a saved request with a new ID to recover its reply. unknown: the tab has no record (the change never reached it, it is older, or the tab was reloaded) or could not confirm it; read get_space before deciding. revision is the one the change made; currentRevision the one to send with the next change. sites.name: seqcraft.onrender.com
sites.description: Inspect plasmids, simulate PCR and restriction digests, compare constructs, and prepare cloning proposals in one exact, private workspace.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_capabilities
tools.description: Discover SeqCraft scientific workflows, coordinate conventions (1-based closed [start1, end1]), privacy boundaries, approval rules, and suggested agent task sequences. Use this when planning a multi-step interaction or deciding which SeqCraft tools to call.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_workspace_context
tools.description: Read the current SeqCraft workspace state, including the active molecule, current selection, selected feature, pending transaction state, active view, and registered tool count. Preferred bootstrap tool for any task involving SeqCraft.

includeDocumentList.description: Whether to include a list of all open document names, IDs, lengths, and topologies in the workspace.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_selected_context
tools.description: Read the currently selected nucleotide sequence slice and overlapping biological features in 1-based closed coordinates. Use this to inspect what the human user or current selection is highlighting without retrieving the entire molecule.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses the currently selected or active construct.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_document_revision
tools.description: Query the current revision number and canonical SHA-256 sequence hash of a document. Essential for revision-locking proposals, avoiding race conditions, and verifying mutation commits.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, checks the active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_transaction_status
tools.description: Check the lifecycle state (awaiting_approval, applied, rejected, or stale) and provenance of a staged sequence transaction. Call this after staging an edit with seqcraft_edit_sequence or candidate staging tools to check if the human approved the change.

transactionId.description: Identifier of the staged transaction to inspect. If omitted, inspects the current pending transaction.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_pending_transaction
tools.description: Check the lifecycle state (awaiting_approval, applied, rejected, or stale) and provenance of a staged sequence transaction. Call this after staging an edit with seqcraft_edit_sequence or candidate staging tools to check if the human approved the change.

transactionId.description: Identifier of the staged transaction to inspect. If omitted, inspects the current pending transaction.

tools.name: seqcraft_set_active_document
tools.description: Switch the active document tab in the SeqCraft workspace. Use this when you want to view, inspect, or edit a different open construct.

documentId.description: ID of the open document to activate.

tools.name: seqcraft_set_active_view
tools.description: Switch the primary workspace visualization view tab. Available views: map (plasmid/linear map), sequence (base-level nucleotide editor), features (annotation table), primers (primer design panel), enzymes (restriction digests), history (revision log), compare (sequence comparison/diff).

tools.name: seqcraft_select_range
tools.description: Select a continuous range of nucleotides on the active or specified molecule using 1-based closed coordinates [start1, end1]. Updates the visible editor selection for human and agent context sharing.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses the active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_select_sequence_range
tools.description: Select a continuous range of nucleotides on the active or specified molecule using 1-based closed coordinates [start1, end1]. Updates the visible editor selection for human and agent context sharing.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses the active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_select_feature
tools.description: Select an existing biological feature/annotation on the active or specified document by its unique feature ID. Highlights the feature in the viewer and opens its properties in the inspector.

documentId.description: Document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_clear_selection
tools.description: Clear the active range selection and unselect any highlighted features or primers in the SeqCraft workspace.

tools.name: seqcraft_focus_region
tools.description: Navigate, scroll, and center the editor view around a specific nucleotide region using 1-based closed coordinates [start1, end1]. Optionally selects the region or switches representation.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

preferredView.description: Optional preferred editor view (e.g. sequence or map).

tools.name: seqcraft_list_documents
tools.description: List all sequence constructs/documents currently loaded in the SeqCraft workspace with their IDs, names, topologies, lengths in base pairs, and revision numbers.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_active_document
tools.description: Retrieve summary details, topological properties, annotations count, primers count, and revision metadata for the active or specified document.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, returns active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_create_document
tools.description: Create a new sequence document in the SeqCraft workspace from a nucleotide string. Validates sequence alphabet (DNA/RNA IUPAC).

sequence.description: Nucleotide sequence (5′→3′). Supports IUPAC degenerate bases.

tools.name: seqcraft_duplicate_document
tools.description: Create an independent, isolated working copy of an existing document. Useful for safe experimentation, staging edits without altering the original construct, and testing modifications.

documentId.description: Document to duplicate. If omitted, duplicates the active document.

newName.description: Optional name for the new copy. Defaults to "<Original Name> (Copy)".

tools.name: seqcraft_update_document_metadata
tools.description: Update metadata for a document, such as renaming it or changing its topology (linear circular).

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, updates the active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_delete_document
tools.description: Remove a document from the SeqCraft workspace. To prevent accidental deletion during exploration, you must explicitly set confirmDelete: true.

documentId.description: Identifier of the document to remove.

confirmDelete.description: Must be explicitly set to true to confirm deletion.

tools.name: seqcraft_edit_sequence
tools.description: Stage an insertion, deletion, or replacement on a DNA/RNA molecule using 1-based closed coordinates. Evaluates biological consequences (CDS frames, amino acid translations, restriction sites) and stages a revision-locked transaction for human review. Does NOT modify the molecule until the human clicks Apply. Follow up with seqcraft_get_transaction_status.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

operation.description: Structured sequence edit operation (insert, delete, or replace).

type.description: Edit operation type.

start1.description: 1-based start coordinate (for delete or replace operation).

end1.description: 1-based end coordinate (for delete or replace operation).

range1.description: Alternative legacy shorthand for replacement [start1, end1].

sequence.description: Alternative legacy shorthand for replacement sequence.

tools.name: seqcraft_reverse_complement_region
tools.description: Stage an in-place reverse complement of a sequence region [start1, end1] on the target molecule. Creates a revision-locked transaction for human review.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_rotate_origin
tools.description: Stage setting a new circular origin (position 1) on a circular plasmid. Re-indexes nucleotide coordinates and feature locations. Requires a circular topology and human review.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

newOrigin1.description: 1-based nucleotide position to become the new origin (position 1).

tools.name: seqcraft_list_features
tools.description: List all annotated biological features (CDS, promoters, genes, origins, resistance markers, tags) on the target construct with their coordinates [start1, end1], strand (+/-), type, and qualifiers.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, lists features for active document.

type.description: Optional filter by feature type (e.g. CDS, promoter, gene, origin).

tools.name: seqcraft_show_feature
tools.description: Highlight and focus a specific feature on the canvas / editor view and reveal its properties in the inspector panel.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

featureId.description: Unique identifier of the feature to display.

tools.name: seqcraft_mutate_feature
tools.description: Create, update, delete, or batch-create biological annotations on the active or specified construct using 1-based closed coordinates [start1, end1]. Immediately updates document annotations and records revision provenance.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

action.description: Annotation mutation action to perform.

feature.description: Single feature input for create or update action.

type.description: Biological feature type.

strand.description: Strand orientation (+ for forward 5'->3', - for reverse complement).

qualifiers.description: Additional GenBank qualifiers (e.g. note, gene, product).

features.description: Array of feature inputs for batch_create action.

featureId.description: Feature ID to delete (for delete action).

tools.name: seqcraft_detect_known_features
tools.description: Scan the active or specified sequence against SeqCraft built-in curated biological feature library (promoters, origins, antibiotic resistance markers, reporters, tags). Returns identified matches with positions and confidence.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_propose_annotation
tools.description: Automatically detect and apply a known annotation match from the built-in database to the molecule.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

matchIndex.description: 0-based index of the detected feature match to apply.

tools.name: seqcraft_list_primers
tools.description: List all custom oligonucleotides and primers configured for the target molecule, including their sequences, lengths, and binding positions.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_mutate_primer
tools.description: Create, auto-bind, update, or delete primers on the construct. Action "add_from_sequence" automatically validates the primer, finds binding loci on the template molecule, and attaches the primer to the document.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

action.description: Primer mutation action.

sequence.description: 5'->3' primer nucleotide sequence (for create or add_from_sequence).

primerId.description: Existing primer ID (for update or delete).

tools.name: seqcraft_analyze_primer
tools.description: Compute melting temperature, GC content, molecular weight, and exact IUPAC-compatible binding loci on the template construct.

documentId.description: Template document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_simulate_pcr
tools.description: Simulate exact-match in silico PCR on a linear or circular template. Returns predicted amplicon coordinates, lengths, GC content, and primer-pair melting temperatures.

documentId.description: Template document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_analyze_restriction_sites
tools.description: Search for recognition and cut sites of standard restriction enzymes (Type II and Type IIS, e.g. EcoRI, BamHI, BsaI, BsmBI, NotI, HindIII) on the target molecule. Returns 1-based coordinates [start1, end1], forwardCut1, reverseCut1, and overhang types.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_show_restriction_site
tools.description: Highlight a restriction enzyme cut site on the map and editor view.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_simulate_digest
tools.description: Simulate single or multi-enzyme restriction digestion on a circular plasmid or linear DNA. Returns predicted fragment sizes, fragment sequences, and terminal overhang types.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

enzymeNames.description: Enzyme names for single or double digest.

tools.name: seqcraft_simulate_golden_gate
tools.description: Simulate Golden Gate multi-fragment assembly using Type IIS restriction enzymes (e.g. BsaI, BsmBI, AarI). Validates compatible overhang pairs, checks junction fidelity, and returns the assembled construct.

documentIds.description: List of document IDs participating in the assembly in order.

enzymeName.description: Type IIS enzyme driving the assembly (default: BsaI).

tools.name: seqcraft_domesticate_sequence
tools.description: Scan a sequence for internal Type IIS or standard restriction sites and return revision-bound synonymous mutation candidates to eliminate internal cut sites without altering protein translation. Follow up with seqcraft_stage_domestication_candidate to stage a proposal for human review.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_plan_domestication
tools.description: Scan a sequence for internal Type IIS or standard restriction sites and return revision-bound synonymous mutation candidates to eliminate internal cut sites without altering protein translation. Follow up with seqcraft_stage_domestication_candidate to stage a proposal for human review.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_stage_domestication_candidate
tools.description: Stage an exact synonymous mutation candidate returned by seqcraft_domesticate_sequence. Checks revision locking to ensure the molecule was not modified since analysis, then creates a revision-locked transaction for human review.

documentId.description: Optional target document ID.

tools.name: seqcraft_stage_sequence_transaction
tools.description: Stage an exact synonymous mutation candidate returned by seqcraft_domesticate_sequence. Checks revision locking to ensure the molecule was not modified since analysis, then creates a revision-locked transaction for human review.

documentId.description: Optional target document ID.

tools.name: seqcraft_prepare_restriction_clone
tools.description: Simulate restriction cloning between an insert construct and a destination vector using compatible restriction enzyme sticky ends.

tools.name: seqcraft_compare_documents
tools.description: Perform pairwise biological sequence comparison and alignment between two documents in the workspace. Returns identity percentage, nucleotide differences (substitutions, insertions, deletions), and feature discrepancies.

tools.name: seqcraft_find_orfs
tools.description: Search for open reading frames across all six reading frames using NCBI genetic code table 1 and a configurable minimum codon count.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

minCodons.description: Minimum ORF length in codons (default: 30 codons = 90 bp).

tools.name: seqcraft_find_crispr_targets
tools.description: Scan sequence for CRISPR-Cas guide RNA target sites and protospacers across multiple Cas effectors (SpCas9, SaCas9, Cas12a/Cpf1, Cas12e/CasX). Computes on-target quality scores, GC balance, Pol III termination penalties, and MMEJ frameshift predictions.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

nuclease.description: CRISPR Cas nuclease system (default: SpCas9). SpCas9 (3' NGG), SaCas9 (3' NNGRRT), Cas12a (5' TTTV), Cas12e (5' TTCN).

maxResults.description: Maximum number of target sites returned (default: 20).

tools.name: seqcraft_screen_biosecurity
tools.description: Run automated biosecurity reference pre-screening against diagnostic signature motifs of regulated Select Agents and Controlled Biological Toxins (Filoviruses, Poxviruses, Henipaviruses, Anthrax, Tularemia, Plague, BoNT, Ricin). Informational diagnostic screening only.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_copy_region_between_documents
tools.description: Extract a nucleotide region [sourceStart1, sourceEnd1] from a source construct and stage its insertion into a target construct at targetPosition1. Stages a revision-locked transaction on the target construct.

sourceStart1.description: 1-based inclusive start position on source document.

sourceEnd1.description: 1-based inclusive end position on source document.

orientation.description: Orientation of the copied fragment (default: forward).

tools.name: seqcraft_create_document_from_region
tools.description: Extract a nucleotide sub-region [start1, end1] from a construct and create a new independent construct in the workspace.

sourceDocumentId.description: Source document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

topology.description: Topology of the new document (default: linear).

tools.name: seqcraft_get_history
tools.description: Retrieve the change history log and undo/redo availability for the active or specified construct.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_undo
tools.description: Undo the most recent sequence edit on the active or specified construct in SeqCraft history.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_redo
tools.description: Redo the previously undone sequence edit on the active or specified construct in SeqCraft history.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_restore_revision
tools.description: Stage restoration of a document to a historical snapshot in the undo stack. Stages a revision-locked transaction.

documentId.description: Target document ID.

historySnapshotIndex.description: 0-based index in the document undo stack to restore.

tools.name: seqcraft_import_sequence_text
tools.description: Import DNA/RNA sequence data into SeqCraft from FASTA, GenBank flat file, or raw sequence text. Creates and opens the construct(s) in the workspace.

content.description: Sequence file content (FASTA, GenBank flat file, or raw sequence text).

name.description: Optional override name for raw sequence inputs.

tools.name: seqcraft_export_document
tools.description: Export the active or specified construct to standard bioinformatic formats: GenBank flat file (including all features and annotations), FASTA, or SeqCraft JSON format. Returns generated text, filename, revision, and sequence hash.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, exports the active document.

format.description: Export format (default: genbank).

tools.name: seqcraft_export_sequence
tools.description: Export the active or specified construct to standard bioinformatic formats: GenBank flat file (including all features and annotations), FASTA, or SeqCraft JSON format. Returns generated text, filename, revision, and sequence hash.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, exports the active document.

format.description: Export format (default: genbank).

tools.name: seqcraft_search_sequence_database

provider.description: Target database provider: 'ncbi' (GenBank/RefSeq), 'ena' (EMBL-EBI), or 'addgene'. Defaults to 'ncbi'.

query.description: Search term, organism, plasmid name, gene symbol, or keyword (e.g. 'pBR322', 'eGFP', 'lambda phage', 'cas9').

tools.name: seqcraft_import_from_database
tools.description: Fetch and import an authoritative biological sequence from a public repository (NCBI Nucleotide / GenBank, RefSeq, ENA, Addgene) by accession ID into the SeqCraft workspace. Use this tool whenever the user references a known public accession (e.g. J01749.1, NC_001416.1, OQ870305.1) or asks SeqCraft to obtain a biological sequence from a public repository. Preserves sequence topology, GenBank annotations, and origin metadata.

format.description: Format preference: 'genbank' (default, preserves annotations and features) or 'fasta'.

openAfterImport.description: Whether to activate and open the imported document in the workspace immediately. Defaults to true.

tools.name: seqcraft_generate_opentrons_protocol

mode.description: Protocol type to generate (pcr or digest).

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

ampliconLengthBp.description: Expected PCR amplicon length in base pairs.

enzymeNames.description: Restriction enzymes for digestion (for digest mode).

incubationTempC.description: Incubation temperature in Celsius for digest (default: 37).

tools.name: seqcraft_execute_actions
tools.description: Execute a batch of SeqCraft tool actions in sequential order. Rejects recursion. If any action stages a sequence mutation (status: awaiting_approval) or errors in stop_on_error mode, execution halts immediately without executing subsequent actions.

tool.description: Name of the tool to invoke.

actions.description: Ordered list of tool calls to execute.

mode.description: Execution mode (default: stop_on_error).

sites.name: tracinginsights.com
sites.description: Analyze Formula 1 racing data with interactive charts for lap times, live telemetry, timing data and race performance. Explore and Compare drivers across multiple seasons from 2018 using…

tools.name: select-f1-data
tools.description: Fill in F1 data selections (year, event, session, drivers) plus chart/telemetry toggles and submit; the dashboard applies them.

tools.name: get-current-selection
tools.description: Returns the homepage's current state as JSON: selected year, event, session, drivers, active tab (chart/data/docs), view mode (essential/expert), all chart/telemetry toggles, chart visibility picks, annotation mode, and saved favorite drivers.

tools.name: list-available-options
tools.description: Returns the current year/event/session/driver dropdown options as JSON (including driver full names/teams when the session drivers.json has loaded). Use this before select-race-data to discover valid values.

tools.name: get-data-status
tools.description: Returns whether lap times have finished loading for the currently selected drivers: status idle|no-drivers|loading|partial|ready, plus loaded/missing driver lists.

tools.name: wait-for-data
tools.description: Polls until lap times are loaded for all currently selected drivers (or until timeout). Returns the final get-data-status payload. Call after select-race-data / set-drivers before reading lap tools.

drivers.description: Optional subset of driver codes to wait for (defaults to current selection).

tools.name: get-lap-times
tools.description: Returns per-lap timing for selected drivers from the loaded homepage dataset (respects Fuel Correction and Hide Outliers toggles unless overridden). Default cleanOnly=true excludes pit-in/out, deleted, and 107% outlier laps.

cleanOnly.description: If true (default), only clean racing laps. If false, all laps with isClean/isOutlier flags.

tools.name: get-stint-summary
tools.description: Returns per-stint pace stats (compound, lap range, best/mean/median, crude deg) for selected drivers from loaded lap data. Uses the same clean-lap / fuel / outlier rules as get-lap-times.

tools.name: get-race-pace-comparison
tools.description: Head-to-head clean-lap pace comparison (shared-lap deltas, stint H2H, rolling pace). delta = driverA − driverB (negative = driverA faster). Defaults to the first two selected drivers.

drivers.description: Two-or-more driver codes (default: current selection; first two used as A/B).

tools.name: get-positions
tools.description: Returns lap-by-lap race position series for selected drivers from loaded lap data.

tools.name: get-data-table
tools.description: Returns the Data-tab style lap table as structured JSON rows (not a file download). Includes compound/stint/life/pos/sectors and clean/outlier flags. Prefer this over trigger-csv-export for agents.

hideOutliers.description: Override outliers toggle (flags only; all rows still returned).

tools.name: get-telemetry-summary
tools.description: Returns which telemetry laps are loaded in state.telData (dataKeys, drivers, laps, channel lists, point counts). Call select-lap first. For channel units see list-telemetry-channels.

tools.name: list-telemetry-channels
tools.description: Returns the TracingInsights telemetry channel catalog (ids, aliases, units, descriptions) from DATA_REFERENCE.md / Q.py tel.json fields: speed, throttle, brake, drs, rpm, gear, distance, rel_distance, acc_x/y/z, x/y/z, DriverAhead, DistanceToDriverAhead, time.

tools.name: get-telemetry-status
tools.description: Returns whether selected telemetry laps are present in state.telData: idle|no-laps|loading|partial|ready.

laps.description: Optional dataKeys or 'DRV-lap' pairs; defaults to selectedLaps.

tools.name: wait-for-telemetry
tools.description: Polls until the requested (or currently selected) telemetry laps are in state.telData. Use after select-lap / auto-fastest.

laps.description: dataKeys or 'ANT-58' style refs (defaults to selectedLaps).

tools.name: get-telemetry-stats
tools.description: Aggregate stats for loaded telemetry laps: top/avg/min speed, throttle/brake/DRS duty, gear shifts, peak accelerations, lap distance. Does not return full sample arrays.

laps.description: dataKeys or DRV-lap refs (default: all loaded / selected).

tools.name: get-telemetry-channel
tools.description: Returns distance/time-aligned samples for one channel on a loaded lap (decimated; default maxPoints=150, max 500). Channels: speed, throttle, brake, drs, rpm, gear, acc_x/y/z, x/y/z, DistanceToDriverAhead, etc. Prefer get-telemetry-stats for aggregates.

lap.description: dataKey or 'ANT-58' / driver+lap via separate fields.

driver.description: 3-letter code if not using full dataKey.

lapNumber.description: Lap number if not using full dataKey.

tools.name: compare-telemetry
tools.description: Distance-aligns lap B onto lap A and returns decimated samples with delta = A − B for a channel (default speed). Both laps must be loaded via select-lap. For cumulative lap-time gap vs Distance (the Time Delta chart), use get-time-delta — do not pass channel "time".

channel.description: Channel to compare (default "speed"). Not "time" — use get-time-delta.

tools.name: get-time-delta
tools.description: Returns the same Distance-vs-gap series as the telemetry Time Delta chart. reference = first lap (lapA), compare = second (lapB). delta = compare − reference in seconds (positive = compare behind/slower). mode auto uses sector-anchored math when Align is on and sector times exist (same as the UI); otherwise classic length-scaled interpolation. Prefer this over compare-telemetry channel=time.

lapA.description: Reference lap dataKey or DRV-lap (default: first selected/loaded).

lapB.description: Compare lap dataKey or DRV-lap (default: second selected/loaded).

mode.description: auto (default) follows Align toggle; "classic" / "sector" force an algorithm.

tools.name: get-fastest-laps
tools.description: From loaded lap-times data, returns each selected driver's fastest clean (non pit-in/out, non-outlier) lap with sector times, plus ranking and head-to-head gap. Optional quali segment filter (Q1/Q2/Q3). Use before select-lap / get-time-delta.

segment.description: Optional qualifying segment filter, e.g. "Q3". Omit for whole session.

tools.name: get-corners
tools.description: Returns corners.json for the current session (number, distance m, x/y, angle) plus track rotation. Loaded automatically when the first telemetry lap is selected.

tools.name: select-race-data
tools.description: Sets the year, event, session and/or drivers on the F1 telemetry homepage in one call. Each provided value is applied in order (year → event → session → drivers), waiting for the UI to load each downstream list. Omit a field to leave it unchanged.

event.description: Event / Grand Prix name as shown in the dropdown, e.g. "British Grand Prix".

tools.name: set-year
tools.description: Selects a season year on the homepage. Resets event, session and drivers (they must be re-selected afterwards).

tools.name: set-event
tools.description: Selects an event / Grand Prix for the currently selected year. Resets session and drivers.

event.description: Event name as shown in the dropdown, e.g. "British Grand Prix".

tools.name: set-session
tools.description: Selects a session (e.g. Race, Qualifying) for the currently selected event. Resets drivers. Waits for the driver list to refresh for the new session.

tools.name: set-drivers
tools.description: Selects which drivers to compare for the current session, by 3-letter code (e.g. VER, HAM). Waits for the driver list to load if needed.

tools.name: switch-tab
tools.description: Switches the main view between the Chart, Data (lap times table) and Docs (FIA documents) tabs.

tools.name: set-view-mode
tools.description: Switches between the Essential (core charts) and Expert (advanced charts) view modes.

mode.description: View mode to activate.

enabled.description: true to enable, false to disable.

tools.name: set-data-table-column
tools.description: Shows or hides a Data-tab column group (same as the table column toggles). Columns: compounds, stints, tyre-life, track-status, positions, personal-best, pitstops, sector-times. Open the Data tab first so the table is rendered.

enabled.description: true to show, false to hide.

tools.name: set-telemetry-layout
tools.description: Reorders telemetry charts (same as Edit layout drag/up-down). Pass an ordered list of chart ids; omitted ids are appended in the default order. Ids: speedchart, deltachart-section, throttlechart, brakechart, driveractionchart, gearchart, rpchart, drschart, driveraheadchart, distancetodriveraheadchart, gaptodriveraheadchart, acc_xchart, acc_ychart, acc_zchart, elevationchart.

order.description: Desired chart id order (partial lists are completed with defaults).

tools.name: set-stint-lowess-frac
tools.description: Sets the stint chart LOWESS smoothing fraction (0.05–1.0), same as the Smoothing slider next to Tyre Performance.

tools.name: clear-selected-laps
tools.description: Removes all laps from the Selected Laps control (clears loaded telemetry compare set).

tools.name: remove-selected-lap
tools.description: Removes one lap from Selected Laps (e.g. driver VER lap 10).

tools.name: set-quali-segment
tools.description: Filters lap/stint/tyre charts to a qualifying segment (Q1/Q2/Q3/SQ1/…). Pass "All" or "" to clear. Only available for qualifying-style sessions after data loads.

tools.name: set-sector-visibility
tools.description: Shows or hides a sector series on the Expert sector chart (S1/S2/S3 chips). Requires Expert mode and loaded lap data so the sector controls exist.

enabled.description: true to show the sector, false to hide it.

tools.name: list-stint-chips
tools.description: Returns the current stint analysis chips (driver, stint number, visible, pinned) from the Expert stint driver form. Empty if Expert mode is off or stint data has not rendered.

tools.description: Toggles a stint checkbox in the Expert stint analysis form (same as the per-stint chips). Pass driver + stint + enabled, or driver + mode "all"|"none" for Select all / Hide all.

stint.description: Stint number (1-based), required unless mode is set.

enabled.description: true to show the stint, false to hide (ignored when mode is set).

mode.description: Bulk action: "all" = Select all, "none" = Hide all for that driver.

tools.name: set-stint-pin
tools.description: Pins/unpins a stint on the Expert stint chart (📌 buttons). Pass driver + stint + pinned, or clearAll:true to unpin every stint.

pinned.description: true to pin, false to unpin.

clearAll.description: If true, clicks Unpin all (ignores other args).

tools.name: set-annotation-tool
tools.description: Selects the active annotation toolbar tool (Expert annotation mode): select, pencil, text, arrow, line, rect, ellipse, eraser.

tools.name: set-annotation-color
tools.description: Sets the global annotation stroke/fill color (hex, e.g. #00ff00).

color.description: CSS hex color, e.g. #00ff00.

tools.name: annotation-undo
tools.description: Undoes the last annotation action on all registered charts.

tools.name: annotation-redo
tools.description: Redoes the last undone annotation action on all registered charts.

tools.name: annotation-clear
tools.description: Clears all annotations on registered charts (same as Clear All on the toolbar).

tools.name: set-chart-visibility
tools.description: Shows or hides a lap-time or telemetry chart (same as the Expert Chart settings modal). Lap charts: lapchart, heatmap, stint, sector, tyre, position, race-trace. Telemetry: speed, delta, throttle, brake, driver-action, gear, rpm, drs, driver-ahead, distance-ahead, gap-ahead, acc-x, acc-y, acc-z, elevation.

chart.description: Which chart to show or hide.

visible.description: true to show, false to hide.

tools.name: reset-chart-visibility
tools.description: Restores the default Chart settings picks so every lap-time and telemetry chart is visible again.

tools.name: reset-telemetry-layout
tools.description: Restores the default telemetry chart order (same as the Reset layout button next to Edit layout in Expert mode).

tools.name: add-favorite-driver
tools.description: Saves a 3-letter driver code to the user's favorites (used for auto-selection when the driver is available).

code.description: 3-letter driver code, e.g. "HAM".

tools.name: clear-favorites
tools.description: Removes all saved favorite driver codes.

tools.name: select-lap
tools.description: Loads and selects a specific lap's telemetry for the current session (e.g. VER lap 12). Year, event and session must already be selected; the lap appears in the selected-laps control once loaded.

tools.name: trigger-chart-screenshot
tools.description: Triggers a PNG download of a chart — the same action as clicking its Download button. Charts: lapchart, heatmap, stint, sector, tyre-strategy, position-changes, race-trace, weather, track-map, speed, delta, throttle, brake, gear, rpm, drs, elevation.

tools.description: Triggers a CSV download of the lap-times data table. The Data tab must be populated first (session + drivers selected).

tools.name: set-annotation-mode
tools.description: Switches the chart annotation toolbar on or off (expert mode).

enabled.description: true to enable annotation mode, false to disable.

sites.name: dashboard.orderly.network
sites.description: Orderly dashboard

tools.name: get_site_overview
tools.description: START HERE. Returns a map of this site: what it is, its areas, which tools back each area, common multi-step flows, parameter conventions, and suggested first queries. Call this once to get oriented before using the other tools. This is a read-only analytics dashboard for the Orderly Network perpetual-futures DEX; it does not place trades.

tools.name: get_dashboard_main
tools.description: Daily platform totals for Orderly: taker/cumulative volume, revenue (fees), TVL, deposits/withdrawals, new accounts/addresses, and active builders, as a historical time series. For a live snapshot use get_market_summary; for weekly/monthly user aggregates use get_metrics_overview. Returns rows newest-last over the trailing `days` window.

tools.name: get_tvl_by_chain
tools.description: Total Value Locked broken down by chain, plus a total row. Drives the TVL By Chain widget. Returns newest snapshot rows.

tools.name: get_tvl_by_token
tools.description: TVL and token balance held per collateral token over a trailing window. Drives the TVL By Token widget.

tools.name: get_weekly_symbol_volume
tools.description: Weekly per-symbol volume and listed-markets count from the analytics API. For the live market list (prices, 24h change, open interest) use get_markets.

tools.name: get_funding_rates
tools.description: 8-hour funding rates for every perpetual symbol, from a trailing start date. For cross-exchange funding comparisons use get_funding_comparison.

days.description: Trailing days for the start date (default 30).

tools.name: get_daily_liquidations_by_symbol
tools.description: Daily liquidation notional aggregated per perpetual symbol across all markets. For individual recent liquidation events of one symbol use get_recent_liquidations.

tools.name: get_staking_daily
tools.description: Daily $ORDER staking metrics: staked/unstaked/net amounts, cumulative staker addresses, buybacks, and burned ORDER. Drives the Staking Daily widget.

tools.name: get_builder_daily
tools.description: Per-builder daily metrics: taker/maker/total volume, active users, broker fees, and net flow. Drives the Builder Volume, Builder Active Traders, Builder Revenue, and Net Flow By Builder widgets.

tools.name: get_fund_flows_by_broker
tools.description: Daily deposits, withdrawals, and net fund flow per broker. Drives the Net Flow By Builder widget (fund-flow variant).

tools.name: get_fund_flows_by_chain
tools.description: Daily deposits, withdrawals, and net fund flow per chain. Drives the Fund Flows By Chain widget.

tools.name: get_dex_users
tools.description: Per-builder user activity snapshot: DAU/WAU/MAU with day/week/month-over-month deltas and new-user counts. Drives the DEX Users widget.

tools.name: get_metrics_overview
tools.description: Weekly and monthly aggregates for new users, active users, trading volume, and Orderly revenue. For daily historical totals use get_dashboard_main.

tools.name: get_volume_segments
tools.description: Weekly trading volume split by market-maker vs retail segment. Drives the Volume Segments widget.

tools.name: get_stake_users
tools.description: Weekly average active stakers. Drives the Stake Users widget.

tools.name: get_stake_vs_supply
tools.description: Weekly ORDER staked vs circulating supply and staking ratio. Drives the Stake vs Supply widget.

tools.name: get_omnivault_tvl
tools.description: Weekly average TVL per OmniVault (USD millions). Drives the OmniVault TVL widget.

tools.name: get_distributor_stats
tools.description: Referral distributor statistics: invitee counts, graduated invitees, revenue share, and fee tier. Drives the Distributors widget. Returns an array of distributor rows.

tools.name: get_distributor_invitees
tools.description: Per-invitee detail for referral distributors: invite date, DEX, status, and 30D volume/revenue share. Returns an array of invitee rows.

tools.name: get_market_share
tools.description: Orderly's DEX perpetuals market share vs. other on-chain perp venues, computed from CoinGecko 24h derivatives volume and DefiLlama open interest. Drives the Market Share widget. Returns ranked protocols with volume, open interest, and share %.

tools.name: get_markets
tools.description: Snapshot of all active perpetual markets: the futures market list, 24h price changes, and per-symbol open interest. Drives the Markets page. Returns an object { markets, priceChanges, openInterest }. Optional search (a case-insensitive substring on the symbol), sort_by (24h_volume | 24h_change | open_interest | symbol), limit (max 200), and desc (default true) filter and rank the markets and trim the priceChanges / openInterest arrays to the same symbol set. Defaults to 50 markets in API order; pass limit: 200 for the full set.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring on the symbol (e.g. "btc", "sol", "perp_btc").

sort_by.description: Rank markets by this metric (default: API order).

limit.description: Max markets to return after filter/sort (default 50; max 200).

tools.name: get_market_detail
tools.description: Composite single-symbol bundle for the market detail page. Returns only the requested sections (default: all of market info, top-50 orderbook levels, recent trades, funding history, and OHLCV candles). Requesting fewer sections keeps the payload small. Drives the Price Chart, Orderbook, Recent Trades, and Funding Chart.

symbol.description: Perp symbol. Accepts a base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

include.description: Sections to return; omit for all.

tools.name: get_symbol_info
tools.description: Full configuration for a single perpetual symbol: leverage limits (1/base_imr), tick/lot sizes, price precision, and status flags. Returns the symbol info object.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (ETH) or full form.

tools.name: get_market_summary
tools.description: Live platform-wide market snapshot: 24h volume, open interest, trader counts, and fee totals across all symbols. For historical daily time series use get_dashboard_main; for weekly/monthly user aggregates use get_metrics_overview.

tools.name: get_funding_comparison
tools.description: Cross-exchange funding rate comparison: last value plus 1d/7d/30d averages per symbol across venues (Orderly vs. Binance, Bybit, etc.). Omit symbol for all symbols. For per-symbol 8h funding history use get_funding_rates.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form; omit for all.

tools.name: get_recent_liquidations
tools.description: Recent individual liquidation events for one symbol: side, size, notional, mark/liquidation price, and the liquidated account. For daily liquidation totals aggregated across all symbols use get_daily_liquidations_by_symbol.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

limit.description: Max events (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: get_top_traders
tools.description: Top addresses ranked by a chosen metric (notional, volume, PnL, or trade count) for a symbol or platform-wide. Paginated via cursor. Drives the Top Traders panel and Whale Leaderboard.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form; omit for platform-wide.

sort_by.description: Ranking metric (default notional).

limit.description: Page size (default 50, max 200).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response — pass it back unchanged.

tools.name: get_whale_context
tools.description: Whale research bundle for a single address: account state (collateral, PnL), open positions, and recent trades. Requires an address; optionally scope to a broker or account_id. Drives the Whale Detail modal.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

tools.name: get_platform_positions
tools.description: Platform-wide open positions for a symbol (large-position liquidation-heatmap data). Returns up to 1000 positions filtered by minimum notional. Drives the Liquidation Heatmap.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form.

tools.name: get_insurance_fund
tools.description: Orderly insurance fund balance, holdings, and status. Drives the Insurance Fund widget.

tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description: Daily trading leaderboard: realized PnL and perp volume per trader over a date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Supports pagination, broker/address filters, sort, and aggregation by address, account, or date. Drives the Leaderboard (trading) tab.

page.description: 1-based page (default 1).

sort.description: Default descending_realized_pnl.

address.description: Filter to a wallet address.

tools.name: get_positions
tools.description: Open-positions leaderboard: largest open positions by notional, optionally filtered by account, broker, or symbol. Drives the Leaderboard (positions) tab.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

offset.description: Pagination offset (default 0).

limit.description: Page size (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: resolve_address
tools.description: Resolve a wallet address or account ID into its Orderly broker/account pairs. Accepts an EVM address (0x + 40 hex), a Solana address (43-44 base58 chars), or an account ID (0x + 64 hex). Returns an array of {broker_id, account_id, …} pairs for the identity. For address queries (not account IDs) each account is enriched with 90-day perp_volume and realized_pnl, sorted by volume descending — matching the Search results page. First step of the Explorer/address flow.

address.description: EVM address, Solana address, or Orderly account ID.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: Historical trading events for an account: trades, settlements, liquidations, ADLs, and margin transfers (versioned v1/v2/v3 already flattened to a uniform shape). Time range is capped at 31 days; omit both times for the most recent page. Drives the address Events tab. Returns { events, nextCursor, pageSizeLimit, tradesCount }; pass the nextCursor back as the cursor param to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor (the nextCursor value from a prior response). Do not construct this object yourself — only pass back the cursor you received.

tools.name: get_account_state
tools.description: Account snapshot for an address: collateral, margin ratios, 24h PnL, and all OPEN positions (qty, notional, entry/mark price, leverage, est. liquidation price). Drives the address Positions tab.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

tools.name: get_portfolio
tools.description: Daily account-value time series with cumulative PnL (equity curve) for an address, up to 365 days. Drives the Portfolio Chart on the address page.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

limit.description: Max snapshots (default 90, max 365).

tools.name: get_brokers
tools.description: Directory of all Orderly brokers (broker_id → human-readable broker_name), sorted by name. Use to label broker_id values returned by other tools.

tools.name: get_all_symbols
tools.description: Every known perp symbol (including delisted) as a hash→name map: {symbol, symbol_hash}. Use to resolve keccak256 symbol hashes in event/position data to display names. Active symbols are also available via get_markets.

tools.name: get_all_tokens
