tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: MANDATORY FIRST STEP for any video editing, review, or enhancement request. Returns the full project: clips, durations, zooms, overlays, audio, plus the Director Playbook and the autonomous decision tree for vague requests like 'edit this video'. All timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds; check timelineRevision — if it changed since your last read, your cached observations are stale and you MUST re-ingest.

tools.name: list_clips
tools.description: Returns all timeline video clips with cumulative start/end timestamps, durations, speeds, and transitions. All times are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

tools.name: list_scenes
tools.description: Returns all timeline segments (scenes) with cumulative timeline start/end timestamps, duration, speed, and transitions. All times are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

tools.name: get_silence_intervals
tools.description: Detects audio silence and dead-air intervals where the speaker is inactive, returned in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. Use for ripple trimming: dead air >= 1.5s is a cut candidate ({op:'cut', dropSilence:true}). Requires transcription — call generate_captions first if status is PENDING_TRANSCRIPTION.

minDurationSec.description: Minimum silence duration threshold in seconds (default 1.0).

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Returns the spoken transcript with timestamps in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. If empty, call generate_captions to transcribe. Re-fetch this after any cut/delete/speed change — earlier timestamps go stale when the timeline shifts.

tools.name: inspect_timeline
tools.description: Detailed inspector of all clips, timeline timestamps, transitions, speed, zooms, and overlays. All times are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

tools.name: get_click_log
tools.description: Returns cursor telemetry in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. Default response is COMPACT: per-20s attention buckets (where the mouse was active), click counts, and suggested zoom timestamps — plus exact cursor (x, y) interpolation via atTimestamp. Pass detail:'full' for the raw point list (token-heavy; rarely needed). Click clusters are prime zoom candidates; a parked cursor (no recent events) is NOT a good zoom target.

atTimestamp.description: Optional: interpolate and return the exact cursor (x, y) at this timeline timestamp

detail.description: 'summary' (default) returns attention buckets only; 'full' also includes the raw point list.

tools.name: export_clip
tools.description: Renders and exports the edited video locally in the browser via WebCodecs. Prompts the human for confirmation before encoding. Returns a downloadable Blob URL and file metadata upon completion.

format.description: Video container format. 'mp4' (H.264) is most compatible; 'webm' (VP9) is smaller.

resolution.description: Export resolution. '1080p' is standard HD, '720p' is faster, '4k' is ultra high-res.

tools.name: propose_zoom_points
tools.description: Proposes zoom-in keyframes at specific timeline timestamps. Proposals appear as ghost diamond markers on the timeline for human review — they are NOT applied until commit_staged_changes. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

timestamps.description: Timeline seconds where zoom-in keyframes should be placed.

focalX.description: Normalized focal X center (0 to 1, default 0.5).

focalY.description: Normalized focal Y center (0 to 1, default 0.5).

tools.name: add_text_overlay
tools.description: Stages a styled text caption or annotation overlay at a specific timeline timestamp and screen position. Supports custom fonts, sizes, colors, backdrops, and entrance/exit animations. Staged overlays appear for review until committed. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

text.description: The text content to display (no emojis).

timestamp.description: When the text should appear (timeline seconds).

color.description: Text color hex or rgba (e.g. '#ffffff', '#facc15').

tools.name: set_background
tools.description: Stages a background color or gradient change. Fills the stage padding area around the video when aspect ratio padding is visible.

kind.description: Background type: 'solid' (single color) or 'gradient' (two-stop linear gradient).

color.description: Hex color for solid background, e.g. '#0a0a0a'.

stops.description: Array of two hex colors for gradient, e.g. ['#007cf0', '#7928ca'].

tools.name: generate_captions
tools.description: Transcribes the video's audio (camera/mic + screen tracks separately) and generates timestamped additive subtitle phrases across the timeline — same pipeline as the manual Auto-Generate button. Always call this first if get_transcript is empty — cuts, zooms and silence detection all depend on speech timestamps.

language.description: Audio language: 'auto', 'hinglish', 'en', 'hi', 'es', 'fr', 'de', 'ja', 'zh'. Default 'auto'.

includeSpeakerLabels.description: Prefix captions with 'Speaker:' / 'Screen:' (default true, matches the manual Speaker toggle).

presetId.description: Caption style preset id: viral, clean, outline, subtitles, electric, highlighter (default 'viral').

speakerFontSize.description: Font size px for Speaker captions (default 36).

screenFontSize.description: Font size px for Screen captions (default 28).

tools.name: split_clip
tools.description: Splits the clip at a timeline timestamp into two segments. Use before delete_clip to remove an unwanted range. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. The response includes the new clip map — use it, not your pre-split observations.

timestamp.description: Timeline second where the split cut should occur.

tools.name: split_segment
tools.description: Splits the video clip at the given timeline timestamp. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds. The response includes the new clip map.

timestamp.description: Timeline second where the split should occur.

tools.name: delete_clip
tools.description: Deletes a clip segment and ripple-joins the adjacent clips. THIS SHIFTS THE TIMELINE: every timestamp after the deleted range moves earlier. The response flags timelineShifted — you MUST re-ingest get_project_state and get_transcript afterwards and never reuse pre-delete timestamps. Cannot delete the only remaining clip.

clipIndex.description: 0-based index of the clip segment to delete.

tools.name: set_clip_transition
tools.description: Sets the incoming transition effect and duration on a clip segment. Does not shift timestamps.

tools.name: set_speed
tools.description: Sets playback speed multiplier for the selected segment (0.5x, 1x, 1.5x, 2x). THIS SHIFTS THE TIMELINE — re-ingest after calling.

tools.description: Sets the stage aspect ratio preset ('16:9', '9:16', '1:1', '4:3', or 'source'). Does not shift timestamps.

Snapshot rendering can take seconds on long recordings — request only the timestamps you need and set includeSnapshot:false when you only need features. Use the grid cells to reference screen regions in locate_visual_target. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

timestamps.description: List of timeline timestamps to query

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to generate base64 image snapshots for visual inspection (default: true)

tools.description: Grounds a visual target into a safe zoom focal point via a 3-tier hierarchy: (1) click telemetry near the timestamp (confidence 1.0), (2) parse VLM output — Gemini-style 0-1000 bbox, 3x3 grid cell (A1..C3), or normalized x/y — from probe_frames snapshots, (3) fallback center with guidance. Timestamps are CURRENT TIMELINE seconds.

query.description: Target element description, e.g. 'elephant' or 'search bar'

tools.name: propose_edits
tools.description: The main editing tool: applies one atomic batch of edit ops in a single call. STAGE BASELINE (automatic): every batch applies the signature look — gradient backdrop, 28px stage padding, 16px rounded frame corners — unless the batch carries its own {op:'bg'}. ZOOMS PERSIST: zoom windows auto-extend until the next scene boundary or a sustained cursor move to a different region (minimum 4s hold). Ops (times in CURRENT TIMELINE seconds): {op:'cut', t0, t1} removes the exact window — the deterministic form, pass the intervals from get_silence_intervals; {op:'cut', t, dropSilence:true} expands t to the matching silence interval; a cut without a window or matching silence is REJECTED, never silently skipped. Also: {op:'zoom', t0, t1, cx?, cy?, scale?, ease?}; {op:'text', t, text, pos?:'top'|'bottom'|'center', dur?, fontSize?, fontWeight?, color?, backgroundColor?, animation?}; {op:'cam', corner:'tl'|'tr'|'bl'|'br', shape?, size?}; {op:'bg', kind:'solid'|'gradient', c0, c1?}; {op:'trans', at, kind, dur?}; {op:'speed', t0, t1, mult}. mode 'replace' clears prior agent zooms/overlays but NEVER Whisper captions. MANDATORY RULES: (1) NO emojis in text. (2) Multi-stage sequential pans (1.6x-1.8x) for long content. (3) Invert overlay position vs zoom half. (4) Verify targets via probe_frames, not a parked cursor. AFTER CUTS: the response sets cutsApplied and timelineShifted — re-ingest get_project_state + get_transcript before any further op batch. CHECK rejectedOps: a rejected cut means dead air was NOT removed.

ops.description: Array of EditOp objects (see description for the exact shapes)

plan.description: Concise explanation of your editorial strategy

mode.description: replace (default) or append

If no `form` surface is listed, no form is open — there is nothing to read, so do not call this. Call it before filling a listed form. Omit form_id only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Changed fields are highlighted for the user and can be undone. Never claim to submit the form — ask the user to review the highlighted fields and submit.

tools.name: get_procurement_report_editor

tools.name: edit_procurement_report
tools.description: Edit sections of the live procurement report draft WITHOUT saving. Requires execution_id and expected_editor_revision from get_procurement_report_editor. Apply at most 20 edits per call; read again before each additional batch. Update only the requested sections; omitted header/body fields and all other sections are preserved. Preserve source citations and links. Put section headings in header, not body_markdown. Insert after a stable ID, or at the start with after_stable_id=null. Remove deletes only that section. Edits apply atomically and fail if the user changed the draft since your read. Read again after a conflict. Never claim changes are saved; the user reviews the editor and clicks Save.

tools.name: prepare_spend_program_workflow_edit

Use form="request" for approval workflows and form="change_request" for dedicated change request workflows. Change request preparation saves the request form first. Await success, then pass the returned template_id and custom_form_collection_log_entry_uuid to GetBlankCanvasConditionFields and ApplyBlankCanvasWorkflowEdits. The template_id is resolved after preparation; use it instead of earlier editor or autosave pointers. Prepare again after question edits; discard cached condition fields when the returned revision changes. On failure, reread the editor and prepare again rather than falling back to published questions. Does not save or publish the program or edit the workflow.

tools.description: Create, name, rename, or remove request form sections and add, update, or remove custom questions in the spend program editor open on the user's screen WITHOUT saving. Requesting programs only. form selects the target: request (default) edits the request form and takes ids from intake.sections; change_request edits the change order form requesters fill in when changing an approved request and takes ids from change_request_intake.sections, which only purchase order programs have. Section operations are only supported for form=request. add_section names the sole untitled section if present, preserving its questions, or appends a new section. update_section names or renames an existing section by section_id while preserving its id, questions, and conditions. remove_section deletes the section and all its questions and clears dependent visibility or required-when rules, including change order rules. A section containing a protected question cannot be removed. Removing the last section leaves a fresh empty untitled section. Create sections first, then use created_section_ids from the result as section_id when adding questions. If the request form uses sections, every section must have a meaningful, nonblank title and at least one question before saving or publishing. When organizing a form into sections, use update_section to name any existing unnamed sections. A sole section with title=null is the default unsectioned form and may remain unnamed and empty, including after removing the last section. Leave new question descriptions blank unless the user explicitly requests them; do not repeat the question title. Only add question types listed in that form's available_question_types; other types are rejected for this program. sites.name: bandarra.me
sites.description: WebMCP-enabled text editor with imperative tools for document I/O, workspace CRUD, on-device translation, and sub-agent (planner / researcher / writer / reviewer) delegation.

tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: Lists all skills available in this workspace. Returns an array of { id, name, description } entries. Use read_skill to fetch the full instructions for a skill, or delegate_to_skill to run one.

tools.name: read_skill
tools.description: Returns the full definition of a skill (id, name, description, instructions, optional model) given its id or name. Use this before delegate_to_skill to inspect what a skill does.

id.description: The skill id. Either id or name must be provided.

name.description: The skill name (case-insensitive). Either id or name must be provided.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Reads the complete current editor content.

tools.name: read_selection
tools.description: Reads the currently selected text in the editor.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Finds all occurrences of a query string in the document. Returns the line and column of each match.

query.description: The text to search for.

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.description: Returns metadata about the current document: character count, word count, and line count.

tools.name: get_current_mode
tools.description: Returns the current UI mode: 'editor' (Monaco editor is visible) or 'preview' (Markdown preview is visible). Check this before making edits to ensure the editor is accessible.

tools.name: request_switch_to_editor
tools.description: Requests the user to switch from Preview mode to Editor mode. This will display a prompt to the user and pause until they accept or decline. Call this before attempting edits when in preview mode.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Proposes a targeted edit. This tool pauses and waits for user approval. ONLY use this for small, localized changes (e.g., 1-2 sentences). Never pass the entire document.

originalText.description: The exact, minimal string of text to replace. Must be short. Do NOT pass the whole document.

replacementText.description: The new text to replace the originalText with.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Proposes a complete rewrite. This tool pauses and waits for user approval. ONLY use this when the user explicitly requests a total rewrite of the entire document.

content.description: The full new document content.

tools.name: get_active_doc_info
tools.description: Returns the id and title of the document currently open in the editor.

tools.name: list_workspace_docs
tools.description: Lists all documents in the workspace. Returns an array of { id, title } objects.

tools.name: read_workspace_doc
tools.description: Reads the full content of a specific document. Returns { title, content } or { error }.

tools.name: query_workspace_doc
tools.description: Asks a question about a specific document using a sub-agent. Returns { summary, excerpt } where excerpt is the most relevant verbatim passage.

query.description: The question about the document.

tools.name: query_workspace
tools.description: Asks a question spanning all workspace documents and synthesizes the results. Returns { summary, sources: [{ id, title, excerpt }] }.

query.description: The question to answer across all documents.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Creates a new document in the workspace with the given title and optional initial content. Providing content avoids a separate write step. Pauses for user authorization before creating.

title.description: The title for the new document.

content.description: Optional initial content for the new document. If omitted the document is created blank.

tools.name: rename_document
tools.description: Renames an existing document in the workspace. Pauses for user authorization before renaming.

title.description: The new title for the document.

tools.name: delete_document
tools.description: Deletes a document from the workspace. Pauses for user authorization before deleting. If the deleted document was active, a different document becomes active.

tools.name: switch_active_document
tools.description: Switches the active document in the editor. Saves the current document content before switching. Does not require user authorization.

id.description: The document ID to switch to.

tools.name: translate
tools.description: Translate a piece of text from one language to another using an on-device AI model. Languages are specified as BCP 47 tags (e.g. 'en', 'fr', 'ja').

text.description: The text to translate.

sourceLanguage.description: BCP 47 language tag of the source language (e.g. "en").

targetLanguage.description: BCP 47 language tag of the target language (e.g. "fr").

tools.name: delegate_to_skill
tools.description: Delegates a task to a named skill (sub-agent). The skill runs with read-only access and returns its response as a string. Interpret the response and act on it accordingly.

skillName.description: The exact name of the skill to invoke.

task.description: The specific task or instructions to pass to the skill.

tools.name: invoke_agent
tools.description: Delegates an ad-hoc task to a generic sub-agent. The sub-agent runs with the given system prompt and optional tool groups. Returns { result: string } with the sub-agent's final response.

systemPrompt.description: The system prompt / instructions for the sub-agent.

task.description: The task or question to send to the sub-agent.

tools.description: Optional tool group names to give the sub-agent. Supported: 'workspace_readonly'.

tools.name: invoke_planner
tools.description: Decomposes a high-level task into a structured step-by-step Plan. Returns a JSON string: { goal, steps: [{ id, instruction, dependsOn }] }. The Orchestrator reads the plan and dispatches each step using the appropriate tools.

task.description: The high-level task to decompose into a plan.

context.description: Optional additional context (e.g. current document summary, workspace doc list).

tools.name: invoke_researcher
tools.description: Queries workspace documents and synthesizes a structured answer. Returns JSON: { summary, sources: [{ id, title, excerpt }] }. Use this when the task requires finding information across workspace documents before writing or reviewing.

query.description: The question or information need to research.

docIds.description: Optional list of document IDs to restrict the search to. If omitted, all workspace documents are queried.

tools.name: invoke_writer
tools.description: Generates draft text for a single targeted section from an instruction and optional research/style context. Returns { draft: string } — raw text only, no edits applied. After receiving the draft, apply it using edit() for the target section. Do NOT use this to rewrite the whole document at once — use invoke_planner to break full-document tasks into per-section steps.

instruction.description: What to write. Be explicit: specify the target section, desired length, and any constraints.

researchContext.description: JSON-encoded ResearchResult from invoke_researcher. Inject when the draft should cite workspace sources.

styleContext.description: A verbatim excerpt from the document the Writer should match in tone, voice, and formatting.

tools.name: invoke_reviewer
tools.description: Evaluates a draft against explicit criteria and returns structured feedback. Returns JSON: { passed: boolean, issues: [{ severity, location?, description, fix? }], summary }. Use after invoke_writer to check a draft before applying it. If passed is false and error-severity issues remain after 3 Writer→Reviewer cycles, present the best available draft via edit() or write() and summarise remaining issues in your response.

text.description: The draft text to review.

criteria.description: Review criteria to check against (e.g. 'grammatical correctness', 'consistent use of past tense', 'no unsupported factual claims').

continuation.title: Continuation

on_sale.title: On sale

page_offset.title: Within-page continuation
page_offset.description: Use the exact page_offset returned in next, with its page/per_page and unchanged filters. Start at zero.

orderby.title: Order by
orderby.description: Price sorts current decimal purchase prices, using the cheapest sellable variation where needed; ties use product ID.

order.title: Order

tools.name: woo_add_to_cart

First call woo_search_products_api to resolve the exact current product; use woo_get_product_api only with an ID returned by that search when more detail is needed. Then use only the product_id and variation_id returned by those lookups. Never infer or guess an ID from a product name.

product_id.description: Exact product ID returned by the current product lookup. Never guess this value.

quantity.description: Quantity to add.

variation_id.description: Optional exact variation ID returned by the current product lookup. Never guess this value.

sites.name: fieldwork-beat-machine.openai.chatgpt.site
sites.description: A tactile 12-voice beat machine with classic drum-machine grooves, deep synths, keyboard and touch pads, WebMCP controls, and stereo WAV export.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Read the current beat-machine preset, tempo, transport, musical key and scale, 24-sound library, six editable instrument slots and their complete sound-design parameters, selected pad bank, all 12 playable pads, plus the 12 by 16 velocity and MIDI-note patterns.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Read the complete portable Fieldwork project document, including its name, pattern, notes, mix, musical key, and six instrument patches. Use it for backup or as input to load_project.

tools.name: load_project
tools.description: Validate and atomically replace the current local project with a Fieldwork project document. Stops playback and recording, preserves an undo step, and autosaves locally. Invalid documents leave the current project unchanged.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Create a portable JSON backup of the current project and optionally download it. This does not render audio; use export_track for WAV audio.

tools.name: undo_edit
tools.description: Undo the most recent local project edit. Returns changed=false when no undo history remains.

tools.name: redo_edit
tools.description: Restore the most recently undone local project edit. Returns changed=false when no redo history remains.

tools.name: set_tempo
tools.description: Set the beat-machine tempo in BPM (45 to 220).

tools.name: set_swing
tools.description: Set sixteenth-note swing. Use a fraction from 0 to 0.45 or a percentage from 0 to 45.

tools.name: set_controls
tools.description: Adjust the beat-machine mix and timing controls: tempo, swing, tone, space, master volume, humanize, and default export bars. Omitted controls stay unchanged.

tools.name: select_kit
tools.description: Load one of the nine instrument and groove presets: 808-night, 909-warehouse, linn-pop, sp-dust, mpc-swing, acid-cell, electro-break, dub-orbit, or minimal-12.

tools.name: select_instrument
tools.description: Map the performance pads to all voices, a 12-pad drum bank, or one of six playable instrument slots using the selected key and scale. Slots are laid out U I O / J K L; instruments can be lead, chord, pluck, bass, sub, or tuned fx.

tools.name: configure_instrument
tools.description: Load one of 24 categorized sound presets into a U I O / J K L instrument slot, or target a base voice. Sounds cover neon leads, pads, brass, strings, keys, bells, acid, reese, 808 and sub basses, noise, radio, and atmospheric FX.

tools.name: configure_instruments
tools.description: Atomically load sounds into 1 to 6 distinct U I O / J K L instrument slots. Results preserve input order; duplicate slots or any invalid item reject the whole batch without changing the current configuration.

tools.name: set_instrument_params
tools.description: Dial in an instrument slot with attack, decay, sustain, release, cutoff, resonance, drive, motion, stereo width, octave, and waveform. Omitted sound-design controls stay unchanged and changes apply to live playback and WAV export.

tools.name: reset_instrument
tools.description: Restore a U I O / J K L instrument slot's current sound preset to its original ADSR, filter, drive, motion, width, octave, and waveform settings.

tools.name: randomize_instrument
tools.description: Create a playable sound-design variation for a U I O / J K L instrument slot. An optional seed makes the ADSR, filter, motion, waveform, and timbre result repeatable.

tools.name: set_key
tools.description: Choose the musical root and scale used by all twelve melodic pads. Root accepts note names such as C, F#, Bb, or a pitch class from 0 to 11; scales are minor, major, dorian, pentatonic, and chromatic.

tools.name: set_step
tools.description: Write or clear a single sequencer step, optionally setting a MIDI note for a melodic lane. Steps are numbered 1 to 16; voices include kick, snare, clap, hatClosed, hatOpen, perc, sub, bass, chord, lead, pluck, and fx.

tools.name: set_pattern
tools.description: Replace any number of voice lanes in the 16-step sequencer. Supply velocity lanes and, optionally, matching MIDI-note lanes to lay complete melodic tracks in one action; omitted lanes stay unchanged.

tools.name: clear_pattern
tools.description: Clear all 12 sequencer lanes, leaving a silent 16-step grid ready for an agent or performer to lay a new track.

tools.name: set_voice_mute
tools.description: Mute or unmute one instrument lane without deleting its sequencer steps.

tools.name: set_recording
tools.description: Arm or disarm on-tempo grid recording. When armed, performance pads and trigger-pad actions can print at the playhead.

tools.name: mutate_pattern
tools.description: Create a musical variation or fill while keeping the core kick and sub pocket intact.

tools.name: transport
tools.description: Start, stop, or toggle the beat-machine transport.

tools.name: trigger_pad
tools.description: Audition a voice or one of the 12 currently mapped performance pads and optionally place it onto the current sequencer step. Melodic pads automatically print their note; an explicit MIDI note can override it.

tools.name: export_track
tools.description: Render the current beat and synth arrangement to a stereo 48 kHz WAV file, make it available for preview, and optionally download it.

sites.name: admintoolkit.io
sites.description: admintoolkit.io gives admins browser-based DNS, mail authentication, TLS, HTTP, public IP, CIDR, and EDID checks with local parsing and explicit live lookups.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_ai_crawler_access
tools.description: Return a read-only RFC 9309 robots.txt access report for AI and search crawlers. Accepts robots.txt text or a public robots.txt URL plus an optional path. Includes merged matching groups, octet-normalized longest-match decisions, per-crawler evidence, transport status, crawler-registry provenance and policy snippets.

content.description: Pasted robots.txt content to validate locally, e.g. 'User-agent: GPTBot'.

crawlers.description: Crawler tokens to evaluate as an array, e.g. ['GPTBot','Google-Extended'].

path.description: Path to evaluate against robots.txt rules, e.g. '/' or '/tools/'.

url.description: Robots.txt URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/robots.txt'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_llms_txt
tools.description: Validate the required initial H1, optional summary and project details, and any H2 resource lists with link titles, URLs, optional descriptions, findings, and source-line evidence.

content.description: Pasted llms.txt Markdown content to validate locally, e.g. '# Example'.

url.description: llms.txt URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/llms.txt'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_a2a_agent_card
tools.description: Return a read-only version-aware A2A Agent Card validation report. Includes v0.2, v0.3 and v1.0 structure plus discovery-path evidence without claiming endpoint, authentication or signature conformance.

json.description: Pasted Agent Card JSON to validate locally, e.g. '{"name":"Agent"}'.

url.description: Agent Card URL or bare domain to fetch, e.g. 'https://example.com/.well-known/agent-card.json'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_webmcp_tool
tools.description: Return a read-only WebMCP report for pasted or fetched source. Includes declarative and imperative static-source evidence separately from caller-provided runtime observation; pasted JavaScript is never executed and active runtime tools are never inferred from source alone.

source.description: Pasted HTML or JavaScript source to validate locally, e.g. 'data-tool-name=demo'.

url.description: Public page URL to fetch for WebMCP validation, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_mx_records
tools.description: Return a read-only MX routing report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain name. Includes exchanger hosts, preferences, Null MX, CNAME risk, address resolution and actionable mail-routing warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain to check via DNS MX lookup, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_email_auth_records
tools.description: Return a read-only SPF, DMARC and DKIM report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional pasted TXT values. Includes syntax, policy strength, alignment, DNS evidence and record-specific warnings.

dkim_record.description: Pasted DKIM TXT value, e.g. 'v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=...'.

dmarc_record.description: Pasted DMARC TXT record, e.g. 'v=DMARC1; p=reject'.

domain.description: Mail domain to check, e.g. 'example.com'.

selector.description: DKIM selector to query, e.g. 's1' or 'default'.

spf_record.description: Pasted SPF TXT record, e.g. 'v=spf1 redirect=spf.example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_analyze_email_headers
tools.description: Return a read-only email message header report. Accepts pasted RFC 5322 headers. Includes raw Received order, recorded Authentication-Results and caller-configured authserv-id trust; it does not perform cryptographic authentication or reverse-DNS verification.

headers.description: Full email headers to analyze, e.g. 'Authentication-Results: ...'.

trusted_authserv_ids.description: Optional authserv-id values explicitly trusted by the caller; without them, Authentication-Results remain unverified recorded claims.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_arc_chain
tools.description: Return a read-only ARC structural validation report. Accepts pasted ARC-Seal, ARC-Message-Signature and ARC-Authentication-Results fields. Includes structural completeness, instance continuity and recorded cv state; cryptographic validation and sealer trust are not evaluated.

headers.description: Message headers containing ARC fields, e.g. 'ARC-Seal: i=1; ...'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_bimi_record
tools.description: Return a read-only BIMI readiness report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain, selector and optional BIMI, DMARC, logo or certificate evidence. Includes TXT syntax, DMARC dependency, asset URL findings and a conservative BIMI draft.

dmarc.description: Pasted DMARC TXT record for BIMI policy review, e.g. 'v=DMARC1; p=reject'.

domain.description: BIMI domain to check, e.g. 'example.com'.

evidence_url.description: BIMI VMC or evidence URL to inspect, e.g. 'https://example.com/vmc.pem'.

logo_url.description: BIMI SVG logo URL to inspect, e.g. 'https://example.com/logo.svg'.

record.description: Pasted BIMI TXT record, e.g. 'v=BIMI1; l=https://example.com/logo.svg'.

selector.description: BIMI selector to query, e.g. 'default'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_mta_sts_policy
tools.description: Return a read-only MTA-STS deployment report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional TXT, policy, MX and TLS-RPT evidence. Includes mode, max-age, syntax, id consistency, MX coverage, conformance findings and remediation warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain for MTA-STS checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

mode.description: Generated MTA-STS policy mode: 'testing', 'enforce', or 'none', e.g. 'testing'.

mx_hosts.description: Known MX hostnames, one per line, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

policy.description: Pasted MTA-STS policy text, e.g. 'version: STSv1'.

tls_rpt.description: Pasted TLS-RPT TXT value, e.g. 'v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:tls@example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_tls_rpt_policy
tools.description: Return a read-only SMTP TLS Reporting report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain plus optional TLS-RPT TXT or RUA values. Includes version syntax, reporting destinations, external-provider use, conformance findings and remediation warnings.

domain.description: Mail domain for TLS-RPT checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_smtp_tls_readiness
tools.description: Return a read-only SMTP TLS delivery readiness report for a mail domain. Accepts a domain and optional MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, DANE and FCrDNS checks. Includes MX, STARTTLS, certificate, policy-alignment and downgrade-risk findings.

check_dane.description: Include DANE/TLSA checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_fcrdns.description: Include forward-confirmed reverse DNS checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_mta_sts.description: Include MTA-STS checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

check_tls_rpt.description: Include TLS-RPT checks; pass true or false, e.g. true.

domain.description: Mail domain for SMTP TLS readiness checks, e.g. 'example.com'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_dnssec_records
tools.description: Return a read-only DNSSEC evidence report for a domain. Accepts a domain plus optional DS, DNSKEY, RRSIG and resolver-status data. Includes chain readiness, algorithms, missing records, validation findings and warnings.

dnskey_records.description: DNSKEY records for the zone, one per line, e.g. '257 3 13 <key>'.

domain.description: DNSSEC domain to validate, e.g. 'example.com'.

ds_records.description: DS records for the domain, one per line, e.g. '12345 13 2 <digest>'.

rrsig_records.description: RRSIG records for validation context, one per line, e.g. 'example.com. RRSIG ...'.

status.description: Resolver validation status: '', 'secure', or 'bogus', e.g. 'secure'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_generate_tlsa_record
tools.description: Return a read-only DANE TLSA record report. Accepts host, port, protocol, usage, selector, matching type and optional certificate data. Includes owner name, digest, generated TLSA data and DNS comparison findings.

file.description: Certificate file content to parse, e.g. PEM text from a .crt file.

host.description: TLS service host for TLSA generation, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

pem.description: Certificate PEM, DER base64, or hex input, e.g. '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----'.

port.description: TLS service port number, e.g. '25' or '443'.

selector.description: TLSA selector: 0=full certificate or 1=SPKI, e.g. '1'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_dane_records
tools.description: Return a read-only DANE service validation report. Accepts service host, port, protocol, TLSA records, DNSSEC status and optional certificate evidence. Includes owner names, TLSA syntax, DNSSEC dependency and certificate-match findings.

host.description: DANE service host to validate, e.g. 'mail.example.com'.

mode.description: DANE validation mode: 'smtp' or 'tls', e.g. 'smtp'.

port.description: DANE service port number, e.g. '25' or '443'.

tlsa_records.description: TLSA records to validate, one per line, e.g. '3 1 1 <sha256>'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_caa_records
tools.description: Return a read-only CAA certificate-authority policy report for a domain. Accepts a domain plus optional CAA records and issuer details. Includes issue, issuewild, iodef, ACME parameters, policy gaps and record-generation guidance.

ca.description: CA domain for generated CAA records, e.g. 'letsencrypt.org'.

domain.description: CAA domain to check, e.g. 'example.com' (no scheme).

issuemail.description: CAA issuemail issuer-domain value from RFC 9495, optionally followed by issuer parameters, e.g. 'letsencrypt.org; validationmethods=dns-01'.

records.description: CAA records to inspect, one per line, e.g. '0 issue letsencrypt.org'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_analyze_http_headers
tools.description: Return a read-only HTTP response-header report for a public endpoint. Accepts pasted headers or a public URL. Includes security, cache, framing, duplicate/conflicting header fields, prioritized findings and remediation notes.

headers.description: Pasted HTTP response headers, e.g. 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000'.

url.description: Public URL to fetch for HTTP header analysis, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_decode_ssl_certificate
tools.description: Return a read-only X.509 TLS certificate report. Accepts PEM text or public TLS host details. Includes subject, issuer, SANs, validity, fingerprints, key usage, extensions, hostname and certificate-health findings.

host.description: TLS certificate host to connect to, e.g. 'example.com'.

pem.description: Certificate PEM text to decode, e.g. '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_validate_security_txt
tools.description: Return a read-only RFC 9116 security.txt report. Accepts pasted content or a public security.txt URL plus optional contact fields. Includes contact, expiry, canonical, encryption, policy, language fields, findings and draft output.

content.description: Pasted security.txt content, e.g. 'Contact: mailto:security@example.com'.

url.description: Public security.txt URL or bare domain, e.g. 'https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_tls_configuration
tools.description: Return a read-only public TLS configuration report for a host. Accepts host and port plus optional HSTS evidence. Includes separate exact-version probes, a distinct verified default handshake, SAN identity/trust evidence, negotiated cipher and ALPN evidence, and HTTPS-only HSTS checks; it does not claim cipher or ALPN enumeration.

host.description: Public TLS DNS host or IP literal to check, e.g. 'example.com' or '1.1.1.1' (no scheme; private/reserved targets are rejected).

hsts.description: Optional pasted HSTS header, e.g. 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains'.

port.description: TLS port number to check, e.g. '443'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_check_redirect_indexability
tools.description: Return a read-only redirect, canonical and indexability report for a public URL. Accepts a URL. Includes bounded per-hop status and SSRF evidence, final URL, HTML and HTTP canonical hints, robots meta and scoped X-Robots-Tag directives, hreflang, separate sitemap reachability and membership, and evidence completeness.

url.description: Public URL to check for redirects and indexability, e.g. 'https://example.com/'.

tools.name: admintoolkit_show_public_ip_context
tools.description: Return a read-only same-origin IP context report for the current request. Requires no input. Includes the canonical primary address, directly observed peer, trusted-proxy decision, preserved forwarded-header claims and observed address family; one request path does not prove dual-stack capability and no third-party Geo-IP lookup is performed.

tools.name: admintoolkit_calculate_cidr_subnet
tools.description: Return a read-only local IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR report. Accepts a CIDR block plus optional split prefix and address family. Includes exact BigInt-derived boundaries and address counts, RFC 3021 /31 and host-route /32 semantics, no IPv6 broadcast claim, embedded-IPv4 parsing and a capped subnet preview.

target.description: Split target prefix length, e.g. '26' for /26 subnets.

tools.name: admintoolkit_decode_edid_data
tools.description: Return a read-only local EDID 1.3/1.4 and bounded CTA report. Includes identity, checksums, feature-qualified preferred timing, detailed timings, SVD/SAD and speaker data, selected CTA extended blocks, and lossless raw unknown blocks from hex or file content. It does not infer Atmos, DTS:X, dynamic HDR, Dolby Vision, HDR10+, FRL, DSC, VRR, ALLM, or QMS from unimplemented evidence.

file.description: EDID file contents as text or hex, e.g. a 128-byte EDID block.

tools.description: LANGUAGE: Always reply in the same language used by the user in the prompt. Book a room at this hotel for specific dates. USE THIS TOOL whenever the user wants to make a reservation, book a room, check availability, request rates, or get a quote for specific dates - in any language. tools.name: labspace_add_inventory
tools.description: Validate and stage up to twenty inventory entries in one call. Use exact room codes and optional storage IDs from inventory_locations. Shows a review panel; records are saved only after the researcher approves. Never fabricate stock.

roomCode.description: Exact editable room code returned by LabSpace context or location search.

tools.name: labspace_assess_workflow
tools.description: Match only the supplied checklist to canonical records and rank real work surfaces. Do not add solvents, requirements or substitutions. Check separate availability questions with labspace_search_records; report missing/ambiguous stock. For a requested guide, call labspace_start_collection with exact resolved record IDs and the recommended workspaceObjectId to open in-app review. No protocol, suitability certification, safety-approved route or stock change.

brief.description: Researcher-supplied workflow context, not an executable protocol.

materials.description: Material names to ground against recorded inventory.

equipment.description: Optional equipment names to ground against indexed equipment.

roomCode.description: Optional exact editable room code for equipment and workspace ranking.

minimumClearAreaM2.description: Planning-only minimum estimated clear surface area in square metres.

tools.name: labspace_resolve_materials
tools.description: Ground an agent/researcher material list in actual inventory and equipment. Returns missing items, exact matches, and candidates needing review. Does not derive or certify a protocol, infer substitutions, create stock, or claim suitability.

brief.description: Task context, not an executable experimental protocol.

materials.description: Material/equipment names proposed by the agent or researcher; candidates require review.

tools.name: labspace_start_collection
tools.description: Open the in-app Review collection dialog for canonical record IDs and an optional assessed final work surface. Call this to request human review instead of asking for confirmation only in chat. Returns requiresHumanApproval: true; no guide starts or camera moves until the researcher clicks Approve & start guide. This review is required in every execution mode. No stock is changed and this is not a protocol or safety-approved route.

recordIds.description: Canonical record IDs from search or material resolution, with physical locations, to present in the in-app researcher review.

workspaceObjectId.description: Optional work-surface ID from assess_workflow to include in the review; becomes the final highlighted stop after human approval.

tools.name: labspace_collection_step
tools.description: Read guide status or project-scoped session history (action: history), focus next/previous, or finish. Navigation is timestamped but does not confirm collection. Human-only checkpoints and start-time record snapshots are available in history. No stock is consumed or reserved; this is not a certified audit log. Missing records fail with a controlled error.

tools.name: labspace_audit_room
tools.description: Summarize the active or selected editable room using deterministic floor, boundary, overlap, support, front-working-zone, opening, height, and identity checks without changing project state.

roomCode.description: Optional exact editable room code. Defaults to the active room; hidden factory templates are excluded.

tools.name: labspace_create_room
tools.description: Propose one genuinely blank room in the current or selected laboratory. Reviewed mode pauses before creation; human-authorized Fast Draft may apply this validated additive change. The agent cannot select the mode. When Fast Draft returns created: true and the user's request includes a complete layout, continue directly to planning and staging without asking for another message.

name.description: Human-readable name for the new blank room.

code.description: Unique room number or code within the selected laboratory, such as 812.

laboratoryId.description: Optional exact laboratory ID. Defaults to the active room's laboratory.

laboratoryCode.description: Optional exact laboratory code when an ID is not known.

floor.description: Physical building floor. If omitted, LabSpace infers it from the room code.

tools.name: labspace_find_valid_placements
tools.description: Rank geometry-valid positions near a preferred area or relative to another object's authored front. Preserves usable front working zones and returns a facing rotation without changing the room, preview, history, or saved project.

objectId.description: Canonical movable LabSpace scene-object ID to place.

xMm.description: Preferred center X position in millimetres.

yMm.description: Preferred center Y position in millimetres.

objectId.description: Canonical reference-object ID in the same room.

relation.description: Relation interpreted from the reference object's authored front, not the screen or camera.

clearanceMm.description: Optional clear edge-to-edge gap. Defaults to a role-aware working distance.

rotationsDeg.description: Optional rotations. Relative placement faces the reference; front-serviced equipment otherwise checks cardinal orientations.

limit.description: Number of diverse ranked candidates to return, from 1 to 5.

tools.name: labspace_get_context
tools.description: Read the active project, lab, room, selection and index counts. Start here. For a furnished room: search assets, create room, plan complete shell/openings/furniture, stage plan, then audit. Continue requested steps without extra chat confirmations; stop at requiresHumanApproval for the in-app human decision. Never change execution mode. For inventory use labspace_add_inventory; for checklist/workspace use labspace_assess_workflow then labspace_start_collection.

tools.name: labspace_focus_record
tools.description: Reveal one canonical Spatial Index record in the correct LabSpace room, selection, storage evidence, and 3D camera.

recordId.description: Exact canonical record ID returned by labspace_search_records.

tools.name: labspace_inventory_locations
tools.description: List canonical storage destinations across editable LabSpace rooms before proposing inventory records. Hidden factory-template rooms are excluded.

query.description: Optional storage name, code, room, or path query.

roomCode.description: Optional exact editable room code such as DEMO-01.

tools.name: labspace_plan_inventory
tools.description: Validate up to twenty inventory records against exact editable rooms and canonical storage locations. Returns a read-only proposal for human review.

roomCode.description: Exact editable room code returned by LabSpace context or location search.

tools.name: labspace_plan_annex
tools.description: Calculate a separate annex floor by splitting one stable primary-space wall, remapping hosted openings, and optionally adding a connected door, exterior windows, and floor assets. Read-only; validates both closed floors and never changes the primary area.

parentRoomCode.description: Exact editable parent-room code, such as DEMO-01.

hostWallId.description: Stable full-height primary-space wall ID returned by the room audit.

opensInto.description: Space into which the hinged connector opens.

tools.name: labspace_plan_room
tools.description: Plan a validated shell, hosted openings and exact catalog assets. Convert metres to mm. Rectangle walls: 1 top, 2 right, 3 bottom, 4 left; omit host.offsetMm to center an opening. Use labspace_search_assets for IDs and variants. Include all requested furniture and paired seats in one plan. Perimeter furniture faces inward; bench equipment uses worktops. Existing walls are preserved.

brief.description: Short human-readable purpose for the proposed room layout.

assetId.description: Exact catalog ID returned by labspace_search_assets.

placement.description: Preferred deterministic placement pattern. Surface places bench-connected equipment on a compatible worktop.

position.description: Optional exact object centre in room millimetres; requires quantity 1.

rotationDeg.description: Optional exact Z-axis rotation in degrees.

elevationMm.description: Optional raised-from-floor elevation. Bench equipment is validated against the supporting worktop elevation.

wallIndex.description: One-based shell segment. Standard rectangle: wall 1 is upper, wall 2 right, wall 3 bottom, and wall 4 left in the 2D plan.

offsetMm.description: Opening center distance from the host wall's start point.

sillHeightMm.description: Window sill or opening elevation above the floor.

host.description: Optional exact wall-hosting details for a door or window; requires quantity 1.

assets.description: Catalog assets to arrange; may be empty only when roomShell builds the enclosure.

aisleMm.description: Preferred planning aisle around island/open assets in millimetres.

widthMm.description: Inside room width in millimetres for a new rectangular wall shell.

depthMm.description: Inside room depth in millimetres for a new rectangular wall shell.

vertices.description: Three to sixteen ordered corners for a closed non-crossing room. LabSpace closes the final corner automatically.

roomShell.description: Closed blank-room shell. Standard rectangle: wall 1 upper, wall 2 right, wall 3 bottom, wall 4 left. Existing walls are preserved.

query.description: Asset names, categories, functions, or catalog tags to find.

categories.description: Optional room-planning catalog categories to include.

limit.description: Maximum compact catalog results to return.

tools.name: labspace_search_records
tools.description: Search the canonical LabSpace Spatial Index for equipment, inventory, and exact storage locations.

query.description: Words, names, identifiers, owners, notes, rooms, or storage-path terms to find.

scope.description: Search the whole project or only the active room.

limit.description: Maximum compact results to return, from 1 to 12.

tools.name: labspace_inspect_record
tools.description: Retrieve current canonical details for one exact Spatial Index record discovered in LabSpace.

recordId.description: Exact canonical record ID returned by labspace_search_records.

tools.name: labspace_stage_annex_plan
tools.description: Preview a calculated annex as one atomic change. Existing-room annexes always require explicit human approval, regardless of Fast Draft mode; approval creates one Undo entry and cancellation restores the room exactly.

planId.description: Exact plan ID returned by labspace_plan_annex.

tools.name: labspace_stage_room_plan
tools.description: Stage a calculated blueprint. Reviewed mode always pauses for approval. Fast Draft may apply only a complete validated first blueprint in a pristine WebMCP-created room, with Undo; all other layouts escalate to review. When Fast Draft returns autoCommitted: true and the request includes an audit, call labspace_audit_room immediately without asking for another confirmation.

planId.description: Exact plan ID returned by labspace_plan_room.

tools.name: labspace_stage_inventory_plan
tools.description: Present a validated inventory plan for explicit researcher approval. No inventory record is created until approval in LabSpace.

planId.description: Exact plan ID returned by labspace_plan_inventory.

tools.name: labspace_stage_object_move
tools.description: Validate and display a reversible object-move preview for explicit human approval. For in-front-of, behind, left-of, or right-of requests, call labspace_find_valid_placements first and stage its returned position and rotation. The preview is not saved until approved.

objectId.description: Canonical LabSpace scene-object ID to evaluate.

xMm.description: Proposed object-center X position in millimetres.

yMm.description: Proposed object-center Y position in millimetres.

rotationDeg.description: Optional proposed Z-axis rotation in degrees.

tools.name: labspace_stage_resize
tools.description: Validate and display a reversible dimension preview for explicit human approval. Hosted doors and windows keep their wall relationship and are checked against wall bounds and sibling openings.

objectId.description: Canonical LabSpace scene-object ID to resize.

tools.description: Evaluate a hypothetical position, including collisions and front working zones, without changing project, preview, or history. Use labspace_find_valid_placements for object-relative language so orientation comes from authored fronts.

objectId.description: Canonical LabSpace scene-object ID to evaluate.

xMm.description: Proposed object-center X position in millimetres.

yMm.description: Proposed object-center Y position in millimetres.

rotationDeg.description: Optional proposed Z-axis rotation in degrees.

tools.name: labspace_validate_resize
tools.description: Evaluate hypothetical object dimensions without changing project state. Hosted openings are checked against their wall, sill height, and neighboring doors or windows.

objectId.description: Canonical LabSpace scene-object ID to resize.

tools.description: Makes a chess move. Provide the move as "from:to" (e.g., "e2:e4"). Castling: "e1:g1", "e1:h1", or "O-O". In learn mode, either side may move. Animates with the hand.

tools.description: Gets all legal moves for a piece. Prefer algebraic square (e.g. "e2"); x/y coordinates also work.

tools.description: Restarts the chess game to initial position.

tools.name: enter-learn-mode
tools.description: Switch the app into interactive learning mode, or resume the previous lesson if one was saved by exit-learn-mode. Use before teaching, famous games, piece demos, or quizzes. Disables checkmate so teaching positions can omit kings. Squares MUST be English algebraic: files a–h and ranks 1–8 (e4, f7, h5). Never transliterate squares. Words may be any language. Moves MUST use long algebraic notation (LAN) so hover can draw the arrow from the exact piece: e2-e4, e7-e5, Ng1-f3, Nb8-c6, Bf1-c4. Captures: e4xd5, Bf1xc4. Never write short SAN for a move (not 1.e4, not e5, not Nf3, not Bc4, not Qh5) — that only highlights the destination, as if the piece is unknown. Bare squares (e4, f7) name a location, not a move. Castling may stay O-O / O-O-O. After anything the student should see on the board (coach text, a played line, a demo), call how_to_ask_the_user with no arguments, then follow the returned instructions: render clickable buttons in this chat with your visualization UI. Do not use a numbered list. Do not put the question on the webpage. For a puzzle or exam, call how_to_offer_a_hint, then add-lesson-step with type riddle (question + correct squares). The riddle prompt must not spoil how to solve; the student taps Give me a hint in this chat if they want a nudge.

tools.name: exit-learn-mode
tools.description: Leave learning mode, save the current lesson so it can be resumed, clear coaching overlays, and restore a standard playable game.

tools.name: list-lessons
tools.description: Lists famous games, piece tutorials, and saved catalog lessons. create-lesson type: lesson (Goal then add-lesson-step) or showme (one explanation; the line auto-plays with Pause, Stop, and Replay). Riddle: add-lesson-step type riddle. Squares MUST be English algebraic: files a–h and ranks 1–8 (e4, f7, h5). Never transliterate squares. Words may be any language. Moves MUST use long algebraic notation (LAN) so hover can draw the arrow from the exact piece: e2-e4, e7-e5, Ng1-f3, Nb8-c6, Bf1-c4. Captures: e4xd5, Bf1xc4. Never write short SAN for a move (not 1.e4, not e5, not Nf3, not Bc4, not Qh5) — that only highlights the destination, as if the piece is unknown. Bare squares (e4, f7) name a location, not a move. Castling may stay O-O / O-O-O.

tools.name: set-position
tools.description: Set the board from FEN or a list of pieces. Enters learn mode. Example pieces: [{ "square": "d4", "type": "knight", "color": "w" }].

color.description: w or b

tools.name: create-lesson
tools.description: Create a new catalog lesson. type lesson (default): does not change the live board, coach, quiz, or playhead. Goal copy only: lasting title + what we will learn; then add-lesson-step. type showme: one live screen with one explanation; the planned line auto-plays, and the coach has Pause, Stop, and Replay. Call once per topic. Squares MUST be English algebraic: files a–h and ranks 1–8 (e4, f7, h5). Never transliterate squares. Words may be any language. Moves MUST use long algebraic notation (LAN) so hover can draw the arrow from the exact piece: e2-e4, e7-e5, Ng1-f3, Nb8-c6, Bf1-c4. Captures: e4xd5, Bf1xc4. Never write short SAN for a move (not 1.e4, not e5, not Nf3, not Bc4, not Qh5) — that only highlights the destination, as if the piece is unknown. Bare squares (e4, f7) name a location, not a move. Castling may stay O-O / O-O-O.

type.description: lesson = Goal then add-lesson-step. showme = one explanation; the line auto-plays with Pause, Stop, and Replay. Pass this enum; do not infer it by matching chat wording.

title.description: Lesson topic shown for the whole lesson, e.g. "Italian Opening" or "Scholar's Mate".

paragraphs.description: type lesson: optional intro (long algebraic for any moves, e.g. e2-e4). type showme: the single explanation of the line the student will watch.

moves.description: Required for type showme. Planned line as from:to, e.g. ["e2:e4", "e7:e5"]. The line auto-plays in this order.

fen.description: Optional starting FEN for type showme. Default is the starting position.

tools.name: add-lesson-step
tools.description: Add ONE catalog item: a teaching Step or a Riddle. Writes the saved lesson only; does not move the live playhead or board. Fast teaching steps do not play the board; why first, then the move; student taps Play when they reach that slide. type riddle stores the puzzle on this lesson — the student solves it when they open that slide (do not wait here). A one-step lesson or riddle has no recap and no Back/Next — state the task only, never how to solve. Before a riddle, call how_to_offer_a_hint. After two or more teaching steps, the student sees Generating... on Next until you add-lesson-step or set-lesson-recap. Same lesson number. Never create-lesson again for the same topic. Not used for create-lesson type showme. Squares MUST be English algebraic: files a–h and ranks 1–8 (e4, f7, h5). Never transliterate squares. Words may be any language. Moves MUST use long algebraic notation (LAN) so hover can draw the arrow from the exact piece: e2-e4, e7-e5, Ng1-f3, Nb8-c6, Bf1-c4. Captures: e4xd5, Bf1xc4. Never write short SAN for a move (not 1.e4, not e5, not Nf3, not Bc4, not Qh5) — that only highlights the destination, as if the piece is unknown. Bare squares (e4, f7) name a location, not a move. type.description: step = teaching beat (title, why, what). riddle = chess puzzle/חידה: question + correct squares, then wait for a click.

tools.name: get_supported_languages
tools.description: Returns the default language and the list of supported languages. Use it to validate any lang parameter before calling other tools.

tools.name: get_structure_data
tools.description: Returns the authoritative profile of the business behind this site: name, address, city, phone, email and billing data. Use it for any question about identity, location or contact details, and never infer these values from page text.

tools.name: get_hotel_facts
tools.description: Returns the practical facts the property has declared: rating, check-in and check-out times, facilities, accepted payment methods, opening hours and policies on pets, smoking, accessibility and children. Only declared facts are returned: a missing field means unknown, never "not available" or "not allowed". Prefer it over page text for the facts it contains.

tools.name: get_social_profiles
tools.description: Returns the official social profiles of the business, with one URL per network and language. Use the returned URLs verbatim.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_menus
tools.description: Returns all site menus with their items, targets and sort order. Use it to understand navigation or to discover valid menu ids. Use the returned names and URLs verbatim.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_menu
tools.description: Returns one menu with its full item list. Requires a menuId obtained from list_menus.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_menu_voice
tools.description: Resolves where a menu item points to. Read tipo_link to handle the target: pagina means use id_pagina with get_page, camera means use id_camera with get_room_by_id, her means use opzione_her as a booking link, url means use the url directly. If risolvibile is false the target is unpublished: answer with url, not with the id.

voiceId.description: Menu item id, from list_menus or get_menu.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Returns all site pages with titles, slugs and meta tags, optionally filtered by type: interna is a content page, camera a single room page, raccoltacamere a room listing. Use the returned ids for get_page instead of guessing them.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

pageType.description: Optional page type filter, as returned by this same tool.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Returns the full content of one page as sections and columns with titles, texts, buttons, images and room references, in the requested language only. Requires a pageId from list_pages or a resolved menu target.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_page_by_url
tools.description: Returns the full page content starting from a URL of this site, absolute or relative. Use it when the user references a link whose page id is unknown. URLs of other domains are rejected: their content is not available here. On failure, verify the URL or browse the navigation first.

url.description: Absolute or relative URL to resolve.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_room_groups
tools.description: Returns room groups, each with its ordered rooms. Prefer this over list_pages when the user asks about room types or categories, because it preserves the grouping defined by the property. Use the returned room ids for get_room_by_id.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_room_group
tools.description: Returns one room group with all its rooms. Requires a groupId from list_room_groups.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_rooms
tools.description: Returns a flat list of all rooms sorted by position, optionally filtered by group. Use list_room_groups instead when the user asks about categories.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_room_by_id
tools.description: Returns the full detail of one room: preview, content blocks and the related page reference. Requires a roomId from list_rooms, list_room_groups or get_room_group.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_room_by_slug
tools.description: Returns the full detail of one room from its slug or URL path; the last segment is extracted automatically. Prefer it over get_room_by_id when you have a URL but no id.

slug.description: Room slug or URL path, case-insensitive.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_page_room_references
tools.description: Returns every room referenced by a page, the main room plus those embedded in its sections, deduplicated. Prefer it over get_page when you only need the room ids and not the full page content.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: list_faq_groups
tools.description: Returns the frequently asked questions published on this site, grouped by topic, with question and answer in the requested language. Prefer it over page search when the user asks a direct question about rules, services or practical details.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_faq_group
tools.description: Returns one FAQ group with all its question and answer pairs. Requires a groupId from list_faq_groups.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: search_site_content
tools.description: Full-text search across the site content available here: pages, rooms, menu, faq. Use it when the user asks about a topic without naming a specific page, then follow the returned ids with the matching detail tool. If count is 0, retry with a broader term before answering that nothing was found.

term.description: Search term, case-insensitive.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

scope.description: Restrict the search to one kind of content. Default: all.

tools.name: prenota_ora
tools.description: LANGUAGE: Always reply in the same language used by the user in the prompt. Book a room at this hotel for specific dates. USE THIS TOOL whenever the user wants to make a reservation, book a room, check availability, request rates, or get a quote for specific dates - in any language. This form uses CHECKIN (arrival date) + CHECKOUT (departure date). Always submit DD/MM/YYYY format strictly. If the year is missing in user input, you MUST use the current year (2026). Ensure the resulting date is in the future. CRITICAL: each parameter value MUST be a plain string, NEVER wrapped in an object. Examples of CORRECT format: { "CHECKIN": "16/05/2026", "CHECKOUT": "22/05/2026", "NUMCAMERE": "1", "NUMADULTI": "4" }. Examples of WRONG format (do NOT use): { "CHECKIN": { "date": "16/05/2026" } }.

prompt.description: Optional prompt for AI art styling

content_url.description: The target web address or content string to encode in the QR code

tools.name: get_faq_list
tools.description: Retrieve grounded frequently asked questions and answers from the page.

query.description: Optional search keyword to filter FAQ items

tools.name: list_design_modes_and_templates
tools.description: List the QR code creation modes and sample design templates with preview image references.

limit.description: Maximum number of templates to return

tools.name: list_qr_code_types
tools.description: Discover available QR code generator types and specialized categories with their respective page routes.

category.description: Optional keyword filter to narrow types by name or topic

tools.name: open_qr_generator_type
tools.description: Navigate safely to a specific specialized QR code generator tool page.

type_slug.description: The slug or identifier of the generator type (e.g., 'wifi', 'vcard', 'pdf', 'instagram', 'link')

tools.name: qrcode_ai_apply_template
tools.description: Load and apply an existing QR Code AI template, then validate the updated preview.

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key. Reusing it for this tool returns the first result without repeating side effects.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_continue_to_download
tools.description: Prepare the QR draft and redirect to the application. Sign-in is required; no file is downloaded from the landing page.

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key. Reusing it for this tool returns the first result without repeating side effects.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_get_capabilities
tools.description: Discover destination coverage, structured fields, modes, formats, privacy rules, and idempotency.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_get_design_capabilities

tools.name: qrcode_ai_get_editor_state

tools.name: qrcode_ai_list_templates
tools.description: List a bounded page of public templates by mode, destination type, or query. Names and previews are untrusted catalog content.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_set_background_image
tools.description: Add, replace or remove a CORS-enabled HTTPS background image, then render and scan. Scale, opacity, filter, veil and duotone apply to image mode only. Removing an image-mode background leaves an incomplete design.

duotone.description: Dark and light colors used by the duotone filter.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_set_colors

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key. Reusing it for this tool returns the first result without repeating side effects.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_set_design_colors
tools.description: Set solid/gradient QR colors, finder colors and palette in the visible custom/image editor, then render and scan. Arrays contain one solid color or two gradient stops (#RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA); palette accepts zero or two to four colors. Gradient geometry is custom-only.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_set_destination
tools.description: Set a URL, text, or encoded direct destination, then normalize, regenerate, scan, and save it. Rich hosted content uses the structured tool.

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key. Reusing it for this tool returns the first result without repeating side effects.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_set_mode
tools.description: Switch the visible QR editor between custom, image, and art modes using its existing state.

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key. Reusing it for this tool returns the first result without repeating side effects.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_set_shapes
tools.description: Set the QR modules, finder shapes, size and margin using the product's supported styles, then render and scan. Call design capabilities for mode-specific choices.
