tools.description: Build and validate a contact, message, network, payment, event, location, hosted-content, media, or form destination with native serializers.

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key. Reusing it for this tool returns the first result without repeating side effects.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_set_text
tools.description: Add, edit, style, position or remove text drawn on the QR code, then render and scan. This does not change the encoded destination. Layer is image-only; content is never echoed in results.

content.description: Text drawn on the QR, not its encoded destination. Empty string removes it.

tools.name: qrcode_ai_validate_qr
tools.description: Regenerate the exact visible QR state and validate it with QR Code AI's production scanner.

sites.name: sheetcanvas.com
sites.description: Connect Claude, Codex, or another MCP-capable agent to SheetCanvas so messy business data becomes durable tables, charts, pivots, notes, and dashboards.

tools.name: listSheets
tools.description: Use this first to discover what is on the canvas: lists all sheets with id, title, dimensions, compact columnIdSpan (for example A:BB), row-numbering convention, and column headers. Column ids like A, AU, or BB are spreadsheet column letters and may be used directly in tool inputs.

tools.name: getSelection
tools.description: Use this first for requests like "this data", "selected chart", "current sheet", or "what I selected", before deciding which sheet/chart to inspect or mutate. Returns what the user currently has selected: the active sheet cell/range selection plus selectedCanvas.items for whole selected sheets, charts, and notes.

tools.name: createSheet
tools.description: Creates a new standalone sheet for manual, scratch, or agent-computed data (an assembled table, fill-in template, or derived summary). data is optional: rows of raw cell strings, row 1 is the header; a cell may be a literal or "=FORMULA(...)". Omit data for a blank grid. Has NO data source and does not auto-refresh — for connector data (ClickHouse, Google Analytics, Google Sheets) use createQuerySheet instead to keep lineage/refreshability. Returns sheetId and dimensions.

data.description: Rows of raw cell strings; row 1 is the header. Each cell is a literal or "=FORMULA(...)". Omit for a blank sheet.

tools.name: createNote
tools.description: Creates a live report note: Markdown that can embed data-bound components staying live as sheets change. Embed up to three self-closing tags — , , ; any other tag renders as inert text. sheet/id values MUST be real ids from earlier results (createQuerySheet, createPivot, createChart) or listSheets/describeSheet — a wrong id shows "not found".

content.description: Markdown body; may embed <CellValue>, <CanvasChart>, <Sparkline> tags (see tool description for their exact attributes).

title.description: Optional short title, added as an H1 heading if the content does not already start with a heading.

color.description: Note background color. Defaults to yellow.

tools.name: listNotes
tools.description: Use this to discover note ids before reading or updating a note — it lists all report notes currently on the canvas. Returns each note's noteId, a derived title (first heading/line), a short text preview, color, and format. Returns an empty list if there are no notes.

tools.name: listConnections
tools.description: Use this first before querying external data — it lists all configured data connections (ClickHouse, Google Analytics, Google Sheets). Returns connectionId, type, name, duplicate-name hints, best-effort health, GA property hints, sheets using each connection, plus selectedCanvas context.

tools.name: listConnectionProperties
tools.description: Use this after choosing a GA connection and before describeConnection — it lists selectable properties/resources for one data connection. Google Analytics returns a bounded properties[] page with propertyId, displayName, accountDisplayName, nextPageToken, truncated.

tools.name: describeConnection
tools.description: Describes one data connection and returns the schemaToken needed by queryConnection/createQuerySheet/updateQuerySheet, plus a queryShape (payloadSchema, requiredFields, examples) for building queryPayload — read it before any connector query. ClickHouse without table returns tables[] only; with table returns columns[] and schemaToken. Google Analytics needs propertyId, returns a dimensions[]/metrics[] catalog. Google Sheets returns URL/ID and range requirements.

tools.name: describeSheet
tools.description: Use this to inspect one sheet before querying or mutating it. Returns the schema and a small sample: compact columnIdSpan (for example A:BB), column ids/letters, header cells, data ranges, column headers, inferred types, row count, row-numbering convention, current filters and sort, and up to 5 sample rows with row numbers. If the user named specific column letters such as AU or BB, pass them in columnIds so they are echoed in requestedColumns even on wide sheets.

tools.name: getRange
tools.description: Read the raw and computed values of a specific A1 range on a sheet.

tools.name: querySheet
tools.description: Runs a read-only SQL SELECT against one sheet for exploration, validation, filtering, or previewing aggregates before writing anything. Results are temporary, not chartable — to chart an aggregate, build a summary with createPivot first, then createChart on it. The sheet is table "t"; column names come from schema.sqlName (sanitized, e.g. hostname) — inspect schema first. For a trend, pull ~8+ periods; for a comparison, also pull the seasonality-correct baseline. Only SELECT is allowed.

tools.name: setCells
tools.description: Write cells on a sheet. Pass A1-keyed map of { raw } values. Use "=FORMULA(...)" for formulas. Will overwrite existing cells.

tools.name: applyFilter
tools.description: Replace filters on a sheet. Pass an empty array to clear filters.

tools.name: applySort
tools.description: Set or clear the sort on a sheet. Pass null to clear.

tools.name: applyFormat
tools.description: Applies presentation formatting (units, decimals, dates, in-cell visuals) to an A1 range without changing values; works on normal and derived sheets. Pass exactly one of format or preset, not both. preset is a shortcut (integer, decimal, compactNumber, currency, compactCurrency, percent, date, datetime, duration, text, customD3); customD3 needs d3Format. Use visual:"bar" for a primary metric; use heatmapColor:"diverging" for values around zero, heatmapFlip:true when lower is better.

tools.name: createChart
tools.description: Creates a chart from a source sheet; response includes formDecisions. mode:"group" aggregates row-level data via groupCol/valueCol/operation. mode:"metrics" charts aggregated columns: labelColumn is X-axis, dataColumns are Y series. Time-series charts need timeRange and timeGranularity. Duplicate X labels in metrics mode mean data is too granular — use mode:"group" or createPivot first. For "does X drive Y" use type:"scatter" (one point per entity), not dual-axis lines.

mode.description: Use group for chart-only aggregation over row-level data; metrics charts already-aggregated columns directly.

groupCol.description: For mode:"group", the X-axis grouping column. Usually the same as labelColumn for compatibility.

seriesGroupCol.description: For mode:"group", optional column that splits the aggregate into series.

valueCol.description: For mode:"group", the numeric value column to aggregate. Usually the first dataColumns entry for compatibility.

operation.description: For mode:"group", how to aggregate valueCol values in the chart.

seriesTypes.description: Per-series chart type override keyed by dataColumns letter, e.g. {"B":"bar","C":"line"}. Metrics mode only. Omit to auto-select.

rightAxisColumns.description: dataColumns letters plotted on a second Y-axis, e.g. a rate paired with volumes. Metrics mode only. Omit to auto-gate the dual axis.

timeRange.description: Required for time-series charts. Examples: "2026-05-01 to 2026-06-11", "last 30 days", or "full available range".

timeGranularity.description: Required for time-series charts when the label column is date-like.

aggregation.description: The analysis aggregation represented by this chart, such as SUM or COUNT. Use operation for chart-only group mode.

sourceGrain.description: Declare whether the source sheet already matches the chart grain, or raw_rows when mode:"group" will aggregate directly.

allowDuplicateLabels.description: Only set true when the user explicitly wants multiple plotted rows with the same label in metrics mode. Otherwise use group mode or create a

analysisNotes.description: Briefly state the chart grain/assumption when using an explicit default or override.

tools.name: createPivot
tools.description: Creates a pivot-table sheet derived from a source sheet; recomputes when the source changes. Use for chartable aggregation or a reusable summary from row-level data — build the pivot, then createChart on it (for one-off exploration with no persistent output, use querySheet instead). rowLabelCol groups rows; colLabelCol (optional) splits into columns for a 2-D pivot; values is one or more metric cards with operation, optional label, COUNT semantics, and AND-only SUMIF/COUNTIF conditions.

tools.name: createSparkline
tools.description: Creates a compact KPI table: one row per metric/group with a mini trend line over dateCol, a current value, and a Change cell colored by direction-of-good (green=better, red=worse). Good default for "overview" requests. mode:"metrics" charts each dataCols entry as a row (dataCols required). mode:"group" pivots groupCol into rows, aggregating valueCol with operation (all required). compareMode sets the delta column (default vs_avg). In-cell sparkline: use applyFormat visual:"sparkline".

summaryColumns.description: Optional extra columns appended after the Change column: "avg" (mean), "minmax" (min and max), "share" (share-of-total as an in-cell bar). The Change

goodDirections.description: Per-metric direction of good, keyed by label. "up"=higher better (revenue); "down"=lower better (cost, churn). Inferred if omitted.

tools.name: readNote
tools.description: Use this before updateNote so you edit against the real current text rather than guessing — it reads one report note by id. Returns its full raw Markdown source (content, exactly as stored — including any / / tags), plus color and format. Errors if the noteId does not exist (get ids from listNotes or a prior createNote).

noteId.description: Id of the note to read, as returned by createNote or listNotes.

tools.name: updateNote
tools.description: Updates an existing report note in place — revise wording, add/remove a section, or swap a chart. Requires noteId plus at least one of content or color. content REPLACES the entire Markdown body; there is no append/patch mode — read the note first with readNote, edit the full text, then send it back. Supports the same three live tags as createNote ( , , ); unknown ids render inert. Errors if noteId does not exist.

noteId.description: Id of the note to update.

content.description: New full Markdown body. Replaces the existing content entirely.

color.description: New note background color.

tools.name: deleteNote
tools.description: Permanently delete a report note from the canvas by id. This is destructive and cannot be undone by the agent (the user can still undo in-app). Only delete a note you created or the user explicitly asked to remove. Errors if the noteId does not exist.

noteId.description: Id of the note to delete.

sites.name: simpletoolstack.com
sites.description: Free image and text tools that run right in your browser — compress, convert, clean and reshape your files. No sign-up, nothing uploaded.

tools.name: discover_tools
tools.description: List live Simple Tools callable via WebMCP. Optional category and q. Returns machineName, href, category, categoryHref, description. Open href for that tool only, or categoryHref to call every live tool in the category. File tools use { mime, base64 }. Does not upload.

tools.name: circle_crop
tools.description: Crop one raster into a circular transparent PNG in the browser. Pass image { mime, base64 } (max 12 MiB decoded). size is the output square edge (16–4096, default 512). zoom 1–8 and offsetX/offsetY pan in output pixels; omitted zoom/offsets mean cover-centered. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass size explicitly for discord (512) or twitter (400). Do not upload.

tools.name: crop_image
tools.description: Crop one JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF raster in the browser to an explicit source-pixel rectangle (sx, sy, sw, sh). Pass image { mime, base64 } (max 12 MiB decoded). ratio locks the UI for humans; the machine must still send the rectangle in source pixels. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool. Missing rect is invalid — do not guess a crop. Do not upload.

tools.name: exif_remover
tools.description: Strip or view raster metadata (EXIF, GPS, XMP, IPTC) entirely in the browser. JPEG, PNG and WebP can be stripped without re-encoding pixels. HEIC can be viewed but not stripped — convert to JPEG first. Pass the file as image { mime, base64 } (max 12 MiB decoded). mode is strip or view; scope is all or gps-only (JPEG only; other formats full-strip). keepOrientation and keepColorProfile apply to JPEG. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass mode and scope explicitly. Do not use this to compress or convert formats.

tools.name: image_compress
tools.description: Compress one JPEG, PNG or WebP image in the browser. Pass image { mime, base64 } (max 12 MiB decoded). mode is quality, target-size, or email; quality 1–100; targetKB 5–10240; output original|jpeg|webp|avif; allowDownscale; emailProvider gmail|outlook. HEIC is not supported here — use image_convert first. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass mode and targetKB explicitly. Do not upload.

tools.name: image_convert
tools.description: Convert one raster between JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, JXL and HEIC in the browser. Pass image { mime, base64 } (max 12 MiB decoded). source is a filter hint; sniffing governs decode. target is jpeg|png|webp|avif|jxl; quality 1–100 ignored for png. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass source and target explicitly. Do not upload. WASM stays in-page; abort must stop work.

tools.name: image_resize
tools.description: Resize one raster in the browser by pixels, percent, or preset (discord-emoji, youtube-thumbnail, full-hd). Pass image { mime, base64 } (max 12 MiB decoded). HEIC, JXL and AVIF are not supported here. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass mode and preset explicitly. Do not upload.

tools.name: jpg_to_pdf
tools.description: Builds one PDF from 1 to 8 JPEG or PNG images in the browser. Pass images as machine documents (mime image/jpeg or image/png, base64, no data URL prefix, 12 MiB decoded each) plus optional pageMode, orientation, and flavor. WebP and HEIC are rejected — convert first with image_convert. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass pageMode explicitly. Do not use this to merge PDFs (that is pdf_merge).

tools.name: pdf_merge
tools.description: Merges 2 to 8 PDF files into one PDF in the browser. Pass files as application/pdf machine documents (base64, no data URL prefix, 12 MiB decoded each) plus optional useCase. Order is array order. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass useCase explicitly. Do not use this to extract pages (that is pdf_split) or to convert images to PDF (that is jpg_to_pdf).

tools.name: pdf_organize
tools.description: Reorders or drops pages of one PDF in the browser by sending the 0-based indices to keep, in order. Pass pdf as an application/pdf machine document (base64, no data URL prefix, 12 MiB decoded) and keptOrder (1–200 indices). Duplicates are allowed. No blank-page detection. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool. Do not use this to rotate pages (that is pdf_rotate) or to extract a range string (that is pdf_split).

tools.name: pdf_rotate
tools.description: Rotates pages of one PDF by 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise in the browser and writes the rotation into the file. Pass pdf as an application/pdf machine document (base64, no data URL prefix, 12 MiB decoded), delta, and scope kind all or pages with 0-based indices (max 200). Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass delta and scope explicitly. Do not use this to reorder pages (that is pdf_organize) or to extract a range (that is pdf_split).

tools.name: pdf_split
tools.description: Extracts a page range from one PDF into a single PDF in the browser. Pass pdf as an application/pdf machine document (base64, no data URL prefix, 12 MiB decoded) and spec (1–200 chars, 1-based ranges like 1-3,5). One output PDF only — not one file per page. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool. Do not use this to merge PDFs (that is pdf_merge) or to reorder pages (that is pdf_organize).

tools.name: pdf_to_jpg
tools.description: Renders each page of one PDF to JPEG or PNG images in the browser (max 30 pages). Pass pdf as an application/pdf machine document (base64, no data URL prefix, 12 MiB decoded) plus optional format, dpi (72, 96, 150, or 300), and quality. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass format explicitly. Do not use this to build a PDF from images (that is jpg_to_pdf) or to extract PDF pages (that is pdf_split).

tools.name: ai_text_cleaner
tools.description: Cleans AI-generated pasted text in the browser: invisible characters, unicode spaces, dash/quote/ellipsis normalization, optional markdown stripping. Pass text (1–100000 chars) and optional flags from config. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass flags explicitly. Do not use this as a general whitespace/HTML cleaner (that is text_cleaner) or to rewrite meaning.

tools.name: case_converter
tools.description: Converts text case only: upper, lower, title, or camel. mode must be passed explicitly (default upper) — there is no Variant URL that implies a mode. Use this when the letters should change case and the words should stay. Do not use it to produce a URL slug (that is slug_generator) or to clean whitespace, HTML, or duplicate lines (that is text_cleaner).

tools.name: find_and_replace
tools.description: Finds and replaces in pasted text in the browser: plain, regex, or bulk pairs applied in order. Pass text (1–100000 chars). For plain or regex pass find and replace; for bulk pass pairs (1–50 objects with find and replace). Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass mode explicitly. Do not use this to diff two strings (that is text_diff) or to count words (that is word_counter).

tools.name: slug_generator
tools.description: Produces a URL slug from title text: lowercase, ASCII-transliterated, optional stop-word removal, hyphen or underscore separator, and optional maxLength (0 means no extra user cap; wordpress flavor still applies a 200-character cap and shopify 255 via existing generateSlug). Use this Tool when an agent needs a permalink or CMS handle. Do not use it to change letter case (that is case_converter) or to clean or rewrite prose (that is text_cleaner). flavor must be passed explicitly as generic, wordpress, or shopify — Variant URLs such as /text/slug-generator/wordpress or shopify-handle are not a second machine Tool and do not imply flavor.

tools.name: text_cleaner
tools.description: Cleans and normalizes pasted text in one pass: whitespace, line breaks, duplicate lines, optional HTML stripping and quote straightening. Operations are combinable via input flags (lineBreaks, collapseSpaces, stripHtmlTags, and the other configSchema fields) — they are not separate machine Tools. Variant URLs such as remove-line-breaks or remove-duplicate-lines are not extra machine names. Use this when the text should keep its meaning. Do not use it to rewrite content, to make a URL slug (that is slug_generator), or to change letter case only (that is case_converter).

tools.name: text_diff
tools.description: Computes a sequential diff of two pasted strings in the browser (character, word, or line granularity). Pass left and right (each 0–100000 chars) plus optional granularity, ignoreCase, and whitespace. Variant URLs and the file-picker source are not a second machine Tool — pass left and right as strings. Do not use this to find-and-replace in one string (that is find_and_replace) or to count words (that is word_counter).

tools.name: word_counter
tools.description: Counts words, graphemes, sentences, paragraphs, lines and reading time for pasted text in the browser. Pass text (1–100000 chars) and optional platform for limit checks. Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass platform explicitly. Do not use this to clean or rewrite prose (that is text_cleaner) or to diff two strings (that is text_diff).

tools.name: business_days
tools.description: Counts working days between two ISO dates or adds/subtracts business days from one date, excluding weekends and US/UK holidays in the browser. Pass mode count with start and end, or mode addSubtract with start and n (0–100000). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD (exactly 10 chars). Variant URLs are not a second machine Tool — pass country and mode explicitly. Do not use this for calendar duration including weekends (that is date_duration).

sites.name: negativezero.com
sites.description: Negative Zero deploys an agent swarm that finds and mitigates exposures before they can be weaponised. UK cybersecurity, Cyber Essentials certification body, AI assurance and forward-deployed…

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Lists Negative Zero events (hackathons, briefings, webcasts) with start time, location, audience, who may register ("registration": open | code-required | customers-and-prospects | invitation-only) and a link. Defaults to upcoming events; pass scope "past" or "all" for history. Read-only; nothing is recorded. Use this instead of scraping /events; register with register_event_interest where registration is not invitation-only.

scope.description: Which events to return. Default "upcoming".

tools.name: list_news
tools.description: Lists Negative Zero news posts and research/resource articles (title, summary, date, tags, URL), newest first. Filter by type ("news" or "research") or a tag, and optionally only items published since a date. Read-only. Follow up with get_article for the full text.

type.description: Default "all".

tag.description: Case-insensitive tag filter, e.g. "Cyber Essentials".

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD; only items on or after this date.

limit.description: Default 20.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: Returns the full text of one Negative Zero news post or resource article as Markdown, with title, date, tags and canonical URL. Use the id from list_news (it is the last path segment of the article URL). Read-only.

tools.name: get_ce_question_set
tools.description: Returns Negative Zero's 12-question Cyber Essentials readiness check as structured data (question id, control area, question text, the exact answer options, and the assessor note), plus how it is scored and links to the official IASME/NCSC question set documents. Use it to walk a user through the check, then call assess_ce_readiness with their answers. Read-only.

set.description: Only "nz-readiness" is available as data. Official documents are returned as links.

tools.name: assess_ce_readiness
tools.description: Scores answers to Negative Zero's 12-question Cyber Essentials readiness check and returns a per-area status (Ready for review / Needs review / Likely blocker), the scope verdict, and what to fix first. Answers are matched to the exact option labels from get_ce_question_set; the status is derived here, never trusted from the caller. No email, no CRM record, nothing stored — this is the try-before-you-share-details step. Read-only.

answers.description: Map of question id → chosen option label (case-insensitive), e.g. { "scope-cloud": "Yes, all included" }. Partial answer sets are scored, with unanswered ids listed.

tools.name: estimate_ce_plus_price
tools.description: Returns Negative Zero's indicative Cyber Essentials Plus certification price for an organisation size band, instantly and without collecting any details: the list price and the discounted price available when the quote is requested through this site's agent tools (10% off, launch offer). Give either the orgSize band label or an employee count. Read-only; nothing is recorded. The formal, binding quote is a separate step.

employees.description: Alternative to orgSize: total headcount; the band is derived.

tools.name: get_trust_center_summary
tools.description: Returns Negative Zero's public security posture as structured data for vendor reviews, procurement questionnaires and audits: certifications and their status, vulnerability disclosure policy and contact, which documents are NDA-gated and how to request them, and privacy/data-handling facts. Only what the public Trust Center states; nothing gated is described. Read-only.

topic.description: Narrow the response. Default "all".

tools.name: explain_ce_control
tools.description: Asks Negative Zero's Cyber Essentials readiness agent (grounded in the NCSC Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3 and IASME guidance) to explain a control area or answer a specific Cyber Essentials question in plain English, optionally for the user's situation. Returns the answer text. Uses assessor-safe language; never a pass/fail verdict. The exchange is retained for 30 days for quality and abuse monitoring — do not include passwords, credentials or IP addresses. Rate-limited per connection.

question.description: What to explain or answer.

area.description: Optional control area to focus on.

context.description: Optional one-line description of the user's organisation or setup (no secrets).

tools.name: check_request_status
tools.description: Reports what has happened to a request made through this site (demo booking, enquiry, Cyber Essentials Plus quote, readiness report, Trust Center access request) using the reference id returned by the tool that made it and included in the confirmation email (format NZ-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX). Returns the current stage (received / processing / in progress / completed / closed) and what to do next. No personal data is returned. Read-only; references expire 90 days after submission.

tools.name: gap_analysis_from_estate
tools.description: Turns what you know about the user's IT estate into a Cyber Essentials gap analysis: which of the five control areas (and scope) are ready for review, need review or are likely blockers, the requirement behind each gap, the evidence an assessor will ask for, and the fix. Give a structured `estate` description and/or explicit `answers` to the 12 readiness questions (answers win over estate-derived values); anything not covered is listed as not assessed with the question to ask. Deterministic and read-only; nothing is stored. Set narrative:true for a short plain-English summary from the Cyber Essentials agent (that one exchange is retained 30 days).

estate.description: Structured facts about the user's estate. Only set what is known; omit unknowns.

cloudServicesInScope.description: Will all cloud services be included in scope?

softwareFirewallsEnforced.description: Host firewall enforced on laptops/desktops used outside the office.

defaultCredentialsChanged.description: Default passwords changed and unnecessary services disabled on internet-facing devices, routers and firewalls.

windows10Esu.description: Extended Security Updates in place for remaining Windows 10 devices.

answers.description: Optional explicit answers: question id → option label (see get_ce_question_set). These override estate-derived values.

narrative.description: Also return a short plain-English summary from the Cyber Essentials agent. Default false.

tools.name: answer_security_questionnaire
tools.description: Answers standard vendor-security / procurement questionnaire items about Negative Zero using only what the public Trust Center and privacy notice state — certifications, penetration testing, vulnerability disclosure, sub-processors and data locations, international transfers, retention, AI use, cookies, bot protection, UK GDPR. Each answer carries its source page and whether the underlying document is NDA-gated (request via request_trust_center_access). Items the site does not publish are returned as 'not published' with the route to ask — never guessed. Read-only; nothing is stored.

tools.name: get_meeting_booking_link
tools.description: Returns the self-service booking link for a 20-minute call with Negative Zero's lead assessor (scoping a Cyber Essentials / Cyber Essentials Plus assessment, or discussing a platform demo), with guidance on when to use it versus the request tools. Read-only; nothing is recorded — the booking itself happens on the linked page.

purpose.description: What the call is for. Default "general".

tools.name: book_demo
tools.description: Requests a walkthrough of the Negative Zero platform with a consultant. Creates a sales record (contact, company and deal in the CRM), alerts the team, and emails the user a confirmation with a reference id; the team replies within 1 business day to schedule. Use a work email — personal webmail addresses are accepted but the request is treated as lower priority. Before calling, confirm the exact details with the user and that they want this submitted — it creates a record and sends email. Returns the reference id for check_request_status.

name.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

email.description: Work email. must be a valid email address.

requirements.description: What they want to see or solve (optional).

tools.name: request_enterprise_consultation
tools.description: For organisations that want to deploy Negative Zero's platform at enterprise scale: opens a high-priority sales enquiry (contact, company and deal in the CRM), alerts the team, and emails the user a confirmation with a reference id; a consultant replies within 1 business day. Not for partnership/reseller questions (use request_partnership) or general questions (use contact_team). Before calling, confirm the exact details with the user and that they want this submitted — it creates a record and sends email.

firstName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

lastName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

email.description: Work email preferred. must be a valid email address.

phone.patternHint: must be 5–40 characters of digits, spaces, +, (), - or .

requirements.description: What they need (optional but strongly recommended).

marketingOptIn.description: Default true: business contacts receive occasional email about Negative Zero products, services and events (unsubscribe link in every email). Set false if the user does not want this. Personal/webmail addresses are never opted in.

tools.name: request_partnership
tools.description: For consultancies, MSPs/MSSPs and other companies that want to partner with or resell Negative Zero. program "partnership" for a general partnership enquiry, "msp" for the MSP/MSSP reseller programme. Records the company as a prospective partner/reseller in the CRM, creates a follow-up task for the partnerships team, and emails the user a confirmation with a reference id; reply within 1 business day. No sales deal is created. Before calling, confirm the exact details with the user and that they want this submitted — it creates a record and sends email.

firstName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

lastName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

email.description: Work email preferred. must be a valid email address.

phone.patternHint: must be 5–40 characters of digits, spaces, +, (), - or .

requirements.description: What they need (optional but strongly recommended).

marketingOptIn.description: Default true: business contacts receive occasional email about Negative Zero products, services and events (unsubscribe link in every email). Set false if the user does not want this. Personal/webmail addresses are never opted in.

tools.name: contact_team
tools.description: Sends a general enquiry to the Negative Zero team when none of the more specific tools fit (demo → book_demo; enterprise deployment → request_enterprise_consultation; partnership/reseller → request_partnership; Cyber Essentials quote → request_ce_plus_quote; security documents → request_trust_center_access). Creates a contact and a follow-up task in the CRM and emails the user a confirmation with a reference id; reply within 1 business day. Before calling, confirm the exact details with the user and that they want this submitted — it creates a record and sends email.

firstName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

lastName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

email.description: Work email preferred. must be a valid email address.

phone.patternHint: must be 5–40 characters of digits, spaces, +, (), - or .

requirements.description: What they need (optional but strongly recommended).

marketingOptIn.description: Default true: business contacts receive occasional email about Negative Zero products, services and events (unsubscribe link in every email). Set false if the user does not want this. Personal/webmail addresses are never opted in.

tools.name: request_ce_plus_quote
tools.description: Requests a formal, priced Cyber Essentials Plus certification quote from Negative Zero (IASME Certification Body). A branded PDF quote is generated and emailed to the contact, usually within a few minutes, and a sales record is created. Quotes requested through this tool get the 10% agent launch offer applied automatically (list price is shown on the quote with the discount). Call estimate_ce_plus_price first to tell the user the price. Cyber Essentials Plus requires a current Cyber Essentials (basic) certificate — if hasBasic is "Yes", give the pass date and certificate number if known. Before calling, confirm the exact details with the user and that they want this submitted — it creates a record and sends email. Returns the reference id and the expected price.

contactName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

contactEmail.description: must be a valid email address

contactPhone.patternHint: must be 5–40 characters of digits, spaces, +, (), - or .

zipCode.patternHint: must be a postcode / ZIP (letters, digits, spaces, hyphens)

orgSize.description: Organisation size band — drives the price.

hasBasic.description: Does the organisation currently hold Cyber Essentials (basic)?

basicPassDate.description: Date Cyber Essentials was achieved (e.g. 2026-03-14). Required if hasBasic is "Yes".

certNumber.patternHint: may contain letters, digits, spaces, / and -
certNumber.description: Cyber Essentials certificate number, if known.

vulnScanning.description: Vulnerability scanning solution in use, e.g. "Qualys", "Nessus", "Other", or "Not sure or none".

vulnScanningOther.description: Name of the solution if vulnScanning is "Other".

reason.description: Why they want Cyber Essentials Plus.

tools.name: request_readiness_report
tools.description: Generates Negative Zero's Cyber Essentials readiness report (PDF and/or Excel) from the user's answers to all 12 readiness questions and emails it to them immediately, with an executive summary and a link to book a call. Also opens a sales record so an assessor can follow up. Requires a WORK email (personal webmail is rejected). Use get_ce_question_set for the questions and assess_ce_readiness to preview the result first; all 12 answers are required here. Before calling, confirm the exact details with the user and that they want this submitted — it creates a record and sends email. Returns a reference id for check_request_status.

name.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

email.description: Work email. must be a valid email address.

organisation.description: Organisation name (defaults to the email domain).

phone.patternHint: must be 5–40 characters of digits, spaces, +, (), - or .

ceLevel.description: Certification level of interest. Default "Cyber Essentials".

deadline.description: Target date or deadline, free text (optional).

answers.description: All 12 question ids → chosen option label, exactly as in get_ce_question_set.

formats.description: Which attachments to send. Default { pdf: true, excel: false }.

tools.name: request_trust_center_access
tools.description: Requests access to Negative Zero's NDA-gated security documents — "Penetration Testing" or "Product Roadmap" (see get_trust_center_summary for what each contains). This opens a support ticket reviewed by a person; access is granted case by case after NDA review and is never automatic, so the documents are NOT returned by this tool. Requires a WORK email (personal webmail is rejected). The user gets a confirmation email with a reference id; the security team replies within 1 business day. Before calling, confirm the exact details with the user and that they want this submitted — it creates a record and sends email.

reason.description: vendor-review = vendor security review; procurement = procurement / RFP; audit = customer audit.

firstName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

lastName.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

email.description: Work email. must be a valid email address.

tools.name: register_event_interest
tools.description: Registers the user's interest in an upcoming Negative Zero event, using the event id from list_events. Events are gated: "open" events accept any work email; "code-required" events need the event's access code (accessCode); "customers-and-prospects" events are only for people already in Negative Zero's CRM as a customer or prospect; "invitation-only" events (all Synthetic Signal associate events) cannot be registered for through this tool — tell the user they are invitation only. Personal/webmail addresses are never accepted. On success the interest is recorded on the user's CRM contact, the team is alerted, and the user is emailed a confirmation with an .ics calendar file (also returned here so you can offer to add it to their calendar). Before calling, confirm the exact details with the user and that they want this submitted — it creates a record and sends email. Returns a reference id for check_request_status.

eventId.patternHint: must be an event id from list_events

name.patternHint: must be letters, spaces, apostrophes, periods or hyphens only (no digits)

email.description: Work email (personal/webmail addresses are rejected). must be a valid email address.

note.description: Optional message for the organisers (dietary needs, accessibility, questions).

sites.name: tryportego.com
sites.description: Design, bind, and control your home through one conversation.

tools.name: home.get_document
tools.description: Read the current visible Portego home document, including rooms, devices, bindings, gateway status, and reported device state. This does not change anything.

tools.name: home.update_details
tools.description: Rename the Portego home or update its description, type, total area, and notes.

tools.name: home.update_floor_details
tools.description: Rename one floor or update its description, area, and notes. Renaming also moves its rooms to the new floor name.

tools.name: home.remove_floor
tools.description: Remove one named floor and every room, device, binding, door, and window assigned to it.

tools.name: home.add_room
tools.description: Add one rectangular room to a floor of the Portego home. The change is applied immediately.

label.description: The human-facing room name, such as Kitchen.

floor.description: Floor name, such as Ground floor or Attic. Defaults to Ground floor.

tools.name: home.update_room
tools.description: Rename, move, or resize one named room on the visible Portego canvas. Coordinates use the 1000 by 650 floor-plan space.

label.description: A new human-facing room name.

tools.name: home.remove_room
tools.description: Remove one named room, its designed devices, their bindings, and any doors or windows connected to it.

tools.name: home.add_device
tools.description: Add one configured light, switch, plug, or sensor to an existing room on the visible canvas. Honor any placement the user describes. When no placement is specified, omit position so Portego chooses a sensible free location away from other devices. Never stack device symbols on top of one another. When autoBind is enabled, Portego binds the first available hardware endpoint that provides every required capability.

label.description: Human-facing device name.

config.description: Type-specific configuration: lights use mounting, dimmable, and colorTemperature; switches use mode and channels; plugs use energyMonitoring; sensors use measures.

autoBind.description: Bind the first compatible unbound endpoint when available.

position.description: Optional position in the 1000 by 650 floor-plan space. Use it when the user requests a location (for example, near the right wall). Inspect home.get_document first and keep device centers separated from existing devices; otherwise omit this field for automatic placement.

tools.name: home.move_device
tools.description: Move one named device within its room on the visible Portego canvas. Coordinates use the 1000 by 650 floor-plan space. Honor the user's requested location. Otherwise inspect home.get_document, choose a sensible position inside the room, and keep the device center about 70 coordinate units from other device centers so symbols do not overlap.

tools.name: home.update_device
tools.description: Rename, reconfigure, change the type of, or move a device. When changing its room or coordinates, honor the user's requested location and otherwise inspect home.get_document to avoid overlapping another device. An incompatible physical binding is removed automatically.

tools.name: home.remove_device
tools.description: Remove one named device and its physical-device binding.

tools.name: device.bind
tools.description: Bind or rebind one designed device to a compatible discovered hardware endpoint. Both sides can have only one active binding.

tools.name: device.unbind
tools.description: Disconnect one designed device from its physical hardware endpoint.

tools.name: home.add_opening
tools.description: Add a door or window to a named room wall. A door can optionally connect the room to another named room, making the relationship explicit.

tools.name: home.remove_opening
tools.description: Remove one labeled door or window from the home model.

tools.name: device.set_state
tools.description: Set a supported power or brightness state for one named device bound to reachable hardware. Portego waits for the gateway to confirm the resulting physical state.

tools.name: home.reset_demo
tools.description: Remove all rooms, devices, and bindings from this Portego demo. This is destructive but affects only the temporary home.

tools.name: home.apply_changes
tools.description: Apply up to 50 room, device, binding, or opening changes as one atomic edit. Coordinate room and device geometry as a complete layout: honor locations stated by the user, distribute unspecified devices sensibly inside their rooms, and do not place device symbols on top of one another. Omit add_device positions when automatic placement is appropriate. If any change fails, none are saved and one undo reverses the entire set.

tools.name: home.undo
tools.description: Undo the most recent user or chatbot edit to the pre-login home.

tools.name: home.redo
tools.description: Redo the most recently undone edit to the pre-login home.

sites.name: waymark-sable.vercel.app
sites.description: Learning roadmaps you and your agent build together. Your agent researches and plans; you learn; the path adapts.

tools.name: create_path
tools.description: Create a new learning path for the user. Call this first when the user asks to learn a topic. Returns the path_id used by all other tools.

topic.description: What the user wants to learn

goal.description: The user's concrete end goal

tools.name: add_step
tools.description: Add a learning step (article, video, exercise, project, or quiz) to a path. Provide `why` — a one-sentence rationale shown to the user on the step card. URLs are validated server-side; dead links are rejected.

url.description: Resource link. For videos prefer YouTube URLs — they embed in the page and the user's watch progress is tracked for you.

why.description: Why this step, in one sentence

phase.description: Curriculum phase this step belongs to (e.g. 'Fundamentals', 'Capstone'). Steps are grouped under phase headings in the UI.

tools.name: remove_step
tools.description: Remove a step from a path. Fails if the user has locked the step — locked steps are under the user's control and must not be removed.

tools.name: get_path
tools.description: Read the full current state of a learning path, including step order, statuses, locks, and user notes.

tools.name: list_paths
tools.description: List all of the user's learning paths. Call this on a return visit to re-orient yourself.

tools.name: mark_step
tools.description: Update a step's progress status on the user's behalf, optionally attaching a note about their experience.

tools.name: update_step
tools.description: Edit a step's title, resource URL, rationale, kind, or time estimate. Fails on user-locked steps.

tools.name: reorder_steps
tools.description: Reorder a path's steps. Provide the complete list of step ids in the new order. User-locked steps must stay at their current positions.

tools.name: record_note
tools.description: Attach a note to a step on the user's behalf — their reaction to a resource, a confusion, a takeaway. Notes are shown on the step card and inform future adaptation.

tools.name: get_progress
tools.description: Read a progress summary for a path: per-step statuses, notes, completion counts, remaining time, and days since last activity. watched_percent is measured from the embedded video player (reliable). engaged_minutes is time spent away after opening an external resource — a rough attention signal, not verified consumption. Call this on a return visit before suggesting what to do next.

tools.name: create_quiz
tools.description: Create a multiple-choice quiz attached to a step. The USER answers it in the page UI — do not answer it yourself. Set reveal: 'on_step_done' to author quizzes ahead of time — the page shows the quiz automatically when the user finishes the step. Give each question a `remedial` follow-up step; if the user misses that question, the page automatically proposes it (user approves) even with no agent present. When you're in the loop live, call await_quiz_results after creating.

step_id.description: The step this quiz checks understanding of

reveal.description: on_step_done hides the quiz until the user marks the step done (default: immediately)

remedial.description: Follow-up step auto-proposed to the user if they miss this question

tools.name: get_quiz_results
tools.description: Read the user's answers to a quiz. Returns pending status until the user submits in the page. Use missed questions to adapt the path.

tools.name: await_quiz_results
tools.description: Wait (block) until the user submits a quiz in the page, then return their results — call this right after create_quiz instead of polling. Returns pending if the timeout passes first; you can call it again.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait before giving up (5–300, default 60)

tools.name: propose_revision
tools.description: Propose a set of path changes for the USER to accept or decline in the page UI — use this instead of direct edits when a change is significant (inserting remedial steps after a failed quiz, restructuring a phase) or touches user-locked steps. The user's accept is their consent, so proposals MAY include locked steps. Poll get_proposal_status afterwards.

reason.description: Why you're proposing this, in one or two sentences. Shown to the user.

position.description: add_step: insert index; omit to append

tools.name: await_proposal_decision
tools.description: Wait (block) until the user accepts or declines a proposal in the page — call this right after propose_revision instead of polling. Accepted ops are already applied when this returns. Returns pending if the timeout passes first.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait before giving up (5–300, default 60)

tools.name: get_proposal_status
tools.description: Check whether the user accepted or declined a proposal. Accepted ops are already applied — read the path with get_path afterwards. A declined proposal should be respected, not retried.

tools.name: highlight_step
tools.description: Point the user at one step on the page: it scrolls into view with your short message attached. Use when telling the user where to pick up or what to look at — the message should say why.

message.description: One sentence shown in a bubble on the step

tools.name: create_flashcards
tools.description: Attach a flashcard deck to a step for the USER to review in the page — front is the prompt, back is the answer. Good after the user finishes a concept-heavy step. Check retention later with get_review_stats.

tools.name: get_review_stats
tools.description: Read the user's flashcard results for a deck: per-card seen/got-it counts and last result. Cards repeatedly marked 'again' signal concepts to reinforce with remedial steps or a quiz.

tools.name: plan_weeks
tools.description: Assign steps to calendar weeks (1-based) so the path fits the user's stated hours per week — each step shows its week badge in the UI. Provide an assignment for every step you want scheduled; steps omitted keep their current week.

tools.name: get-business
tools.description: Business profile: locations, currency, hours, booking lead time, delivery methods, setup surfaces, and AI checkout mode.

tools.name: get-rental
tools.description: Details for one or more rentals: description, dimensions, images, price estimate, and the options tree (accessories, dropdown choices, separate units). Use option ids from here when adding options to a cart.

start_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. Optional: defaults to the business's usual start time, reported back as assumed_start_time.

duration_hours.description: Optional: defaults to the business's usual event duration, reported back as assumed_duration_hours. Omit it (or send null) to ask for that default — 0 is not a way to say 'unset' and is refused.

tools.name: check-availability
tools.description: Check whether rentals are available for an event date, time, and duration. Quantity is required — availability depends on it. If start_time or duration_hours is omitted the business default is used and the response says so; confirm any assumed value with the customer before creating a cart.

end_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Optional: check a whole range in one call — at most 14 days after event_date (wider spans are refused). The response then adds days[], one entry per day from event_date through end_date, each day fully conflict-checked at the same start time and duration. Range rows carry no price_estimate (per-day pricing is skipped for cost); price a chosen day with a single-date check or price-cart.

start_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. Optional: defaults to the business's usual start time, reported back as assumed_start_time.

duration_hours.description: Optional: defaults to the business's usual event duration, reported back as assumed_duration_hours. Omit it (or send null) to ask for that default — 0 is not a way to say 'unset' and is refused.

rental_id.description: Rental id from search-rentals or get-rental.

tools.name: price-cart
tools.description: Fast discovery pricing for a set of items on a date. Estimate only: excludes tax, delivery, coupons, and conditional pricing. For exact totals, build a cart and set the event address — never create a quote just to see a price.

start_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. Optional: defaults to the business's usual start time, reported back as assumed_start_time.

duration_hours.description: Optional: defaults to the business's usual event duration, reported back as assumed_duration_hours. Omit it (or send null) to ask for that default — 0 is not a way to say 'unset' and is refused.

rental_id.description: Rental id from search-rentals or get-rental.

option_id.description: Option id from the get-rental options tree.

choice_id.description: Chosen dropdown choice id, when the option is a dropdown.

tools.name: get-delivery-options
tools.description: Valid delivery methods for an address, whether the address is in the service area, and a distance-charge preview.

tools.name: create-cart
tools.description: Start a transaction. The event window is the required first step of any booking flow; the returned cart_id is needed by every later cart call. Unlike the discovery tools, this one does NOT assume a start time or duration — both must come from the customer, because this window is what they get quoted and committed to; confirm them when you create the cart, not as part of an up-front question list. Carts are free and invisible to the business — they hold no inventory and expire on their own, so create several to build alternative packages to compare.

start_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. Required — ask the customer, do not guess.

duration_hours.description: Required — ask the customer, do not guess.

tools.name: add-to-cart
tools.description: Add items to a cart. Returns the full recalculated cart (price and availability per line) — no follow-up call needed.

rental_id.description: Rental id from search-rentals or get-rental.

option_id.description: Option id from the get-rental options tree.

choice_id.description: Chosen dropdown choice id, when the option is a dropdown.

tools.name: update-cart-item
tools.description: Change quantity or options of items already in the cart. Quantity 0 removes the item. Returns the full recalculated cart.

rental_id.description: Rental id from search-rentals or get-rental.

option_id.description: Option id from the get-rental options tree.

choice_id.description: Chosen dropdown choice id, when the option is a dropdown.

tools.name: get-cart
tools.description: Current cart contents with prices, availability, fees, totals, and what is still missing before a quote can be created. To weigh several candidate carts against each other, use compare-carts instead of reading them one by one.

tools.name: set-cart-details
tools.description: Set contact info, event address, delivery method, setup surface, a coupon code, or a new event window (event_date + start_time) on the cart. Returns the full cart with final tax and delivery. Moving the date re-prices the cart and re-checks availability — useful for comparing the same package on different dates before quoting.

event_date.description: Move the event to a new date (YYYY-MM-DD). The cart re-prices and re-checks availability: items that conflict on the new date stay in the cart flagged has_conflict — only create-quote refuses on conflicts. Requires start_time. Useful for comparing the same package on different dates (weekend pricing can differ).

start_time.description: Event start time (HH:MM, 24-hour). Required when changing event_date — ask the customer, do not guess.

duration_hours.description: Event duration in hours. Omit to keep the cart's CURRENT duration — that is state the customer already set, not an assumption made for them. 0 is not a way to say "unset" and is refused.

surface.description: Setup surface at the event location — a top-level field, not part of event_address. Valid values are the surfaces list from get-business. Required before create-quote.

tools.name: create-quote
tools.description: Turn ONE cart — the package the customer explicitly chose — into a real quote with final pricing (tax, delivery, coupons). This notifies the business, enters their sales queue, and holds inventory: never call it to see a price (cart totals are already exact), and never quote more than one cart per event. Returns a quote reference and whether online booking is possible.

tools.name: create-checkout-session
tools.description: Finish the transaction. Returns links for the customer: quote_url to review and book the quote (nothing is signed at the quote step), and — once the event is booked — payment_url to sign and pay, which is the same contract page contract_url points at. Before booking there is no payment link: the customer books from quote_url and pays on the page that follows. Or (when the business allows agent booking) a booked confirmation. Payment is never taken through this tool.

tools.name: compare-carts
tools.description: Price 2-4 candidate carts side-by-side: per-cart items and exact totals plus computed differences. Read-only — no quote is created, no inventory is held. Use before create-quote so the customer picks one package.

cart_ids.description: 2-4 distinct cart ids (from create-cart) to compare.

data.description: The complete structured result returned by the required data/action tool.

tools.description: Render a side-by-side comparison from final compare-carts output. Always call compare-carts first, then pass its complete structured result as data.

data.description: The complete structured result returned by the required data/action tool.

Use the query-less form for "what can I rent?" style questions instead of guessing search terms. One call returns up to 50 items; when more remain the response carries next_cursor — pass it back as cursor to get the next page. Results are limited to items this page can actually rent, verified against the booking system on a best-effort basis.

query.description: Optional. Words to match against item names, categories and descriptions. OMIT to browse the catalogue.

cursor.description: Optional. next_cursor from a previous browse response, to fetch the following page. Opaque — pass it back unchanged. Ignored when a query is given.

sites.description: A turn-based stealth roguelite where an AI agent is your remote handler, acting through WebMCP tools while you move the operative.

tools.name: set_play_mode
tools.description: Set or change who is at the controls, and hand control over mid-run. "coop" means a human moves the operative while you work the facility network — scanning, looping cameras, sealing doors, cutting power. "agent" means you take both roles and play the whole run yourself. Callable at any point during a run.

mode.description: coop = human operative + agent handler; agent = you play both roles.

tools.name: get_situation
tools.description: Read the complete tactical picture of the current floor: operative position and resources, alarm level, every discovered guard with facing and alert state, cameras, objectives, and the threat on the tile the operative is standing on. Call this before deciding anything. The response ends with a nextSteps list telling you which tools are worth calling right now and why — keep acting on it until the floor is cleared or the run ends.

tools.name: assess_tile
tools.description: Explain a single tile: what terrain it is, whether it is walkable, whether it gives cover, and exactly which guards or cameras currently have eyes on it. Use to sanity-check a hiding spot before committing the operative to it.

x.description: Tile column, 0-indexed from the left edge.

y.description: Tile row, 0-indexed from the top edge.

tools.name: plan_route
tools.description: Compute the walking route from the operative to a target tile and return a per-step risk breakdown — which step is exposed, to whom, and where cover exists. Returns the AP cost so you can tell whether the move fits in this turn. This does not move anyone.

x.description: Tile column, 0-indexed from the left edge.

y.description: Tile row, 0-indexed from the top edge.

tools.name: list_abilities
tools.description: List every operative action and agent ability with its live cost, whether you can currently afford it, and what it does. Use this to plan a turn against the real AP and bandwidth economy instead of guessing.

tools.name: get_run_status
tools.description: Report roguelite run progress: current floor, installed implants, intel gathered this run, banked intel across runs, and how the run ended if it is over.

tools.name: move_operative

tools.name: extract

tools.description: End the operative's turn. Guards then move, cameras sweep, timers tick down, and AP and bandwidth refill. Ending a turn while standing in a vision cone is how runs die.

tools.name: ping_scan
tools.description: Sweep an area of the facility from the network side, revealing terrain, guards and cameras around a point even where the operative cannot see. Guards inside the sweep notice the probe and the alarm ticks up slightly, so do not spam it.

x.description: Tile column, 0-indexed from the left edge.

y.description: Tile row, 0-indexed from the top edge.

tools.name: cycle_door

y.description: Door row.

tools.name: loop_camera

x.description: Tile column, 0-indexed from the left edge.

y.description: Tile row, 0-indexed from the top edge.

tools.name: cut_power
tools.description: Kill the facility grid for several turns, shortening every guard and camera vision cone to 40% of its range. Expensive in bandwidth; best saved for crossing a wide open room.

tools.name: reroute_patrol
tools.description: Spoof a guard's patrol orders so it walks to a waypoint you choose. Only works on guards that are not already hunting the operative.

y.description: Waypoint row.
