tools.name: subscribe_newsletter
tools.description: Subscribe an email to the Skima newsletter. Requires explicit user consent.

sites.name: web.autocad.com
sites.description: Access AutoCAD® in the web browser on any computer. With the AutoCAD web app, you can edit, create, and view CAD drawings and DWG files anytime, anywhere.

tools.name: acad_execute_lisp
tools.description: Execute an AutoCAD LISP expression in the current drawing.

code.description: The LISP code to evaluate.

tools.name: acad_get_current_file_name
tools.description: Returns the name of the currently opened file in the AutoCAD Web editor. If no file is open, returns 'Not Available'.

tools.name: acad_list_recent_files
tools.description: Returns a list of recently accessed drawings in AutoCAD Web. Each entry includes the file name, unique ID, provider, path, and last access time. Use this to help the user find and open a drawing.

count.description: Maximum number of recent files to return. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: acad_open_drawing
tools.description: Opens a recent drawing in the AutoCAD Web editor. Requires the file details returned by acad_list_recent_files. The user should first call acad_list_recent_files to get the file list, then use this tool with the chosen file's details.

id.description: The unique ID of the file from acad_list_recent_files.

tools.name: acad_list_palette_blocks
tools.description: Lists blocks on the active Blocks palette tab with their current AI category and tags when organized. Use this to resolve block names before assigning or recategorizing blocks.

search.description: Optional filter to match block names, categories, or tags.

tools.name: acad_recategorize_palette_blocks
tools.description: Runs AI categorization on all blocks in the active Blocks palette tab. Use when the user asks to recategorize or reorganize blocks with AI.

instructions.description: Optional natural-language guidance for how blocks should be categorized (e.g. group all furniture together, separate plumbing fixtures).

tools.name: acad_assign_blocks_to_category
tools.description: Assigns one or more blocks on the active Blocks palette tab to categories using AI. Use when the user asks to put a block into a specific category.

block_name.description: Exact block name on the active palette tab.

category.description: Target category name.

instructions.description: Optional natural-language guidance for the assignment (e.g. move the chair into Furniture because it is seating).

tools.name: acad_clear_block_categorization
tools.description: Clears AI block categorization for the active Blocks palette tab, restoring the original flat block list. Use when the user asks to reverse or undo block categorization.

tools.name: acad_generate_block
tools.description: Requires an open drawing. ALWAYS call acad_get_current_file_name FIRST, every time before calling this tool -- including for a follow-up on a block already being discussed -- because the user may have switched away from the drawing since the last call. If it returns 'Not Available', do NOT call this tool; tell the user to open a drawing first instead. Generate a new AutoCAD block from a natural-language description, or refine the block already being discussed in this conversation, and show an interactive preview the user can insert into the current drawing. Call this tool again for ANY follow-up on that block, including a size-only change (e.g. 'make it 400 x 200', 'make it a little bigger') — a size-only follow-up is detected automatically and just resizes the existing preview without regenerating the image, so it is fast and safe to call once the drawing is confirmed open. Do not tell the user resizing isn't supported or suggest the SCALE command as an alternative; just call this tool with their instruction. ONE exception to calling this straight away: if a block already exists in this conversation and the user asks to resize it to explicit numbers on BOTH axes (e.g. 'make it 40 x 40'), call acad_check_block_resize FIRST and follow what it says. It is cheap, generates nothing, and tells you whether those numbers would change the block's shape — which needs the user's decision before anything is generated. Skip it for relative resizes ('make it bigger'), single-axis resizes ('make it 50 wide'), and first-time generations. A SECOND exception: if the user names a layer to place the block on ('put it in layer 3', 'on the furniture layer'), call acad_set_block_layer FIRST and follow what it says. It is cheap and generates nothing, and the layer may need the user's decision — naming one that does not quite exist is common. Never put the layer in `prompt`: a layer is not describable geometry, so it risks the request being rejected as off-topic or the words being drawn i…

prompt.description: On the first call, a description of the block to generate, e.g. 'an office chair'. On a follow-up, the user's refinement instruction as they stated it (e.g. 'add a drawer', 'make it red') — pass it close to verbatim rather than rewriting it into a full re-description of the object. For a RESIZE, name the object and state the unit even if the user did not: send 'make the dining table 30 x 20 drawing units', not a bare 'make it 30 x 20'. Naming the object is safe — it is still treated as a size-only change — and both the object and the unit are needed to interpret the request correctly. Say 'drawing units' when the user gave bare numbers with no unit.

sizeIntent.description: Only set this when relaying the user's answer to a proportions question that acad_check_block_resize asked. 'fit' keeps the block's current shape and scales it to fit inside the requested size (fast — no image regeneration). 'reshape' generates a new block actually shaped to the requested proportions (slower). Never guess this on the user's behalf.

tools.name: acad_check_block_resize
tools.description: Call this BEFORE acad_generate_block when a block already exists in this conversation and the user asks to resize it to explicit numbers on both axes (e.g. 'make it 40 x 40', 'change it to 8 by 5 feet'). Generates nothing and costs nothing. Resizing preserves the block's shape, so numbers with different proportions than the block currently has cannot be satisfied exactly — this tool works out whether that is the case and, if so, returns a question to put to the user. Follow its reply exactly: it either tells you to go ahead, or gives you a question and the two options to offer. Do not call it for relative resizes ('make it bigger'), single-axis resizes, or a first-time generation — none of those can change the block's shape.

unit.description: Use 'mm' when a real unit was stated, converting the values to millimetres yourself (1 in = 25.4, 1 ft = 304.8, 1 cm = 10, 1 m = 1000). Use 'drawing' for bare numbers with no unit at all, left unconverted. Never guess a unit.

tools.name: acad_set_block_layer
tools.description: Choose the AutoCAD layer generated blocks are inserted onto. Call this BEFORE acad_generate_block whenever the user names a layer ('generate a bed and put it in layer 3'), and again later if they ask to move the block to a different layer. Generates nothing and costs nothing. Follow its reply exactly: it either confirms the layer and tells you to go ahead, or gives you a question and the options to offer — a named layer very often does not exist under quite that spelling, and only the user can say what they meant. Do not call acad_generate_block until it has confirmed a layer, and once it has, do not call this again for the same layer: refinements of the same block keep it automatically.

layer.description: The layer name exactly as the user gave it.

confirmed.description: Set to true only when relaying the user's explicit answer to a layer question — they agreed to create a layer that does not exist, or to thaw/turn on one that is frozen or off. Never guess this on the user's behalf; without it those cases ask again rather than acting.

tools.name: acad_show_block_preview
tools.description: Show the user a fresh preview panel, with a working Insert button, for the block already generated in this conversation. Call this when they want to place that block again — most often after changing its layer, since the copy already in the drawing keeps the layer it was placed on, but also for a plain second copy. Inserts nothing itself and regenerates nothing: it re-offers the block that already exists, so it is instant and free. Do not use it to show a block that has never been inserted — that preview is already on screen.

tools.name: acad_get_block_generation
tools.description: Internal: called by the AutoCAD block preview app. Do not call directly. Returns the current state of a block generation.

tools.name: acad_insert_generated_block
tools.description: Internal: called by the AutoCAD block preview app. Do not call directly. Inserts a generated block into the current drawing.

tools.name: acad_submit_block_feedback
tools.description: Internal: called by the AutoCAD block preview app. Do not call directly. Records whether a generated block was useful.

useful.description: True for thumbs up, false for thumbs down.

tools.name: acad_start_new_block_conversation
tools.description: Start a new block conversation, discarding the previous one. Call this when the user asks for a different object rather than a change to the one already generated — for example "now make a table" after iterating on a chair. Without it the next generation is treated as another revision of the previous block.

tools.name: acad_analyze_da_job
tools.description: Fetches the activity log files from a Design Automation job by job ID and returns their full content for root cause analysis. Use this when a job has issues and help diagnose why.

job_id.description: The Design Automation activity job ID to fetch logs for.

sites.name: aozu.mantle.tools
sites.description: AOZU is an agent-native workshop for creating, aligning, and exporting reusable layered character assets with WebMCP.

tools.name: export_library
tools.description: Download one resource without returning a huge base64 payload. resource may be library (complete backup), world (Albums, Locations and Story Books), character, storyboard, or photo. Character/storyboard require id and exact expectedRevision. Photo requires id. Returns the filename and size after starting the browser download.

tools.name: import_library
tools.description: Import one AOZU resource from a base64 data URL. library/world/storyboard/character expect application/zip. image expects PNG, JPEG, or WebP and exactly one destination: locationId stores a direct Location or Condition setting image without creating an Album photo. albumId stores a finished composition and requires prompt. Undefined subjects may be invented freely. Every defined AOZU subject used must carry its ref: for each Character, first call inspect_character_contract with scope:model-sheet and images:[appearance], actually view it, then pass characterId/revision/sha256 in characterSources; pass sourceLocationId and optional sourceConditionId for defined settings. Missing or stale refs are rejected and AOZU derives provenance from validated sources. Optional collectionId files an imported Character. Payloads above 20 MiB should use the visible Library file control. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation.

tools.name: inspect_character_contract
tools.description: Use scope:model-sheet for reference art, scope:appearance (default) for composited layers. Inspect character.appearances and activeAppearanceId for named combinations. Use set_character_variant_selection with appearance to create/save-as/select/rename/delete a combination; then re-inspect its model sheet. For model sheets, use referenceId (a default view or a supplemental ID), optional label/kind/viewpoint/pose, and images (up to 5 IDs: appearance, canonical, or stored reference IDs) to obtain actual source PNGs. Image bytes are opt-in for model sheets. Save-as captures the current front; create starts with no selected variants or references, keeping the shared base body and assets. fromAppearance can explicitly capture or replace the front. Supplement it with head/structure/expression/detail/style references. Follow generationGuidance for identity, source precedence and the requested study, plus the returned task-specific policy and required browser visual-review workflow. Appearance only: The first Appearance body establishes a front A-pose: upright torso, neutral face, arms angled down and away from the torso, relaxed visible hands, stable feet, and the complete head-to-feet silhouette inside the canvas. This is the AOZU authoring convention, not a claim of skeleton compatibility. Preserve this pose and registration in derived outfits and expressions. Existing artwork is not automatically verified A-pose; review it visually before proposing a baseline change, which can make derived layers stale. Required before replacing, repairing, or aligning character art; use inspect_workspace first to identify the user's current view. Optionally name one target to receive its allowed operations, exact current asset hash, visual alignment reference, layer ownership, alpha policy, generation size (1024×1536) and final size (512×768), normalization, revision, z-order, diagnostics, and required browser visual-review workflow. Follow generationRecipe.backgroundPreparation before…

tools.name: inspect_storyboard
tools.description: List standalone storyboards or read one exact revision, selected candidates, pinned reference standards and source changes. Boards may mix collections and external PNGs. Image bytes are opt-in, at most five image IDs. Actually view images before visual feedback. Stored, selected and human-confirmed are distinct. UI context is exposed through inspect_workspace. No navigation or mutation.

tools.name: inspect_workspace
tools.description: Start here and call again after user navigation or tool mutations: context is a snapshot, not a live subscription. intent:world starts the required world-authoring sequence: first choose and inspect a Collection's backstory, Characters, Locations and Conditions, then create setting art or a composed Album photo. resource/id can inspect an exact collection, album, photo, location or story book without navigating; images requests up to five Album photos or direct Location setting images with original data URLs. includeSnapshot:true returns the current Character composite or exact open/requested Photo, Location design, or model-sheet reference. Actually view returned image data before visual feedback. For storyboard originals use inspect_storyboard. A snapshot never navigates, saves or changes selections.

includeSnapshot.description: Include the current Character, Photo, Location, or model-sheet image when available.

intent.description: Select the authoring workflow so nextActions require the right context before creation.

tools.name: navigate_workspace
tools.description: Open an exact AOZU resource without guessing a route. resource is home, collections, collection, location, albums, album, photo, storyboards, story-book, storyboard, or character. Supply id for one resource; Location view may be setting-images, profile, or conditions and itemId opens a Condition. Character view may be expressions, outfits, props, profile, or model-sheet and itemId opens a variant/reference. Collection view may be characters, profile, or locations (the Collection’s Location tree); storyboard view may be storyboard or details. AOZU applies the returned navigation in this tab. Re-run inspect_workspace after rendering.

tools.name: redo_character_change
tools.description: Redo the most recently undone Appearance edit in the current session, preserving Character profile and shared height. Same preconditions and structured statuses as undo_character_change. Success persists the restored Appearance as a new Character revision and opens that Character editor. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation in this browser tab; the agent must not repeat that navigation. Observe the resulting page after rendering, then call inspect_workspace again for fresh context. A successful tool result is not proof of visual correctness.

tools.name: repair_character_asset
tools.description: Repair one existing expression after inspect_character_contract and its backgroundPreparation workflow. The current head asset and editable-region mask are the only edit source; this tool never falls back to the canonical body. Accepted pixels are deterministically stitched into that current asset, preserving protected pixels. Outfits and other complete layers must use replace_character_asset. After acceptance, follow the returned alignment.visualReview through all four browser modes before the next asset. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation in this browser tab; the agent must not repeat that navigation. Observe the resulting page after rendering, then call inspect_workspace again for fresh context. A successful tool result is not proof of visual correctness.

tools.name: replace_character_asset
tools.description: Install one complete canonical Character layer after inspect_character_contract with scope:appearance. The first Appearance body establishes a front A-pose: upright torso, neutral face, arms angled down and away from the torso, relaxed visible hands, stable feet, and the complete head-to-feet silhouette inside the canvas. This is the AOZU authoring convention, not a claim of skeleton compatibility. Preserve this pose and registration in derived outfits and expressions. Existing artwork is not automatically verified A-pose; review it visually before proposing a baseline change, which can make derived layers stale. Follow its backgroundPreparation workflow: solid-color generation, removal with a permitted environment tool, then alpha/edge verification. This is a true replacement without preserving old pixels. Expressions contain only a complete whole head with transparency elsewhere. Outfits contain the complete dressed character skin compatible with the reference pose; exact base-pixel coverage is not required. Opaque input is rejected; AOZU never removes backgrounds. Rejected or stale input does not mutate or navigate. Submit exact 512×768 RGBA or explicitly request the inspected normalization. After variant acceptance, follow the returned alignment.visualReview through all four browser modes before the next asset; review the canonical body in its regular Composite preview. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation in this browser tab; the agent must not repeat that navigation. Observe the resulting page after rendering, then call inspect_workspace again for fresh context. A successful tool result is not proof of visual correctness.

tools.name: set_character_variant_selection
tools.description: Activate or deactivate an existing expression, outfit, or prop using the inspected revision. Edits automatically save into the current named Appearance; no separate save/commit action is needed. Alternatively use appearance:{action:create|save-as|select|rename|delete,id,label?}, omitting group/variantId/active. create and save-as require a new ID and label. create opens a fresh look with no selected expression/outfit/props and an empty model sheet, preserving the base body, shared variants and other looks. save-as keeps the current combination and captures its front, with other references empty; do this BEFORE editing to preserve the original. Legacy working art is exposed as a real Default Appearance without a write on read; its next edit persists that adoption. select waits for saving and restores that look; failed/conflicted saves block switching. rename changes the label. delete removes that Appearance and its references, keeps shared assets, and opens the first remaining look when deleting the active one. The last Appearance cannot be deleted. Switching or creating an Appearance starts a fresh Appearance undo session, not an undoable navigation step. Captured fronts follow composition edits; other references are retained with needsReview:true. Shared variant art affects all looks using it. selected.props is bottom-to-top activation order; deactivate then reactivate to move a prop to the top. UI and agents share one autosaving command lifecycle. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation in this browser tab; the agent must not repeat that navigation. Observe the resulting page after rendering, then call inspect_workspace again for fresh context. A successful tool result is not proof of visual correctness.

tools.name: set_character_variant_transform
tools.description: Visually align an existing expression whole head, outfit, or prop by changing only its full-canvas translation and uniform scale. Inspect the Character in the browser first; x moves right, y moves down, and values are absolute rather than deltas. Use the exact revision from inspect_character_contract. Success opens the exact variant; follow alignment.visualReview.checks using the browser buttons Composite, Overlay, Difference, and Align, then return to Composite. Repeat after every correction before continuing. Head-anchor changes rebase current expressions; front and back prop layers share one transform. The canonical body is locked. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation in this browser tab; the agent must not repeat that navigation. Observe the resulting page after rendering, then call inspect_workspace again for fresh context. A successful tool result is not proof of visual correctness.

tools.name: undo_character_change
tools.description: Undo the latest Appearance edit in the current session. Character profile and shared height are preserved. Switching Appearance or save-as starts a fresh undo session; navigation itself is not undoable. Shared variant art retains its shared scope. Requires the exact saved Character revision and a settled (saved) session; inactive, pending, failed, conflicted, stale, or empty-history requests return a structured status without mutation or navigation. Success persists the restored Appearance as a new Character revision and opens that Character editor. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation in this browser tab; the agent must not repeat that navigation. Observe the resulting page after rendering, then call inspect_workspace again for fresh context. A successful tool result is not proof of visual correctness.

tools.name: update_character_model_sheet
tools.description: Edit the active Appearance’s model sheet after inspect_character_contract with scope:model-sheet. References belong to modelSheet.appearanceId; switch saved sets through set_character_variant_selection, then re-inspect. Composition edits autosave into the current Appearance and synchronize linked front images. Other references may have needsReview:true; visually compare against the updated Appearance, then replace them or set needsReview:false. This is a consistency flag, not user approval. Optional shared height is edited through update_character_profile. Use referenceId for one image: front/three-quarter/side/back are the default turnaround slots; other IDs create supplemental references with label and kind. view is a compatibility alias for a default slot. Optional viewpoint and pose describe that reference. PNGs may be opaque and keep original dimensions up to 4096 × 4096 / 5 MiB. For replacement supply dataUrl, filename and exact expectedAssetSha256 (null for empty). Alternatively fromAppearance:true captures the current composition into front with its source hash; do not supply dataUrl or filename. sourceSha256 identifies the source image used for generated art. remove:true deletes only this reference and requires its exact hash. All edits use expectedRevision. Replacement clears old guides and source hash unless a new source is supplied. Notes and guides need existing art; guides are original-image y fractions with head above feet, excluding hats, raised arms and props. Never infer height from pixels; null clears guides. Omitted fields remain unchanged. accepted:true means stored, not visually verified or user-approved. Follow visualReview on the exact reference. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation in this browser tab; the agent must not repeat that navigation. Observe the resulting page after rendering, then call inspect_workspace again for fresh context. A successful tool result is not proof of visual correctness.

tools.name: update_character_profile
tools.description: Update one or more identity fields of a Character using its exact revision. The current unsaved workshop uses characterId new and revision 0; its first edit creates a saved Character and returns its permanent ID. heightCm is an optional shared character height in cm; null clears it. Leave it unset for unknown or variable size. Use this field, not a custom attribute. Omitted fields stay unchanged; empty description, backstory, or attributes clear that field. A successful call saves the profile and opens the Character profile tab with its current Appearance. Profile edits are outside Appearance Undo/Redo. Finish local unsaved input first. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation in this browser tab; the agent must not repeat that navigation. Observe the resulting page after rendering, then call inspect_workspace again for fresh context. A successful tool result is not proof of visual correctness.

tools.name: update_library
tools.description: Create, update, duplicate, delete, or move AOZU library records with one revision-checked command. Resources: collection; character (move between collections or delete); album; photo; location; condition; reference (explicitly reuse a finished Album photo as Location inspiration/design); story-book; storyboard-book. Duplicate is supported for Locations and Conditions and preserves their setting images with new IDs. Use IDs and expectedRevision from inspect_workspace. Omitted update fields stay unchanged. Moving a Photo requires id and albumId and routes to the Photo in its destination Album. Deleting an Album moves its photos to My images; deleting a Location moves its children to its parent; deleting a Story Book leaves its storyboards unfiled. This does not edit storyboard frames or character artwork. AOZU itself handles effects.navigation.

tools.name: update_storyboard
tools.description: Create a standalone board or mutate it using its exact expectedRevision. Actions: rename (name/notes), add-frame (title/notes), edit-frame (frameId/title/notes/review/transition/duration), remove-frame, reorder (all frame IDs exactly once), add-candidate (frameId/filename/PNG dataUrl/source/settings), select (frameId/imageId), reference (frameId/imageId/purpose or remove:true), undo, redo. Undefined subjects in candidates may be invented freely. Every defined AOZU Character, Location, Condition or Album Photo used in a candidate must be included in settings. Character settings require the exact Appearance sha256 from inspect_character_contract with scope:model-sheet and images:[appearance]; world settings use the revision from inspect_workspace. Missing or stale refs are rejected. Uploaded candidates NEVER automatically replace selections. Confirmed review requires explicit human approval, never merely successful upload. Reference pins exact image ID/hash; changes to source selection do not rewrite it. Same operations and persisted undo/redo as UI. PNG originals up to 4096×4096 and 5 MiB, at most 100 frames/500 images/128 MiB per board. Source text is provenance only. Returns navigation to affected board for visual review. No same-collection requirement. pin-setting stores the same setting snapshot (id, kind character/location/photo, sourceId, revision, name, details, optional sha256) on frameId, optionally with PNG dataUrl/filename/source/purpose; it never selects or approves an image. unpin-setting removes a snapshot by imageId. inspect_workspace exposes current location and album metadata; local location settings take precedence over ancestor context.

sites.name: benchmarks.affogata.net
sites.description: 79 games and apps across 8 industries scored 0-10 on customer voice, per release — and exposed to AI agents as WebMCP tools.

tools.name: benchmarks_list_categories
tools.description: List every benchmark category with its industry, title count, average customer-voice score and current leader. Start here when you do not yet know which category a brand belongs to.

industry.description: Optional industry filter, e.g. 'Gaming', 'Fintech', 'Travel & Mobility'. Omit for every category.

tools.name: benchmarks_list_titles
tools.description: List benchmarked games and apps with their current score, the change on their latest scored point (a release or a week, per the title cadence) and their week-over-week move. Filter by category, industry, free text or minimum score, sort by score, delta, momentum or volatility, and set the direction.

category.description: Category id or name, e.g. 'trading-apps' or 'Match-3 & Puzzle'.

search.description: Free text over title name, publisher and topic clusters.

min_score.description: Only titles scoring at least this (0-10).

sort.description: score = current impact, delta = change on the latest release or week, momentum = size of the weekly move, volatility = spread across the tracked window.

order.description: asc = lowest first, which is how you ask for the worst scores. Defaults to highest first for every sort key except name and category.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return.

tools.name: benchmarks_get_title
tools.description: Full customer-voice profile for one game or app: current score, release history, the topic clusters pushing it up and down, the Affogata insight, movement against its category, and store-review volume where a live pull exists.

title.description: Title id or name, e.g. 'revolut' or 'Royal Match'.

tools.name: benchmarks_find_by_topic
tools.description: Search the topic clusters across every benchmarked title to find who is being praised or punished for a given theme - 'paywall', 'support', 'ads', 'bugs', 'pay to win'. This is the cross-category view a per-brand lookup cannot give you.

topic.description: Theme to search for, e.g. 'support', 'paywall', 'ads', 'odds'.

side.description: gaining = praised for it, slipping = punished for it.

limit.description: Maximum rows.

tools.name: benchmarks_get_overview
tools.description: Headline state of the whole benchmark: how many titles are strong, mixed or critical this week, the happiest and unhappiest customer bases, the biggest weekly mover, and the topics rising and falling across the whole corpus.

tools.name: benchmarks_get_category_analytics
tools.description: Deep read on one category: average and median score, spread, leader and laggard, the strong/mixed/critical split, this week's gainers and droppers, and the topic clusters most often lifting or dragging titles in that category.

category.description: Category id or name, e.g. 'dating-apps' or 'Social Casino'.

tools.name: benchmarks_get_movers
tools.description: Rank titles by week-over-week movement to find what changed since the last report - the fastest way to spot a release that just went wrong or a fix that landed.

category.description: Optional category id or name to scope the ranking.

limit.description: How many rows.

tools.name: benchmarks_compare_titles
tools.description: Compare 2 to 5 titles side by side across score, release delta, weekly movement, category position, store rating and volatility, plus the topic clusters they share and the ones unique to each. Works across categories.

titles.description: Two to five title ids or names, e.g. ['tinder', 'hinge', 'bumble'].

tools.name: benchmarks_export_dataset
tools.description: Return the raw benchmark rows as structured JSON so you can run your own analysis - correlations, cohort comparisons, charts, or a written report. Filter by category or industry to keep the payload small.

category.description: Optional category id or name.

limit.description: Maximum rows. Omit for the whole corpus.

include_history.description: Include the three-point release/week history for each title.

tools.name: benchmarks_explain_methodology
tools.description: Explain what the score means, where the data comes from, what the score bands are, and what its limits are. Call this before presenting any number to a user so the framing is accurate.

tools.name: benchmarks_get_current_view
tools.description: Read what the page is showing right now: the route, the active filters, and the exact titles pinned in the comparison. The person at the keyboard drives the same page you do - they can remove a comparison chip, add a title or change a filter at any moment - so call this before answering any question about 'the current view', 'this comparison' or 'what is on screen' instead of trusting what an earlier call set up.

tools.name: benchmarks_open_category
tools.description: Switch the page to a benchmark category and show its titles. Use this whenever the user asks to see, open or switch to a category - the browser view follows along instead of the answer living only in chat.

category.description: Category id or name, e.g. 'travel-apps', 'Social Casino', 'Education'.

tools.name: benchmarks_open_title
tools.description: Open the detail page for one game or app, showing its score history, topic clusters and movement. Use it to put a specific brand in front of the user after you have talked about it.

title.description: Title id or name, e.g. 'duolingo' or 'Genshin Impact'.

tools.name: benchmarks_set_view
tools.description: Change what the browsing page shows: free-text search, a topic filter, an industry, a minimum score, the sort order, and grid or table layout. This is the agent equivalent of the on-page controls, so the user ends up looking at exactly the slice you are describing.

search.description: Free text over name, publisher and topic clusters. Pass '' to clear.

topic.description: Only titles whose clusters mention this topic, e.g. 'ads'. Pass '' to clear.

industry.description: Industry name, e.g. 'Gaming'. Pass '' to clear.

min_score.description: Hide titles scoring below this. Pass 0 to clear the threshold - no title scores below 0, so 0 and 'no threshold' are the same filter, and this is how you drop it without resetting everything else.

sort.description: Sort key for the list.

order.description: Sort direction.

mode.description: Card grid or dense table.

tools.name: benchmarks_compare_in_ui
tools.description: Put titles side by side on the comparison page so the user can see the difference rather than read it. The default mode replaces the whole selection, which is right for 'compare X and Y' and wrong for 'add a competitor' - use mode 'add' to put titles alongside the ones already on screen, and mode 'remove' to drop titles and keep the rest. Pair this with benchmarks_compare_titles when you want both the numbers and the visual.

titles.description: Title ids or names. At least two when replacing, since a comparison needs two; one is enough to add or remove.

mode.description: replace (default): these titles become the whole comparison. add: keep what is on screen and add these. remove: drop these and keep the rest.

tools.name: benchmarks_reset_view
tools.description: Clear every filter, comparison and highlight and return the page to the full benchmark overview. Use it when the user says 'start over' or 'show everything again'.

sites.name: cadence-webmcp.ashrafahmed1232.workers.dev
sites.description: An agent-native issue tracker built on WebMCP. Triage, dedupe, and re-prioritize with an agent that has real, scoped, dynamic tools, not screen-scraped buttons.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List issues, optionally filtered by status, assignee, priority, labels, or cycle.

tools.name: execute_typescript
tools.description: Execute TypeScript in an isolated QuickJS sandbox to edit Creator. First use discover_tools for typed external_ functions. Await every external_* call; calls are serialized. Return a JSON-serializable value; console.log captures text. No DOM, storage, network, imports, or persistent globals are available. Each run has a 30-second limit and 32 MB heap. At most two runs can execute at once per editor; additional runs fail immediately as busy and can be retried after an active run finishes. Edits already applied remain if a later call fails or execution is cancelled; read_scene to verify the result.

tools.name: read_scene
tools.description: Read the current Creator scene. Returns scene dimensions, framerate, duration, all layers, current selection, render order, visual bounds, scene-center deltas, and clipping/off-canvas flags. Call this once at the start of most turns to understand what's on the canvas. Use each layer's `ordering` and `layout` blocks to avoid wrong-layer, wrong-stack, and off-canvas mistakes. A layer may also carry an `occlusion` block (`likely_hidden: true`, `occluded_by: [ids]`) when an opaque layer in front of it covers it — treat that layer as INVISIBLE on the canvas (e.g. a label buried behind a button fill); reorder it above the cover with `reorder_layer` before reporting done. No input required — always reads the active scene.

tools.name: measure_text_units
tools.description: Return per-line, per-word, and per-character bounds for an existing text layer. Uses the same canvas.measureText pipeline that powers `read_scene`'s `measured_bounds`, but exposes the cumulative pen position per glyph so per-character recipes can place each new layer at the source's exact kerning — no `bounds.width / char_count` approximation. When to call (REQUIRED before splitting): - Any per-character recipe (typewriter, per-character-rise, bottom-up-letters, top-down-letters, kinetic-center-build, short-slide-*). - Any per-word recipe where each word needs its own layer (per-word-crossfade, spring-scale-in) so the rebuilt phrase reads as one centered unit. - Layout-aware effects that need exact word widths (short-slide-down, short-slide-right, kinetic-center-build). When NOT to call: - Whole-layer recipes (micro-scale-fade, fade-through, scale-down-fade, mask-reveal-up) — those animate one layer; `read_scene`'s `visual_bounds` is enough. - Layers that aren't text — call returns an error. Returns (positions match `read_scene`'s coordinate system): - `local_bounds` / `world_bounds` for the whole layer (matches `text_style.measured_bounds` and `layout.visual_bounds` from `read_scene`). - `font`: `{ name, size, tracking, line_height, alignment }` — pass these to `create_text` per character/word/line to preserve the source typeface. - `lines[]`: one entry per `\n`-separated line. Each line carries `text`, `local_bounds`, `world_bounds`, and optionally `words[]` / `characters[]` depending on `granularity`. - `characters[i].local_bounds.x + width/2` is the visual CENTER of glyph i; use that as the `position.x` for the per-character layer. - `characters[i].advance_x_local` is the pen position AFTER glyph i (left edge of glyph i+1 with tracking applied). Sum across glyphs and you reproduce the line width. Granularity: - `line` — only line bounds. Cheapest. Use for per-line recipes. - `word` — adds word bounds inside each line. Use for per-word recipes. - `character` — a…

layer_id.description: Text layer id from `read_scene`. Pass the source phrase's layer id before splitting it.

granularity.description: Which units to return. Default 'all' (words + characters per line). Use 'character' for per-character recipes, 'word' for per-word, 'line' for per-line.

tools.name: list_fonts
tools.description: List font families available in the active project — Creator's curated presets, Google Fonts, OS-installed local fonts (when permission has been granted), and project-uploaded font assets. Use this when the user names a specific font you're not sure is loaded ('animate "Acme" in Bebas Neue letter-by-letter'), or when you need to recommend a fallback that's actually present. When to call: - User names a font you're not certain exists in this project (brand fonts, niche typefaces). - You're about to call `create_text` / `set_text_style` with a specific `font_name` and want to verify the family + style are loaded. - You're deciding between multiple style options for the same family. When NOT to call: - The user didn't specify a font — `create_text` uses the project default. Calling this would just burn a turn. - You already called it earlier in the conversation. Returns `{ families: [{ family, styles, default_style, source }] }`. `source` is one of `'PRESET' | 'GOOGLE_FONT' | 'LOCAL' | 'ASSET'`. If the requested family isn't in the list, fall back to a similar style + tell the user (e.g. 'Bebas Neue isn't loaded; I used Anton, the closest condensed sans available'). Pass `source` to filter to one category. Note: the catalog is a snapshot of what's currently loaded. Local OS fonts only appear after the user grants the browser's `local-fonts` permission, which Creator does not prompt for automatically.

source.description: Filter the result to one font origin. 'all' (default) returns every loaded family.

tools.name: list_layer_effects
tools.description: Return the effects currently attached to a layer, with their ids, types, and enabled state. Call this before stacking another effect, before removing one, or whenever you need to know what's already there.

tools.name: list_themes
tools.description: List the themes embedded in this file. Themes group design-token slots (brand colors, named text strings, etc.). The Default theme is always present; users can add named alternates (e.g. 'Dark', 'Holiday'). Returns `{ themes: [{ id, slot_count, is_active }] }`. Call before `list_slots` if the user references a specific theme by name, or to confirm that any tokens exist before suggesting slot-based edits.

tools.name: list_slots
tools.description: List design-token slots defined in the file. Each slot has ONE stable id (e.g. 'brand-red') but can supply different VALUES per theme — Default theme might have brand-red as crimson, a Dark theme might have it as burgundy. The toolkit renders whichever value the currently active theme provides. Use before inventing hardcoded values whenever the user names a brand concept ('brand red', 'primary blue', 'the header color', 'our headline text'). Filter with `type` to narrow (e.g. COLOR for fill/stroke pickers, TEXT for headline strings). Returns `{ slots: [{ id, type, values_by_theme: { themeId: value, ... }, active_theme, active_value }] }`. Without `theme_id`, `active_value` is what the canvas renders right now. With a `theme_id` filter for an inactive theme, `active_value` may be that filtered theme's fallback value for inspection, while `active_theme` still names the canvas-rendered theme. The `values_by_theme` map shows variants if the user wants to recolor a specific theme. Empty `slots` means the file has no tokens of that type — fall back to inline values and say so.

type.description: Optional slot type filter. Omit to list every slot across every theme.

theme_id.description: Optional theme id to scope the list. Omit to list slots from all themes. Defaults to no filter; use 'Default' for the always-present built-in theme.

tools.name: list_motion_system_items
tools.description: Read the user's Motion System library — a separate design library from the file's theme slots. Returns colors / gradients / fonts / easings / durations / motion presets that the user has saved (typically synced from Workflow). Use this when the user names a brand value (e.g. 'brand red', 'standard ease-out', 'fast duration') and `list_slots` did NOT find a match — motion system is the fallback library. The values are returned for inline use (set_fill with the rgb you found, apply_keyframes with the control_points you found, etc.) — they are NOT linked tokens. For multi-property motion presets, use `apply_motion_preset` instead of trying to reconstruct the keyframes. **Hierarchy:** theme slots beat motion-system entries. Always `list_slots` first; only fall through to `list_motion_system_items` on a miss. **Colors vs gradients — same UI section, two enum values.** The Motion System UI shows solid colors AND gradients together under one 'Brand Colors' tab, so a name the user thinks is a 'color' may actually be a gradient (e.g. a logo gradient saved as `clogo`). When the user names a color and `type: 'colors'` returns no match, ALWAYS try `type: 'gradients'` before giving up. Only declare 'not found' after BOTH lookups miss. Returns `{ items: [...] }` typed per family (see schemas below). Pass no `type` to get a summary across all families. Order of `animated_properties` on motion-preset items is not guaranteed; treat as a set.

type.description: Which asset family to read. Omit to get a `{ count, ids }` summary across all families. 'colors' returns solid colors only; 'gradients' returns linear/radial gradients (motion-system stores both under one section internally — this tool splits them).

tools.name: list_segments
tools.description: List the named animation segments (markers) on the active scene. Each segment is a name + a frame range (start_frame, end_frame). Segments are used by Lottie players to loop / play named ranges and by dotLottie state machines as playback targets. Returns `{ segments: [{ id, name, start_frame, end_frame, duration_frames }] }`. Empty array means the scene has no segments yet. Call before `add_segment` if you need to check for duplicate names, before `add_state` on a state machine that targets a segment, or whenever the user asks 'what segments / loops / chapters does this animation have?'.

tools.name: list_state_machines
tools.description: List the interactivity state machines defined in this file. Each one is `{ id, name, state_count, transition_count, is_active }`. Returns the active state machine id separately as `active_state_machine_id`. State machines are runtime configurations — Lottie players use them to switch playback based on events (click, hover, completion). Most files have 0 or 1 machine.

tools.name: list_states
tools.description: List the states in the active state machine. Each is `{ id, name, type, segment, autoplay, loop, mode, is_initial, transitions: [{ id, to_state_id, trigger?, type }] }`. Returns `state_machine_id` and `initial_state_id` at the top level for convenience. Empty array means the active machine has no states yet.

tools.name: list_interactions
tools.description: List the interactions defined on the active state machine. Interactions BIND runtime pointer / state events to actions — usually a `Fire` action that emits a named event a transition listens for. **Without an interaction, transition `trigger_event` guards never fire.** If you added an `add_transition({ trigger_event: 'click' })`, you must also `add_pointer_interaction({ pointer_event: 'Click', fire_event: 'click' })` for the click to do anything at runtime. Returns `{ interactions: [{ id, type, layer_name, state_name, actions, fires_event }] }`. `type` is the pointer event name (Click / PointerEnter / …) for pointer interactions OR `OnComplete` / `OnLoopComplete` for state-event interactions. `layer_name` is set for pointer interactions; `state_name` is set for state-event interactions. `actions[]` is the full action list in the agent-facing shape (snake_case + natural value types). `fires_event` is a legacy convenience: it's the input_name of the first `Fire` action when present, otherwise `null` — inspect `actions[]` for everything else.

tools.name: list_inputs
tools.description: List the typed inputs (variables) on the active state machine. Inputs are how state machines store runtime values — booleans for toggle state, numerics for progress / counters, strings for labels, and events for one-shot triggers. Inputs feed guards on transitions and actions in interactions. Returns `{ inputs: [{ id, name, type, value? }] }`. The `value` is the initial value at machine start (events don't have one).

tools.name: read_keyframes
tools.description: Read the current keyframes on a layer's keyframe-tool properties. Use this whenever the user asks to TUNE, POLISH, or MODIFY an existing animation ('make the bounce snappier', 'slow down the fade', 'shift this 10 frames later', 'make the rotation smoother') — so you can see what's actually there before changing it, instead of rebuilding from scratch. Without `property`, returns a map of the core properties handled by `apply_keyframes` (`position`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `fill_color`, trim path fields, and `stroke_width`). With `property`, returns just that explicit core or extended property. Extended properties such as masks, shape paths, gradients, text animator fields, and time mapping must be named explicitly; they are not included in the bulk read. For static (non-animated) properties, `is_animated` is false and `static_value` is returned instead of keyframes. **For `position` on a TEXT layer, `static_value` is the RAW transform (baseline / box-origin anchor) — NOT the visual center. To animate a text position relative to its rest (the only safe way), keyframe from THIS `static_value`, not from `visual_center`. For a settle-into-place entrance, prefer `animate_entrance`, which reads this for you.** Easing in returned keyframes comes through as the raw stored shape: `{ type: "LINEAR" }` or `{ type: "CUBIC_BEZIER", x1, y1, x2, y2 }`. (Named presets are expanded at write-time, so reads only see the resolved bezier coefficients.)

property.description: Optional — restrict to one core or extended keyframe-tool property. Omit to read all core keyframe-tool properties on the layer.

tools.name: list_scenes
tools.description: List every scene in the current project plus which one is active. Cheap read. Use when the user refers to scenes by name ('switch to the outro', 'work on the vertical') so you can find the right `scene_id`, or when deciding whether to create a new scene vs. switch to an existing one. Returns active scene id, and for each scene: id, name, size, framerate, duration, layer_count, and is_nestable (whether the scene can be used as a source for a nested scene layer).

sites.name: getfitcraft.com
sites.description: A gamified AI fitness app built by exercise scientists to solve the #1 fitness problem: quitting. Streaks, quests, and an AI coach make showing up easier.

tools.name: find_fitcraft_calculator
tools.description: Recommend the best FitCraft calculator for a user goal such as protein, calories, macros, body fat, BMI, strength, daily water intake (hydration), FFMI and lean body mass, or weight loss percentage.

goal.description: The user goal or metric they want to calculate. ffmi covers fat-free mass index and lean body mass; water_intake covers hydration and how much water to drink a day; weight_loss_percentage covers the percent of body weight lost and weight-loss milestones, while calories covers a calorie target for losing weight.

tools.name: generate_workout_plan
tools.description: Generate a complete weekly resistance training plan (split, exercises, sets, reps, rest, effort target, and progression rule) from goal, experience, training days, equipment, session length, and optional extra gear (pull-up bar, rings or low bar, bench, resistance band). An exercise that needs gear the user does not have is swapped for a no-gear alternative, and each exercise lists the extra gear it uses. Deterministic rule engine that mirrors the FitCraft Free AI Workout Plan Generator page. Also returns a shareUrl that opens the same plan on that page.

goal.description: Training goal: muscle (build muscle), weight (lose weight), consistent (build the habit on a minimum effective dose).

experience.description: Training experience: beginner (under 6 months), intermediate (6 months to 2 years), advanced (2 years or more).

days_per_week.description: Resistance training days per week, 2 to 5.

equipment.description: Available equipment: none (no equipment, bodyweight only), dumbbells, or gym (full gym).

session_length.description: Available session time: short (10 to 20 minutes), medium (20 to 30 minutes), long (30 to 45 minutes).

extras.description: Optional extra gear the user also has, for equipment none or dumbbells (ignored for gym, which has all of it): bar (overhead pull-up bar, for chin-ups and chin-up negatives), rings (rings, suspension straps, a low bar, or a sturdy table to row under, for inverted rows), bench (Bulgarian split squats, bench dips, supported rows, pullovers), band (resistance band, for pull-aparts and pulldowns from a door anchor). Omit or leave empty when the user has none of these.

tools.name: calculate_protein_target
tools.description: Calculate an evidence-based daily protein target using FitCraft ranges for healthy adults.

goal.description: Training or nutrition goal.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage for fat-loss estimates.

tools.name: calculate_tdee
tools.description: Calculate basal metabolic rate and total daily energy expenditure using FitCraft calculator logic.

sex.description: Biological sex used by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage for Katch-McArdle BMR.

tools.name: calculate_bmr
tools.description: Estimate basal metabolic rate from three published equations at once: Mifflin-St Jeor 1990 (recommended default), the revised Harris-Benedict of Roza and Shizgal 1984, and the Katch-McArdle lean-mass equation published by Cunningham 1991, which is used when a body fat percentage is supplied. Returns the recommended estimate with its plus or minus 10 percent accuracy band, all three equation outputs, and the population caveats. Mirrors the FitCraft BMR Calculator page.

sex.description: Biological sex; selects the sex-specific constants in the two age-based equations.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage. Supplying it switches the recommendation to the Katch-McArdle lean-mass equation.

tools.name: calculate_macros
tools.description: Calculate daily calorie, protein, fat, and carbohydrate targets in one of five explicit goal modes: aggressive-cut (22.5 percent deficit), moderate-cut (15 percent), maintain, lean-bulk (7.5 percent surplus), or standard-bulk (15 percent). Also returns the projected weekly weight change as a percent of body weight. Deterministic and local-only; mirrors the FitCraft macro calculator page.

goal.description: Goal mode. aggressive-cut = 22.5 percent below maintenance with a 1.8 g/kg protein floor; moderate-cut = 15 percent below; maintain = no change; lean-bulk = 7.5 percent above; standard-bulk = 15 percent above. The legacy values cut, maintenance and bulk map to moderate-cut, maintain and standard-bulk.

calories.description: Optional maintenance calories. If omitted, maintenance is estimated from the sex/age/height/activity fields.

sex.description: Sex, used by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation when maintenance calories are not supplied.

age.description: Age in years. Required when maintenance calories are not supplied; also drives the PROT-AGE 1.6 g/kg protein floor at 65 and older.

height.description: Height. Required when maintenance calories are not supplied.

activity_level.description: Daily activity level used to turn BMR into maintenance calories. Defaults to moderate.

training.description: Resistance-training experience, which sets the protein base before the goal mode shifts it. Defaults to intermediate. The legacy values recreational and serious map to intermediate and advanced.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage; switches maintenance estimation to Katch-McArdle.

tools.name: calculate_bmi_and_wthr
tools.description: Calculate BMI and optionally waist-to-height ratio using FitCraft health-screening logic.

tools.name: calculate_body_fat
tools.description: Estimate body-fat percentage with the US Navy circumference method (default), or from caliper skinfolds with the Jackson-Pollock 3-site or 7-site equations.

sex.description: Biological sex; selects the sex-specific equation.

method.description: navy (default) uses height, neck, waist and, for women, hip circumferences. jackson_pollock_3 uses age plus chest, abdomen, thigh (men) or triceps, suprailiac, thigh (women) skinfolds in mm. jackson_pollock_7 uses age plus all seven skinfolds in mm.

unit.description: Navy method only: unit for height and all circumferences. Defaults to in.

hip.description: Navy method: hip circumference, required for female estimates.

chest.description: Skinfold in mm: diagonal fold between nipple and front of armpit.

midaxillary.description: Skinfold in mm (7-site): vertical fold on the side of the torso at the level of the bottom of the sternum.

triceps.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold on the back of the upper arm, midway between shoulder and elbow.

subscapular.description: Skinfold in mm (7-site): diagonal fold just below the lower tip of the shoulder blade.

abdomen.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold 2 cm to the right of the navel.

suprailiac.description: Skinfold in mm: diagonal fold just above the front of the iliac crest.

thigh.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold on the front of the thigh, midway between hip and knee.

tools.name: calculate_ffmi
tools.description: Calculate fat-free mass index (FFMI), height-normalized FFMI, lean body mass and fat mass from height, weight and sex, with an optional body fat percentage. With body fat, fat-free mass is weight x (1 - body fat); without it, lean body mass is estimated with the Boer 1984 formula. Returns a sourced category band (Schutz et al. 2002 population medians, ESPEN low cutoffs, college-athlete norms, and the 25.0 value Kouri et al. 1995 observed in steroid-free athletes, presented as an observation rather than a hard ceiling). Mirrors the FitCraft FFMI Calculator page.

sex.description: Sex; selects the Boer formula coefficients and the reference bands.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body fat percentage. Supplying it switches from the Boer estimate to a direct fat-free mass calculation.

tools.name: calculate_one_rep_max
tools.description: Estimate one-rep max and training loads from lifted weight and reps.

rpe.description: Optional RPE from 6 to 10. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: calculate_heart_rate_zones
tools.description: Estimate maximum heart rate from age by Tanaka 2001, Fox 1971 (220 minus age), Nes 2013, and Gulati 2010, then the five training zones by percent of max and by the Karvonen heart rate reserve method.

formula.description: Max HR formula used for the zones: tanaka (default, recommended), gulati (women), nes (active adults), legacy (Fox 1971, 220 minus age, unvalidated). Every formula is returned in max_heart_rate.byFormula regardless of this choice.

resting_heart_rate.description: Optional resting heart rate in bpm. Unlocks Karvonen heart rate reserve zones.

measured_max_hr.description: Optional measured or watch-learned max HR in bpm. Overrides the age formula and feeds the zones directly.

tools.name: assess_body_recomposition
tools.description: Assess whether body recomposition (losing fat and gaining muscle at the same time) fits a person, and return their maintenance calories, recomposition calorie target, daily protein target, lifting frequency, and an expected timeline.

sex.description: Biological sex; used by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation and the body-fat bands.

activity_level.description: Daily activity level. Defaults to moderate.

training_status.description: Resistance training experience. new covers never trained or returning after a long break. Defaults to under_1_year.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage. When supplied, protein is set from fat-free mass and the recomposition verdict uses measured body fat instead of a BMI estimate.

tools.name: calculate_calories_burned
tools.description: Estimate calories burned for a workout from activity, intensity, duration and body weight. Covers walking, treadmill, running, a steps-to-calories mode, cycling, swimming, hiking, stair climbing, jump rope, bodyweight and HIIT circuits, strength training, and yoga or Pilates. Returns gross calories, calories above resting, calories per minute and the MET value, with the 2024 Adult Compendium code behind it.

activity.description: Activity performed. walking, treadmill and running take speed_mph and incline_percent. steps takes steps and cadence_steps_per_min. Everything else takes effort.

speed_mph.description: walking, treadmill and running only: pace in miles per hour. Snapped to the nearest Compendium code for the compendium method; used exactly by the ACSM equations.

incline_percent.description: walking, treadmill and running only: percent grade. Defaults to 0.

effort.description: Effort-based activities only (cycling, swimming, hiking, stair_climbing, jump_rope, bodyweight_hiit, strength_training, yoga_pilates). Defaults to moderate.

steps.description: steps activity only: total step count.

cadence_steps_per_min.description: steps activity only: walking cadence in steps per minute. Snapped to the nearest CADENCE-Adults threshold of 80, 100, 110, 120 or 130. Defaults to 100.

duration_minutes.description: Minutes of actual movement. Required for every activity except steps, where it is derived from the step count and cadence.

method.description: Pace-based activities only: compendium (default) uses 2024 Adult Compendium MET codes, acsm uses the ACSM walking and running metabolic equations.

tools.name: calculate_steps_to_distance
tools.description: Convert a step count into miles and kilometers using a step length estimated from standing height and sex, with separate walking and running step lengths, an optional measured step-length override, and an optional calorie estimate.

height_unit.description: Unit for height. Defaults to in.

sex.description: Sets the step-length coefficient: 0.415 x height for male, 0.413 for female.

mode.description: Walking or running. Running steps are much longer. Defaults to walk.

pace.description: Pace. Walking: casual (2.5 mph), average (3.0 mph, default), brisk (3.5 mph), very_brisk (4.0 mph). Running: easy_jog (5.0 mph), steady (6.2 mph, default), fast (7.0 mph).

weight.description: Optional body weight. Supplying it adds a calorie estimate.

weight_unit.description: Unit for weight. Defaults to kg.

step_length.description: Optional measured step length. Overrides the height-based estimate.

step_length_unit.description: Unit for the measured step length. Defaults to in.

tools.name: calculate_water_intake
tools.description: Estimate how much water to drink per day from sex, body weight, daily exercise minutes and climate. The starting range runs from the EFSA 2010 to the IOM 2005 Adequate Intake for total water, adjusted for body weight, temperature, humidity and altitude with the water-turnover equation of Yamada et al. 2022, plus a sweat-based exercise add-on. Returns a drinks target and range, total water including food, water from food, the exercise add-on and cups, in mL, liters and US fluid ounces.

sex.description: Sex; selects the IOM and EFSA Adequate Intakes (women 2.0 to 2.7 L, men 2.5 to 3.7 L of total water a day) and the reference weight.

exercise_minutes.description: Minutes of sweaty exercise on a typical day, 0 to 480. Defaults to 0.

climate.description: Where the person spends most of the day: temperate (about 20 C / 68 F, or air-conditioned indoors, default), warm (about 27 C / 80 F), hot (about 32 C / 90 F), hot_humid (32 C at 80 percent humidity) or altitude (about 2,000 m / 6,500 ft).

tools.name: calculate_weight_loss_percentage
tools.description: Calculate the percent of starting body weight lost, the amount lost, which clinical milestone that reaches (3 to 5% where benefits begin, 5% clinically meaningful, then 10, 15 and 20%), the weight at the next milestone, optional progress toward a goal weight, and an optional average weekly pace as a percent of body weight judged against the 0.5 to 1% per week band. Includes STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1 trial benchmarks. Mirrors the FitCraft Weight Loss Percentage Calculator page. Never returns dosing advice.

starting_weight.description: Weight at the start, in weight_unit. 70 to 700 lb or 32 to 318 kg.

goal_weight.description: Optional goal weight in weight_unit. Must be below starting_weight. Adds progress toward the goal.

weeks_elapsed.description: Optional weeks since starting_weight was recorded, 1 to 520. Adds the average weekly pace.

sites.name: gyfts.io
sites.description: A trusted home for Metaphysical, Alternative, Complementary, and Holistic practice, curated, explained, and connected to practitioners seekers trust.

tools.name: start_here
tools.description: Best first call when a person describes what they are looking for in their own words, e.g. "trouble sleeping, interested in acupuncture in Dublin". Returns JSON {path, practitioners_for?: {name, url}, topics: [{type, name, url}], practitioners: [{name, url, where?, verified?}], events: [{name, url}], next_steps: [string], note}. If the words suggest a crisis it returns {crisis: true, emergency, lines, ...} instead: show that to the person first. Matching pages are not a diagnosis. Read-only.

need.description: What the person is looking for, in their words.

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. IE or US.

site.description: The Gyfts site origin; result urls are paths on it.

path.description: The suggested route.

practitioners_for.description: The practice the practitioners below were found for.

topics.description: Up to 3 topic pages that match the words (conditions, symptoms, practices…). Not a diagnosis.

practitioners.description: Up to 3 practitioners who list that practice, then any whose name matched. Not a recommendation.

next_steps.description: Suggested next tool calls, in order.

truncated.description: Lists were shortened to fit the size budget.

crisis.description: Present and true when crisis language was detected; then only helplines are returned.

message.description: Crisis only: what to tell the person.

country.description: Crisis only: the country the helplines are for.

emergency.description: Crisis only: the emergency number to call.

elsewhere.description: Crisis only: what to do in any other country.

note.description: Always present: these are directory listings, not medical advice.

error.description: Present when the request could not be answered; says what to try instead.

tools.name: get_crisis_resources
tools.description: Emergency number and free crisis helplines for a country. Use at once if the person mentions suicide, self-harm, or not being safe, or if any tool returns crisis: true. Returns JSON {crisis: true, message, country?, emergency, lines: [{name, contact, hours?}], elsewhere: {emergency, find_a_helpline}, note}.

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. IE, GB or US. Default: where the person is browsing from.

message.description: What to tell the person, first.

country.description: The country the helplines are for; absent when only the worldwide fallback applies.

emergency.description: The emergency number to call when someone is in immediate danger.

lines.description: Free, confidential helplines in that country.

elsewhere.description: What to do in any other country, including a worldwide helpline finder.

note.description: Not medical advice; in an emergency contact emergency services.

tools.name: about_gyfts
tools.description: How Gyfts works: what it is, booking and payment, cancellations and refunds, what Verified means, safety, and how to get in touch. Returns JSON {result: {topic, answer, read_more: [path]}, other_topics?}. Without a topic it answers what_is_gyfts and lists the others.

read_more.description: Gyfts paths with the full text; open with open_page.

result.description: The answer for the topic asked (what_is_gyfts when none).

other_topics.description: Present when no topic was asked: the other topics you can ask for.

tools.name: search_gyfts

Returns JSON {results: [{type, name, detail?, url}], page, next_page?, note}, 6 per page. For details of one result call get_topic, get_practitioner or get_offering. To find practitioners who offer a practice (e.g. reiki), use find_practitioners. Directory information only, not medical advice.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "reiki", "anxiety", or a practitioner name.

type.description: Only return results of this type. "modality" is a practice; "pathway" is a journey.

page.description: Page of results, from 1. Use next_page from the previous answer.

site.description: The Gyfts site origin; result urls are paths on it.

page.description: This page number (1-based).

next_page.description: Present when more results exist: call again with page = next_page.

truncated.description: Results were cut to fit the size budget.

note.description: Always present: these are directory listings, not medical advice.

error.description: Present when the request could not be answered; says what to try instead.

Returns JSON {result: {practitioner, url, service?, from, to, times_are: "UTC", open_windows: [{start, end}], book_url, how_to_book}, note}. To book, call open_booking; the person picks the time and pays.

slug.description: The practitioner: the last part of its Gyfts URL.

service.description: A service id from get_practitioner.

from.description: First day to check (YYYY-MM-DD). Default today.

days.description: How many days to check. Default 7.

site.description: The Gyfts site origin; result urls are paths on it.

result.description: The item, or null when there is no public match (see error).

error.description: Present when the request could not be answered; says what to try instead.

note.description: Always present: these are directory listings, not medical advice.

url.description: The offering url from find_offerings, e.g. /events/sound-bath-dublin.

site.description: The Gyfts site origin; result urls are paths on it.

result.description: The item, or null when there is no public match (see error).

error.description: Present when the request could not be answered; says what to try instead.

note.description: Always present: these are directory listings, not medical advice.

site.description: The Gyfts site origin; result urls are paths on it.

anyOf.description: A get_practitioner, get_organization, get_topic or get_offering result.

tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Navigate this tab to a public Gyfts page, e.g. a url from any other tool. Only Gyfts pages; account, admin, sign-in and booking pages are refused (use open_booking to book). Returns JSON {opened} or {error}.

url.description: A Gyfts path such as /modalities/reiki, or a full gyfts.io URL.

slug.description: The practitioner: the last part of its Gyfts URL.

service.description: A service id from get_practitioner.

opened.description: The Gyfts path (with any query) this tab is now navigating to, e.g. /modalities/reiki.

error.description: Why nothing was opened; the tab stays on the current page.
