tools.name: describe_form
tools.description: Return full details of a single Contact Form 7 or custom form by ID, including all fields, their types, purposes and result signals. Use this when list_cf7_forms or list_custom_forms does not include enough field detail.

id.description: Form ID to look up. For CF7 forms use the numeric ID as a string; for custom forms use the machine name.

type.description: Form type: "cf7" for Contact Form 7 or "custom" for admin-configured custom forms. Defaults to "custom".

tools.name: fill_custom_form_on_page
tools.description: Fill a configured custom form on the current page using CSS selectors defined in WordPress admin. Use this when you have collected all required field values and want to populate the form before the user reviews and submits manually.

form_id.description: Machine name of the custom form to fill. Obtain it from list_page_forms or list_custom_forms.

fields.description: Key-value map of field names to values. Field names are defined in the WordPress admin custom form configuration.

tools.name: get_menu
tools.description: Return navigation menu items by menu location or menu slug. Use this to understand site structure and discover available pages before navigating or searching.

location.description: Registered menu location slug. Omit to return the default menu. Provide only if the user specified a particular location.

menu.description: Menu name or slug. Used as fallback when location is not provided.

tools.name: get_post
tools.description: Return the full Markdown content and metadata of a single WordPress post or page by ID or slug. Use this after search_posts to read a specific item in full.

id.description: Numeric post ID. Takes precedence over slug when both are provided.

slug.description: URL slug of the post or page, e.g. "about-us".

post_type.description: Post type slug used when resolving by slug, e.g. "post" or "page". Defaults to "post".

tools.name: get_site_info
tools.description: Return site name, description, URL, language and available WebMCP endpoints. Use this as the first call to understand what site you are on and which tools and endpoints are available.

tools.name: get_terms
tools.description: Return terms (categories, tags or custom taxonomy entries) from a taxonomy. Use this to discover filtering options before searching posts, or to understand site structure.

taxonomy.description: Taxonomy slug to query, e.g. "category" or "post_tag". Call list_taxonomies first to see valid slugs.

search.description: Optional keyword filter applied to term names.

limit.description: Maximum terms to return (max 50). Include only if the user explicitly requests a specific count; omit otherwise.

tools.name: list_cf7_forms
tools.description: List enabled Contact Form 7 forms with their field schemas, purposes and success/error selectors. Use this before submit_cf7_form to get correct field names and types.

tools.name: list_custom_forms
tools.description: List custom forms configured for browser-agent interaction, including selectors, field names and purposes. Use this before fill_custom_form_on_page or submit_custom_form_on_page.

tools.name: list_page_forms
tools.description: List Contact Form 7 and configured custom forms available on the current page. Use this before fill_custom_form_on_page or submit_custom_form_on_page to discover which forms and field names are available here.

tools.name: list_post_types
tools.description: List the content type slugs published on this site (e.g. post, page, custom types). Use this when asked what kinds of content, post types, or content types are published or available, and before search_posts or get_post to know which type slugs are valid.

tools.name: list_taxonomies
tools.description: List public taxonomies available on the site. Use this before get_terms to discover valid taxonomy slugs.

tools.name: search_media
tools.description: Search public media attachments and return direct URLs, titles, MIME types and alt text. Use this when you need an image URL or to verify available media before referencing it.

query.description: Keywords to search in attachment titles and descriptions. Omit this field to list recent media.

limit.description: Number of attachments to return. Always include this parameter; default to 10 unless the user specifies a different count (max 20).

tools.name: search_posts
tools.description: Search published WordPress posts, pages and configured custom post types and return titles, excerpts and URLs. Use this to find content by keyword before calling get_post for full details.

query.description: Keywords to search in post titles and content. Omit this field to list recent posts.

post_type.description: Post type slug to filter results, e.g. "post" or "page". Omit to search all exposed types.

limit.description: Number of posts to return. Always include this parameter; default to 10 unless the user specifies a different count (max 20).

tools.name: submit_cf7_form
tools.description: Submit a Contact Form 7 form using provided field values. Use this only after list_cf7_forms or describe_form to confirm field names. Requires authenticated REST nonce and triggers a real email send.

form_id.description: Numeric ID of the Contact Form 7 form to submit. Obtain it from list_cf7_forms.

fields.description: Key-value map of field names to values. Field names and types are returned by list_cf7_forms or describe_form.

tools.name: submit_comment
tools.description: Submit a WordPress comment for a published post. Use this only after confirming the post accepts comments and the user has provided their name, email and comment text. Requires authenticated REST nonce.

post_id.description: ID of the post to comment on. The post must have comments open.

author_name.description: Display name of the comment author.

author_email.description: Email address of the comment author.

author_url.description: Optional website URL of the comment author.

comment_content.description: Comment body text. HTML is stripped; plain text only.

tools.name: submit_custom_form_on_page
tools.description: Fill and submit a configured custom form on the current page. Use this only after confirming the user wants to submit - this triggers an actual form send.

form_id.description: Machine name of the custom form to fill and submit. Obtain it from list_page_forms or list_custom_forms.

fields.description: Key-value map of field names to values. All required fields must be provided or the tool will return ok: false without submitting.

sites.name: ippodotea.com
sites.description: We are a family-run Japanese tea company founded in 1717, in the heart of Kyoto. For generations, we have upheld a tradition of aromatic, well-balanced teas.

tools.name: ippodo_recommend_tea
tools.description: Use when a shopper wants Ippodo tea recommendations based on taste, caffeine, brewing style, experience, gift intent, time of day, or tea category rather than a product name. Ranks the live tea-quiz assortment of matcha, gyokuro, sencha, bancha, and teabags, returning in-stock products with match reasons and the cheapest available variant. Prefer this over search_catalog for preference-based discovery such as a first latte, caffeine-free evening tea, or first-time matcha. After the shopper chooses a tea, call get_product for variants, ippodo_get_brewing_guide for preparation, or ippodo_build_tea_setup for utensils, then Shopify update_cart to add items. Leaves the cart unchanged.

category.description: Tea family to keep in the result set. Use "matcha", "gyokuro", "sencha", "bancha", or "teabags" when the shopper named a category. Use "any" when they did not. Matched against product handle, title, and type — not tags or description boilerplate.

occasion.description: When the shopper plans to drink the tea. Evening and after_meal boost lower-caffeine and roasted options; morning and daytime prefer brighter or standard-caffeine teas.

format.description: How the shopper wants to prepare tea. "matcha" keeps powdered teas, "loose_leaf" keeps leaf teas, "teabags" keeps bagged teas, and "any" does not filter by format.

flavor.description: Dominant flavor the shopper asked for. "umami" and "balanced" favor classic matcha and gyokuro; "roasted" and "smoky" favor hojicha and similar; "any" skips flavor ranking.

caffeine.description: Caffeine preference. "none" returns only caffeine-free teas such as mugicha; "low" boosts hojicha, genmaicha, and mugicha; "standard" keeps typical green-tea caffeine; "any" does not filter.

preparation.description: Brewing or serving style. "latte" boosts Ikuyo and similar culinary matcha; "koicha" boosts thicker usucha/koicha grades; "usucha" favors everyday whisking matcha; "cold_brew" and "iced" favor teas that drink well chilled.

experience.description: Shopper familiarity. "first_time" boosts approachable daily teas such as Sayaka and Ikuyo; "experienced" leaves room for richer grades such as Ummon.

gift.description: Set true when the purchase is a gift. Boosts giftable cans, classic matcha, and the Ippodo gift card.

limit.description: Maximum number of teas to return. Defaults to 3. Use 5 only when the shopper wants a wider shortlist.

error.description: Human-readable error the agent can show or use to retry. Present when ok is false.

recommendations.description: Ranked in-stock teas, best match first.

tools.name: ippodo_get_brewing_guide
tools.description: Use when a shopper asks how to prepare, brew, whisk, steep, or care for a specific Ippodo product they already named. Returns the published recipe quantities and step-by-step directions for that product handle. Optional method filters recipes such as usucha, koicha, latte, hot, iced, or cold brew. tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to update_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

id.description: Cart line GID from get_cart. Pass back to update_cart as line_items[].id to update or remove this line.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

line_price.description: Total price for the line (quantity × unit_price).

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

deduped.description: True when this exact add was applied moments ago and was skipped to avoid a duplicate. When true, nothing changed on this call and updated is false.

line_items.description: Items added by this mutation, with product/variant details filled in from the post-mutation cart.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

resolved_items.description: Present only on the clarification-needed path (nothing was applied). Items that could have been added, with pre-mutation lookup titles when available.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

To use WordPress functions, start your code with: require("/wordpress/wp-load.php"); Always include the opening <?php tag. The response JSON contains three fields: - "text": stdout output - "errors": PHP warnings, notices, and fatal error messages from stderr - "exitCode": 0 on success, non-zero on fatal error Check both "errors" and "exitCode" to determine whether the call succeeded. WARNING: output is returned in full with no truncation — avoid queries that produce unbounded output (e.g. SELECT * without LIMIT). Keep output under 50 KB to avoid filling the context window.

code.description:
PHP code to execute. Example:
					"<?php echo get_bloginfo('name');"

tools.name: playground_request
tools.description: Make an HTTP request to the WordPress site running in Playground. REST API requests (/wp-json/* or ?rest_route=) are automatically authenticated with a valid nonce — no manual auth needed. Tool selection guide: 1. Use this tool (playground_request) with the REST API for standard content CRUD — posts, pages, users, terms, comments, settings, etc. The REST API handles serialization, pagination, and field filtering for you. Prefer compact REST responses: use _fields to request only the fields needed and per_page/page for large collections. Before using endpoint-specific filters, inspect the route metadata from /wp-json/ and use only args documented for that route. 2. Use this tool with the WordPress REST API to discover and call registered abilities when the site exposes the Abilities API: - GET /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities lists registered abilities. Always assume this response may be large and start with _fields, e.g. /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities?_fields=name,category,label,description Do not assume filters like search or category exist unless /wp-json/ route metadata documents them. - GET /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/{name} gets one ability, including schemas and metadata. Ability names include "/" in the path; do not encode it. For example, use /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/memex/save-note for "memex/save-note". - GET, POST, or DELETE /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities/{name}/run executes the ability. Inspect the ability metadata first, then call /run with the documented method. POST bodies usually wrap arguments in an "input" object, e.g. {"input":{"title":"Hello"}}. - GET /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/categories lists ability categories. Each category includes _links.abilities; follow that URL to list abilities in that category. The abilities collection can also be filtered directly with /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities?category={slug}. 3. Use playground_execute_php when the data you need is not exposed by the REST API (e.g. raw options, dire…

tools.name: playground_navigate

On 404 or error pages, navigation still succeeds from the tool's perspective — check the returned URL or use playground_request to verify the HTTP status code if needed.

path.description:

tools.name: playground_read_file
tools.description: Read a file from the WordPress virtual filesystem. Returns the file contents as text.

path.description:

tools.name: playground_write_file
tools.description: Write content to a file in the WordPress virtual filesystem. WARNING: Overwrites the entire file — existing content is permanently lost. Read the file first with playground_read_file if you need to preserve any content. Creates the file if it does not exist. Parent directories are NOT created automatically — call playground_mkdir first if needed, otherwise the write will fail with a "no such file or directory" error.

path.description:
Absolute path to write to, e.g.
					"/wordpress/wp-content/test.txt"

tools.name: playground_list_files
tools.description: List files and directories at a given path in the WordPress virtual filesystem. Returns a flat, non-recursive listing of the immediate contents. To explore subdirectories, call this tool again with the subdirectory path.

path.description:
Absolute path to list, e.g.
					"/wordpress/wp-content/plugins"

tools.name: playground_mkdir
tools.description: Create a directory (and all required parent directories) in the WordPress virtual filesystem. Call this before playground_write_file when writing to a path whose parent directories do not yet exist.

path.description:
Absolute path of directory to

tools.name: playground_delete_file
tools.description: Delete a file from the WordPress virtual filesystem. WARNING: Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. Returns an error if the file does not exist — use playground_file_exists first if deletion is conditional.

path.description: Absolute path of file to delete

tools.name: playground_delete_directory
tools.description: Delete a directory from the WordPress virtual filesystem. WARNING: Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. By default (recursive=false), the directory must be empty or the call will fail. Set recursive=true to delete a directory and all its contents — use with care.

path.description: Absolute path of directory to delete

recursive.description:
If true, delete directory and

tools.name: playground_file_exists
tools.description: Check whether a file or directory exists in the WordPress virtual filesystem.

path.description: Absolute path to check

tools.name: playground_list_sites
tools.description: List all WordPress Playground sites available. Call this before any other playground tool — it returns the siteId required by every other operation. If this returns no sites, the user may need to open Playground in their browser. Use playground_get_website_url to get the exact URL to send to the user. Returns site names and storage type. "temporary" sites are lost on page reload, "opfs" sites persist across reloads. Call playground_save_in_browser to persist a temporary site.

tools.name: playground_save_in_browser
tools.description: Save a temporary WordPress Playground site to browser storage so it survives page reloads. Safe to call even if the site is already saved (no-op). Sites start as temporary by default and are lost when the browser tab is closed or the page is reloaded. Call this early in any multi-step workflow where losing progress would be costly.

tools.description: Return the URL the user must open in their browser to use WordPress Playground with this MCP server. Use this tool whenever you need to send the user to Playground or open it autonomously — always obtain the URL from this tool rather than constructing it manually.

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Every call runs against the current visitor site; do not set `scope`, `siteId`, or auth headers. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

tools.name: GetSitePages
tools.description: Returns the COMPLETE list of pages that exist on this site, as route patterns. Only these pages exist; never guess or invent a URL (e.g. /shop, /store, /checkout, /account) - a path not listed here will show a 404. `title` is the page's name in the site menu; match it against what the visitor asks for. Static routes are exact paths (e.g. /cart). Dynamic routes contain [param] placeholders (e.g. /products/[slug]) or a rest placeholder ([...path]); `identifiers` says what fills each placeholder (e.g. slug: STORES.PRODUCT.SLUG means the product's slug from the Stores products API) and `pageIdentifier` names the Wix page type. A route with `acceptsSubpath` also accepts a concrete path below it, e.g. the product page URL returned by the Stores API. Navigate with NavigateToPage, passing the route pattern and a `params` value for every placeholder. If the page the visitor asks for is not in the list, say so instead of navigating.

topic.description: Optional: filter by topic name, e.g. "Faith", "Psychology & Mental Health", "Sharia", "History"

Use this when you need the complete abstract, author, topics, and canonical URL for a specific piece of content — or when you want to quote or cite a passage from the article. Set include_content to true to receive the first 800 characters of the article body, which you can use to quote or cite specific text in your response.

slug.description: The URL slug of the article, e.g. "depression-the-darkness-before-dawn"

include_content.description: Set to true to include the opening 800 characters of the article body. Useful for quoting or citing specific text. Defaults to false.

slug.description: URL slug of the video, e.g. "the-beginning-and-the-end-ep-1"

slug.description: URL slug of the scholar, e.g. "omar-suleiman" or "tesneem-alkiek"

slug.description: Optional: slug of a specific book for its full detail

year.description: Optional: filter by fiscal year, e.g. 2024

Returns direct links to the imam well-being report and the institutional dataset.

tools.name: get_new_muslim_resources
tools.description: Return curated starter resources for new Muslims (converts/reverts) and born-Muslims returning to practice. Use this tool when a user says: 'I just became Muslim', 'I took my shahada', 'I'm a revert', 'I'm a convert', 'where do I start learning about Islam?', 'how do I pray?', 'it's my first Ramadan', 'I'm not sure how to practice as a new Muslim', 'I feel pressure to give up my culture as a convert', or 'I want to reconnect with my faith'. tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

sites.name: pitchtheai.com
sites.description: Pitch your idea to four AI judges. Lose their patience, win a bidding war, and climb the public pitch board.

tools.name: start_pitch
tools.description: Fast-start the visible Pitch The AI lobby. The required roomCode is checked before any state changes, so this may be the first tool call from the room-bound handoff prompt. On success it secretly varies judge patience, runs the visible 3-2-1 launch, starts the twenty-minute clock, and returns the full room context. Repeating the same start request for an already-live room safely returns its current context instead of restarting it. Equity may be 0 for a prize or non-equity contest ask. Difficulty controls response time, pressure, scoring severity, rescue tolerance, and bid standards.

roomCode.description: Exact six-character room code from the founder handoff. The pitch will not start in a different tab.

agentSignature.description: Your self-reported agent or model identity for the public pitch receipt, for example Codex · GPT-5.6 Sol.

pitchVenue.description: The host browser or application where this pitch is taking place, for example BringMy.ai beta or Codex in-app browser.

tools.name: update_pitch_details
tools.description: Update the visible pitch brief and the panel’s immediate room read after extracting details from the founder’s speech or text. Call as soon as the company name and ask are known, then whenever those facts or the panel mood materially change. Equity may be 0 for a prize or non-equity contest ask. Select a soundtrack that matches the tension; the founder controls whether browser audio is enabled.

tools.name: get_pitch_context
tools.description: Read this tab's unique room code, opening draft, live pitch transcript, difficulty, founder/judge dialogue, response gate, judge-rescue gate, presentation-reset gate, founder pause state, founder-camera evidence, offer-decision gate, timer, ask, uploaded evidence links, prior offers, accepted deal, and all four judges. start_pitch performs its own required room-code check and returns this same full context, so a normal room-bound handoff should call start_pitch first instead of using this tool as a preflight. Use get_pitch_context to locate the correct tab after a room mismatch or to refresh state later. Equity 0 means competition mode: judge WebMCP fit, user experience, human-agent collaboration, implementation, originality, and resilience instead of pretending it is a normal investment. Before any judge enters, open and inspect every uploaded file, then call review_pitch_evidence with a grounded summary for each pending material. The newest file named founder-readiness-* is the exact opt-in image shown on the founder card; older files with that prefix are prior retakes. It may inform only observable pitch-readiness feedback such as framing, lighting, eye contact, and attire preparedness. Never infer or score attractiveness, age, race, ethnicity, gender, disability, health, religion, income, identity, or other sensitive traits. Run the pitch interactively: post one judge question, then call wait_for_founder_response in consecutive 12-second slices while the founder reads, clicks Respond, and answers. The response clock begins only when they click Respond, and any submitted answer remains available across slices. In Hard and Legendary modes, judges may challenge answers that suddenly become generic, over-polished, or inconsistent with the founder's prior voice, but must never claim to have detected AI. Ask for an immediate concrete example, calculation, personal decision, or implementation detail that the founder should know without outside help; score the substanc…

tools.name: review_pitch_evidence
tools.description: Confirm that every currently pending uploaded pitch file has actually been opened and reviewed. Supply a concise grounded summary for each pending material id. Judge tools remain blocked until this gate is complete; uploading a new file creates a new pending review. For founder-readiness images, record observable presentation readiness such as framing, lighting, visible eye contact, and whether deliberate attire choices support or undermine pitch credibility. Sunglasses that visibly obscure eye contact or conspicuously casual presentation in a formal pitch are fair to note and may be challenged in character, but the founder must be allowed to explain a deliberate brand choice. Never infer sensitive traits, rate attractiveness, or comment on cultural, religious, disability-related, or medical attire.

tools.name: post_judge_turn
tools.description: Post exactly one judge turn. The arena moves that investor to a large center-stage card above the pitch controls while the other three mounted screens stay in place. The founder must click Respond before the input returns and before the difficulty-based answer clock begins. Keep it focused and under 90 spoken words. Respect pitch.difficulty: Easy coaches, Medium balances, Hard presses and may test whether an answer is authentically grounded, Legendary is ruthless, frequently demands founder-only specifics, and makes offers rare. Never pretend to detect AI from prose. In Hard or Legendary, if an answer abruptly becomes generic, over-polished, or inconsistent with the founder's earlier voice, say that it sounds assisted and demand one immediate concrete example, calculation, personal decision, or implementation detail. Score whether the founder can substantiate it. When equity is 0, use competition criteria—WebMCP fit, UX, human-agent collaboration, implementation, originality, and resilience—not ordinary investment traction. Set answerQuality to rate the founder's immediately preceding answer, or unrated for the first question. Ground reactions in reviewed evidence. A founder-readiness photo has real but limited weight and no generic attire score: interpret the same visible choice through each persona. Priya may question seriousness and unobstructed eye contact; Theo may ignore style if the operating proof is excellent; Maya may challenge whether the look is performative or authentic to the customer; Julian may reward confidence when the presentation is coherent with the brand. An appropriate judge may call out visible choices that undermine credibility—such as sunglasses obscuring eye contact or conspicuously casual headwear in a formal pitch—and may joke in character, then must let the founder explain whether the look is a deliberate brand choice. For an easily reversible issue, set presentationReset true, omit question, explicitly tell the founder what to change,…

tools.name: wait_for_founder_response
tools.description: Wait up to 12 seconds while the human reads the active judge, clicks Respond, and types an answer. The difficulty-based response clock starts only on Respond, not when the judge speaks. A submitted answer persists across calls, and a five-second transport grace reconciles answers already in flight. If the result is waiting, call this again immediately without analysis or another judge turn. If answered, evaluate the exact response; if timed_out, burn patience.

tools.name: wait_for_founder_readiness_photo
tools.description: Wait up to 12 seconds while the room clock is paused and the founder follows a judge presentation-reset request and uploads a new readiness photo. If waiting, call this tool again immediately. When submitted, open and inspect the returned exact material URL, then call review_pitch_evidence. The same judge must react to the new photo before anyone else speaks.

tools.name: wait_for_judge_rescue
tools.description: Wait while an out judge hangs halfway above the room. The founder has twenty seconds to click “Wait, don't go!” and, after clicking, twenty seconds to give one concrete reason the judge should stay. If answered, the same judge must respond next with post_judge_turn and may return to pressing/listening or say no and remain out. Never invent the appeal and never let another judge speak while this gate is open.

tools.name: complete_panel_judge_turn
tools.description: Compatible four-agent panel hosts only: release your assigned judge seat after you have completed exactly one judge cycle and every founder-answer, rescue, or presentation-reset gate you opened is closed. The room will securely wake the configured agent assigned to the next judge. Never use this during a normal single-agent Codex or ChatGPT pitch. If the result says panel_complete, the current final-seat agent closes the room with post_panel_verdict; competition mode uses amountRaised 0 and no offer.

tools.name: post_judge_round
tools.description: Legacy opening montage only: post one brief non-question reaction from each judge before interactive questioning begins. Do not use this tool for Q&A. Every reaction must omit question; use post_judge_turn plus wait_for_founder_response for the actual pitch.

tools.name: post_bid_round
tools.description: Investment mode only: put one or more visible offers on the founder’s deal table. Competition mode is judgment-only and rejects this tool. Two or more offers create a competitive bidding round; one offer may answer a founder counter. The founder—not the agent—must then choose a judge, counter one offer, or reject them all. Immediately call wait_for_founder_offer_decision in consecutive short slices and do not continue until it returns answered or timed_out. Judges may steal, improve, or form a joint offer, but every offer must be earned by the live pitch.

tools.name: wait_for_founder_offer_decision

If the founder accepts, close with post_panel_verdict using the exact accepted judge, amount, and equity. If the founder counters, let that judge accept, reject, or improve the deal through another post_bid_round.

The verdict is displayed large, so write like a ruthless game-show judge, not a professional investment memo. Call out the founder's actual evasions and unanswered questions in plain language. Repeated evasion or silence with no credible answers belongs below 15; if every judge is out and the founder never answered the core questions, score 0–8. tools.name: user.events-sites-toggle-favorite.create
tools.description: 행사를 즐겨찾기에 넣거나 뺀다. 🔴 **토글이다** — 현재 상태의 반대로 바뀌므로, 「넣어 달라」는 요청이면 상세 도구로 현재 상태를 먼저 확인한다. 로그인이 필요하다. 🔴 **대상이나 행위가 모호하면 지르지 말고 멈춘다** — 무엇을 가리키는지와 어느 도구를 부를지가 **둘 다 좁혀져야** 실행한다. 한 낱말이 서로 다른 도구 둘 이상에 맞으면(예: 「없애줘」는 삭제와 숨김 중 무엇인지 정해지지 않는다) 아직 좁혀진 것이 아니다. 둘 다 좁혀졌으면 그 지시가 곧 승인이다.

id.description: 즐겨찾기 토글할 행사 ID. `GET /v1/events/sites/{siteId} → data.content[].id` 값 사용.

tools.name: user.events-sites.list
tools.description: 행사(이벤트) 목록을 조건으로 찾는다. 검색어·카테고리·모집상태·등록일 구간·정렬·페이지를 파라미터로 받는다. 화면의 행사 목록과 같은 데이터를 돌려준다.

recruitmentStatus.description: 모집상태 — OPEN(모집중) / CLOSING_SOON(마감임박, 종료 7일 이내) / CLOSED(마감). 모집 종료일에서 실시간 파생하며 생략 시 전체.

createdFrom.description: 등록일(createdAt) 시작 — 해당 날짜 00:00:00 이상. 형식: yyyy-MM-dd. 생략 시 하한 없음

createdTo.description: 등록일(createdAt) 종료 — 해당 날짜 23:59:59 이하(포함). 형식: yyyy-MM-dd. 생략 시 상한 없음

page.description: 페이지 번호(1-based, 모든 도메인 공통). page ≥ 1이며, 1 미만(0/음수) 값이 들어오면 첫 페이지(1)로 자동 보정된다.

desc.description: 정렬 방향 배열. `sort` 와 인덱스로 짝을 이룬다(true=내림차순, 미지정=오름차순). Spring 표준 표기 `sort=필드,desc` 를 쓰면 이 배열은 필요 없다.

sort.description: 정렬 키 배열. 허용 키는 **오퍼레이션마다 다르며** 대개 그 목록의 백킹 테이블 컬럼이다. camelCase(`createdAt`)·snake_case(`created_at`) 둘 다 받는다(서버가 폴백 변환). ⚠️ 모르는 키의 처리가 **오퍼레이션마다 다르다** — 대부분은 `F302`(400)로 거부하지만 일부 목록은 **조용히 무시**하고 200 을 돌려준다(정렬만 안 먹는다). 허용 키를 명시한 오퍼레이션은 그 설명을 따른다. 생략 시 도메인 기본 정렬이며, 정렬을 명시하면 상단고정(`fixed`) 우선 정렬이 해제된다.

sites.name: varioroam.com
sites.description: Set the gigabytes, days and networks for Japan, Korea, the USA, Europe & 180+ countries. One price for exactly that, hotspot included, starts on first connect.

tools.name: get_shop_facts
tools.description: What varioroam is and how it works, in the shop’s own words: the configurable eSIM, ranges, delivery, payment, hotspot, activation, support. Use for any question that is not a price. Answer from the returned facts in the shop’s own words; do not add refund windows, speeds or rules that are not returned.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: Every country varioroam can build an eSIM for, with the number of selectable networks and the starting price (1 GB, 1 day, cheapest network). Use to check coverage or to compare many countries at once. from_price is the starting price (1 GB x 1 day x cheapest network) - call quote_esim for the configuration the customer actually wants.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_networks
tools.description: The mobile networks the customer can tick for one country (operator name, 4G/5G) with the price of a reference eSIM on each network alone (1 GB · 7 days), so you can say which network is the cheapest and what the others add. reference_price is for 1 GB x 7 days on that network alone - a comparison aid, not a plan. The cheapest network is pre-selected in the shop; every extra network adds a small fee, a dearer one also raises the data price. Never invent coverage or speeds.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per eSIM.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: quote_esim
tools.description: The exact price of one eSIM configuration: country, data (GB, 1–100), days (1–90), networks. This is the server price the customer pays — quote it as returned, never compute or scale it yourself. Returns buy_url with the configurator pre-set. price is the FULL amount of exactly this configuration (price_basis total) - never per day, never per GB; quote it as returned and never compute or scale it. data_gb is one pool for the whole validity. networks lists the operators exactly as returned. Hand the customer to buy_url exactly as returned: the configurator opens pre-set, they press "Get it" and pay.

sites.name: coverredact.com
sites.description: Redact a PDF in your browser

tools.name: describe_capabilities
tools.description: Describe the in-page Cover redaction engine for an agent: what it detects, what it refuses, how a document gets onto the page, what the tools return and what they never return. Read this first. Privacy: the document is processed inside this browser tab (WebAssembly); nothing is uploaded and the document never leaves the page. These tools return counts, ids, categories, state and page-relative geometry only — never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way. How a document gets here: the person using the page drops or opens the PDF; tools cannot accept file bytes or URLs. If get_status lists no document and there is no person to ask - a headless run - call load_sample_document: it puts this page's own built-in sample document on the page so the tools have something to work on. It is the ONLY document a tool can introduce.

output_schema.description: What this page's engine detects, refuses, returns and never returns.

tools.name: load_sample_document
tools.description: Put this page's own built-in sample document on the page, as if a person had dropped it, and return its document_id. For a HEADLESS run: the tools take their input from a human hand, so on a page nobody has dropped a file onto, every other document tool has nothing to act on and get_status returns an empty list. This is the way in. It takes NO input - not file bytes, not a URL, not a path - and always loads the SAME fixed document: a synthetic residential lease agreement (one page) that this site already publishes. It cannot be pointed at anything else, so it is not a way to get a document into this page from outside. Calling it twice adds a second copy rather than replacing the first; call get_status if you are unsure whether one is already loaded. It never counts against the daily document limit, so it cannot be refused with daily_limit however many times it is loaded. It returns immediately; the document then REDACTS IN THE BACKGROUND and takes about 60 seconds to finish on a fresh browser (a one-time ~265 MB name-model download, not the redaction itself). Poll rather than assuming it failed. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

output_schema.description: The loaded sample, plus how long it will take to finish.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Where things stand: engine readiness, whether the names tier is enabled, and every document on the page with its document_id, name, page count, state (queued | running | done | refused), stage (waiting | structured | names | done; edits need names or done), refusal (error code + next step), detections by category, names_checked, watermark and a short structured event log per document (its milestones plus the latest two entries; bar tallies, timings and the fuller log are on get_redaction_result). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. How a document gets here: the person using the page drops or opens the PDF; tools cannot accept file bytes or URLs. If get_status lists no document and there is no person to ask - a headless run - call load_sample_document: it puts this page's own built-in sample document on the page so the tools have something to work on. It is the ONLY document a tool can introduce.

include_events.description: Include each document's event log (default true).

output_schema.description: Engine readiness and every document on the page.

engine.description: What the engine is doing right now. status "failed" means more polling will not help.

boot.description: Boot progress, timing only: last_stage is none | modules_loaded | engine_wasm_received.

tools.name: get_redaction_result
tools.description: The result of the engine run on one document: redacted (true/false), status, counts by category (detections and painted bars), tier, names_checked, not_covered, watermark, timings and the event log. It RETURNS PROMPTLY and is meant to be POLLED IN A LOOP: it blocks at most 10 seconds, then returns status "pending" with retry_after_s and a next_step. Pending is NOT a failure and NOT a reason to stop. A first run on a fresh browser needs roughly 60 seconds in total (nearly all of it a one-time ~265 MB name-model download), so EXPECT ABOUT 6 TO 8 CALLS. Do not try to cover that with one long wait - timeout_s is capped at 10 and a longer request is clamped. status is "done" or "refused" when it is final. A refused document returns {error: "needs_ocr" | "encrypted_unsupported", next_step}. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way.

wait.description: Wait for the run to finish (default true).

wait_for_names.description: When waiting, wait for the names tier too, not just the structured tier (default true).

timeout_s.description: Seconds to block before returning status "pending" (default 10, max 10). This tool NEVER blocks longer than that: poll it repeatedly instead of asking for one long wait.

output_schema.description: The run's outcome. status "pending" is normal and means poll again.

engine.description: What the engine is doing right now. status "failed" means more polling will not help.

boot.description: Boot progress, timing only: last_stage is none | modules_loaded | engine_wasm_received.

detections.description: Per-category tallies. Category names are stable strings (US_SSN, PERSON, US_ADDRESS...).

bars.description: Per-category tallies. Category names are stable strings (US_SSN, PERSON, US_ADDRESS...).

tools.name: list_redactions
tools.description: Every redaction on a document as the editor holds it right now: id, page (1-based), category (e.g. US_SSN, PERSON; null for a drawn bar), origin (engine | user), active (false = an engine detection the editor turned off), and its rectangle as page-relative fractions. Ids: "e " engine, "u " user-drawn; engine ids are reissued when the names tier lands (see revision). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

page.description: Only this page (1-based). Default: all pages.

output_schema.description: Every redaction the editor holds, with geometry but no text.

rect.description: Page-relative rectangle: fractions 0..1 of the page width/height, origin top-left, x0<x1, y0<y1.

tools.name: remove_redactions
tools.description: Turn the given redactions off (an engine detection becomes inactive and can be restored; a user-drawn bar is deleted). The page repaints so the person watching sees the change. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus what was turned off and what was not recognised.

allOf.description: Receipt for an edit: what the document holds now, not what changed in the page.

tools.name: restore_redactions
tools.description: Turn inactive engine redactions (ids "e ") back on. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many were turned back on.

tools.name: add_redaction
tools.description: Add a user-drawn redaction bar on a page at a page-relative rectangle (fractions of the page, origin top-left). The page repaints. Returns the new id and counts. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

page.description: 1-based page number.

rect.description: Page-relative rectangle: fractions 0..1 of the page width/height, origin top-left, x0<x1, y0<y1.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus the new bar's id (redaction_id, "u<n>"), page and rect as applied.

rect.description: Page-relative rectangle: fractions 0..1 of the page width/height, origin top-left, x0<x1, y0<y1.

tools.name: redact_similar
tools.description: The magic tool, keyed by an EXISTING redaction id: the engine reads the value under that bar (in-page; it is never returned) and redacts every other occurrence of it across the document, on every page. Returns only the number of bars added. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

redaction_id.description: An existing, active redaction id from list_redactions.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many other occurrences were covered. The value itself is never returned.

tools.name: unredact_similar
tools.description: The magic tool in reverse, keyed by an EXISTING redaction id: every other active redaction of the same value across the document is turned off. The keyed bar itself stays. Returns only the number turned off. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

redaction_id.description: An existing, active redaction id from list_redactions.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many other occurrences were turned off.

tools.name: remove_category
tools.description: Turn off every active engine redaction of one category (e.g. PERSON, US_ADDRESS) on a document. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many of that category were turned off.

tools.name: restore_category
tools.description: Turn every inactive engine redaction of one category back on. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

category.description: A category name as returned by list_redactions / get_redaction_result counts.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many of that category were turned back on.

tools.name: finalize
tools.description: Bake the current redaction set into the ORIGINAL document (edited sets go through the engine's apply-rects; an untouched set is the engine's own output) and hand the redacted PDF to the person through the page's download. The file goes to their machine, never through this tool: the result carries filename, byte size, page count, the number of active redactions, and watermark (whether the engine stamped THIS file). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way.

output_schema.description: The handoff receipt. The FILE is not returned here - it goes to the person through the page download.

tools.name: book-airport-transfer
tools.description: Create a confirmed transfer booking with Airport Pickups London. THIS CREATES A REAL RESERVATION AND DISPATCHES A DRIVER. Required workflow: 1) call get-transfer-quote and show the customer the car type and exact price; 2) collect passenger name, phone, email, and the flight number for airport pickups; 3) read ALL details back to the customer (route, date, time, car, price) and get their explicit approval; only then call this tool with customer_confirmed=true. No payment is taken now — the customer pays the driver in cash, or by card/Apple Pay/Google Pay via the manage-booking link in the confirmation.

origin.description: Pickup: airport/terminal name, full UK postcode, or street address

destination.description: Dropoff: airport/terminal name, full UK postcode, or street address

transfer_time.description: Pickup time HH:MM (24h). For airport pickups use the flight arrival time

car_type.description: Car type exactly as named in the quote (e.g. 'Saloon', 'People Carrier'). Auto-selected if omitted

passenger_name.description: Lead passenger full name (shown on the driver's name board)

passenger_phone.description: Passenger mobile in international format, e.g. +447123456789

passenger_email.description: Email for the confirmation and manage-booking link

flight_number.description: Required for airport pickups, optional for dropoffs (e.g. 'BA2534'). Auto-validates and detects the terminal

door_number.description: House/door number when the destination is a postcode

special_requests.description: e.g. child seat ages, extra stops, accessibility needs

customer_confirmed.description: Set true ONLY after the customer explicitly approved the exact price, car, route and date/time read back to them

tools.name: lookup-booking
tools.description: Look up the current status and details of an existing booking. Requires BOTH the booking reference and the passenger email on file — the same verification as the manage-booking page. Never guess or invent the email.

booking_ref.description: APL booking reference (e.g. 'APL-X7K9M2') or numeric reservation ID

email.description: Passenger email on the booking — must match exactly (case-insensitive)

tools.name: amend-booking
tools.description: Amend an existing booking — change flight number, transfer date/time, phone number or special requests (one or more at once; the email on file cannot be changed). Self-service amendments are allowed up to 24 hours before pickup; for urgent same-day changes the customer must call the 24/7 office line instead. Requires the booking reference and the passenger email on file. Read the exact changes back to the customer and get explicit approval before calling with customer_confirmed=true.

email.description: Passenger email on the booking — must match exactly

changes.description: ONLY the fields to change, e.g. {"flight_number":"BA2590","transfer_time":"15:00","transfer_date":"2026-09-16","passenger_phone":"+447999888777","special_requests":"child seat age 3"}

customer_confirmed.description: Set true ONLY after the customer explicitly approved these exact changes

tools.name: cancel-booking
tools.description: Cancel an existing booking. Free 12+ hours before pickup — no admin fee for bookings made through this tool or the MCP/A2A agents; bookings made on the website form follow the Terms (£10 admin fee if paid by card). Within 12 hours of pickup it CANNOT be cancelled here — the customer must call the office. Requires the booking reference and the passenger email on file. Cancellation cannot be undone: confirm explicitly with the customer before calling with customer_confirmed=true.

email.description: Passenger email on the booking — must match exactly

reason.description: Reason for cancellation, e.g. 'Flight cancelled'

customer_confirmed.description: Set true ONLY after the customer explicitly confirmed they want this booking cancelled

tools.name: manage-booking
tools.description: How to look up, amend or cancel an existing booking. Returns the secure manage-booking page; the customer logs in with their booking reference and email. Amendments and cancellations are confirmed by the customer there — never assume a change is done without it.

sites.name: argos-ci.com
sites.description: Argos is an open-source visual regression testing tool for Playwright, Storybook, Vitest and Cypress that diffs screenshots for review on every pull request.

tools.name: get_argos_overview
tools.description: What Argos is: four things it does for every pull request, Diff (screenshots and any text file, not just pixels), Review (humans and agents approve what changed), Stabilize (flaky-test history and debugging) and Deploy (free preview URLs for Storybook and static sites), plus a map of every page, doc, API and agent surface. Start here.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Argos plans and prices: Hobby (free), Pro (flat monthly price plus per-screenshot overage), Enterprise, add-ons, what counts as a screenshot, and the pricing FAQ. Use estimate_monthly_cost to price a specific usage.

tools.name: estimate_monthly_cost
tools.description: Estimate what Argos costs per month for a given usage: screenshots, Storybook screenshots, media uploads (images and videos), and the GitHub SSO or SAML SSO add-ons. Uses the same arithmetic as the pricing page.

screenshots.description: Screenshots uploaded per month from Playwright, Cypress, Vitest, or any non-Storybook SDK or the CLI.

storybookScreenshots.description: Storybook screenshots uploaded per month (billed at a lower rate).

mediaImages.description: Standalone images uploaded per month through media sharing.

mediaVideos.description: Standalone videos uploaded per month through media sharing.

githubSso.description: Add the GitHub Single Sign-On add-on.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Read an argos-ci.com page as markdown, by path or full URL. Pages: /, /deploy, /diff, /review, /stabilize, /ai-agents, /media-sharing, /pricing, /security, /compare/applitools, /compare/backstopjs, /compare/chromatic, /compare/percy, /compare/playwright, /dpa, /privacy, /terms, /blog/ , /changelog/ . Documentation paths (/docs/...) work too.

path.description: Page path such as /pricing or /blog/<slug>, or a full https://argos-ci.com URL.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the Argos documentation (setup guides, SDK references, CI integrations, review workflow, flaky tests, API, agents) and get the matching pages with their URLs. Follow up with get_docs_page.

query.description: Keywords, e.g. 'playwright quickstart', 'gitlab', 'baseline build', 'flaky'.

tools.name: get_docs_page
tools.description: Read one Argos documentation page as markdown. Pass the path from search_docs or a docs URL, e.g. 'quickstart/playwright-quickstart' or https://argos-ci.com/docs/learn/review-workflow. An empty path returns the documentation index.

path.description: Docs path without the /docs prefix, or a full docs URL.

tools.name: get_quickstart
tools.description: Step-by-step guide to set up Argos with a test framework: install the SDK, capture screenshots, run it in CI. Use 'other' for any framework not listed (upload screenshots with the Argos CLI).

framework.description: The test framework to set up Argos with.

tools.name: compare_with
tools.description: How Argos compares to another visual testing tool: feature-by-feature table, prices at sample volumes where the competitor publishes them, migration guide, and FAQ.

competitor.description: The tool to compare Argos with. 'playwright' means Playwright's built-in toHaveScreenshot().

tools.name: get_security_compliance
tools.description: Argos security and compliance: SOC 2 Type II (auditor, report access), GDPR, data location and encryption, access controls, open source, responsible disclosure, and the security FAQ.

tools.name: get_latest_changelog
tools.description: Recent Argos product updates and new features (the changelog), most recent first, as markdown. Read one entry in full with get_page.

tools.name: get_service_status
tools.description: Current operational status of the Argos service (live, from the status page).

tools.name: get_mcp_connection_info
tools.description: How to connect an AI agent to Argos itself: the MCP server endpoint, OAuth and personal access token authentication, and the REST API endpoints.

sites.name: beardedcolonel.co.uk
sites.description: With the Bearded Colonel, you’ll get fresh shaving razors delivered to you every month (or when you like!), at a fair price. One less thing to worry about!

tools.name: search_content
tools.description: Search the pages and articles on Bearded Colonel. Read-only. Returns { text, results[] } where each result has title, extract and url.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words.

limit.description: How many results to return.

text.description: The results as readable text.

id.description: The WordPress post ID. Stable, unlike the title.

tools.name: get_site_overview
tools.description: What Bearded Colonel is, and the main sections of the site. Read-only. Use it first to see what the site covers. Returns { text, name, tagline, sections[] } where each section has title and url.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Browse or search what Bearded Colonel sells when the product is not known by name: a keyword, a category, or a need like "dry skin". Returns a shortlist. For one named product, call get_product_details instead. Read-only. Returns { text, products[] } where each product has id, sku, name, price, in_stock and url - hold the id and use it for the next call.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words.

limit.description: How many products to return.

id.description: The product ID. Pass it back to get_product_details or add_to_cart instead of the name.

price.description: Formatted, including any subscription terms.

tools.name: get_product_details
tools.description: Everything about ONE product at Bearded Colonel, looked up by name: price, subscription frequencies, stock, category. This is the tool to use whenever a product name is known, including a partial one. Read-only. Some products carry no written description, so follow the link for the full page. Returns { text, found, ambiguous, alternatives[], id, sku, name, price, in_stock, categories[], options[], url } - when several products match, one is chosen and the rest are named in alternatives.

name.description: The product name, or part of it. Ignored when `id` is given.

id.description: The product ID from an earlier answer. Exact, and never ambiguous - prefer it over a name when you have one.

ambiguous.description: True when several products matched and one was chosen.

alternatives.description: Other products that matched the name.

id.description: The product ID. Stable; pass it to add_to_cart rather than the name.

tools.name: list_delivery_options
tools.description: Where Bearded Colonel delivers and what postage costs. Postage is charged by item type and is free above an order threshold, so this returns both. Read-only. The figure for a particular basket is confirmed at checkout. Returns { text, zones[] } where each zone has zone, free_over and postage[] of item type and cost including VAT.

free_over.description: Order total above which delivery is free. Empty if there is none.

items.description: The kind of item, by shipping class.

postage.description: Cost including VAT, or a note that it is set at checkout.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: The product categories at Bearded Colonel. Read-only. Returns { text, categories[] } where each category has id, slug, name, products count and url.

tools.name: get_subscription_terms
tools.description: How subscriptions work at Bearded Colonel: commitment, changing delivery frequency, pausing and cancelling. Read-only. Returns { text, contract, can_change_date, can_pause, can_cancel, self_service, manage_url } as booleans plus the account URL.

self_service.description: Whether a member does all of it themselves.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Put a product in the basket at Bearded Colonel. Changes the basket; it does not take payment or place an order, and anything added can be removed again. Subscription products need the delivery frequency in `option` - call get_product_details first to see what they are, and if it is missing this returns the choices instead of guessing. Returns { text, added, needs_option, options[], name, quantity, items, total, cart_url }.

product.description: The product name, or part of it. Ignored when `id` is given.

id.description: The product ID from an earlier answer. Exact, and never ambiguous - prefer it over a name when you have one.

option.description: For a subscription product, the delivery frequency, for example "Every 2 months".

quantity.description: How many to add.

needs_option.description: True when a frequency has to be chosen before this can be added.

items.description: How many items the basket now holds.

tools.name: view_cart
tools.description: What is in the basket at Bearded Colonel right now, line by line, with the total and any discount applied. Read-only. Returns { text, empty, items[], count, total, cart_url } where each item has id, name, quantity and subtotal - the id is what update_cart_item wants.

id.description: The product ID of this line. Pass it to update_cart_item.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change how many of a line already in the basket, or remove it by setting quantity to 0. Changes the basket; it does not take payment. Returns { text, updated, name, quantity, count, total }.

product.description: The name of a line already in the basket, or part of it. Ignored when `id` is given.

id.description: The product ID of a line in the basket, as view_cart reports it.

quantity.description: The new quantity. 0 removes the line.

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount code to the basket at Bearded Colonel. A code that is invalid, expired or not valid for what is in the basket fails harmlessly and says why. Changes the basket; it does not take payment. Returns { text, applied, code, discount, total }.

code.description: The discount code, exactly as the customer received it.

tools.name: go_to_checkout
tools.description: Take the visitor to the checkout page at Bearded Colonel with the basket as it stands. This moves the browser to the checkout; it fills nothing in, pays for nothing and orders nothing - the person completes it themselves. Returns { text, ready, count, total, navigate }.

ready.description: False when the basket is empty, and nothing happens.

navigate.description: The checkout URL the browser is being sent to.

from_date.description: Letzter lokaler Kalendertag des begrenzten Suchzeitraums, einschließlich dieses Tages.

to_date.description: Letzter lokaler Kalendertag des begrenzten Suchzeitraums, einschließlich dieses Tages.

language.description: Gewünschte Sprache für Texte und Anzeigeformate: de, en oder ru.

tools.name: coworking_get_account
tools.description: Den aktuellen Freigabestatus des eigenen Coworking-Kontos prüfen. Die Antwort nennt Workspaces mit freigeschalteten Preisen und nächste Schritte, ohne Preise anderer Nutzer offenzulegen.

language.description: Gewünschte Sprache für Texte und Anzeigeformate: de, en oder ru.

tools.name: coworking_get_booking
tools.description: Eine eigene Coworking-Buchung und die tatsächlichen Entscheidungen über Änderungsanfragen lesen. Fremde Kennungen erlauben keinen Zugriff.

booking_id.description: Kennung einer eigenen Mietbuchung aus coworking_list_bookings.

language.description: Gewünschte Sprache für Texte und Anzeigeformate: de, en oder ru.

tools.name: coworking_get_invoice
tools.description: Eine eigene Rechnung anhand ihrer Kennung abrufen. Eine fremde oder unbekannte Kennung wird als nicht verfügbar behandelt.

invoice_id.description: Kennung einer eigenen Rechnung aus coworking_list_invoices.

language.description: Gewünschte Sprache für Texte und Anzeigeformate: de, en oder ru.

tools.name: coworking_get_price
