Use `get_product_detail` for full information about one product. ## Returns `items[]` with public product summaries (name, url, from-price, security rating, availability) and `next_cursor` for pagination (null = end). - `price` is the from-price in EUR including VAT as shown in the shop. - `in_stock` is a flag, not a quantity. - Max 100 items per call. ## Example `{"search":"cilinder","brand_slug":"dom","price_max":150,"limit":10}`

search.description: Keywords; every word must match the product name or brand name.

category_id.description: Filter to products in this category.

type.description: Product type: "simple" or "configurable" (cylinder sets).

price_min.description: Minimum from-price in EUR.

price_max.description: Maximum from-price in EUR.

country.description: Only products available in this country: nl, be or es.

cursor.description: Cursor from a previous response.

limit.description: Number of items to return (max 100, default 25).

tools.name: get_product_detail
tools.description: ## Use when You need **everything a customer can see about one product**: description, USPs, pros/cons, specifications, price (incl. any active sale), delivery expectation, security certifications, return policy, cross-sells and review score. Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug` (one of the two is required). Only active products are returned. ## Returns One `product` object. Long texts come as `{html, text}` pairs — quote from `text`. - `specs[]` are the frontend-visible attributes with their values. - `sale` is the active promotion (percentage) or null. - For product-specific FAQs call `search_faqs` with this `product_id`. - `locale` (nl/be/es, default nl) applies translated texts when available. ## Example `{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder","locale":"nl"}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

locale.description: Language for texts: nl (default), be or es.

tools.name: get_product_options
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks what is possible for a **configurable product** (cylinder sets): available sizes, colors, knobs, panic function, smartlock adapters, accessories — and what each option costs extra or adds to the delivery time. Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`. Only active products. ## Returns - `options[]`: one entry per configurator option group with its choices. `surcharge` is the extra price in EUR (0 = included; null = unknown — never tell a customer an option is free or included when surcharge is null), `extra_delivery_days` adds to the base delivery time, `related_product` links choices that are themselves products (e.g. a smartlock added to a cylinder). - `included_keys`: how many keys come with the set for free. Either `keys_per_cylinder` (multiply by the number of cylinders) or `per_set_size` (total free keys per set size; a set larger than the largest listed size gets that largest amount). `null` = unknown for this product — never promise a number of keys then. - `sizes[]`: available cylinder size combinations (`a`/`b` in mm as the customer measures them) with the price per size. `sizes_total` may exceed the returned list (capped). Answers questions like "kan deze cilinder in het zwart met knop?" or "is maat 35/45 leverbaar en wat kost die?". ## Example `{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder"}` or `{"product_id":3}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

tools.name: find_cylinder_size
tools.description: ## Use when A customer wants to know which cylinder size to order for a configurable cylinder. Always use this tool for size advice — never calculate a size yourself. Call it **directly** with the measured millimetres per side (outside named first; centre of the fixing bolt to the end on that side). Do not ask follow-up questions before calling — whether and what to ask the customer is defined by the client's agent instructions, not by this tool. `outside_fit`/`inside_fit` are **optional** refinements (default `flush`). Pass them, with the offset in mm, only when the customer already mentioned that the current cylinder protrudes or is recessed relative to the door hardware. ## What it does Per side it computes the real depth to the door face (flush = measured, protruding = measured − offset, recessed = measured + offset), then picks from this product's size series the size that protrudes at most 3 mm, or else recesses at most 3 mm. Sides are computed independently and combined (e.g. `32/47`). ## Returns Structured data only — how to phrase the advice is up to the client (chatbot prompt / agent instructions). - `status`: `ok`, `below_minimum`, `above_maximum`, `outside_3mm_rule` or `not_applicable` (product has no adjustable sizes). - `recommended_size`: the size to order (e.g. "32/47") with `price`, or null when a side falls outside the range. - `sides`: per-side detail — `effective_mm` (real depth), `recommended`, `overshoot_mm`, `within_rule`, `below_minimum`, `above_maximum`. - `half_cylinder_possible`: true when this product also offers a half cylinder (short 10 mm side); relevant when a side is below the smallest standard size. - `specialist`: name + phone of the cylinder specialist, for referral when no size fits. Sizes are symmetric data: 32/47 is the same catalog row as 47/32; order only matters when a knob is chosen (knob belongs on the inside). ## Example `{"product_id":3,"outside_mm":30,"outside_fit":"flush","inside_mm":45,"inside_fit":"flush"}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

outside_mm.description: Measured outside dimension in mm (named first).

outside_fit.description: How the current cylinder sits on the outside: flush (default), protruding, or recessed.

inside_fit.description: How the current cylinder sits on the inside: flush (default), protruding, or recessed.

outside_offset_mm.description: mm the cylinder protrudes/recesses on the outside (required when not flush).

inside_offset_mm.description: mm the cylinder protrudes/recesses on the inside (required when not flush).

tools.name: get_delivery_info
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks **"wanneer heb ik het in huis?"** for a specific product. Returns the same delivery expectation the shop shows: base delivery days, the expected delivery date (NL business days, holidays excluded, 17:00 cut-off, evening delivery via Red je Pakket when applicable) and which configurator options add extra days. Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`. Pass `extra_days` to recompute for a chosen option (e.g. a color with +2 days from `option_delays`). ## Returns - `in_stock`, `delivery_days` and `expected` (ISO date + the Dutch human-readable text shown in the shop). - `option_delays[]`: option choices that extend the delivery time. The estimate is for delivery within the Netherlands, calculated at the moment of the call. ## Example `{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder"}` then `{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder","extra_days":2}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

extra_days.description: Extra delivery days from a chosen option (see option_delays).

tools.name: get_product_reviews
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks about **experiences with a product**, or you want to quote real customer feedback. Only approved, published reviews are returned — the same set shown on the product page, including reviews of the product's color/version variants. Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`. ## Returns - `summary`: total count, average score and the score distribution (1-5). - `items[]`: most recent reviews first (title, content, score, date). Reviews are anonymous here; no customer names are exposed. ## Example `{"product_id":88,"limit":5}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

min_score.description: Only reviews with at least this score (1-5).

max_score.description: Only reviews with at most this score (1-5).

limit.description: Number of reviews to return (max 50, default 10).

tools.name: search_faqs
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks a question that may already be answered in the shop's **FAQ**: shipping, returns, certificates, keys, installation, product-specific questions. Search by keyword, browse a category, or pass a `product_id` to get the FAQs shown on that product's page (linked directly and via the product's FAQ category). ## Returns `items[]` with question, answer (`{html, text}`) and category. Ordered by category position; max 100 items. For keyword searches, `page_faqs[]` additionally holds matching Q&As that live inline on published advice pages (with a `page` title + URL to cite) — those are not in the FAQ table. - `product_only` FAQs are only shown on product pages in the shop; without a `product_id` filter they are still included here so you can answer customer questions. ## Example `{"search":"certificaat"}` or `{"product_id":42}`

search.description: Keyword match on question or answer.

product_id.description: FAQs shown on this product's page (direct links + product FAQ category).

limit.description: Number of items to return (max 100, default 25).

tools.name: get_help_block
tools.description: ## Use when You need one of the shop's **curated help texts** (table `blocks`) — the same texts shown to customers on product pages, the configurator and checkout. These are the canonical explanations; prefer them over improvising an answer. Fetch by exact `slug`, or search by keyword in slug/title/body. The full slug index is available as resource `products://blocks`. Common slugs: `cilinder-keuze-uitleg`, `certificaat`, `skg-keurmerk-uitleg`, `kerntrekbeveiliging-uitleg`, `gelijksluitend`, `paniekfunctie`, `laagsteprijsgarantie`, `maatgarantie`, and per brand `knoppen-merk-{brand-slug}` / `cilindermaat-merk-{brand-slug}`. ## Returns `items[]` with slug, title and body (`{html, text}`). Max 20 items. ## Example `{"slug":"skg-keurmerk-uitleg"}` or `{"search":"kerntrek"}`

search.description: Keyword match on slug, title or body; used when slug is not given.

limit.description: Number of items to return (max 20, default 5).

tools.name: search_advice
tools.description: ## Use when A customer needs **guidance rather than a spec**: which lock to choose, how to measure a cylinder, how to remove or install one, burglary prevention. The shop's advice pages ("advies") are written buying guides and how-tos with recommended products. Search by keyword or browse a category (resource-style list when no filters are given). Results mirror what the website shows on /advies: published landing pages. ## Returns `items[]` with title, public URL, category, a plain-text `body` (truncated to ~2000 chars) and `recommended_product_ids` — feed those ids to `get_product_detail` to suggest concrete products. ## Example `{"search":"opmeten"}` or `{"advice_category_id":1}`

search.description: Keyword match on title, slug or page content.

include_body.description: Include the page text (default true; truncated to ~2000 chars).

limit.description: Number of pages to return (max 25, default 10).

tools.name: resolve_certificate_code
tools.description: ## Use when A customer sent a photo of a security card / certificate, or typed its code, and you need to know which model to reorder. Read the code off the card and pass it verbatim; never derive a model from a code yourself. A card can show other printed boxes next to the code, such as a generation marker (e.g. "G2"). Those do not belong to the code: leave them out, pass only the code itself. Pass `brand` whenever the card shows one (M&C, ABUS, DOM, NEMEF, EVVA). It is how a wrong reading gets caught: if the code resolves to models of another brand, `brand_conflict` comes back true and you must not answer from this result. Pass `reorder_type` only when the customer already said whether they need a cylinder (1) or keys (2). ## What it does Normalises the code (strips spaces and punctuation, uppercases) and matches it against the reorder code patterns of the webshop, the same list the shop's own reorder filter uses. Returns the candidate models plus the matching reorder products. ## Returns - `code`: the normalised code. - `models`: candidate models, most often one. Several means the code alone cannot tell them apart; the model name printed on the card decides, otherwise ask the customer. - `products`: reorder products per candidate model, with `url`, `brand` and `reorder_type` (1 = cylinder, 2 = keys). More than one product of the same `reorder_type` can come back for a single model, for example a sluitplan variant next to the regular version, or two different SKG levels, and they are genuinely different products. This tool never picks between them; ask the customer which one matches their situation instead of guessing. - `brand_conflict`: true when `brand` was given and none of the products carry it. Candidates are matched by name, so a `products` entry can belong to a model whose name only resembles the resolved model (e.g. a "+" variant of it). Have the customer confirm the exact product before ordering; never just take the first one. An empty `models` means the…

code.description: The code as printed or stamped on the card, verbatim.

brand.description: Brand shown on the card (M&C, ABUS, DOM, NEMEF, EVVA), for the conflict check.

tools.name: current_promotions
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks whether there is **a sale or discount right now** ("is er korting?", "zijn er acties?"), without pointing at one specific product. For the effective sale price of one product, `get_product_detail` already returns its active `sale`. ## Returns `promotions[]`, one entry per active sale: - `name` and `discount_percent` (percentage off the shop price). - `brand`: the brand the sale applies to (sales are brand-scoped). - `product_overrides[]`: products with a deviating percentage; `excluded` true means the product does not join the sale at all. An empty list means there are no active promotions; say so, do not invent one. ## Example `{}` or `{"brand_slug":"dom"}`

brand_id.description: Only promotions for this brand id.

brand_slug.description: Only promotions for this brand slug (e.g. "dom").

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

tools.name: search_esim_plans
tools.description: Find e-eSIM eSIM plans for one destination or several (countries or regions, any language). Returns the best-value plans first with full facts, coverage lists and a direct link; multi-country plans that include the destination are returned too and marked covers_via. Use when a user wants mobile data abroad; use recommend_plan when they describe a whole trip. Present only returned facts. price is the full fixed plan price, never per day or per GB. Every All You Can Surf grade has a daily full-speed allowance, then a reduced speed - never call a plan uncapped. Mention validity_clock, expires_on and notice when present. Use url and all_plans_url exactly.

destination.description: Country or region in any language, e.g. "Thailand", "Japon", "Europa", or a 2-letter ISO code. For a city, pass its country.

destinations.description: Several countries for one trip; only plans covering ALL of them are returned. Overrides destination.

type.description: Plan type. Default any.

min_days.description: Only plans valid for at least this many days.

limit.description: How many plans to return, best value first. Default 10; all_plans_url always lists everything.

sort.description: value = best price per GB delivered / cheapest All You Can Surf per day first (default); price = cheapest first; data = most data first.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

destinations.description: How each requested destination was understood.

iso.description: Resolved ISO code or region slug of the (first) destination.

from_price.description: Lowest price in this result set, shop-formatted (per-day plans count with their day price).

pricing_bucket.description: The language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in: the one the customer is browsing, unless the agent asked for another language or currency.

returned.description: Number of plans in this result.

note.description: Present when part of the request could not be honoured (e.g. more than 5 destinations).

total_available.description: Number of plans the shop matched; the rest are on all_plans_url.

items.description: One eSIM plan. Every field is present only when the catalogue holds a value for it; an absent field is unknown, never "no".

product_id.description: Product id. Use it for get_plan_details and start_checkout.

name.description: Short plan name: destination · data · validity · type.

title.description: Full product title in the requested language.

type.description: Plan type. Brand names — keep in English.

grade.description: All You Can Surf tier (standard, premium, titanium). Present only the returned value; every grade has a daily full-speed allowance then a reduced speed.

family_id.description: Plans sharing a family_id are day-length variants of the same package.

summary.description: Short description in the requested language, from the product page.

coverage_countries.description: Every country the plan works in.

name.description: Country name in the requested language.

covers_via.description: Present when the plan was returned for a country it covers as part of a multi-country plan: the plan's own region name.

coverage_note.description: Coverage caveat to present verbatim, e.g. traffic routed via Hong Kong.

coverage_label.description: Human-readable coverage label as the shop shows it (localized).

data_gb.description: Data amount in GB. Meaning given by data_period.

data_period.description: "total": data_gb is the whole plan (Trip Surf). "per_day": data_gb is the daily full-speed allowance (Daily Surf, All You Can Surf).

data.description: Trip Surf: total data label, e.g. "5GB".

daily_high_speed.description: Daily Surf / All You Can Surf: daily allowance at full speed, e.g. "2GB".

always_on_rate.description: Reduced speed after the allowance, e.g. "5 Mbps" / "128 kbps" (for the rest of that day on per_day plans; for the rest of the trip on Trip Surf). All You Can Surf stays unlimited in volume at this speed.

throttle_kbps.description: The same reduced speed in kbps. 0 = no throttle stated for this plan.

fair_use.description: All You Can Surf fair-use policy in plain words (daily full-speed allowance, then the still-unlimited reduced speed). Present it as returned.

network_generation.description: Network generation, e.g. "5G/4G". Never an operator name.

carrier.description: Local network operator when specified (1.0.x name; also in networks). NEVER invent one when absent.

networks.description: Operator name(s) for the plan, as the shop states them.

validity_clock.description: What the days count means for THIS plan: 24-hour periods from activation, or calendar days ending at a fixed clock (e.g. "ends 23:59 (UTC+8)"). State it; a 1-day calendar plan activated in the evening lasts only hours.

daily_reset_time.description: When the daily allowance refreshes (per_day plans only), e.g. "00:00 (UTC+8)" or "every 24 h after activation".

expires_on.description: Hard supplier end date (YYYY-MM-DD) after which the plan stops working and unused data is lost, whatever validity the customer picks. Say it plainly when present.

voice_sms.description: Always "none": data only, no telephone number, no SMS.

kind.description: Always "none" on e-eSIM: no top-ups or recharges exist; each plan is a self-contained eSIM.

plan_note.description: Customer-facing caveat for this plan in plain words: a daily cut-off, a coverage exclusion, an activation or verification step. Present it as returned whenever present.

price.description: FULL fixed price of the plan in currency; not per day, not per GB. The price shown is the price paid.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of every price in this object.

price_is_final.description: Always true: no tax or fee is added at checkout.

pricing_bucket.description: language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in, e.g. "en-us".

rating.description: Average customer rating (1-5). Present only when reviews exist.

review_count.description: Number of reviews. Present only when > 0.

last_updated.description: Date the plan was last updated in the catalogue (YYYY-MM-DD).

url.description: Product page in pricing_bucket. Use verbatim.

message.description: Present when nothing matched: says why and what to try.

tools.description: Hand the customer to the e-eSIM shop to buy one plan. Returns buy_url (the product page where they tap Buy now and pay securely — card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal; there is no discount-code field) plus the plan name and price in the customer's bucket or currency. tools.description: Read the visitor's current cookie-consent state on this site. Necessary cookies are always on. bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

from_price.description: Lowest price in this result set, shop-formatted (per-day plans count with their day price).

returned.description: Number of plans in this result.

title.description: Full product title in the requested language.

type.description: Plan type.

summary.description: Short description in the requested language, from the product page.

name.description: Country name in the requested language.

networks.description: Operator names in that country, as the supplier lists them.

covers_via.description: Present when the plan was returned for a country it covers as part of a multi-country plan: the plan's own region name.

data_gb.description: Data amount in GB. Meaning given by data_period.

data_period.description: "total": data_gb is the whole plan (Data Pack). "per_day": data_gb is the daily full-speed allowance (Unlimited Flex, Daily Pack).

data.description: Data Pack: total data label, e.g. "5GB".

daily_high_speed.description: Unlimited Flex / Daily Pack: daily allowance at full speed, e.g. "2GB"; "unlimited" = unlimited data every day at full speed (fair-use policy).

always_on_rate.description: Unlimited Flex / Daily Pack: reduced speed after the daily allowance, e.g. "512 Kbit/s". Empty when the plan has a speed_cap or is unlimited.

speed_cap.description: Present only on plans with a PERMANENT speed cap, e.g. "10 Mbit/s". Never call such a plan high-speed.

network_generation.description: Network technology, e.g. "4G/LTE/5G". Never an operator name.

networks.description: Operator names across the plan (deduplicated). Per-country detail is in coverage_countries.

days.description: Validity in days (Data Pack, Daily Pack).

days_range.description: Unlimited Flex: choosable durations in days, e.g. "1-30".

daily_reset_time.description: When the daily allowance resets, as the vendor states it (clock and time zone). Absent = resets 24 h after activation is NOT implied; simply unknown.

activation_trigger.description: "install": validity and billing start the moment the eSIM is installed — install only when ready to use. "first_connection": the eSIM can be installed before travel; validity starts on first connection to a network at the destination.

install_before_travel.description: true when the eSIM can safely be installed before departure (activation_trigger first_connection).

unused_valid_days.description: Days the eSIM may remain unused after purchase before it expires (supplier value).

start_date_required.description: true when a start date must be chosen at checkout.

expires_on.description: Stock expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the product itself has one.

hotspot.description: Hotspot / tethering rule as the vendor states it, e.g. "Supported" or a device limit.

apn.description: APN to set when the vendor requires one.

kyc_required.description: true when the vendor requires real-name registration (ID verification) on arrival before data works.

voice_sms.description: Always "none": data only, no telephone number, no SMS.

kind.description: What TopUp can add without a new eSIM: data (Data Pack), days (Unlimited Flex / Daily Pack), or none.

refund_class.description: Vendor refund/cancellation class for this plan.

refund_rule.description: The refund class in words - present verbatim.

plan_note.description: One-sentence vendor fact to present verbatim when present; overrides the generic type description.

transparency.description: A per-order Transparency link shows remaining data in near real-time.

price.description: Price in currency, read WITH price_basis: the full price of the plan when "total", the price of ONE day when "per_day". Never a per-GB rate. The price shown is the price paid.

price_max.description: Only on price_basis "per_day": the price for the longest duration in days_range, discount applied — the figure to quote for a full period. Never infer it by multiplying.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of every price in this object.

price_is_final.description: Always true: no tax or fee is added at checkout.

pricing_bucket.description: language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in, e.g. "en-us".

rating.description: Average customer rating (1-5). Present only when reviews exist.

review_count.description: Number of reviews. Present only when > 0.

last_updated.description: Date the plan was last updated in the catalogue (YYYY-MM-DD).

url.description: Product page in pricing_bucket. Use verbatim.

message.description: Present when nothing matched: says why and what to try.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Hand the customer to the eSIM-Global.VIP shop to buy one plan. Returns buy_url (the product page where they tap Buy now and pay securely — card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, with an optional discount code) plus the plan name and price in the customer's bucket or currency. No account needed; the eSIM is emailed right after payment. There is no in-chat order tracking. Hand the customer to buy_url exactly as returned, as one clear link; they pay on that page, where a discount code can be applied. No cart here, no order tracking.

product_id.description: Product id to buy.

days.description: Unlimited Flex only: the duration the customer wants; the returned total_for_days is the checkout total for it.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

price.description: Read WITH price_basis.

total_for_days.description: Unlimited Flex: checkout total for the requested days, discount applied.

pricing_bucket.description: The language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in: the one the customer is browsing, unless the agent asked for another language or currency.

buy_url.description: The exact product page to send the customer to. Use verbatim.

tools.name: recommend_plan
tools.description: Turn a trip into up to three plan recommendations: countries (1-5, any language), number of days and how much data the traveller uses. Each fit carries the full plan facts, the total price for the whole trip and a one-sentence reason built only from catalogue facts. Use this first whenever the user describes a trip rather than asks for a list.

countries.description: Countries or regions of the trip, any language.

usage.description: light ≈ 0.5 GB/day (maps, messaging), normal ≈ 1.5 GB/day (social, some video), heavy ≈ 4 GB/day (video, hotspot). Default normal.

gb_per_day.description: Overrides usage with an explicit daily need in GB.

budget.description: Optional maximum total for the trip, in the result currency.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

plans_needed.description: 1, or the number of consecutive Data Packs needed to cover the trip length.

decided.description: true once the visitor has made any choice.

sites.name: eulermotors.com
sites.description: Euler Motors' range of electric commercial vehicles in India, including 3-wheelers, 4-wheelers, and cargo solutions. Built for efficiency, sustainability, and cost savings.

tools.name: search_vehicle
tools.description: Search and filter Euler Motors electric vehicles based on vehicle type (3-wheeler/4-wheeler) and payload capacity.

vehicleType.description: The category of the vehicle: THREE_WHEELER or FOUR_WHEELER

city.description: The city where the vehicle is required (optional, used for local availability checks)

tools.name: compare_vehicles
tools.description: Compare specifications of multiple Euler Motors electric vehicles (e.g., HiLoad EV vs Storm EV T1500).

vehicles.description: List of vehicle names to compare (e.g., ['HiLoad EV', 'Storm EV T1500'])

tools.name: calculate_emi
tools.description: Calculate the monthly EMI, total interest, and total payable amount for a vehicle based on down payment and tenure.

vehicle.description: The name/model of the vehicle (e.g., 'HiLoad EV', 'Storm EV T1500')

tools.name: find_dealer
tools.description: Find nearby Euler Motors dealerships and service centers in a specified city.

city.description: The name of the city to search for dealers (e.g., 'Chennai', 'Agra')

tools.name: book_test_drive
tools.description: Book a test drive for an Euler Motors electric vehicle.

vehicle.description: The model of the vehicle to book (e.g., 'HiLoad EV', 'Storm EV T1500')

city.description: City name for the test drive location

tools.name: download_brochure
tools.description: Get the brochure download link for a specific Euler Motors electric vehicle.

vehicle.description: The vehicle name to get the brochure for (e.g., 'HiLoad EV', 'Storm EV T1500')

tools.name: find_charging_station
tools.description: Find nearby Euler charging stations and partner charging points in a specified city or along a route.

city.description: City name to search for charging stations (e.g., 'Delhi', 'Bangalore')

tools.name: search_blog
tools.description: Search Euler Motors blogs and news articles by keyword or get the latest articles.

query.description: Search keyword (e.g., 'EV subsidy', 'HiLoad review', 'charging')

limit.description: Number of articles to return (default: 5)

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: Get frequently asked questions and answers about Euler Motors vehicles, charging, warranty, service, and financing. For vehicle-specific FAQs, use the vehicle parameter (e.g. hiload, storm, stormlr, turbo).

vehicle.description: Optional: Vehicle to get FAQs for. Use this for model-specific questions (e.g. hiload for HiLoad EV, storm for Storm EV T1500)

category.description: FAQ category to filter by (only applies to general FAQs, not vehicle-specific)

query.description: Optional: Search keywords within FAQs

tools.name: get_vehicle_specs
tools.description: Return detailed technical specifications for an Euler Motors vehicle. Use this for payload, range, battery, dimensions, motor, brakes, and features.

vehicle.description: Vehicle to get specs for: hiload = HiLoad EV, storm = Storm EV T1500, stormlr = Storm EV LongRange 200

brandUrl.description: The brand's site to audit, e.g. 'yourbrand.com' or a full URL.

tools.name: read_api_docs

tools.name: view_blog
tools.description: Sends the user to Catalog's blog, which publishes field notes on agentic commerce, AI search visibility for e-commerce, product data infrastructure, PIM comparisons, and related topics. Use this when a user wants to read articles, learn about AI commerce trends, or explore educational content published by Catalog.

tools.name: view_careers
tools.description: Opens Catalog's job board on Ashby, listing current open roles at the company. Use this when a user asks about career opportunities, wants to apply for a position, or is curious whether Catalog is hiring.

tools.name: search_esim_plans
tools.description: Find IbiPoint eSIM plans for one destination or several (countries or regions, any language). Returns the best-value plans first with full facts, coverage lists and a direct link; multi-country plans that include the destination are returned too and marked covers_via. Use when a user wants mobile data abroad; use recommend_plan when they describe a whole trip. Present only returned facts. Read price with price_basis: "total" is the full plan price; "per_day" is the price of ONE day - say "from X per day", quote price_30_days for about a month, never multiply. Never per GB. Use url and all_plans_url exactly.

destination.description: Country or region in any language, e.g. "Thailand", "Japon", "Europa", or a 2-letter ISO code. For a city, pass its country.

destinations.description: Several countries for one trip; only plans covering ALL of them are returned. Overrides destination.

type.description: Plan type. Default any.

min_days.description: Only plans valid for at least this many days (Unlimited Flex counts when days_range allows it).

limit.description: How many plans to return, best value first. Default 10; all_plans_url always lists everything.

sort.description: value = best price per GB / cheapest Flex first (default); price = cheapest first; data = most data first.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

destinations.description: How each requested destination was understood.

iso.description: Resolved ISO code or region slug of the (first) destination.

from_price.description: Lowest price in this result set, shop-formatted (per-day plans count with their day price).

pricing_bucket.description: The language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in: the one the customer is browsing, unless the agent asked for another language or currency.

returned.description: Number of plans in this result.

note.description: Present when part of the request could not be honoured (e.g. more than 5 destinations).

total_available.description: Number of plans the shop matched; the rest are on all_plans_url.

items.description: One eSIM plan. Every field is present only when the catalogue holds a value for it; an absent field is unknown, never "no".

product_id.description: Product id. Use it for get_plan_details and start_checkout.

name.description: Short plan name: destination · data · validity · type.

title.description: Full product title in the requested language.

type.description: Plan type.

summary.description: Short description in the requested language, from the product page.

coverage_countries.description: Every country the plan works in, with the network operators per country when known.

name.description: Country name in the requested language.

networks.description: Operator names in that country, as the supplier lists them.

covers_via.description: Present when the plan was returned for a country it covers as part of a multi-country plan: the plan's own region name.

ip_breakout.description: Country whose internet connection the customer appears to use (IP breakout), ISO code(s) — matters for banking apps, streaming and mainland-China access. Vendor fact.

coverage_note.description: Coverage caveat to present verbatim, e.g. traffic routed via Hong Kong.

data_gb.description: Data amount in GB. Meaning given by data_period.

data_period.description: "total": data_gb is the whole plan (Data Pack). "per_day": data_gb is the daily full-speed allowance (Unlimited Flex).

data.description: Data Pack: total data label, e.g. "5GB".

daily_high_speed.description: Unlimited Flex: daily allowance at full speed, e.g. "2GB"; "unlimited" = unlimited data every day at full speed (fair-use policy).

always_on_rate.description: Unlimited Flex: reduced speed after the daily allowance, e.g. "512 Kbit/s". Empty when the plan is unlimited.

fair_use.description: Fair-use policy text from the supplier, when stated.

network_generation.description: Network technology, e.g. "4G/LTE/5G". Never an operator name.

networks.description: Operator names across the plan (deduplicated). Per-country detail is in coverage_countries.

days_range.description: Unlimited Flex: choosable durations in days, "1-365".

activation_trigger.description: "install": validity and billing start the moment the eSIM is installed — install only when ready to use. "first_connection": the eSIM can be installed before travel; validity starts on first connection to a network at the destination.

install_before_travel.description: true when the eSIM can safely be installed before departure (activation_trigger first_connection).

unused_valid_days.description: Days the eSIM may remain unused after purchase before it expires (supplier value).

expires_on.description: Stock expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the product itself has one.

voice_sms.description: Always "none": data only, no telephone number, no SMS.

tethering.description: Hotspot / tethering is supported where the network and device allow it (shop rule).

kind.description: What TopUp can add without a new eSIM: data (Data Pack), days (Unlimited Flex), or none.

plan_note.description: One-sentence vendor fact to present verbatim when present; overrides the generic type description.

transparency.description: A per-order Transparency link shows remaining data in near real-time.

price.description: Price in currency, read WITH price_basis: the full price of the plan when "total", the price of ONE day when "per_day". Never a per-GB rate. The price shown is the price paid.

price_30_days.description: Only on price_basis "per_day": the price for 30 days with the duration discount applied — the reference figure to quote for a stay of about a month. Never infer it by multiplying.

price_max.description: Only on price_basis "per_day": the price for the longest duration in days_range (365 days), discount applied. Never infer it by multiplying.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of every price in this object.

price_is_final.description: Always true: no tax or fee is added at checkout.

pricing_bucket.description: language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in, e.g. "en-us".

rating.description: Average customer rating (1-5). Present only when reviews exist.

review_count.description: Number of reviews. Present only when > 0.

last_updated.description: Date the plan was last updated in the catalogue (YYYY-MM-DD).

url.description: Product page in pricing_bucket. Use verbatim.

message.description: Present when nothing matched: says why and what to try.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to add_to_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to add_to_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

id.description: Cart line GID from get_cart. Pass back to update_cart_lines as line_items[].id to update or remove this line.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

line_price.description: Total price for the line (quantity × unit_price).

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: How many to add. Defaults to 1.

deduped.description: True when this exact add was applied moments ago and was skipped to avoid a duplicate. When true, nothing changed on this call and updated is false.

line_items.description: Items affected by this mutation, with product/variant details filled in from the post-mutation cart.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

resolved_items.description: Present only on the clarification-needed path (nothing was applied). Items that could have been added, with pre-mutation lookup titles when available.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description: Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details. When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions. Some examples of questions you can ask are: - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"]) - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"]) - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

policies.description: Store policies and contact information matching the query.

type.description: Policy kind: refund, shipping, privacy, terms_of_service, terms_of_sale, subscription, legal_notice, or contact.

body.description: The policy text (may contain HTML).

pages.description: Store pages (e.g. FAQ, help) matching the query.

body.description: The page body (may contain HTML) for the top matched pages.

tools.name: imicalculator
tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

CompanyId.description: Identifier of the company/agency to query (optional, defaults to the company’s internal one).

tools.name: loancalculator
tools.description: Calculates financing values for a property, including monthly payments, IMT tax, total loan duration in months, and the total applied interest rate. This endpoint allows customization of parameters such as property value, loan amount, bank spread, Euribor, loan term in years, and whether it is a permanent own residence.

PropertyValue.description: Total purchase price of the property in euros. Used as the basis for IMT and Stamp Duty calculations.

LoanAmount.description: Total amount to be borrowed from the bank (capital). Must be less than or equal to the property value.

Spread.description: The bank's profit margin (spread) as a percentage. Combined with Euribor, it forms the total interest rate (TAN).

EuriborRateMaturity.description: Maturity period of the Euribor applied to the loan. Possible values: 1M (1 month: rate revised monthly), 3M (3 months: rate revised quarterly), 6M (6 months: rate revised semi-annually), 12M (12 months: rate revised annually).

LoanTermYears.description: Loan duration in years. Usually between 5 and 40 years depending on the applicant’s age.

IsPermanentHousing.description: Indicates if the property is for Own Permanent Housing. Affects IMT tax brackets and exemptions in Portugal.

Email.description: User's email address (required if no phone number is provided).

Phone.description: User's phone number (optional if email address is provided).

PhoneCountryCode.description: Phone country code including the plus sign, e.g., "+44" for United Kingdom, "+33" for France, "+49" for Germany.

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Image URL (absolute, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Who Isaac Solomon is: role, availability, location, background, the services he takes on and the clients he's built for. Start here when asked a general question about him.

tools.description: List portfolio projects with year, category, tags and a summary. Optionally filter by a free-text query matched against title, category and tags.

query.description: Filter by title, category or tag, e.g. "e-commerce".

tools.description: Full detail for one project, including its live URL and case study link. Accepts the project title or its slug (from list_projects).

project.description: Project title or slug, e.g. "Mivi" or "saut".

tools.name: list_writing
tools.description: List the case studies and essays, with reading time and year. Optionally filter by a free-text query.

query.description: Filter by title, description or tag.

tools.name: search_site
tools.description: Free-text search across projects, writing, services and work history. Use when you do not know which category an answer lives in.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "SvelteKit" or "RTL".

limit.description: Max results (default 10).

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: How to get in touch with Isaac — email, social links and current availability for work.

tools.name: describe_article
tools.description: What one piece of writing actually covers — its section headings in order, opening paragraph, length and reading time — without pulling the full text. Use this to decide whether an article is worth reading in full. Accepts a slug from list_writing (e.g. 'saut' or 'saut/three-hats') or the title.

article.description: Article slug or title, e.g. 'godrej' or 'saut/three-hats'.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: The complete text of one case study or essay, as markdown-style prose with its headings. Use when you need to quote it or answer detail questions; prefer describe_article first if you only need to know what it covers.

article.description: Article slug or title, e.g. 'mivi' or 'saut/worksheet-builder'.

tools.name: list_photos

limit.description: Max results (default 30).

query.description: Đặc điểm bất động sản, KHÔNG phải khu vực (VD: "nhà hẻm xe hơi", "sổ hồng riêng"). Tên tỉnh/quận/phường phải đặt vào tham số location — để ở đây sẽ khớp nhầm sang khu vực trùng chữ.

Ghi đủ tên — "Bình Thạnh" đúng, "1" thì mơ hồ giữa Quận 1 và Phường 1. Khớp cả tên trước và sau sáp nhập 2025, nên "Hồ Chí Minh" bao gồm cả Bình Dương và Bà Rịa – Vũng Tàu cũ; trường address của kết quả có thể vẫn ghi tên tỉnh cũ.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to add_to_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

tools.name: browse_store

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known.
