Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

id.description: Cart line GID from get_cart. Pass back to update_cart as line_items[].id to update or remove this line.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

line_price.description: Total price for the line (quantity × unit_price).

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

deduped.description: True when this exact add was applied moments ago and was skipped to avoid a duplicate. When true, nothing changed on this call and updated is false.

line_items.description: Items added by this mutation, with product/variant details filled in from the post-mutation cart.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

resolved_items.description: Present only on the clarification-needed path (nothing was applied). Items that could have been added, with pre-mutation lookup titles when available.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description: Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details. When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions. Some examples of questions you can ask are: - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"]) - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"]) - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

policies.description: Store policies and contact information matching the query.

type.description: Policy kind: refund, shipping, privacy, terms_of_service, terms_of_sale, subscription, legal_notice, or contact.

body.description: The policy text (may contain HTML).

pages.description: Store pages (e.g. FAQ, help) matching the query.

body.description: The page body (may contain HTML) for the top matched pages.

site_url.description: The site to check, as the user gave it (domain or URL).

email.description: Email for the report. Only an address the user gave in this conversation; leave it out otherwise.

path.description: coding_agent: build the tools in the user's codebase (default). hosted_scan: scan the live site and get suggested tools.

coding_agent.description: The coding agent the user works with; 'other' for any agent not listed.

site_url.description: The user's site as they gave it. Used by hosted_scan.

tools.name: search_webmcp_guides

type.description: Only this kind of content. resource = curated external docs, tools and videos.

tools.name: get_benchmark_results
tools.description: Returns WindTunnel benchmark results comparing WebMCP agents with screenshot, page-structure and code-running agents on the same tasks. Use when the user asks whether WebMCP is faster, cheaper or more reliable, or how an AI model performs.

model.description: AI model as the user names it, e.g. 'Claude' or 'gpt-5.6'. Matches every tested model that contains it.

interface.description: Only this way of operating the website.

tools.name: record_unsupported_request
tools.description: Notes a request that none of this site's other tools can handle, so the webmcp.com team can decide what to build next. Use only as a last resort, e.g. editing or removing a directory entry or exporting data. Then tell the user it was noted and that no tool exists for it yet.

request.description: The user's request in their own words.

interpreted_goal.description: Your one-line reading of what the user is ultimately trying to do.

tools.name: suggest_resource

email.description: Contact email for the person suggesting it.

sites.name: 1001parts.nl
sites.description: Agricultural, garden and engine replacement parts from Van der Perk.

tools.name: searchProducts
tools.description: Search the 1001Parts catalog of agricultural & garden spare parts. The query can be a part number - a Bestelnummer (order number) or an OEM Artikelnummer (manufacturer part number), with or without separators - or free-text keywords (brand, machine, part). Returns matching parts with the shop's headline price (EUR EXCL. VAT, with price_incl_vat beside it), part numbers, stock availability (in_stock/out_of_stock, or price_on_request when the shop quotes no price) and a link. Narrow with the optional filters, order with 'sort' (relevance/price/newest), and page through results with 'offset' (the response's 'more_available' flag says whether another page exists).

query.description: Part number or keywords, e.g. 'AL120024' or 'john deere hydrauliekfilter'.

category.description: categories_id from listCategories (optional).

min_price.description: Minimum price in EUR excl. VAT (price-on-request parts are excluded when a range is set).

max_price.description: Maximum price in EUR excl. VAT (price-on-request parts are excluded when a range is set).

in_stock.description: If true, only return in-stock parts.

limit.description: Max results, 1-24 (default 12).

sort.description: Result order (default relevance).

offset.description: Skip this many results for pagination, 0-240 (default 0).

tools.name: getProductDetails
tools.description: Get full details for one 1001Parts part, looked up by numeric productId, Bestelnummer (model), or EAN barcode. Returns price, Bestelnummer (model), Artikelnummer (mpn), EAN, availability, description and link. productId and Bestelnummer are unique to 1001Parts, so each identifies exactly one part. EAN is the global barcode (GTIN) and is usually unique but can occasionally be shared - when shared, the primary match is returned. The response also includes the OEM Artikelnummer (mpn), but mpn is NOT a lookup key here because manufacturer part numbers can collide across brands and are only filled for some parts.

model.description: Bestelnummer (order number), unique to this shop.

tools.name: listCategories
tools.description: Browse the 1001Parts category tree (Landbouw, Tuin & Park, Motoren, Aandrijftechniek, banden & wielen, bevestigingsmateriaal, olie en vetten, ...). With no argument it returns the shop's top-level sections; pass a category id as 'parent' to list its sub-categories. Each result has id, name and has_children (whether you can drill in further). Use a category id as the 'category' filter in searchProducts.

parent.description: Category id to list children of. Omit for the top-level sections.

tools.name: getFilterOptions
tools.description: Describe the filters searchProducts accepts (category, price range, in-stock) and their allowed values.

tools.name: getStoreInfo
tools.description: Get orientation facts about the 1001Parts store: a Dutch webshop for agricultural & garden spare parts (parts for tractors, garden & park machinery and engines), where parts are identified by Bestelnummer (always present) and often an OEM Artikelnummer, that most parts ship within 1-2 working days (rush service available) AND that it has a physical counter/warehouse in Beesd, NL (right next to the A2 motorway, free parking), plus currency, homepage URL, current promotions and policy links. Read-only; no personal data.

tools.name: getCartContents
tools.description: Return the items in THIS shopper's cart (name, chosen quantity, price incl. VAT), the item count, the subtotal, any automatic discounts that currently apply and the discounted subtotal. May also include 'offers' nudges (e.g. spend a little more to unlock a promo). Excludes shipping, which is calculated at checkout. Session-scoped; contains no personal data.

tools.name: getCheckoutUrl
tools.description: Return the URL where the shopper completes checkout on 1001Parts (the site's own checkout page), plus the current cart summary. Use this to hand the shopper off to finish their order themselves - this tool does NOT check out and collects no address or payment details.

tools.name: addToCart
tools.description: Add a part to THIS shopper's 1001Parts cart by product id. Asks the shopper to confirm before adding anything, and returns the updated cart. Does not check out.

quantity.description: Quantity to add, 1-99 (default 1).

tools.name: siteSearch
tools.description: Open the 1001Parts search results page for a keyword, so the shopper sees the live, filterable listing of parts. This navigates the browser to the results page. To get structured product data back - price, EAN, stock availability - call searchProducts instead.

keyword.description: Zoek op artikelnummer, ook met streepjes of spaties

sites.name: actmorehuman.com
sites.description: Make ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok sound natural. Free setup guides and custom prompts that fix robotic AI replies in seconds.

tools.name: search_guides
tools.description: Search this site's guides about making AI-written text sound human: which tells give AI writing away, how to fix them, and how to set up each AI assistant. Returns matching guide titles, summaries and slugs, ranked by relevance, without the full text. Use it to answer a visitor's question about AI writing, then call get_guide for the one you want to read. Returns an empty list with a note when nothing matches.

query.description: What to search for, in the visitor's own words.

limit.description: How many results to return. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Fetch the full text of one guide by its slug, as returned by search_guides. Returns the guide's title, summary, body and URL. Use it after search_guides when you need the detail to answer accurately rather than the summary. Fails if no guide has that slug.

slug.description: The guide slug, exactly as search_guides returned it.

tools.name: list_assistants
tools.description: List the AI assistants this site has setup instructions for: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok and Copilot. Returns each one's id, display name and which platforms have written steps. Pass compare with two or more ids to get them side by side instead. Use it when a visitor asks which assistants are supported, or how two of them differ.

compare.description: Assistant ids to compare side by side. Omit to list them all.

tools.name: get_setup_steps
tools.description: Get the step-by-step instructions for applying a custom voice prompt to one AI assistant, optionally for a specific platform such as "Web & Desktop" or "iOS & Android". Returns numbered steps with any links, plus the date the steps were last checked. Use it when a visitor asks how to install or apply their prompt. Returns covered: false when nobody has written steps for that combination, which means you should say so rather than guessing.

platform.description: Platform label, exactly as list_assistants reports it. Omit for the default steps.

Returns each question with its exact option ids and labels, and whether it takes one answer or several. Call this before build_humanizer_prompt so you use real option ids instead of guessing at them. Takes no arguments.

tools.name: build_humanizer_prompt

Every field is optional and sensible defaults fill the rest, so pass only what the visitor actually asked for. Call get_wizard_options first to get valid option ids. Returns the finished prompt text, ready to copy.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List what this site sells, with current prices: the Rollout Pack, the Voice Review, the Company Voice engagement and the one-to-one consultation. Only products currently on sale are returned, so the list may be short. Pass configuration to price a Company Voice engagement including add-ons. Use it whenever a visitor asks about cost, or before start_checkout to confirm a product is available.

consultantHours.description: Additional consultant hours, billed per hour, capped at 10.

configuration.description: Only for pricing a Company Voice engagement. Omit to list the catalogue.

tools.name: start_checkout

Creates a Stripe checkout session and returns its URL, where the visitor enters payment details and completes the purchase themselves. This tool never takes payment and never completes an order. Confirm the product and price with list_products first, and check the visitor actually wants to buy before calling it.

product.description: Which product to buy.

email.description: The buyer's email, used to prefill Stripe and deliver the purchase.

sites.name: aicertificates.study
sites.description: Original practice questions written to the published exam blueprints, with every answer option explained including the wrong ones. First form free, no signup.

tools.name: list_exams
tools.description: The Claude certifications covered here, with exam codes, item counts, fees and the full domain list with published weights. Call this first to get valid exam slugs.

tools.name: get_practice_question
tools.description: Returns one original practice question with its options and no answer key. Present it to the user and let them choose before calling check_answer. Pass every id already served in exclude_ids — this server is stateless and remembers nothing.

domain.description: Optional domain id (e.g. "d3") to drill one area. Domain ids come from list_exams.

exclude_ids.description: Question ids already served in this session, so they are not repeated.

tools.name: my_progress
tools.description: Their recorded history for one exam, broken down by blueprint domain with the weakest first. Call this at the start of a study session to decide what to drill, and after a run of questions to show what moved. Only a signed-in account has history; anonymous callers are told so rather than shown zeros.

tools.name: open_study
tools.description: Open or resume the study page for an exam, optionally focused on a domain or a sub-objective. Use this when someone asks to study rather than to be quizzed in chat: the page gives them a visible question they answer themselves, and once it is open a richer set of tools appears for reading and steering that screen. Returns the URL; a browser agent should navigate there.

domain.description: Optional blueprint domain, e.g. "d3".

sub_objective.description: Optional concept, e.g. "d1.5". Ids are per-exam.

tools.name: check_answer
tools.description: Grades the user's choice and returns an explanation for EVERY option, including the ones they did not pick. On this exam two options are frequently defensible and only one is credited, so the reasons the wrong options lose are the part worth teaching.

selected.description: Option letters the user chose, e.g. ["B"] or ["B","D"].

tools.name: get_screen
tools.description: What the person is looking at right now in the practice player: the question, its options, which they have selected, and how far through the form they are. Before they commit to an answer this deliberately does NOT include the answer key — you are coaching, not solving. Call this before answering any question about 'this question' or 'the one on screen'.

tools.name: explain_current
tools.description: The full reasoning for the question on screen: why the credited option wins and why each other option loses. Refuses until the person has committed to an answer, because the explanations name the correct option.

tools.name: present_question
tools.description: Put a specific question from this form on the person's screen — the one you think they need next. To follow up a specific miss, pass related_to_question_id: it finds another item testing the SAME blueprint sub-objective, which is the grain at which someone actually fails. A domain is far too coarse for that; d1 is seventeen percent of the exam. Falls back to the same domain when this form has no sibling for that concept, and tells you which it did. You must say why you chose it; that reason is shown to them on the page, so write it for them to read.

related_to_question_id.description: Follow up this item, e.g. "u1-d1-09". Prefers another question on the same sub-objective; falls back to the same domain and says so.

domain.description: Blueprint domain id, e.g. "d3". Ignored when related_to_question_id is given.

sub_objective.description: Target a concept directly, e.g. "d1.5". Get these from get_screen.

only_unanswered.description: Skip items they have already committed to. Default true.

reason.description: One sentence, addressed to them, on why this question next.

tools.name: get_session_progress
tools.description: How this sitting is going, by blueprint domain: answered, correct, and accuracy for the questions committed so far in this form. Use it to decide what to review, not to predict an exam score — a single form is a small sample.

tools.name: book_meeting
tools.description: Book a 30-minute Talk to Sales call with Atlan on the team's cal.com calendar at the slot the user picked, and record the contact in HubSpot. Ask the user for basic details first: first name, last name and work email (required), plus company and what they want to discuss (optional). Call only after the user has explicitly confirmed the slot. Required: startTime, exactly as returned by get_meeting_slots. Contact fields (firstname, lastname, email, company, interest) may be passed directly; when omitted, the details staged by fill_lead_form are used. Returns a confirmation like { ok: true, startTime, endTime, meetingUrl, host, hubspotForm }; the user also gets a calendar invite by email.

startTime.description: The chosen slot's startTime, exactly as returned by get_meeting_slots (ISO 8601).

firstname.description: First name. Falls back to the lead staged by fill_lead_form.

lastname.description: Last name. Falls back to the staged lead.

email.description: Work email address. Falls back to the staged lead.

interest.description: What the user wants to discuss, in their words (optional).

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the attendee. Defaults to the visitor's browser timezone.

tools.name: fill_lead_form
tools.description: Validate and stage the user's contact details for Atlan's talk-to-sales flow, and prefill the human-visible form. Required: firstname, lastname, email (work email). Optional: company, interest. This tool NEVER submits anything — after staging, ask the user to explicitly confirm, then call submit_lead_form. Returns the staged summary or the list of invalid fields.

interest.description: What the user is interested in, in their words (optional).

tools.name: get_atlan_resources

tools.name: get_meeting_slots
tools.description: Show live availability for a 30-minute Talk to Sales call with Atlan, read from the team's cal.com calendar. Use this when the user wants to book time with Atlan: call it first to get open slots, let the user pick one, then call book_meeting with that slot's startTime. Optional: days (how far ahead to search, 1-14, default 7), timezone (IANA name; defaults to the visitor's own). Read-only: reserves nothing. Returns JSON {host, durationMinutes, timezone, daysSearched, days: [{date, slots: [{startTime, label}]}]}.

days.description: How many days ahead to search (1-14). Default 7.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the labels, e.g. America/New_York. Defaults to the visitor's browser timezone.

Includes minimum-stay restrictions where the property supplies them. `available: null` is unpublished (not unknown-but-bookable) and sets `partial_calendar` / `cannot_confirm_stay` when mixed with published nights. `open_for_booking` is the catalog/HDP gate — dated HMS nights can still exist when it is false; see `catalog_vs_hms`. pickup_address.description: Full pickup address (e.g. 'CDG Terminal 2E' or street address)

num_hours.description: Number of hours (required for hourly, min 3)

tools.name: book_ride
tools.description: Create a secure payment link to book a private chauffeur transfer. The reservation is created automatically ONLY after the customer completes payment. REQUIRED: call get_quote first and pass the resulting quote_id + the chosen vehicle_id. The price is taken from the stored quote (not from any price field you pass). Pass idempotency_key to make retries safe: the same key returns the same payment link instead of creating a duplicate.

quote_id.description: quote_id returned by get_quote. Must be passed. Expired quote (>15 min) requires a fresh get_quote.

vehicle_id.description: Vehicle ID chosen from the get_quote results

flight_number.description: Flight number for airport pickups (e.g. AF123)

idempotency_key.description: Optional agent-generated key (e.g. UUID) to deduplicate retries. Same key + same params returns the same payment link for 24 h. Same key + different params returns an IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT error.

channel.description: Caller channel identifier for observability. If omitted, the channel stored with the quote (from get_quote) is used.

tools.name: book_meetgreet
tools.description: Create a secure payment link for a VIP Meet & Greet booking, with optional transfer combo. M&G prices are FIXED (CDG/Orly 250€ base for 2 pax + 50€/extra, Gare du Nord 500€ per STARTED group of 2 pax (1-2=500€, 3-4=1000€, 5-6=1500€), Gare de Lyon 350€ + 75€/extra) — do NOT call get_quote for the M&G part. A connection (service_type='connection': arrival flight → connecting departure flight with fast-track between terminals) is billed as TWO M&G services = the location price ×2 (e.g. CDG 2 pax = 500€). For a combo with a transfer (e.g. CDG M&G + transfer to a hotel), call get_quote first for the transfer leg and pass the resulting quote_id + vehicle_id in `transfer`. If lead time is below the minimum (12h before pickup; 48h for Gare du Nord), returns LEAD_TIME_TOO_SHORT — the caller must fall back to manual notification instead of retrying. lead_time_override=true bypasses the 12h minimum ONLY after Sylvain has explicitly confirmed greeter availability for this exact request (WhatsApp admin approval 'mg ok'); never set it on your own initiative. Not available for Gare du Nord; a 90-minute floor always applies. If flight cannot be validated, returns FLIGHT_NOT_FOUND — ask the customer to re-confirm the flight number, or set flight_unverified=true with manual_airline + manual_origin to force-accept.

location.description: M&G location. cdg/orly = airport, gare_du_nord/gare_de_lyon = train station.

service_type.description: arrival (pickup at airport/station), departure (drop-off + greeter for check-in), connection (transit: arrival flight → connecting departure flight; billed as 2 M&G services = location price ×2).

flight_number.description: Flight number for airports (AF1234) or train/Eurostar number for stations.

pickup_time.description: HH:MM in Paris time. For arrivals this is the flight/train arrival time; for departures the time the greeter meets the client.

children.description: Number of children (in addition to adults).

bags.description: Number of bags (used for vehicle sizing when combo transfer).

email.description: Client email — used for booking confirmation and Stripe receipt.

additional_info.description: Free-text notes (special requests, tail number for private aviation, etc.).

train_pnr.description: Eurostar / TGV reservation reference (PNR). Required when location is gare_du_nord or gare_de_lyon.

train_coach.description: Train coach number. Required for train stations.

train_seat.description: Train seat number(s). Required for train stations.

quote_id.description: quote_id from a prior get_quote call covering the transfer leg (e.g. CDG → Le Bristol).

vehicle_id.description: Vehicle ID chosen from that quote.

transfer_pickup_time.description: HH:MM — time the chauffeur picks up the client AFTER the greeter has escorted them out. Usually 30-60min after the greeter_time (pickup_time).

transfer.description: Optional combo: bundles a private transfer in the same Stripe Checkout session. Generates 2 line items + 2 Zeplan bookings (M&G + transfer).

flight_unverified.description: Set true only if the client confirmed the flight after AeroDataBox couldn't validate it. Requires manual_airline + manual_origin.

manual_airline.description: Required if flight_unverified=true. The airline name as stated by the client.

manual_origin.description: Required if flight_unverified=true. Departure city as stated by the client.

manual_arrival_time.description: Optional. Local arrival time as stated by the client.

idempotency_key.description: Optional UUID for safe retries. Same key returns the same payment_url for 24h.

lead_time_override.description: Bypass the 12h minimum lead time. ONLY when Sylvain has explicitly approved this exact booking after manually confirming greeter availability ('mg ok' admin flow) — never on client insistence. Refused for gare_du_nord; hard 90-minute floor.

channel.description: Caller channel identifier for observability (whatsapp, chatbot, mcp-direct, ...).

query.description: Free-text location. Examples: 'CDG', 'Charles de Gaulle Terminal 2E', 'Hotel Le Bristol Paris', 'Gare du Nord', '15 rue de la Paix Paris', '48.8566, 2.3522'.

flight_number.description: Flight number in any format: 'AF007', 'AF 007', 'af-7', 'AFR007'. Server normalizes.

tools.name: resolve_train

sites.name: pixlpal.com
sites.description: PixlPal — AI-assisted photo editing. The AI never generates the photo, it only applies filters.

tools.name: set_operations
tools.description: Turn one or more editing knobs. Parameters you pass are merged into the current edit, so you can nudge a single value without restating the rest; omitting `params` entirely enables the operation at its default strength. Optional `mask` (from a prior segment, create_mask, or invert_mask call) limits the op to that region. Prefer invert_mask when the user wants edits on everything except a subject; `invertMask: true` on this tool is a quick alternative that does not create a selectable complement mask. `maskStrength` (0..1, default 1) softens how hard the mask applies without changing the op's own amount — use it to dial in local edits. For local lighten/darken prefer dodge_burn with a range (shadows|midtones| highlights) plus a mask; prefer shadows_highlights for whole-frame shadow/ highlight recovery; keep exposure for whole-frame EV. Prefer blacks_whites for endpoint clip/crush (the black and white points) rather than the broad shadows/highlights bands. Prefer hsl_mixer (no mask) for 'make the grass pop' and other color-of-things requests. Operations and their parameter ranges: - exposure (Brightens or darkens the whole image in photographic stops.) amount -1..1 - contrast (Expands or compresses tones around middle gray.) amount -1..1 - shadows_highlights (Opens or recovers shadows and highlights independently (Lightroom-style). Prefer for whole-frame tonal recovery.) shadows -1..1, highlights -1..1 - tone_curve (Remaps tones through a named response curve.) preset one of linear|soft|hard|film - blacks_whites (Moves the black and white points. Negative blacks crush shadows; positive lifts them. Positive whites stretch brights and can clip; negative pulls the white point in. Prefer over shadows_highlights when you want the endpoints, not the broad bands.) blacks -1..1, whites -1..1 - dodge_burn (Lightens (dodge) or darkens (burn) a tonal range — shadows, midtones, or highlights. Best used with a mask for local edits.) amount -1..1, range one of shadows|midtones|hig…

mask.description: Mask id returned by segment, create_mask, or invert_mask.

invertMask.description: When true, apply the op outside the mask without creating a complement mask. Prefer invert_mask when both the subject and its surroundings need separate selectable edits.

maskStrength.description: 0..1 scale on the mask before invert. Requires mask. Default 1.

tools.name: remove_operations
tools.description: Switch operations off entirely, removing them from the edit. Use this rather than setting a parameter to zero when the user wants an effect gone.

tools.name: reset_edits
tools.description: Clear every adjustment and return to the untouched original photo.

tools.name: get_image_stats
tools.description: Measure the photo currently open in the editor: brightness, black and white points, clipping, saturation and color cast. Returns precise numbers to complement the preview image attached to each user message. Call this when you need quantitative measurements (for example exact clipping or color-cast values).

tools.name: segment
tools.description: Find a subject in the open photo by referring expression and create a mask. Use this for discrete nameable objects (a dress, a person, a car). For tonal or positional areas (bright sky, the top of the frame) prefer create_mask. For 'make the grass pop' prefer hsl_mixer, not segmentation. Returns a maskId you then pass to set_operations via `mask`, or to invert_mask to select everything else. Runs fully on-device; no pixels leave the device. If segmentation fails, fall back to a global edit and say so.

prompt.description: Referring expression, e.g. "the red dress" or "the sky".

tools.name: set_frame
tools.description: Reframe the photo non-destructively: rotate in 90-degree steps and/or crop. The crop only trims the frame — it cannot remove an object from the middle of the picture; if a subject the user wants gone is not near an edge, say so instead of cropping. Rotation is absolute and clockwise; an existing crop follows the rotation. The crop rectangle is normalized (0..1 fractions of the rotated frame). Three ways to crop, use exactly one per call: (1) `subjectMaskId` from a prior segment call, plus optional `aspect` and `padding` — fits the crop around that subject; this is the right tool for 'crop to portrait, centered on the person' (segment first, then set_frame). (2) `aspect` alone — largest centered crop with that shape, e.g. '4:5' portrait, '1:1' square, '16:9' wide, '9:16' story, 'original'. (3) explicit `crop` rect when you know exact fractions from looking at the preview (the preview you see is always the full uncropped frame; the crop shows there as a brighter window). Pass `crop: null` to clear the crop, `rotate: 0` to clear rotation.

crop.description: Explicit normalized crop rect in the rotated frame, or null to remove the crop.

subjectMaskId.description: Mask id from segment/invert_mask; the crop is fitted around this subject.

padding.description: Margin around the subject as a fraction of its size. Default 0.15; use more for loose framing.

tools.name: invert_mask
tools.description: Create a selectable mask that is the inverse of an existing mask from segment. Use after segment when the user wants edits on everything except a subject, for example 'blur everything except the person' or 'emphasize this object' (boost the subject mask, then de-emphasize the inverse). Returns a new maskId for set_operations. Prefer this over set_operations invertMask:true when both the subject and its surroundings need their own edits.

maskId.description: Mask id returned by a prior segment call.

tools.name: create_mask
tools.description: Create an engine-computed area mask without running segmentation. Use luminance_range for tonal areas ('the bright sky', 'crushed shadows'). Use linear_gradient or radial_gradient for positional areas ('the top of the image', 'the corners', 'the center'). Use color_range when a non-color op must hit a hue ('sharpen just the greens'); for 'make the grass pop' prefer hsl_mixer with no mask instead. Returns a maskId for set_operations / invert_mask. Evaluated on the original photo, so it stays put as other sliders move.

type.description: luminance_range, color_range, linear_gradient, or radial_gradient.

id.description: Optional mask id. Defaults to luma, color, gradient, or radial.

feather.description: Edge softness as a fraction of the shorter side. Default 0.02.

softness.description: Falloff 0..1 for luminance_range, color_range, and radial_gradient.

range.description: color_range: full-inclusion half-width in degrees. Default 25.

satMin.description: color_range: exclude pixels below this saturation. Default 0.08.

y0.description: linear_gradient: start Y 0..1 (0 is the top).

tools.name: get_edit_state
tools.description: Read the current state of the PixlPal editor: whether a photo is open, the declarative pipeline of active operations (the same JSON shown in the editor's pipeline panel), the masks available for local edits, and whether undo/redo are available. Call this first to see what the user and you have done so far before making further edits.

sites.description: Open Steam data API for AI agents and bots: profiles, SteamID converter, FACEIT, friends. No API key, markdown and JSON output, agent-friendly.

tools.name: steam_summary
tools.description: Steam player overview in one call. presets: include=[] equals full; for competitive checks pass include ["faceit","bans"]. Responses carry provenance.fresh and sources/partial - branch on them. Overview: Steam summary, Steam ban status (VAC/game/community), SteamID conversions, FACEIT stats and the first 100 friends. include LIMITS the response to the blocks you list: omit it for everything, ["steam"] for the Steam block only (cheapest), ["bans"] for a ban check only, ["faceit","bans"] to drop the friend list. friends_limit caps the friend list (default 100).

id.description: any SteamID format: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id, a steamcommunity.com link or a vanity name

include.description: restricts the response to the listed blocks; omit for bans+faceit+friends. Example: ["bans"] returns the Steam summary plus ban status only

friends_limit.description: max friends in the response, default 100

friends_detail.description: friend entry shape, default full; short/medium are much smaller

tools.name: steam_bans
tools.description: Steam ban status of a player: VACBanned, NumberOfVACBans, NumberOfGameBans, DaysSinceLastBan, CommunityBanned, EconomyBan - fields exactly as Steam reports them. First thing to check when reviewing a cheating report. Unresolvable ids or an unavailable upstream return an error result, never guessed data.

id.description: any SteamID format: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id, a steamcommunity.com link or a vanity name

tools.name: steam_profile
tools.description: Steam summary only (raw GetPlayerSummaries object + SteamID conversions). Cheapest profile tool; data no older than 48 hours, unknown profiles are fetched live from Steam. Private profiles return the public subset of fields (not an error); unresolvable ids return an error result.

id.description: any SteamID format: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id, a steamcommunity.com link or a vanity name

tools.name: steam_convert
tools.description: SteamID converter: turns one identifier into EVERY other form, instantly. Accepts steamid64, STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex (110000...), steam:hex (FiveM), a 32-bit account id or a steamcommunity.com/profiles/ link. Returns steamid64 (dec and hex), SteamID, legacy STEAM_0 form, SteamID3, account id, steam:hex and the profile URL. CHEAPEST TOOL - prefer it over steam_identity whenever you only need format conversion. Vanity names (steamcommunity.com/id/name) are not a computable format: use steam_identity for those.

id.description: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id or a /profiles/ link. NOT a vanity name

tools.name: steam_identity
tools.description: Pure identifier resolver: steamid64, SteamID (STEAM_1:0:x), SteamID3 ([U:1:x]), steam hex, vanity name and profile URL. No profile data - fewest tokens. If the id cannot be resolved, returns an error result with a machine-readable message - never a partial guess.

id.description: any SteamID format: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id, a steamcommunity.com link or a vanity name

tools.name: steam_friends
tools.description: Known friends of a player from the platform's snapshot of the public Steam friend graph (cache only, no live Steam call; the snapshot can be partial). detail picks token cost: short - steamid64 array, medium - steamid64 + personaname, full - raw Steam objects. Use short unless you need names.

id.description: any SteamID format: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id, a steamcommunity.com link or a vanity name

limit.description: max friends to return, default 100

tools.name: steam_faceit
tools.description: FACEIT player object (nickname, country, per-game skill level and ELO) plus known FACEIT bans. Players without a FACEIT account return an error result saying so - absence of FACEIT data is reported explicitly, never silently.

id.description: any SteamID format: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id, a steamcommunity.com link or a vanity name

tools.name: steam_batch
tools.description: Up to 100 Steam profiles in one call. When you need several players, ALWAYS use this instead of per-player calls - one batch of 100 costs one request. Accepts any SteamID format as STRINGS - steamid64, STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id or a /profiles/ link. Never send them as JSON numbers (a 17-digit number loses precision and points at another account) and note that vanity names are not supported here - resolve those with steam_identity first. Players unknown to the platform come back in not_found - fetch those with steam_profile. include can add FACEIT (one query for the batch) and Steam bans (one upstream call for the batch) - the cheapest way to review a full match roster.

ids.description: steamid64 list, max 100 - prefer one batch over per-player calls

include.description: extra blocks per player: faceit level/ELO, Steam ban status

tools.name: steam_compare
tools.description: Two players side by side: identity, account age, visibility, Steam bans, FACEIT and shared friends (compared over the full friend lists). HEAVIEST tool - it builds two summaries plus both friend graphs; for a single player prefer steam_summary.

id1.description: any SteamID format: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id, a steamcommunity.com link or a vanity name

id2.description: any SteamID format: steamid64 (17 digits), STEAM_1:0:x, STEAM_0:0:x, [U:1:x], hex, steam:hex, a 32-bit account id, a steamcommunity.com link or a vanity name

sites.name: 09city.co.kr
sites.description: Online retailer of tools and hardware.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: 1card.in
sites.description: NFC business cards and digital networking products from 1Card.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Compatibility search across verified 1Card catalogue text and structured material, category, colour, build, Pop family, connection method, customization, box contents, and use-case fields. Returns all matching public products up to 100; use find_products for deterministic filters. Product pages remain final for live price and stock.

query.description: Text found in a product title or a structured catalogue field.

tools.name: get_store_config
tools.description: Read public 1Card store configuration: free-shipping threshold, standard shipping cost, and cash-on-delivery availability. Values are null when the commerce backend is temporarily unavailable.

tools.name: get_product_catalog
tools.description: Read the structured 1Card agent catalog of active NFC business card products with indicative pricing and availability. Follow each product URL for final live public details.

tools.name: find_products
tools.description: Filter the complete public 1Card catalogue using verified structured facts. Exact filters cover material, category, controlled colour/finish, the explicitly named Pop family, stock, displayed price, logo customization, NFC/QR/LED, built-in RFID blocking, and an included RFID-blocking sleeve. Built-in RFID blocking and an included sleeve are deliberately separate. Null fields mean the source does not prove the fact.

color.description: Exact controlled finish value such as Gold, Golden, Rose Gold, or Matte White; aliases are not merged.

product_family.description: Verified family currently derived only from the exact YIMSYS-synced '1Card Pop ...' product-name prefix.

price.description: Exact catalogue price; products with ranges or unknown prices do not match.

rfid_blocking_product.description: Built-in RFID blocking explicitly proven by the controlled product use-case field; this is not an included sleeve.

rfid_blocking_sleeve_included.description: Whether structured box contents explicitly include an RFID Blocking Sleeve.

tools.name: get_product_facts
tools.description: Get the structured facts and explicit unknown fields for one public 1Card product slug. The linked product page remains final for live price and stock.

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: Compare two to five exact 1Card product slugs using the same structured catalogue fields. Missing facts remain null and missing slugs are reported explicitly.

tools.name: get_store_policy
tools.description: Read current shipping and COD policy with source availability, observation time, age, and current/stale/unknown status. Do not state stale or unavailable policy as current fact.

tools.name: estimate_order
tools.description: Estimate INR shipping and total from a caller-supplied current basket subtotal and current store policy. This is not a checkout quote and never creates a cart or order.

subtotal.description: Current basket item subtotal in INR, before shipping.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. tools.name: search-products

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

url.description: Same-origin image URL (absolute same-origin, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect. Cross-origin URLs are rejected.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: almangmarket.co.kr
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.
