tools.description: Go to another DomainValuator page: home, login, register, dashboard, privacy, or terms. Available on every page. After start_login or start_register, stay on this page and call list_domain_for_sale instead of navigating.

page.description: Destination page of the appraisal and listing journey.

tools.name: valuate_domain
tools.description: Return a structured domain appraisal for one registered domain: estimated market value, TLD, creation date, mozRank, monthly search volume, extracted keywords, and whether the name contains digits or hyphens. This is an asynchronous check: a first call may return status "processing" with retry_after_seconds — wait that long and call again with the same domain. Do not wait inside one call. Read-only; does not list or sell the domain.

domain.description: Fully qualified domain name including TLD. No protocol, path or www. Examples: example.nl, example.com.

tools.name: get_appraisal_methodology
tools.description: Explain how DomainValuator estimates a domain market value: the factors used (age, keywords, search volume, comparable sales, mozRank) and what an appraisal does and does not guarantee. Read-only.

tools.name: start_login
tools.description: Sign the user into their DomainValuator portfolio. Works on /login whether the login or register form is visible: this tool switches to the login form first, then signs in via fetch so this page stays loaded. After success, call list_domain_for_sale on this same page. Never echo the password back.

password.description: Account password. Used only to fill the form; never returned.

tools.name: start_register
tools.description: Create a DomainValuator account. Works on /login whether the login or register form is visible. After success the user is signed in on this same page so list_domain_for_sale can be called immediately. Never echo the password back.

email.description: New account email address, e.g. you@example.com.

password.description: Password, at least 6 characters. Never returned.

tools.name: get_privacy_policy
tools.description: Return the DomainValuator privacy policy text from this page: what personal data is collected, how it is used, and how to contact support. Read-only.

tools.name: get_terms_of_service
tools.description: Return the DomainValuator terms of service from this page: conditions for using the free appraisal tool and related services. Read-only.

sites.name: dooda365.com
sites.description: Online retailer of clothing and fashion accessories.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: dradol.com
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

sites.name: drdew.co.kr
sites.description: Online retailer of cosmetics and skincare.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

email.description: Email address the user authorized for their EasyAIVoice account.

query.description: Optional model name. Leave blank to list the selected library.

library.description: Search the public catalog or private models owned by the signed-in account.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.description: Online retailer of cosmetics and skincare.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: edwardmax.com
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

slug.description: The service slug, for example 'website-design', 'local-seo', or 'google-business-profile'.

tools.name: check_service_area
tools.description: Check whether Egmer Marketing serves a given city or area. Egmer is based in the Denver metro and works with clients nationwide, so this reports both the local relationship and the nationwide answer.

city.description: The city or area the visitor is asking about, for example 'Littleton' or 'Kansas City'.

tools.name: search_faqs
tools.description: Search Egmer Marketing's published answers to common small business marketing questions (websites, SEO, local SEO, Google Business Profile, ads, funnels, conversion). Use this to answer a visitor's question in Egmer's own words rather than guessing.

query.description: The visitor's question or a few keywords from it, for example 'how long does SEO take' or 'google maps ranking'.

tools.name: get_contact_info
tools.description: Get Egmer Marketing's contact details: phone, email, booking page, service area, and the free community. Use when a visitor asks how to reach Egmer or wants to get in touch.

tools.name: get_free_tools
tools.description: List the free, no-signup tools and resources Egmer Marketing offers: an instant website audit, a free homepage redesign snapshot, a lead leak calculator, the Visibility Score, and a resource library. Use this when a visitor is interested but not ready to talk to anyone, or asks whether there is something free they can try first. Prefer this over book_a_call for anyone still deciding.

tools.name: get_industry_page
tools.description: Get the page Egmer Marketing wrote for a specific type of practice or business, when one exists. Egmer specializes in healthcare practices, so dentists, chiropractors, physical therapists, occupational therapists, optometrists, and general medical practices each have a dedicated page. Use this as soon as a visitor says what kind of business they run.

business_type.description: The visitor's line of work in their own words, for example 'dentist', 'chiropractic clinic', or 'I run a physical therapy practice'.

tools.name: book_a_call
tools.description: Open Egmer Marketing's booking page so the visitor can schedule a free discovery call. This navigates the current tab to the booking page; the visitor picks the time themselves. Use only when the visitor has said they want to book or talk to someone.

topic.description: Optional. What the visitor wants to talk about, so the agent can tell them what to expect on the call.

sites.name: ego-ut.com
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: ekcpapro.com
sites.description: Accounting, tax preparation and consultation services from EK CPA Pro.

tools.name: answer_question
tools.description: Answer a visitor's question about EK CPA Professional Accountants, a Whitby, Ontario CPA firm led by Elena Kanter, CPA, CA (personal tax, corporate tax, bookkeeping, payroll, financial statements, incorporation, CRA reviews, advisory, who the firm is a fit for, location, hours, how to get started). ALWAYS use this tool for questions about the firm instead of guessing; it returns the firm's own site content to answer from, and records the question. If nothing is found, it is flagged for the firm to follow up. Note: EK CPA does not quote fees online; a fee is given after a free consultation.

question.description: The visitor's question, in their own words.

email.description: Visitor email, if they want the firm to follow up (optional).

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List the accounting and tax services EK CPA offers (personal tax, corporate tax, bookkeeping and payroll, financial statements and accounting, incorporation and advisory), each with a link. Use when a visitor asks what the firm does, which service fits their situation, or how the firm can help.

tools.name: get_firm_info
tools.description: Get EK CPA's location, phone, office hours, the area served, and how to get started. Use when a visitor asks where the firm is, how to contact it, hours, or how to become a client. The firm does not publish an email address; inquiries go by phone or the contact form. Fees are not listed and are given after a free consultation.

tools.name: contact_ek_cpa
tools.description: Help a visitor send a message or question to EK CPA (a service, a CRA issue, incorporation, pricing, etc.). Fills the firm's contact form for them (opening the contact page if needed). It does NOT send: the visitor checks the form, completes a quick security check and presses "Send message". To send it for them instead, use send_inquiry. Elena reads every message and replies within one business day.

name.description: Visitor full name, if you do not have first and last separately.

topic.description: What they need help with.

message.description: The visitor's question or situation in their own words, 1 to 5 sentences.

question.description: Same as message (kept for older callers).

tools.name: send_inquiry
tools.description: Send a message or free-consultation request to Elena Kanter, CPA, CA at EK CPA on the visitor's behalf. This really sends it: Elena gets it right away and replies personally within one business day, and the visitor gets a confirmation email. Only use real details the visitor gave you, show them the message first, and set visitor_confirmed to true only after they agree. No human-verification step is needed for this tool.

topic.description: What they need help with.

message.description: The visitor's question or situation in their own words, 1 to 5 sentences.

assistant.description: Which AI assistant you are (e.g. chatgpt, claude, gemini, perplexity, copilot).

visitor_confirmed.description: true only after the visitor has seen the exact message and agreed to send it.

tools.name: get_prep_checklist
tools.description: Get EK CPA's self-employed tax prep checklist for Canada (Ontario): what papers to gather for income, expenses, vehicle, home office and equipment, the key payment and filing dates, and what the CRA won't let you claim. Free, no details needed.

tools.name: send_prep_pack
tools.description: Email the visitor EK CPA's free self-employed tax prep pack: a printable checklist (PDF) and an Excel workbook that works out vehicle, home office and HST totals. Ask the visitor for their name and email first, and whether they also want tax tips and deadline reminders by email (only set email_tips_opt_in to true if they say yes). Set visitor_confirmed to true only after they agree. To just read the checklist, use get_prep_checklist. No human-verification step is needed for this tool.

email.description: Visitor email. The files are sent here.

email_tips_opt_in.description: true only if the visitor said yes to tax tips and deadline reminders by email.

assistant.description: Which AI assistant you are (e.g. chatgpt, claude, gemini, perplexity, copilot).

visitor_confirmed.description: true only after the visitor gave their name and email and agreed to have the files emailed.

tools.name: book_consultation
tools.description: Book a FREE 30-minute introductory consultation with Elena at EK CPA. Use when someone wants to talk to an accountant, get a fee quote, switch accountants, deal with a CRA letter, or figure out if incorporation makes sense. Fills the consultation request form for the visitor (opening the contact page if needed). It does NOT send: the visitor checks the form, completes a quick security check and presses "Send message". To send it for them instead, use send_inquiry. No payment information is collected. Elena replies within one business day.

name.description: Visitor full name, if you do not have first and last separately.

topic.description: What they need help with.

message.description: The visitor's question or situation in their own words, 1 to 5 sentences.

sites.name: elephantap.com
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: elisabettarosso.com
sites.description: Wedding photography, planning information and courses from Elisabetta Rosso.

tools.name: sfoglia_matrimoni_per_luogo
tools.description: Cerca matrimoni reali fotografati da Elisabetta Rosso per zona (es. Torino, Lago di Como, Langhe), per venue (es. Villa Balbianello, Reggia di Venaria) o per ambientazione/stile (es. castello, villa, lago, montagna, reggia). Restituisce guide-zona e storie con titolo, venue, URL e descrizione.

luogo.description: Zona o venue, es. "Lago di Como", "Reggia di Venaria", "Langhe". Vuoto = tutte.

ambientazione.description: Stile di location, es. "castello", "villa", "lago", "montagna", "reggia". Vuoto = tutte.

formato.description: guida-zona = landing di area/venue; storia = singolo matrimonio. Default: tutti.

tools.name: elenca_location_matrimonio
tools.description: Elenca le location e i venue dove Elisabetta Rosso ha fotografato matrimoni (Reggia di Venaria, Villa Balbianello, castelli, ville, rifugi di montagna, ecc.), con zona, ambientazione e URL.

ambientazione.description: Filtro opzionale per stile, es. "castello", "villa", "lago". Vuoto = tutte.

tools.name: consiglia_location
tools.description: Consiglia le location/storie piu adatte a una coppia in base a stile (ambientazione), zona, stagione e atmosfera (es. intimo, elegante, informale, invernale). Restituisce una lista ordinata per pertinenza con la motivazione.

tools.name: prova_sociale
tools.description: Restituisce credenziali e prova sociale di Elisabetta Rosso: valutazione e recensioni, esperienza, riconoscimenti e membership internazionali, stampa. Per spiegare a una coppia perche sceglierla.

tools.name: info_prezzi
tools.description: Fornisce la fascia di prezzo indicativa per un matrimonio con Elisabetta Rosso e i fattori che la determinano. Il prezzo finale e personalizzato: per un preventivo reale serve una richiesta con i dettagli.

tools.name: pianifica_timeline_foto
tools.description: Dato il luogo, la data e l'ora della cerimonia, calcola il tramonto e la finestra di luce d'oro per i ritratti, e propone una scaletta foto. Utile per pianificare con lo stile di luce naturale di Elisabetta Rosso.

luogo.description: Luogo o venue, es. "Lago di Como", "Reggia di Venaria", "Bardonecchia".

data.description: Data in formato AAAA-MM-GG (accetta anche GG/MM/AAAA o "12 settembre 2027").

ora_cerimonia.description: Ora di inizio cerimonia, es. "16:00". Opzionale.

tools.name: verifica_disponibilita_data
tools.description: Verifica se Elisabetta Rosso risulta (indicativamente) disponibile in una certa data: disponibile / limitata / occupata / da confermare. La disponibilita e indicativa e va sempre confermata contattandola.

data.description: Data in formato AAAA-MM-GG (accetta anche GG/MM/AAAA o "12 settembre 2027").

tools.name: richiedi_disponibilita
tools.description: Compila la richiesta di contatto/disponibilita per un matrimonio con Elisabetta Rosso. Di default PRECOMPILA il modulo visibile e lo porta in vista, per la conferma dell'utente. Passa invia=true SOLO se l'utente ha gia confermato esplicitamente di voler inviare ora.

data.description: Data del matrimonio, anche solo mese/anno

location.description: Location o citta del matrimonio

invia.description: true SOLO dopo conferma esplicita: invia subito. Default false = precompila soltanto.
