navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: gauravtiwari31.github.io
sites.description: Interactive PID tuning bench with live step response, Bode and root-locus plots, and WebMCP site tools that expose the numeric simulation results to an AI agent.

tools.name: get_system
tools.description: Read the complete current state of the control design: the plant transfer function, the PID gains, the resulting controller and closed-loop transfer functions, whether the loop is stable, all step-response and frequency-domain metrics, and how the design measures up against the active targets. Start here to find out what you are working with.

tools.name: run_step_response
tools.description: Simulate the closed-loop unit-step response and return its exact numeric transient metrics: percent overshoot, rise time, peak value and peak time, 2% settling time, final value and steady-state error. Use this instead of trying to read the step-response plot: the plot is a canvas rendering, so its numbers cannot be recovered visually, and these are the actual simulated values.

include_samples.description: When true, also return about 40 evenly spaced (time in seconds, output) pairs from the response, so the shape of the transient can be inspected directly. Defaults to false, which returns the metrics only.

tools.name: get_frequency_response
tools.description: Return the open-loop stability margins: gain margin in dB and as a linear factor, phase margin in degrees, and both crossover frequencies in rad/s. Both crossovers are located by bisection, so they are exact rather than read off a plot. Use this to judge robustness and how much more gain the loop can tolerate before it goes unstable.

include_samples.description: When true, also return about 30 log-spaced (frequency in rad/s, magnitude in dB, phase in degrees) triples of the open-loop Bode data. Defaults to false, which returns the margins only.

tools.name: get_pole_zero_map
tools.description: Return the closed-loop poles and zeros as exact complex numbers, the damping ratio and natural frequency of the dominant pole, and the critical loop gain at which the system would become unstable. Use this to understand why the transient looks the way it does, or how far the design is from the stability boundary. The pole-zero plot is a canvas rendering, so these values cannot be read off the screen.

tools.name: evaluate_design
tools.description: Check the current design against the active target specification and return, for each target, the measured value, the target, a PASS or FAIL verdict and the signed margin by which it passes or fails, then an overall verdict. Use this to decide whether tuning is finished, and when it is not, to see which requirement is furthest from being met.

tools.name: set_controller_gains
tools.description: Set one or more PID gains on the live page and immediately return the full resulting design report: the new gains, stability, every step-response metric, both stability margins, the closed-loop poles and the spec verdict. Because the post-change metrics come back with the change, one call is enough per tuning iteration. Any parameter left out keeps its current value, so a single gain can be adjusted on its own. The plots on the page redraw as this is applied.

Kp.description: Proportional gain. Raising it speeds up the response and reduces steady-state error, at the cost of more overshoot and less phase margin. Clamped to [-1000, 1000]. Omit to leave unchanged.

Ki.description: Integral gain, in units of 1/s. Any non-zero value drives the steady-state error for a step reference to zero, but adds phase lag and so tends to increase overshoot. Clamped to [-1000, 1000]. Omit to leave unchanged.

Kd.description: Derivative gain, in seconds. Adds phase lead, which damps overshoot and increases phase margin, but amplifies high-frequency content. Clamped to [-1000, 1000]. Omit to leave unchanged.

N.description: Derivative filter pole in rad/s, which makes the derivative term realizable: the term is Kd*N*s/(s+N). Larger N approaches an ideal derivative. Clamped to [1, 10000], default 100. Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: set_plant
tools.description: Replace the plant being controlled, either by naming one of the built-in presets or by giving numerator and denominator coefficients directly, then return the full resulting design report with the current controller applied to the new plant. Use this to try the same controller against a different system, or to enter a specific transfer function.

preset.description: Name of a built-in plant. Give either this or numerator and denominator, not both.

numerator.description: Numerator coefficients in descending powers of s, so [1] is 1 and [-1, 1] is 1 - s. Must be given together with denominator.

denominator.description: Denominator coefficients in descending powers of s, so [1, 0.6, 1] is s^2 + 0.6s + 1. Must have degree at least that of the numerator, and must be given together with numerator.

tools.name: set_design_spec
tools.description: Set the target specification that the controller is being tuned to meet, then return the current design re-evaluated against the new targets. Use this when the user states requirements, so that evaluate_design and every write tool report progress against the right goal. Any target left out keeps its current value.

max_overshoot_percent.description: Largest acceptable percent overshoot of the step response. Must not be negative. Omit to leave unchanged.

max_settling_time_s.description: Largest acceptable 2% settling time in seconds. Must not be negative. Omit to leave unchanged.

max_steady_state_error.description: Largest acceptable absolute steady-state error for a unit step, so 0.02 means 2% of the reference. Must not be negative. Omit to leave unchanged.

min_phase_margin_deg.description: Smallest acceptable open-loop phase margin in degrees; 45 to 60 is a common robustness requirement. Must not be negative. Omit to leave unchanged.

sites.name: ggongnyang-bbyu.com
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

sites.name: gilibookings.com
sites.description: Booking site for ferry, fast boat and transfer tickets to the Gili Islands, plus island hopping, diving, activities, hotels and travel tips.

tools.name: list_locations
tools.description: List the bookable origins and destinations (ports, islands, hotels/areas) on this website. Returns id, name, type and parent_id per location; use the ids as `from`/`to` in search_trips. Sub-locations (parent_id set) can also be given as "parentId_childId".

tools.name: search_trips
tools.description: Search available ferry / fast boat / transfer trips between two locations on a date. Returns trips with idavailability, company, departure/arrival time, seats left and the total price for the given passengers. For a round trip pass type="return" and a return date; the return leg options come back as return_results. Next step: add_trip_to_cart with the chosen idavailability (and return_idavailability).

from.description: Origin location id from list_locations.

to.description: Destination location id from list_locations.

children.description: Number of children (the age band is shown on the site).

infants.description: Number of infants (usually free, still need a name).

seniors.description: Number of seniors — only on sites whose booking context lists the senior passenger type as enabled.

tools.name: add_trip_to_cart
tools.description: Put a trip from search_trips into the booking cart for the given passengers (for a round trip pass the outbound idavailability plus return_idavailability from return_results). Returns the cart, the passenger details that are still required (passenger_requirements) and the checkout status.

return_idavailability.description: idavailability of the return trip (round trips only).

children.description: Number of children (the age band is shown on the site).

infants.description: Number of infants (usually free, still need a name).

seniors.description: Number of seniors — only on sites whose booking context lists the senior passenger type as enabled.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Show the current booking cart: items, total, which contact/passenger details are still required (passenger_requirements with the exact slot ids for set_passenger_details) and whether checkout is possible.

tools.name: remove_from_cart

tools.name: set_passenger_details
tools.description: Provide the booking contact (email, optionally phone) and the details of each passenger in the cart. title.description: MR, MRS, MS, MISS or MSTR — only when the slot lists it.

passport_number.description: Only when the slot lists it.

passport_expiry_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD — only when the slot lists it.

sites.name: gioco.kr
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: go.lmm.best
sites.description: go.lmm.best

tools.name: join_go_match
tools.description: Join the FIFO human-vs-AI Go queue with a real model ID. If no human is waiting, the AI remains queued until a human arrives. Success result: { ok: true, status: "queued" | "matched", revision: integer, latestHumanMessageId: integer, actionRequired: string, ... }. Failure result: { ok: false, error: string, ... }. The page compatibility bridge exposes the formal outputSchema through window.goWebMCP.describeTools().

modelId.description: Required real model identifier, for example openai/gpt-5.6-sol.

tools.name: get_go_game_state
tools.description: Read the phase, revision, action required, compact ASCII board with standard Go coordinates, turn, scoring, messages, captures, and move log. Success result: a phase-discriminated object; playing/finished adds boardSize, board { coordinateSystem, legend, diagram, black, white, emptyCount }, colors, captures, moves, scoring, messages, endReason, and revision. Failure result: { ok: false, error: string, ... }. The page compatibility bridge exposes the formal outputSchema through window.goWebMCP.describeTools().

tools.name: wait_for_go_turn
tools.description: Wait without polling while queued, during setup, or on the human turn. Returns for a new human message, AI action, scoring, game end, room stop, or timeout. Success result: { ok: true, waitStatus: "ready" | "waiting" | "stopped", waitReason: string, phase: string, revision: integer, ... }. Failure result: { ok: false, error: string, ... }. The page compatibility bridge exposes the formal outputSchema through window.goWebMCP.describeTools().

afterRevision.description: Latest revision returned by join_go_match, get_go_game_state, an AI action, or the previous wait result.

afterMessageId.description: Latest human message ID already observed. Pass latestHumanMessageId to catch newer human chat without changing the game revision; if omitted, waiting starts from the current message.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum wait before returning a harmless still-waiting result.

tools.name: play_go_move
tools.description: Play a legal AI move using exactly one standard Go coordinate such as D4 or Q16; columns omit I. Do not send x/y fields. Success result: { ok: true, revision: integer, latestHumanMessageId: integer, phase: "playing" | "finished" }. Failure result: { ok: false, error: string, ... }. The page compatibility bridge exposes the formal outputSchema through window.goWebMCP.describeTools().

coordinate.description: Required standard Go coordinate. Use a letter A-H or J-T plus row 1-19; x/y fields are not accepted.

expectedRevision.description: Revision returned by get_go_game_state.

tools.name: pass_go_turn
tools.description: Pass the AI turn using the latest revision. Two consecutive passes finish and score the game. Success result: { ok: true, revision: integer, latestHumanMessageId: integer, phase: "playing" | "finished" }. Failure result: { ok: false, error: string, ... }. The page compatibility bridge exposes the formal outputSchema through window.goWebMCP.describeTools().

expectedRevision.description: Revision returned by get_go_game_state.

tools.name: resign_go_game
tools.description: Resign the current game using the latest revision. Success result: { ok: true, revision: integer, latestHumanMessageId: integer, phase: "finished" }. Failure result: { ok: false, error: string, ... }. The page compatibility bridge exposes the formal outputSchema through window.goWebMCP.describeTools().

expectedRevision.description: Revision returned by get_go_game_state.

tools.name: respond_go_scoring
tools.description: Accept or reject the human scoring request using its latest revision. Acceptance ends the game with Chinese-style area scoring and White +7.5 komi. Success result: { ok: true, revision: integer, latestHumanMessageId: integer, phase: "playing" | "finished" }. Failure result: { ok: false, error: string, ... }. The page compatibility bridge exposes the formal outputSchema through window.goWebMCP.describeTools().

expectedRevision.description: Revision returned by get_go_game_state.

tools.name: send_go_message
tools.description: Send one plain-text AI message to the human during the current game. Maximum 240 characters. Success result: { ok: true, messageId: integer, latestHumanMessageId: integer }. Failure result: { ok: false, error: string, ... }. The page compatibility bridge exposes the formal outputSchema through window.goWebMCP.describeTools().

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: gosundang.com
sites.description: Online retailer of watches and accessories.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: habitat815run.com
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: handsend.kr
sites.description: Online retailer of clothing and fashion accessories.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url

Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

sites.name: harmanirentals.com
sites.description: Search Harmani rental properties and access application and inquiry information.

tools.name: search_rentals
tools.description: Search Harmani Rentals apartment buildings in Alberta, Canada. Filter by city, neighborhood, bedroom type, availability, maximum starting rent, pet policy and amenity keywords. Returns each match's availability, bedroom types, starting monthly rent (CAD), size, pet policy, amenities and page link. Call with no arguments to list every building; use list_rental_areas for valid city and neighborhood names.

bedrooms.description: Bedroom types wanted; a building matches if it offers any of them.

availability.description: "available_now" = buildings with vacancies; "waitlist" = no vacancy or coming soon. Default "any".

max_rent.description: Maximum starting monthly rent in CAD.

pets_allowed.description: true = only buildings whose published policy allows pets.

keywords.description: Words that must all appear in the listing's features, amenities or description, e.g. ["dishwasher", "underground parking"].

sort.description: Default "availability" (available buildings first, then by name).

limit.description: Maximum results (default 25).

tools.name: get_rental_details
tools.description: Full details for one Harmani Rentals building: description, unit features (size, baths, lease term, deposit, pet and smoking policy), unit and building amenities, photos, map location, starting rent, availability and how to request a callback, join the waitlist or apply.

name.description: Building name, if the id is unknown (e.g. "Bella Vista").

tools.name: list_rental_areas
tools.description: Cities and neighborhoods where Harmani Rentals has buildings, with listing and available-now counts, the bedroom types offered and the starting-rent range.

tools.name: get_contact_info
tools.description: Harmani Rentals phone, email, office address and hours, plus links to the rental application and tenant service pages.

tools.name: request_property_callback
tools.description: Ask Harmani Rentals staff to phone the visitor about a specific building (availability, viewings, rent). Sends the visitor's name, email and phone to Harmani, so confirm the details with the visitor before calling. Works for any listing; staff call back during office hours.

message.description: Optional questions or needs (bedroom type, pets, parking...).

tools.name: join_waitlist
tools.description: Add the visitor to the waitlist for a building with no current vacancy (availability "no_vacancy" or "coming_soon"); they are emailed when a suite with their chosen bedroom type opens up. Requires the visitor's explicit consent to those emails. Sends their name and email to Harmani, so confirm with the visitor first.

phone.description: Optional; staff may call when a suite opens.

bedroom_preferences.description: Bedroom types wanted (must be types the building offers).

consent_to_email_notifications.description: Set true only after the visitor has agreed to receive availability emails from Harmani Rentals for this property.

tools.name: get_rental_application_questions
tools.description: The questions to ask when helping someone apply to rent a Harmani Rentals property: each answer's field name, wording, format and whether it is required, plus the background-check authorization the applicant must agree to. Call this before submit_rental_application and interview the applicant with it.

tools.name: submit_rental_application
tools.description: Submit a tenancy application to Harmani Rentals on the applicant's behalf, for a building that is available now or coming soon. Use get_rental_application_questions first and use only the applicant's own answers. Sends personal, employment, income and reference details to Harmani and authorizes a background check, so the applicant must agree to the authorization and confirm every detail before you call this.

preferred_occupancy_date.description: Desired move-in date, YYYY-MM-DD (today or later).

support_details.description: Optional: any support currently received, with details.

landlord_name.description: Current or previous landlord: name and/or company.

additional_lease_holder.description: Optional: a second person on the lease. If given, all four fields are required.

pet_description.description: Optional: pets the applicant wishes to have, described.

how_did_you_hear.description: How the applicant heard about Harmani Rentals.

additional_information.description: Optional: anything else the applicant wants to add, or questions.

applicant_authorizes_background_check.description: Set true only after reading the applicant this authorization and they agreed: "I authorize Harmani Property Management to conduct a background check in my name for the purpose of evaluating my tenancy application. applicant_confirmed_details_correct.description: Set true only after reading every answer back to the applicant and they confirmed it is correct.

sites.name: haru-balance.com
sites.description: Online store with product search, cart management and checkout tools.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Searches products in this store. In addition to a product name you can pass situational tags (season, style, place, purpose) for a more precise search. Present the results in the order they appear in the array. Reordering them makes the user pick a different product when they refer to one by position, such as the second one.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Adds a product to the cart. With no arguments it adds the variant and quantity the user has selected on the product page they are viewing. The result is reflected in the store cart page as-is. Some products can be shipped either domestically or internationally, and domestic and international items go into separate carts. For those products you must ask the user which one they want and pass delivery_type; never choose it yourself.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Changes the quantity of items already in the cart, or removes an item. Specify only the items you want to change; the rest stay as they are. A quantity of 0 removes that item. Identify items by the item.id from a get_cart result.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after updating. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empties the whole cart. This cannot be undone, so the tool does not run it immediately; it shows a confirmation button on screen and the user has to press it.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for buying one product immediately. This bypasses the cart and cannot order multiple products at once. To order everything in the cart, use create-cart-checkout-url instead. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

product_no.description: Product number. Omit it to use the product on the page the user is currently viewing. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

variant_code.description: Variant code. Omit it to use the variant the user has selected on the current product page.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

tools.name: create-cart-checkout-url
tools.description: Creates a checkout page for the items in the cart. Without item_ids it orders the entire cart. When the user wants only part of it, such as just what I added, only this one, or only the jeans, you must call get_cart first and pass those item.id values in item_ids. Without them the other items in the cart are ordered too. Domestic and international shipping items cannot be checked out together; if the cart has both, ask the user which group to check out and pass that group's item_ids. To buy one product immediately without using the cart, use create-checkout-url. This tool always moves the browser to the checkout page it creates. Navigation is not optional, so do not tell the user to click a link.

item_ids.description: Restricts the order to these items. Pass item.id values from a get_cart result. Omit it to order the entire cart.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
tools.description: Retrieves the detail of one product by product number. When the user refers to a product by position, such as the second one, use the product_no at that index of the previous search-products result. The array order is the reference, not any order you presented.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to that product page. When the request identifies a single product, set true whether the user says tell me or show me, because the user is about to look at it. Omit it only while looking up several products in a row to compare them. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

product_no.description: Product number

variants_verbose.description: Set to true to expand variant detail. Each variant then carries additional_amount and option_axes, up to 100 variants are returned, and the response includes variants_total and variants_truncated. Defaults to false, which returns at most 5 variants.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Retrieves the items and amounts in the user cart. Called with no arguments it reads the cart shown on the store cart page. Use it for requests such as what is in my cart or what is the total.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

cart_id.description: Cart identifier to read. Omit it to read the cart on the screen the user is viewing; normally omit it.

tools.name: create_cart

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after adding. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

delivery_type.description: Shipping the user chose for products that offer both domestic and international shipping. Ask the user before setting it. It is ignored for products that ship only one way.

cart.description: Items to add. Omit it to use the selection on the current product page. It cannot be omitted on pages other than a product detail page.

quantity.description: Quantity to add

context.description: Context such as shipping country, region and postal code

tools.name: update_cart

items.description: Items whose quantity should change. Items you do not list stay as they are.

item_id.description: item.id from a get_cart result, for example cafe24_mall_1_22_P000000W000A

quantity.description: New quantity. 0 removes the item from the cart.

tools.name: cancel_cart

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the cart page after emptying. Only set true when the user asks to be taken somewhere (show me / open it / go there). Omit it when the user is only asking a question. Defaults to false; when true the page actually changes.

tools.name: create-checkout-url

quantity.description: Quantity to buy. Omit it to use the quantity field on the current page, falling back to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

sites.name: hezro.co.kr

tools.name: search-products

navigate.description: Set to true to move the browser to the search results page. If exactly one product matches, it moves to that product page instead. product_name.description: Product name to search for, for example 't-shirt' or 'sneakers'. Separate multiple names with commas. Map the central product type of the user request to this field.

product_tag.description: Situational tags such as season, occasion or purpose, extracted from the user request. For example: summer, commute, hiking, home workout. Separate multiple tags with commas.

price_min.description: Minimum price. Map expressions such as 'over 10,000 won', 'at least $10' or 'from $20'. Pass digits only; currency handling is done by the store.

price_max.description: Maximum price. Map expressions such as 'under 50,000 won', 'under $50' or 'at most 30,000 won'. Pass digits only.

sort.description: Sort key for the results. Map it when the user asks for newest first, by name, or recently updated.

order.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc. Map it when the user asks for ascending order, lowest price first, or most recent first.

limit.description: Maximum number of results. Map it when the user names a count such as 'just 10' or 'top 5'. Omit to use the default.

tools.name: search-products-detail
