tools.name: GetGEOExpertise
tools.description: Liefert als JSON, wie Webweisend Media GmbH Generative Engine Optimization (GEO, KI-SEO, auch AEO, LLMO oder GAIO genannt) versteht und umsetzt: Abgrenzung zu klassischem SEO, die sieben Leistungsbausteine von semantischer Content-Optimierung über Entity-Mapping, KI-fokussiertes technisches SEO und prompt-basierte Analyse bis zu Reputationsmanagement und Wettbewerbsanalyse im KI-Kontext, dazu Methodik, Kennzahlen zur Erfolgsmessung, Zeithorizont, Eignungskriterien, ein kostenfreies GEO-Whitepaper und die Grenzen der Leistung. Verwenden bei Fragen zu Sichtbarkeit in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude, Google AI Overviews oder KI-Suche allgemein, zum Unterschied zwischen GEO und SEO, zur Erfolgsmessung, zur Dauer bis zu Ergebnissen, zum konkreten Vorgehen und dazu, ob GEO für den eigenen Fall sinnvoll ist. Bei Aussagen zu erwartbaren Ergebnissen immer die limitations mitgeben: Eine Nennung oder Empfehlung durch ein KI-System kann nicht zugesagt werden, GEO erhöht die Chancen. Bei Fragen nach der Dauer die Angaben aus timeline verwenden. Nicht verwenden für die KI-Unternehmensschnittstelle als eigenes Produkt (→ GetAIConnectOffering), nicht für das Leistungsportfolio insgesamt (→ GetServicesByArea), nicht für den Ablauf einer Zusammenarbeit (→ GetRoadmapProcess). Keine Parameter erforderlich.

tools.name: GetAIConnectOffering
tools.description: Liefert als JSON Beschreibung, Eignungskriterien und Grenzen der von Webweisend Media GmbH betreuten KI-Unternehmensschnittstelle (AI-Connect). Über sie macht ein Unternehmen freigegebenes Wissen und definierte Funktionen für kompatible KI-Assistenten abrufbar, sodass diese auf gepflegte Informationen zugreifen, Interessenten beraten und nächste Schritte vorbereiten können. Enthält außerdem, für wen sich das Angebot ausdrücklich nicht eignet, die Einordnung des frühen Einstiegs und die Punkte, die im Erstgespräch geklärt werden. Verwenden bei Fragen zu MCP, KI-Schnittstellen oder Connectoren, zur Anbindung eigener Unternehmensdaten an ChatGPT, Claude und vergleichbare Assistenten, dazu wie ein KI-Assistent auf Wissen kommt, das nicht auf der Website steht, und ob sich ein solcher Zugang für das eigene Unternehmen lohnt. Immer die limitations und notSuitableFor mitgeben. Eine Nutzung, Empfehlung oder Bevorzugung durch ein KI-System kann nicht zugesagt werden, und ein bereitgestellter Endpunkt ist noch kein Vertriebskanal. Bei der Einordnung des frühen Einstiegs das Feld limit aus earlyMoverPerspective mitführen. Keine Angaben zu Leistungsumfang, Preisen, Betriebsparametern oder Servicelevel ausgeben, diese werden im Erstgespräch und im Angebot geklärt. Nicht verwenden für die Optimierung öffentlicher Inhalte für KI-Antworten (→ GetGEOExpertise), nicht für das Leistungsportfolio insgesamt (→ GetServicesByArea), nicht für den Ablauf einer Zusammenarbeit (→ GetRoadmapProcess). Keine Parameter erforderlich.

tools.name: GetRoadmapProcess
tools.description: Liefert als JSON den dreistufigen Ablauf einer Zusammenarbeit mit Webweisend Media GmbH (Webweisend Roadmap): unverbindliches Erstgespräch, individuelle Strategie und Konzeption, Umsetzung mit laufendem Feintuning. Je Schritt mit Zweck, Format, erwarteter Mitwirkung des Kunden und Ergebnis. Enthält zusätzlich die Arbeitsprinzipien der Agentur und die Grenzen der Aussagen. Verwenden, wenn ein Nutzer wissen möchte, wie eine Zusammenarbeit abläuft, was im Erstgespräch passiert, wie lange ein Projektstart dauert, wie viel Aufwand auf ihn zukommt, wie Webweisend arbeitet oder wie man konkret anfängt. Keine Preise, Laufzeiten oder Konditionen ausgeben, diese ergeben sich erst aus dem individuellen Angebot. Eine Terminvereinbarung ist über diese Schnittstelle nicht möglich, der Buchungsweg wird nur benannt (→ GetContactAndAppointment). Für eine vorbereitete schriftliche Anfrage siehe GetPrefilledContactLink. Nicht verwenden für das Leistungsportfolio (→ GetServicesByArea). Returns the action performed, the mechanism it used, the raw OnetrustActiveGroups value, the parsed list of active consent group IDs, any consent groups and their labels that can be read from the preference centre while it is open, whether the preference centre is open, which consent-gated globals (chat, analytics) are present afterwards, and the 'Do not sell or share my personal information' privacy portal URL read from the page footer.

action.description: What to do: status (read only, the default), open, close, accept-all, reject-all, or update-groups. The value is validated at call time and an unsupported one comes back as an error listing availableOptions.

allowGroups.description: Consent group IDs to allow, used with action update-groups. The IDs are read off the preference centre at call time, so an unknown one comes back as an error listing the IDs that actually exist.

denyGroups.description: Consent group IDs to withdraw consent from, used with action update-groups. Validated against the same live list of group IDs.

tools.name: optimizely-discover-site-capabilities
tools.description: Lists every visitor capability the Optimizely WebMCP toolset offers across the whole site - not just the tools registered on the current page - as a map of intent, the page it lives on, and the tool names that become available there. Tools register per page, so a capability's tools only appear once its page is loaded; pass goTo with a capability id (or a site path) and this tool navigates the browser there, and the toolset for that page registers when the new document loads. Use this from any page to answer 'what can I do on this site?' and to reach the page where a capability's tools live.

goTo.description: Optional capability id from the returned map (for example site-search, find-partner, register-beta-interest) or a site path (for example /connectors). When given, the browser navigates to that capability's page; call the capability's tools once the page has loaded and its toolset has registered. Omit to just read the map.

tools.name: optimizely-request-demo-lead-form
tools.description: Fills the Optimizely lead capture form embedded in the page's main region (the 'Let's grow' / 'Get started' contact form) so a buyer can request a demo, pricing or a custom plan. It scrolls to the form, highlights it, writes First name, Last name, Work email, Company, Job title, Phone and the free-text 'What products are you interested in?' note, and picks the country from the option list the form's own combobox renders. Returns the values read back out of each input, the required fields it could not populate, whether the form is ready to send, which optional controls (state selection, marketing-consent choice, captcha) it found rendered and their state, the Optimizely end-user id carried by the form, and the name of the companion submit tool. Nothing is sent until that submit tool is called.

firstName.description: Value for the First name field.

lastName.description: Value for the Last name field.

email.description: Value for the Work email field.

jobTitle.description: Value for the Job title field.

phone.description: Value for the Phone field, for example +1 234 567 8901.

country.description: Country name to choose in the Country combobox. It is matched against the options the page renders at call time; if it does not match, the tool returns the options that were actually on screen.

state.description: Optional state name. The state control is rendered by the page only for some countries; the tool fills it when it is present.

productsOfInterest.description: Optional free text for the 'What products are you interested in?' box.

marketingConsent.description: Optional marketing email preference, matched against the choices the consent control renders at call time.

tools.name: optimizely-request-demo-lead-form-submit
tools.description: Clicks the submit button on the Optimizely lead capture form that optimizely-request-demo-lead-form filled, waits for the page to settle, and reports what it observes: the confirmation or thank-you text if the lead was accepted, each per-field validation message paired with the label of the field it belongs to, any captcha message, and the URL after the click. confirm.description: Set true to confirm the reviewed form should be sent. Defaults to true; set false to abort without clicking.

tools.name: places_search
tools.description: Resolve a town, beach, harbour or cove name to Peskio placeIds (Europe, North Africa and US coasts). Call this first whenever the user names a place, then pass the placeId to the other tools. candidates[0] is the best match: when `ambiguous` is false, use it without asking (a harbour or beach listed after a town of the same name is part of that place). Ask which one the user means only when `ambiguous` is true (the same name in different regions). Never ask the user for coordinates.

query.description: The place name as the user wrote it, optionally with its region.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, lower case, to restrict to one country.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: places_get_profile
tools.description: What a place is: tide regime and range, coast exposure and which wind/swell directions it is sheltered from or exposed to, distance to the nearest river mouth, nearby places and landmarks. Use for "is X sheltered from a north wind?", "big or small tides here?" and "near a river mouth?". Does not cover species, depth or dive sites.

placeId.description: Peskio place id returned by places_search, e.g. "es:es-3108877". Never invent one. Optional in this browser tab: when omitted, the place currently open in the tab is used.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: tides_get_table
tools.description: Tide times, heights and Peskio coefficient estimates for one place over up to two weeks, with sunrise, sunset, daylight low tides and moon phase. Use for tide times, spring/neap tides, grandes marées, pêche à pied, tidal islands and boat launching. Heights are in metres above the stated datum. Information only: for tidal crossings, tell the user to follow the official crossing schedule. Peskio has no tidal-current or slack-water data: never derive them from these times. Explicitly label coefficients as Peskio estimates in the user language (French: estimation Peskio). Include a clickable link to place.url exactly as returned, query string included.

placeId.description: Peskio place id returned by places_search, e.g. "es:es-3108877". Never invent one. Optional in this browser tab: when omitted, the place currently open in the tab is used.

from.description: First local date: YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'tomorrow' or an English weekday (the next one, today included); default today at the place. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

date.description: Alias of `from` (the name the other Peskio tools use); `from` wins when both are given. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

minCoefficient.description: Keep only days whose Peskio coefficient is at least this. Grandes marées: 95. Pêche à pied: 70.

daylightLowOnly.description: Keep only days with a low tide in daylight.

rankBy.description: coefficient = biggest first; low_tide = lowest low first; moon = closest to new/full moon first. Omit for date order.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: conditions_get_day
tools.description: One place, one day: bite score and best windows, go/marginal/no verdict per discipline (shore, boat, rock, kayak, spearfishing) with reasons, tide, sun, moon and solunar periods, wind and sea summary, water-clarity estimate, and how fresh the forecast is. Use for "is tomorrow good for…", "why is Saturday poor", "too rough today?", "water temperature now" (include hourly). Peskio has no current or slack-water data: never infer them from tide times. Surface temperature and clarity only: no temperature or visibility at depth or thermocline; never infer them. Include a clickable link to the returned place.url with its query string unchanged. State the returned planning disclaimer when giving GO/marginal/NO; never assess whether a crossing, dive or trip is safe.

placeId.description: Peskio place id returned by places_search, e.g. "es:es-3108877". Never invent one. Optional in this browser tab: when omitted, the place currently open in the tab is used.

date.description: Local date at the place: YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'tomorrow' or an English weekday (the next one, today included); default today. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

discipline.description: Only this discipline in decision.disciplines; default all five.

include.description: "hourly" for time-of-day or "right now" questions; "tideCurve" for a tide chart.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: conditions_compare_days
tools.description: Rank up to 7 consecutive days at one place by bite score (default), verdict (overall or for one discipline) or water clarity, with tide coefficient, lowest low, moon and a wind/wave headline per day. Use for "best day to fish this weekend", "today or Thursday?", "clearest day this week". Name the days with `dates` and let the server resolve them: "this weekend" -> dates: ["weekend"]; "today or Thursday" -> dates: ["today", "thursday"]; or use from + days for a run of days. Days with no weather forecast (beyond the ~14-day horizon, or not available) are marked astroOnly and rank last for verdict and clarity. Include a clickable link to place.url exactly as returned, including the query string. GO/marginal/NO are conditions ratings for planning, not safety; say so. Bite score is fish activity, not a discipline conditions score.

placeId.description: Peskio place id returned by places_search, e.g. "es:es-3108877". Never invent one. Optional in this browser tab: when omitted, the place currently open in the tab is used.

dates.description: Specific days to compare, resolved at the place: YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'tomorrow', an English weekday (the next one, today included) or 'weekend' (the coming Saturday and Sunday; from today if it is Saturday, just today if Sunday). Overrides from/days.

from.description: First local date (YYYY-MM-DD or a day word); default today. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

discipline.description: Fishing discipline: shore, boat, rock, kayak or spearfishing.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: spots_find_best
tools.description: Rank up to 10 places within 5-25 km of a centre place for one day, on a given local hour or on each place's best daylight hour, by bite score, verdict or water clarity. Use for "where near X is best tomorrow", "best spot at 7 am", "clearest water near Y". When placeId is omitted, use the place currently open in this tab as the centre; if no place is open, ask for a town or beach name and resolve it with places_search. This does not locate the user. tools.name: read_store_guide
tools.description: Returns the store's guide as plain text: the catalog with prices, how x402 payment works here, the free instruments, and the house promises. Free; no purchase is made and nothing is stored.

tools.name: preflight_endpoint
tools.description: Probes one x402 endpoint unpaid and returns whether it serves a well-formed x402 v2 payment challenge right now: the verdict, the level reached on the L0–L6 evidence ladder, each check's tri-state result, and what a single probe cannot establish. A shape check at one moment, not an uptime or delivery claim. Free and rate limited; the ceiling travels with the result.

url.description: The https endpoint a buyer would GET expecting a 402 challenge.

tools.name: look_at_door
tools.description: Returns what the store holds about one x402 door: one unpaid probe now, folded with the signed weekly record of that host — rounds probed of rounds since first seen, the passport tier with its fraction, the last probed round's failed checks, and whether the door answers now the way the last signed round saw it. Not a score or a rank; counts carry their denominators. Free.

url.description: The https x402 door you are asking about.

since.description: Optional. A signed week, e.g. 2026-W34, to reproduce against that week's row.

tools.name: check_before_you_pay
tools.description: Probes one x402 door unpaid and replays the stock @x402/core client selection over the accepts it returned, under the caller's own profile. Returns which accept a stock client would sign — network, asset, amount, signing window — or that it would refuse locally before signing, with the stage and the setting that decided it. Free; nothing is signed and nothing is paid.

url.description: The https x402 door you are about to pay.

client_profile.description: The caller's own x402 client settings. Absent, the replay runs against a client configured with nothing, the case that loses money quietly.

max_amount_per_payment_usd.description: Your spendControls.maxAmountPerPayment, in dollars; false if you set it to false.

spend_controls_disabled.description: True if you pass spendControls: false — the one escape from the whole filter.

tools.name: check_conformance
tools.description: Verifies any issuer's signed x402 offer or receipt (a compact JWS): structure, the signature against the issuer's did:web key, and liveness. Returns a verdict with every check named. With public_key_hex supplied the check runs fully offline. Free; the method is MIT-licensed and identical to the published verifier.

artifact.description: The signed offer or receipt as a compact JWS: header.payload.signature, base64url.

kind.description: Optional: offer | receipt. Detected from the artifact when absent.

public_key_hex.description: Optional ed25519 public key, hex. Supplying it makes the check fully offline.

tools.name: verify_artifact
tools.description: Verifies a certificate, visit stamp or context anchor by its id against the store's own ed25519 key. Returns valid (true or false), the artifact kind, and a one-line note. Free and unlimited, for artifacts anyone bought or none.

id.description: A cert_, stamp_, or anchor_ id.

tools.name: check_order
tools.description: Returns the current state of a human-queue order by its order_id: status (queued or completed), the promised window in hours, and the deliverable once completed. The same record GET /api/order/{order_id} serves. Free; past its window the order carries a window_breached block stating what is owed.

order_id.description: The order_id from a human-queue purchase result.

tools.name: find_in_catalog
tools.description: Searches this store's shelf and returns compact rows: id, name, price in USDC, instant or human-fulfilled, and what each item reads. Filters by a price ceiling, a text match, or both; an item_id returns that one item with its description. Free and read-only. Nothing is ranked or recommended.

q.description: Words to match against an item's id, name, subtitle and description.

max_price_usdc.description: A ceiling in USDC. Items at or below it match.

item_id.description: One item's id. The answer carries that item alone, in full.

nationality.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. GB.

date_of_birth.description: YYYY-MM-DD — only when the slot lists it.

title.description: MR, MRS, MS, MISS or MSTR — only when the slot lists it.

passport_number.description: Only when the slot lists it.

passport_expiry_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD — only when the slot lists it.

gender.description: male, female or other — only when the slot lists it.

additional_fields.description: Values for entries of passenger_requirements.additional_fields, keyed by their name.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout

tools.name: search_devices
tools.description: Discover supported devices by name or structured filters. Query is optional: browse by device type, manufacturer, operating system, release year, screen size, height, width, depth (thickness), storage, review score and deal budget. Measurement limits are inclusive; screen size is diagonal inches and physical dimensions are recorded height x width x depth in millimetres. Devices with unknown or ambiguous measurements are excluded when those filters are used. Reviews are out of 5 and missing reviews are unknown. Price filters require eligible deals matching the selected variant specifications; without dealType they default to contracts. Select a precise candidate and pass its versionId to the other device tools. Results contain up to 20 devices per page. Follow nextPage; at the 100-page cap paginationLimited=true means more matches exist and filters must be narrowed. Without dealType or a price filter, devices without current deals may be returned. Correct obvious spelling or simplify a text query if no matches are found.

maxReleaseYear.description: Latest recorded release year, inclusive. Devices with unknown release years do not match.

maxMonthlyGbp.description: Maximum monthly deal price in GBP; applies to contract or upgrade discovery. For SIM-free use maxUpfrontGbp.

maxUpfrontGbp.description: Maximum upfront price in GBP; the purchase budget for SIM-free discovery.

tools.name: search_device_deals
tools.description: Find live contract, SIM-free purchase or upgrade deals for one exact device version using the versionId returned by search_devices. Select dealType: contract (default), sim_free or upgrade. SIM-free purchases exclude PAYG bundles and do not accept airtime/network filters; use maxUpfrontGbp for purchase cost. Upgrades require existing-customer eligibility checks with the retailer. unlimitedData=true requires unlimited data and cannot be combined with minDataGb greater than zero. networkBrands filters the advertised tariff network brand, which may differ from the underlying network that carries the service. Use get_networks to discover brands on a requested underlying carrier. All costs are in GBP. A stored total cost may span a device payment term longer than the recorded airtime commitment. pricing.contractMonths comes from the recorded tariff; airtimeCostedMonths and totalCostHorizonMonths describe the stored calculation. Inspect pricing.adjustments before quoting a price: codes or redemption may be required. priceConditionsTruncated=true means read get_deal for full requirements. Cashback filters apply to tariff/deal cashback; separate device promotional cashback may remain and is included in returned pricing. Cashback values mean: none excludes tariff/deal cashback, automatic_or_none allows automatic cashback or no cashback, and manual_or_none allows redemption cashback or no cashback. The first page includes availableFilters for the versionId and dealType, even when no deals match the other filters. Start with just versionId to discover deals and valid choices together, then refine. Pass colours as names, slugs or recorded colour groups (for example Blue or natural-titanium); exact names/slugs take precedence, otherwise a group matches all its available variants. Pass network names as networkBrands, retailers[].id as retailerId, and storageGb/contractMonths as listed. Multiple values within a list are alternatives; different filters must all match. Omitted limi…

dealType.description: Deal category: new contract, SIM-free purchase (no PAYG bundle), or existing-customer upgrade.

unlimitedData.description: Require an unlimited data tariff. Do not combine with minDataGb greater than zero. Not supported for SIM-free purchases.

See page-one availableFilters.colours[].name and .group; appliedFilters.colours returns resolved manufacturer names. Unknown values return INVALID_ARGUMENT; empty lists impose no restriction.

tools.name: search_sim_only_deals
tools.description: Find live SIM-only deals without a device versionId. SIM rows have device=null and an explicit simType. Choose phone SIMs or data-only SIMs with simType. Network brands are advertised tariff brands, not underlying carriers. unlimitedData=true requires unlimited data and cannot be combined with minDataGb greater than zero. The first page includes availableFilters with eligible network names, retailer IDs and contractMonths for the selected simType, regardless of the remaining search filters. Start with simType alone to discover deals and choices together, then refine. Choices do not guarantee every combination has deals; empty choices mean none available and truncated=true means lists were capped at 100 choices each. Later pages return availableFilters=null. Use get_networks for underlying-carrier relationships and select entries with dealTypes=sim_phone or sim_data accordingly. Multiple values within a list are alternatives; different filters must all match. Omitted limits and empty lists impose no restriction. Costs are GBP. Inspect pricing.adjustments for code/redemption requirements; priceConditionsTruncated=true requires get_deal for full conditions. Cashback modes: any, none (no tariff/deal cashback), automatic_or_none, manual_or_none. Results contain 10 deals per page; follow nextPage, and narrow filters if paginationLimited=true.

tools.name: get_device
tools.description: Get a device's recorded specifications, average review score out of 5, review count and recorded variants using a versionId from search_devices. The average review score is null when there are no reviews. Missing specifications are unknown, not proof a feature is absent. allVariants contains every colour/storage pair recorded for this device in our catalogue, including variants without current eligible deals; this is not a complete manufacturer catalogue or proof of availability. availableVariants contains only pairs with current eligible contract, upgrade or SIM-free deals. Both lists are capped at 100 pairs; detailsTruncated=true signals incomplete details. Reviews appear once in device. Specifications use typed nullable values; null means unknown. Deal filter metadata belongs to page one of search_device_deals for the requested dealType. Use search_device_deals for live prices.

versionId.description: Exact device identifier returned by search_devices.

tools.name: get_device_price_history
tools.description: Read recorded device price history using a versionId from search_devices. Omit specifier to discover a paginated scopeCatalog; follow nextPage. Use advertised scope specifiers, including historical networks that may have no current deals. get_networks describes current eligibility, not historical coverage. Scoped calls omit the catalog unless includeScopeCatalog=true. Default results are lightweight lifetime summaries; request includePoints=true for up to maxPoints daily values (maximum 366). History requires a 7-day inclusive calendar span, not seven observations. Calendar dates use UK dates; daily prices represent recorded intervals, not a capture every day. plausibleMinValueGbp/plausibleMaxValueGbp exclude values outside 0.25 to 4 times the series median; consult statisticsPolicy and statisticsPeriod. These are recorded-scope statistics, not an all-time market low or current offer. unlimited-data and no-upfront-cost have separately recorded scopes across networks; never infer those lows from overall/network history. Only storage/colour and contracts/term composite scopes are supported. Other scopes cannot be combined; gifts and bad-credit-specific history are unsupported. hasHistory=false does not prove a deal never existed.

specifier.description: Optional history scope. Prefer an exact specifier from the response scopeCatalog.items list for this device. Use unlimited-data for unlimited-data deals or no-upfront-cost for zero-upfront deals (each across networks). Other scopes: a network slug from scopeCatalog.items; storage (256gb, 2tb); colour (silver); storage/colour (2tb/silver); contracts; sim-free; pay-as-you-go; upgrades; refurbished; 100gb-data (phones only); contracts/24-months; contracts/36-months. Network plus data/upfront combinations are not supported. Omit for overall device history. Gift scopes are not supported. Each slug is lowercase and at most 80 characters. No full URLs, query strings or arbitrary combinations.

includePoints.description: Include bounded daily price detail. Default false returns lifetime summaries without daily points.

maxPoints.description: Maximum daily points per series, only valid with includePoints=true. Defaults to 366 when detail is requested.

includeScopeCatalog.description: Include the paginated scope catalog on a scoped request. Discovery without specifier includes it automatically.

scopePage.description: One-based scope-catalog page. Follow scopeCatalog.nextPage; requires catalog inclusion, implicit for discovery or explicit for a scoped request. At the 100-page cap paginationLimited=true means coverage is incomplete.

tools.name: get_sim_only_price_history
tools.description: Read recorded monthly GBP history for 30-day rolling phone SIM deals; data-only SIMs and longer commitments are not represented. Omit specifier to discover stored networks through paginated scopeCatalog, including networks without current deals. Scoped calls omit the catalog unless includeScopeCatalog=true. Optionally select dataBand; availableDataBands describes reportable bands for the selected network (or all networks). Finite bands mean at least the allowance and may include unlimited tariffs. Default results are lightweight lifetime summaries; includePoints=true adds up to maxPoints daily values (maximum 366). History requires an inclusive calendar span of at least 7 days, not seven observations. Dates use UK calendar dates; daily values represent recorded intervals. plausibleMinValueGbp/plausibleMaxValueGbp exclude values outside 0.25 to 4 times the series median; consult statisticsPolicy and statisticsPeriod. These are recorded-scope statistics, not an all-time market low or evidence of current availability. Network plus dataBand is supported. hasHistory=false does not prove a deal never existed.

specifier.description: Optional exact network specifier from scopeCatalog.items returned by this tool. Do not derive historical availability from current get_networks results. Omit for history across all networks.

dataBand.description: Optional stored SIM-only band: 5gb, 20gb, 50gb, 100gb, 200gb, 300gb, 500gb, 750gb, 1000gb or unlimited. Finite bands mean at least that allowance. May be combined with a network specifier. Omit for all available lines.

includePoints.description: Include bounded daily price detail. Default false returns lifetime summaries without daily points.

maxPoints.description: Maximum daily points per series, only valid with includePoints=true. Defaults to 366 when detail is requested.

includeScopeCatalog.description: Include the paginated scope catalog on a scoped request. Discovery without specifier includes it automatically.

scopePage.description: One-based scope-catalog page. Follow scopeCatalog.nextPage; requires catalog inclusion, implicit for discovery or explicit for a scoped request. At the 100-page cap paginationLimited=true means coverage is incomplete.

tools.name: get_networks
tools.description: Discover network brands with currently eligible deals and their underlying carrier, using the recorded catalogue relationships. Filter underlyingNetwork by carrier name or slug (for example EE). Choose dealType from all (default), device_contract, device_upgrade, sim_phone or sim_data. Optionally provide versionId for device categories; all with a versionId means all applicable device categories. SIM categories do not accept versionId. Pass returned name values to search_device_deals or search_sim_only_deals as networkBrands. A carrier operating its own brand reports itself as its underlying network. An empty list means no eligible deals match; shared carrier does not imply identical features or service terms.

dealType.description: Eligible deal category. all includes every applicable category; a versionId restricts all to device categories. SIM-free purchases have no network.

underlyingNetwork.description: Optional underlying carrier name or slug, case-insensitive; use EE, O2, Three or Vodafone, or discover carriers by omitting this filter.

versionId.description: Optional exact device identifier from search_devices. Valid with all, device_contract or device_upgrade; restricts results to that device.

tools.name: get_deal
tools.description: Get current details for one deal returned by search_device_deals or search_sim_only_deals. All costs are in GBP; a stored total cost may span a device payment term longer than the airtime contract. Review existingCustomerOnly, pricing.adjustments, scheduledIncreases, pricing payment components, legalText, promotionDetails and chargeableExtras before recommending a deal. A null allowance is unknown unless its corresponding unlimited flag is true; null monetary values are unknown, not zero; discount method=unknown means the requirements are unknown. An unknown valueUnit means the recorded value cannot safely be interpreted as GBP or a percentage. If detailsTruncated is true, use the dealUrl to review complete terms and extras before making a recommendation.

dealId.description: Opaque deal identifier returned by search_device_deals or search_sim_only_deals.

tools.name: describe_model
tools.description: Return the full specification of this intersection: tunable parameters with units and ranges, metric definitions, the hard constraints that govern what may be deployed, and the available demand scenarios. Call this first — it is sufficient to understand the problem without any prior traffic-engineering knowledge.

tools.name: read_state
tools.description: Return what is currently on screen: the committed signal timing, the active demand scenario, metrics measured so far on the live run, the controller's current phase, per-arm queues, and which parameters the operator has locked. Locked parameters cannot be changed by apply_config — read this before proposing a timing.

tools.name: run_batch
tools.description: Evaluate up to 50 candidate signal timings headlessly and return the resulting metrics for each. Runs off the main thread; the live junction keeps running while this executes. Deterministic: identical (config, seed) pairs always produce identical metrics. Single-seed figures carry roughly ±2 s of noise on mean_wait_s, so average across at least 3 seeds before concluding that one timing beats another by a small margin. This tool reports physics, not policy: it evaluates timings that are illegal to deploy and tells you honestly how they perform. Each row carries an `admissible` flag and, when false, the constraints it violates — so you can see the fast illegal options without spending a search on them. Enforcement still belongs to apply_config. If `admissible_count` comes back much lower than the batch size, the region you are searching is mostly out of bounds. Read `constraints` in describe_model before continuing. Results are sorted by mean_wait_s ascending. The top 3 carry the full per-arm breakdown; the rest carry the summary metrics needed to rank them. Pass detail="full" if you need per-arm figures for every row.

yellow_s.description: Yellow after every green, seconds. Safety-derived floor of 4 s — see the min_yellow constraint.

all_red_s.description: All-red clearance, seconds. Safety-derived floor of 2 s — see the min_all_red constraint.

left_protected.description: Give NS left turns an exclusive phase.

ns_left_green_s.description: Protected left phase duration. Must be 0 when left_protected is false.

seeds.description: Random seeds to average over. Defaults to [1,2,3].

sim_minutes.description: Simulated minutes per run after a 5-minute warm-up. Defaults to 20. Shorter runs are faster but noisier.

scenario_id.description: Demand scenario to evaluate against. Defaults to the active one. Evaluating against a scenario does not switch the live view.

detail.description: summary (default) gives full per-arm figures for the top 3 rows and summary metrics for the rest. full gives per-arm figures for every row, which for 50 configs is a large payload.

tools.name: apply_config
tools.description: Commit a signal timing to the junction the operator is watching. This is the only tool that changes what is on screen. Applying a timing RESTARTS the live run: changing timing mid-cycle would leave the controller in an inconsistent phase and contaminate the measured figures with the previous timing. Expect roughly four minutes of simulated time before live metrics settle. Refuses, with the specific rule and rationale, if the timing violates a constraint from describe_model, or if it would change a parameter the operator has locked. A refusal is a fact about what may be deployed, not a scoring signal — a refused timing may well be the fastest one.

yellow_s.description: Yellow after every green, seconds. Safety-derived floor of 4 s — see the min_yellow constraint.

tools.name: set_scenario
tools.description: Switch the demand profile the junction is running under, and what the operator sees. Like apply_config, this RESTARTS the live run. The best timing differs substantially between scenarios, and so does which left-turn phasing is admissible — a timing that is legal under one demand profile may be prohibited under another. To evaluate against a scenario without switching the operator's view, pass scenario_id to run_batch instead.

tools.name: pin_result
tools.description: Add a timing to the operator's comparison tray with a short rationale. Use this to surface the two or three candidates worth a human decision — for example the fastest admissible timing alongside one that trades a little mean wait for a much shorter worst case. Pinning does not commit anything. The operator applies a pinned timing themselves, or asks you to. Pin the trade-offs, not every candidate you evaluated — the search trace already shows those. Refuses to pin an inadmissible timing. The tray is a shortlist the operator can apply with one click, so anything in it must be legal to deploy. Use unpin_result to remove a pin.

scenario_id.description: Scenario the metrics were measured under. Defaults to active.

tools.name: unpin_result
tools.description: Remove a timing from the operator's comparison tray, or clear the tray entirely. Use this when a pin turns out to be wrong — superseded by a better candidate, or measured under assumptions that have since changed. Without it you would have to ask the operator to clean up after you.

yellow_s.description: Yellow after every green, seconds. Safety-derived floor of 4 s — see the min_yellow constraint.

all_red_s.description: All-red clearance, seconds. Safety-derived floor of 2 s — see the min_all_red constraint.

left_protected.description: Give NS left turns an exclusive phase.

ns_left_green_s.description: Protected left phase duration. Must be 0 when left_protected is false.

config.description: The pinned timing to remove. Omit to clear the tray.

clear_all.description: Remove every pin. Ignored when config is supplied.

tools.name: play_sequence
tools.description: Hand the operator a scrubbable, narrated walkthrough of your reasoning. Each step puts a timing — or a pair of timings — on the cycle diagram with a one-line caption. The operator can pause, scrub and replay it. Two kinds of step: - focus="structure" (default) draws the cycle diagram: where the phases sit, what a protected phase costs in cycle time. - focus="metrics" compares OUTCOMES side by side: mean wait, 95th percentile, left-turn wait, max queue, throughput. Requires compare_config. Use a metrics step whenever the argument is about tail delay, queues or throughput rather than phase layout. Two plans can be structurally near-identical and still differ by twenty seconds of 95th-percentile wait. The cycle diagram cannot show that; a metrics step can. REACH FOR THIS when the answer is structural and a diagram carries it better than a sentence: · the fastest timing is not the one you recommend · a phase was added or removed, and you want to show what it cost · the cycle length moved substantially, or the split rebalanced · the right answer differs between two scenarios · you are explaining a refusal, and the legal timing looks different When two plans are structurally near-identical but differ in outcome, do not skip the replay: use focus="metrics" instead. Fall back to prose only when neither structure nor outcomes differ meaningfully. A comparison step draws both timings to the same seconds-per-pixel scale, so a difference in cycle length is visible rather than asserted. Captions should say what changed and what it cost — the diagram already shows the shape, so do not narrate the shape. This does NOT change the committed timing. It is an explanation, not a deployment. Metrics for every referenced timing are re-measured here so the captions cannot drift from what is on screen.

query.description: An NC case number (e.g. 26CV001234-012) or citation number (e.g. 92403H2).

tools.name: courthouse_info

caseNumber.description: NC case number, e.g. 26CR031353-910 (county is derived from it).

tools.name: check_traffic_charge
tools.description: Check whether NC traffic charges from a citation can be waived or require a court appearance, and how to request a reduction — no case number needed. Provide the charge(s) from the paper citation. Read-only. NC only. Not legal advice.

county.description: Optional NC county, for reduction guidance.

tools.name: estimate_license_points
tools.description: Estimate NC driver's-license points under G.S. 20-16(c) for traffic charges, plus any mandatory suspension for excessive speeding — no case number needed. DMV points only, not insurance (SDIP) points. Read-only. NC only. Not legal advice.

priorPoints.description: Points already on the license, if known.

tools.name: check_expunction_options
tools.description: Find which NC expunction statute and AOC petition form fit how each charge on a case ended. With a case number (e.g. 22CR702455-520) it routes against the live case; with no case number it returns the full NC expunction statute table. Routing only — not an eligibility determination. Read-only. NC only. Not legal advice.

caseNumber.description: NC case number, e.g. 22CR702455-520. Omit to get the full statute table.

felony.description: Treat charges as felony where the record degree is ambiguous.

tools.name: check_court_scam
tools.description: Check whether a demand for payment supposedly from a North Carolina court — missed jury duty, unpaid court costs, a warrant, a bond — matches known court-impersonation scam patterns. Returns deterministic FINDINGS and a severity (0 low, 1 caution, 2 high), never a verdict. IMPORTANT: severity 0 means only that none of the patterns checked for are present — it is NOT a finding that the demand is legitimate, and must never be reported as one. Pass ids from the enums verbatim. If a case or citation number is involved, also call lookup_court_case; a real case number does not make a payment demand legitimate. Read-only. NC only. Not legal advice.

claim_type.description: What the contact claimed the money was for.

contact_channel.description: How they made contact. Real NC court notices arrive by mail.

case_or_citation_number.description: Any case or citation number they cited, if one was given. Not verified here — use lookup_court_case for that.

amount_demanded.description: Amount demanded, in whole US dollars.

payment_method_requested.description: How they asked to be paid. No NC court takes gift cards, crypto or wires.

behavioral_flags.description: Every tactic that applies. More detail gives a better assessment.

raw_description.description: The person's own account, in their words. Scanned for scam language; never stored.

tools.name: subscribe_to_case_updates
tools.description: Sign up for email alerts about an NC court case — new hearing dates, changes and dispositions. This SENDS ONE CONFIRMATION EMAIL to the address given. It does not start monitoring: no alerts are sent, and nothing is activated, until the recipient clicks the link in that email. Use it only when the person has asked for alerts and has given you their own email address; do not subscribe an address on someone else's behalf. NC only. Not legal advice.

name.description: The person's full name, first and last.

email.description: Where the confirmation email is sent. Must belong to the person asking.

caseNumber.description: NC case number (e.g. 26CV001234-012) or citation number (e.g. 92403H2).

phone.description: Optional 10-digit US phone number, digits only.

sites.name: arenna.link
sites.description: Arenna helps instructors manage availability, take bookings, and let AI fill their schedule. Free to start, 30-second setup.

tools.name: ask_concierge
tools.description: Ask this business's concierge a question in natural language — hours, policies, recommendations, anything a guest would ask at the desk. Replies come from the same knowledge and conversation engine the human-facing chat on this page uses, and context is kept across calls so follow-ups work. Use this for judgement and nuance. Do NOT use it for facts the free lookup tools already return — prefer get_business_info for contact details and list_offerings for services, which are instant and cost nothing. Returns { ok, answer, conversation_id }.

question.description: The visitor's question, in natural language. One question per call; the concierge answers conversationally.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

conversation_id.description: The conversation this reply belongs to. Stable across calls on this page.

tools.name: get_business_info
tools.description: Verified public facts about this business: name, how it introduces itself, published contact details, the topics it invites questions about, and whether it can take a booking. Free and instant, no conversation started. Call this FIRST for anything factual — it is cheaper and more reliable than asking the concierge. Returns { ok, name, introduction, contact { email, phone, url }, suggested_topics[], booking_available }. Every Lobby tool returns that same envelope: `ok`, plus `error` with `code` and `message` when `ok` is false, alongside its own payload.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

introduction.description: How the business introduces itself to a visitor.

contact.description: Published contact details, or null if none.

suggested_topics.description: Topics this concierge is prepared to discuss.

booking_available.description: True when this concierge exposes booking tools. When false, nothing here can be scheduled — offer the contact details instead of implying a booking is possible.

tools.name: list_offerings
tools.description: The services this business offers, as structured data an agent can compare, filter or present. Each offering carries an explicit `bookable` flag — check it before attempting to schedule anything. Free and instant. Returns { ok, offerings[] of { id, name, description, price, currency, bookable, action_url, contact_required }, total, booking_available }.

bookable_only.description: When true, return only offerings that can be scheduled through the booking tools. Default false (return all).

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

offerings.description: The business’s services, comparable and filterable.

id.description: Stable id to pass to other tools.

price.description: Null when the business does not publish a price.

bookable.description: True only when this specific offering can be scheduled through the booking tools. Never assume a bookable offering from the presence of a booking tool.

contact_required.description: True when arranging this offering needs a human — use the contact details from get_business_info.

booking_available.description: Whether this concierge can book at all. False means every offering is contact-only regardless of its own flag.

tools.name: get_booking_options
tools.description: What can be booked with this business, and for how long. Returns the bookable appointment types with their durations. Call this before check_availability — availability is always relative to one booking type, because duration determines which slots fit. Returns { ok, booking_types[] of { id, name, description, duration_minutes, price, currency, location_kind }, timezone }.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

timezone.description: IANA zone the business keeps its hours in. Slot times are returned as absolute UTC instants regardless, so a visitor in another zone is never offered a time that does not exist.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Free times for one booking type in a date range. Every slot is a real opening: the business’s published hours minus anything already on its calendar. An empty list is a definite "nothing free in that range", not an error — widen the range or offer to take a message. Returns { ok, slots[] of { start_utc, end_utc, start_local }, total, timezone, searched { from_date, to_date } }.

to_date.description: Last date to consider, YYYY-MM-DD, INCLUSIVE. Omit for a single day. At most 60 days after from_date.

visitor_timezone.description: The visitor's IANA timezone, if known (e.g. 'Europe/Berlin'). Slot times are echoed in it for display. Omit and the business’s own zone is used.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

start_local.description: Same instant, formatted in visitor_timezone, for showing a person. Never pass this back — pass start_utc.

tools.name: start_booking
tools.description: Book one of the free slots from check_availability. THIS COMMITS the visitor to an appointment and emails the business, so it is deliberately two-step: call it first WITHOUT `confirmed`, show the returned summary to the visitor in their own words, and only call it again with `confirmed: true` once they have explicitly agreed. Never set `confirmed: true` on the first call, and never infer agreement from the visitor merely having asked about times. Returns { ok, status, summary { what, when_utc, duration_minutes, guest_name, guest_email, business }, booking_id }. The visitor is emailed a confirmation with a calendar invitation attached and their own cancellation link. `cancel_url` is null here and stays null on purpose: that link is the visitor’s only credential for their appointment and it is not handed to a tool caller. If the visitor later wants to cancel, ask them for the token in that email and use cancel_booking — do not send them to the business, and do not try their booking_id.

start_utc.description: Exactly as returned by check_availability. Do not construct or round this yourself.

guest_name.description: The name the visitor gave you, as they gave it. This is what the business will see on the appointment.

guest_email.description: Where the confirmation goes. Ask the visitor; never invent, guess or reuse an address from elsewhere on the page.

notes.description: Anything the business should know beforehand.

confirmed.description: The visitor has seen the summary and explicitly agreed. Omit or false on the first call.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

status.description: `needs_confirmation` means NOTHING was booked yet. `booked` means the appointment exists, is on the business’s calendar, and a confirmation email has gone to the address given — carrying a calendar invitation and the visitor’s own cancellation link. Tell them to expect it. The appointment itself does not depend on that email: `booked` is the record, and a mail delay is not a booking that failed.

summary.description: Exactly what will be, or has been, booked. Read this back to the visitor verbatim before confirming.

tools.name: cancel_booking
tools.description: Cancel an appointment the visitor already has, using the cancellation token from their own confirmation email. THIS RELEASES the slot, tells the business, and cannot be undone, so it is two-step exactly like start_booking: call it first WITHOUT `confirmed`, read the returned summary back to the visitor, and only call it again with `confirmed: true` once they have explicitly agreed. Ask the visitor for the cancellation link or token from their confirmation email — that token is the ONLY thing that authorises this, and a booking id will not work and must not be tried. Never guess, construct, or reuse a token, and never take one from anywhere but the visitor you are speaking to. Returns { ok, status, summary { business, cancels, when_utc } }.

cancel_token.description: The token from the visitor’s confirmation email — either the token itself or the last path segment before /cancel in their cancellation link. This is a secret belonging to that one appointment. It is NOT the booking_id that start_booking returns, and passing an id here is refused.

confirmed.description: The visitor has seen the summary and explicitly agreed to cancel. Omit or false on the first call.

ok.description: False when the request could not be fulfilled.

error.description: Present only when ok is false.

status.description: `needs_confirmation` means NOTHING was cancelled yet and the appointment still stands. `cancelled` means the slot is free again, the calendar entry is gone, and both the visitor and the business have been emailed. Cancelling twice is safe and reports `cancelled` both times — the backend is idempotent, so a repeated call is never an error and never a second cancellation.

summary.description: What will be, or has been, cancelled. Read this back to the visitor before confirming.

cancels.description: Plain-language description of the appointment the token belongs to, for reading aloud.

when_utc.description: When the cancelled appointment was to start, as the backend reports it. NULL before confirmation: nothing previews a booking by token, so the time is genuinely not known until the cancellation is made. Do not invent a time for the visitor on the first call — ask them to confirm from their own email instead.

tools.name: asus_product_filters
tools.description: Browse and filter ASUS official website products by product line (ProductLevel1Code / ProductLevel2Code), with optional category, series, spec, price and sort filtering. Product URLs in the returned productList are already absolute — use them as-is. TOOL SELECTION (important): this is the DEFAULT tool for product discovery. Use asus_product_filters whenever the user does NOT name a specific model or product name — i.e. when they describe a need, a category, or any set of conditions (e.g. "laptops under $1000", "a lightweight ultrabook for work", "gaming desktops", "cheapest monitor", "newest AiO PCs", "OLED 14-inch notebooks"). Only use asus_product_search when the user explicitly names a concrete product or model keyword (e.g. "ZenBook 14 OLED", "Vivobook S 15", "ProArt P16", "RT-AX88U"). If the request mixes both a model name and conditions, prefer asus_product_search for the named model. When in doubt (vague or need-based request), choose asus_product_filters. REQUIRED FIRST STEP: call asus_productLine with a product category keyword to obtain ProductLevel1Code and ProductLevel2Code, then pass them here together with websiteCode. FILTER VALUES ARE DYNAMIC: the valid values for CategoryName, SeriesName and spec depend on the product line and websiteCode, and can only be obtained from THIS tool's own response (they are NOT available from asus_productLine). Then call this tool again with those values to get the filtered product list. NO DISCOVERY NEEDED FOR PRICE OR SORT: pass a concrete budget directly via minPrice / maxPrice as plain numbers (e.g. "under $30000" → maxPrice:…

sites.name: cocktail.glass
sites.description: Cocktail recipe catalogue — find drinks by ingredient, movie/TV scene, or family; check what you can make with what's on your shelf; pull a full recipe or a random pick.

tools.name: search_cocktails
tools.description: Search the cocktail catalogue by name (substring, case- and diacritic-insensitive, so "carre" matches "Carré"). Returns up to 25 summary results — name, page URL, family, glassware — ranked exact match first, then prefix, then suffix, then any substring. Use this when the user names a drink (even fuzzily) and you want to confirm it exists or disambiguate similar names; once you have a single name, call get_cocktail_recipe for the full recipe. For ingredient-based discovery use find_cocktails_by_ingredient instead.

query.description: Cocktail name or part of one — a single drink name, not an ingredient or category.

tools.name: list_cocktails
tools.description: List the whole catalogue: every cocktail as a summary (name, page URL, family, glassware), in catalogue order, optionally restricted to one drink family. Unlike search_cocktails and find_cocktails_by_ingredient — which cap their results and need a query — this takes no query and returns every matching cocktail, so use it to browse or enumerate the full set of 500 drinks (or a whole family) when there is nothing specific to search for. For one named drink use get_cocktail_recipe; to discover by ingredient use find_cocktails_by_ingredient.

family.description: Optional drink family — one of: Spirit-Forward, Sour, Highball, Fizz & Collins, Spritz, Champagne Cocktail, Tiki, Punch, Flip & Nog, Hot Drink, Shot. Matched exactly (case- and diacritic-insensitive); an unknown family returns an empty list. Omit to list the entire catalogue.

tools.name: get_cocktail_recipe
tools.description: Get the full recipe for one cocktail by name: ingredients with measures and units, preparation steps, garnish, glassware, family, page URL, and any film or TV appearances. Matching is case- and diacritic-insensitive: it tries an exact name match first, then falls back to the first substring match. Returns one cocktail object, or an { error } if nothing matches. Use this when you have a specific drink name; if the name is ambiguous or you want a list, call search_cocktails first.

name.description: The cocktail name. Exact is best; partial names work but resolve to the first substring match, so prefer search_cocktails when the name is uncertain.

tools.name: find_cocktails_by_ingredient
tools.description: Find every cocktail in the catalogue that uses one specific ingredient. Matching is a case- and diacritic-insensitive substring match against each cocktail's ingredient names, so "gin" will also match "sloe gin" and "ginger beer" — use a more specific term if that matters. Returns up to 60 summary results (name, URL, family, glassware) in catalogue order. Takes one ingredient only; for "what can I make from X, Y, and Z?" use find_makeable_cocktails instead, which handles multiple ingredients and reports near-misses.

ingredient.description: A single ingredient term. One value only; passing a comma-separated list is treated as one literal string and will rarely match. Use find_makeable_cocktails for multi-ingredient queries.

tools.name: find_cocktails_in_movie
tools.description: Find every cocktail that appears in a given film or TV show. Case- and diacritic-insensitive substring match against both the title and the scene description, so a character or actor works too — e.g. "Casablanca", "Bond", "Hemingway". Each result names the cocktail, the film/show title, the year, and the scene. Returns up to 60 appearances ordered oldest year first, then by cocktail name. A single cocktail can appear multiple times if it shows up in multiple scenes that match. Use this only for on-screen appearances; for a drink by name use search_cocktails, and to browse the whole catalogue use list_cocktails.

movie.description: A film or TV show title, full or partial

tools.name: find_makeable_cocktails
tools.description: Given the ingredients you have on hand, find every cocktail you can make completely — one where you already have all of its ingredients. Garnishes are treated as optional and plain water is assumed available; soda and tonic water are not. Matching is word-based, not substring: "gin" matches "London dry gin" but not "ginger beer", and generic terms do not match product-class extras ("gin" will not cover "sloe gin" or "orange bitters"). Returns two lists: "makeable" (drinks you can make now, up to 60) and "almostMakeable" (drinks exactly one ingredient short, up to 25, each naming the missing ingredient). Drinks needing two or more extra ingredients are omitted entirely. Both lists are ordered simplest first — fewest distinct ingredients in the full recipe, then alphabetical by name. Use this for multi-ingredient "what can I make?" questions; for a single ingredient use find_cocktails_by_ingredient.

ingredients.description: The ingredients you have available — spirits, liqueurs, juices, mixers, etc.

tools.name: random_cocktail
tools.description: Suggest one cocktail picked uniformly at random from the catalogue (or from one family if "family" is given) and return its full recipe — ingredients with measures, preparation steps, garnish, glassware, page URL, and any film or TV appearances. Each call returns an independent draw, so repeated calls give different drinks. The "family" filter matches the family name exactly (case- and diacritic-insensitive); if no cocktail matches that family the call silently falls back to the full catalogue rather than erroring. Use this only when the user wants a suggestion or inspiration with no specific drink in mind. For a named cocktail use get_cocktail_recipe; for "anything with gin" use find_cocktails_by_ingredient; for "what can I make from what I have" use find_makeable_cocktails.

family.description: Optional drink family — one of: Spirit-Forward, Sour, Highball, Fizz & Collins, Spritz, Champagne Cocktail, Tiki, Punch, Flip & Nog, Hot Drink, Shot. Other values fall back to the full catalogue. Omit for an unrestricted random pick.

sites.description: Dutch shop for Mini-Z and Traxxas RC cars, parts and upgrades, selling online and from its store and Mini-Z race track in Oldemarkt.

tools.name: minizshop_search_products
tools.description: Search public products by focused catalog terms or a known exact SKU; browse a category by omitting query. For a generic part on a named brand/vehicle, use complementary queries for the part and brand plus part in one call: investigate original-brand and aftermarket options, then compare the relevant candidates. Titles mix Dutch and English; alternate names can help. Put suitability context in context_terms. Categories can be incomplete or inaccurate: they help orientation but do not replace keyword searches. When a chosen category misses relevant options, search without that inferred category while keeping explicit customer constraints. Refine noisy results with a discriminating noun/brand rather than accepting the first page. At most three results have detail_read=true with current detail records already returned by the Store API; use those facts without a duplicate read. Read other shortlisted IDs when needed. Compare suitability; search rank and metadata are not proof of fit. Prices are strings in minor currency units; recheck the product before purchase.

browse.description: Enabled by default in Dex. Keep enabled for product discovery and requests for a product type or range, even without the word browse. Returns up to 100 matching identities and a browse.id: use that ID as browse_search_id in the final answer. Set false only for focused identification or a fixed comparison that needs no collection. It does not claim compatibility. Prefer the narrow relevant published category and explicit required_terms to keep accessories and wrong specifications out; refine an irrelevant first search before choosing the collection.

required_terms.description: Hard filters from explicit customer requirements: every group must match the current product name or public attribute; alternatives inside each group are OR. Choose literal variants from catalog names, e.g. a requested hardness might appear as 20°, 20deg or 20 degree. Select appropriate language/synonym variants semantically; no automatic translation. Use the narrow product category for the requested kind. Omitted/undocumented values do not pass this strict filter; context_terms alone only ranks. Never claim a literal match guarantees compatibility.

context_terms.description: Separate the product noun/query from relevant public constraints resolved from the whole conversation and selected vehicle: chassis, dimensions, drive, scale or product type. Choose short catalog-language terms, e.g. MR-04, 98 mm, RWD. These rerank up to 100 current candidates using title, visible attributes, categories and Showcase metadata without removing undocumented candidates. Do not include private customer data, a transcript, negative constraints or an unverified event-eligibility claim. context_match lists actual metadata matches and still-unverified terms; it never guarantees compatibility.

exclude_ids.description: Previously returned product IDs the shopper explicitly rejected. They remain excluded across alternative queries and contextual ranking.

price_currency.description: Currency of max_price_minor. Pass the shopper’s stated currency; a mismatch with the shop currency returns a clarification instead of treating CHF as EUR.

query.description: Short catalog keywords. Omit or leave empty to browse the selected category.

queries.description: Optional alternative short searches for the same customer goal, chosen from the conversation and observed results. Searches the whole public catalog unless you explicitly set a category. Use instead of query/sku to combine spelling, language or part-name variants in one bounded read. Results are deduplicated; each query retains its matched IDs and pagination. Follow with exact product reads and manual/manufacturer research for unresolved evidence, not more identical searches.

category_slug.description: Published catalog category. For browsing cars use autos (Mini-Z cars/chassis) or voertuigen-kits (Traxxas vehicles/kits), without a generic query. For Mini-Z setup/measuring tools use gereedschap. Categories include descendants. Read category_scope.path: similar category names can belong to different brands or vehicle families. If the path does not match the known vehicle, retry without that category; do not keep querying the wrong family. Check whether each result is the requested product type.

in_stock.description: Set true only when the shopper explicitly requires immediate stock. This excludes ALL backorder/preorder products, even when purchasable. Omit for model information, identification and ordinary product discovery.

tools.name: minizshop_get_product
tools.description: Read one public product with its detailed description, published shop guidance, price, stock_label, attributes and shop URL. stock_label follows the storefront stock-visibility settings: quote it as supplied, never infer exact inventory from a lower bound or a qualitative label. Includes service terms supplied by shop features; use these for digital credit, validity and how a shop service works. Hidden, private and password-protected products are excluded. Internal metadata and hidden inventory counts are never exposed. related_products lists up to 6 products that often share an order with this product or its product line, or that the shop links to it: useful suggestions for what else a shopper may want, to read and verify before recommending. A relation is not proof of fit, necessity or box contents.

tools.name: minizshop_compare_products
tools.description: Read full public details of two to four products in one call, including descriptions, attributes and shop guidance. Use to compare candidate dimensions, connectors, included items and stated chassis compatibility after discovery. Missing or nonpublic products are reported as unavailable. An omitted specification remains unknown.

tools.name: minizshop_find_parts
tools.description: Find parts linked to the exact public model product_id in the shop parts catalog. When the requested part is known, use query for its name or SKU within this model’s parts, e.g. bumper; omit query for an overview. A catalog relationship is evidence, not a guarantee of fit for an unspecified variant. Empty results do not prove incompatibility; try a shorter part term or its original catalog language once.

query.description: Use the manufacturer’s catalog noun, usually English (for example wheels). The shopper’s language is for the answer; this literal parts index does not automatically translate Dutch synonyms.

tools.name: minizshop_search_content
tools.description: Search the local index of anonymous rendered shop pages, including events, guides and plugin-generated information. Page descriptions and Dutch search topics help identify what each page can answer; original excerpts provide the evidence. Only Dutch source pages are indexed, once per page. Use short topic keywords in the site language (Dutch), resolving synonyms/typos from the conversation, e.g. rijderspas geldigheid. Returns relevant passages and source URLs with freshness. Use read_site_page for more surrounding terms. Use search_products for cars/parts, current price and stock; empty site results say nothing about catalog availability.

tools.name: minizshop_read_site_page
tools.description: Read a known public information or shop-service URL from a site search, page context or service index. Includes rendered plugin/shortcode information, headings and source timestamps. Products and catalogue listings are excluded: use search_products and get_product for their live public metadata. Explicit service sources such as the rider pass remain available. Use offset=next_offset when relevant terms continue. No account, checkout, queries or external URLs. Never infer personal balances or dates from public terms.

url.description: Prefer the root-relative path from the source, such as /contact-2/. An exact tool-provided absolute URL also works; never retype or guess its hostname.

tools.name: minizshop_get_store_info
tools.description: Read the public shop introduction and links to current store information. Follow the schedule source for opening hours; never infer hours if it is unavailable.

sites.name: n-ix.com
sites.description: Software development and technology consulting

tools.name: get_company_facts
tools.description: Returns verified corporate facts about N-iX: founding year and operating history, headcount, delivery locations, client retention, long-term client tenure examples, business continuity record, partnership tiers (AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, Snowflake and others), and awards. Each fact carries the page on n-ix.com that states it and the date it was verified. Use for track-record, vendor-stability, and "about the company" questions.

topic.description: Filter facts by topic; "all" (or omitting it) returns the full set.

offset.description: Pagination offset (max 10 items per response).

tools.name: get_compliance_evidence
tools.description: Returns N-iX certification and compliance status with evidence: ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR DPA availability and turnaround time, EU AI Act readiness, ISO 42001 status, FSQS qualification, EU data residency options. Each entry includes status, scope, last audit date, and a verification URL or artifact request path (with turnaround in business days where a buyer asks how fast). Use for procurement, vendor-qualification, and regulatory questions. Calling with no parameters returns the full registry.

framework.description: Return a single framework entry; omit for the full registry.

offset.description: Pagination offset (max 10 items per response).

tools.name: get_engagement_terms
tools.description: Returns N-iX engagement models and commercial terms: the APEX model (Assess, Pilot, Expand, eXcel) with duration and output per phase, fixed-scope pilots, dedicated teams, staff augmentation, and managed services. Includes phasing, entry commitment, pricing structure, IP ownership, notice period, and exit terms per model. Use for questions about starting small, avoiding lock-in, commitment structure, or exit clauses. Terms Legal has not cleared for publication are returned as "discussed_in_msa" rather than omitted.

model.description: Return a single engagement model; omit for all models.

offset.description: Pagination offset (max 10 items per response).

tools.name: get_team_ramp_options
tools.description: Returns N-iX delivery locations and team ramp-up facts: countries in CEE and Latin America, typical time to the first engineer and to a full team, seniority distribution, English proficiency, and time-zone overlap with US and European business hours. Use for nearshoring, staff augmentation, ramp speed, and location comparison questions.

client_timezone.description: Return locations with working-hours overlap with this client time zone.

stack.description: Free-text technology stack to match against location skill notes.

offset.description: Pagination offset (max 10 items per response).

tools.name: request_consultation
tools.description: Pre-fills the N-iX contact form to request a consultation or a small paid assessment/pilot (including an APEX Assess engagement). This tool only pre-fills the form: it returns the prefilled state and the submit itself is performed by the in-browser handler on a user-confirmed action. The endpoint additionally enforces a same-origin guard, a single-use token bound to the hash of the exact payload, per-IP rate limiting and spam scoring; these are anti-abuse controls, not a proof of human presence. Provide name, work email, company, and a short description of the need.

name.description: Full name of the person requesting the consultation.

phone.description: Optional phone number for a call back.

message.description: Short description of the need or goal.

interest.description: Type of engagement the user is interested in.

tools.name: search_delivery_proof
tools.description: Searches verified N-iX delivery records. Each record is a real engagement with the client (or NDA status), industry, services, tech stack, a short problem/solution narrative, and a structured list of measured outcomes (before/after metrics such as velocity gains, cycle-time reduction, deployment reliability, cost savings, ROI - each with baseline, result, measurement method, evidence tier, and source URL). Use this both when the user asks for proof of measurable outcomes and when they ask for comparable references or case studies in a given industry or technology. Set metrics_only=true to receive a flat list of quantified outcome facts without narratives.

service.description: Filter by N-iX service line.

metric_type.description: Filter outcomes by the kind of measured metric.

named_reference_only.description: Return only engagements where a named client reference is available.

metrics_only.description: If true, return a flat list of quantified outcome facts without narratives.

query.description: Free-text search over narratives and technology stack.

offset.description: Pagination offset (max 10 items per response).

tools.name: search_services
tools.description: Searches the N-iX service catalog (AI and GenAI engineering, AI agents, data engineering and governance, cloud and DevOps, application modernization, custom development, embedded/IoT and computer vision, team extension). Returns the service name, a scope summary, the typical smallest paid entry engagement, and the service page URL. Use for "what does N-iX offer in area X" and "how small can we start" questions.

category.description: Filter by service line.

query.description: Free-text search over service names and scope summaries.

offset.description: Pagination offset (max 10 items per response).
