tools.name: check_fiber_availability
tools.description: Check whether NTE can deliver fiber broadband (TV og internett) to a Norwegian street address. Pass the address as the customer wrote it. If the result is 'multiple_addresses', ask the customer to pick one of the candidates and call again with it exactly. On 'checked', the 'result' field means: deliverable: fiber can be ordered now; campaign: deliverable with a campaign price, the customer identifies on nte.no to see it, so no products are listed; brl: NTE has an agreement with the customer's housing company (borettslag/sameie), so no products are listed; continueUrl leads to the housing company's offer, or to a form where the customer asks NTE for help choosing the right product; partner: delivered by another Altibox partner, named in 'partner' when known, otherwise the customer finds their partner on altibox.no; lead or notDeliverable: not available yet, the customer can register interest on nte.no; If the status is 'unit_selection', the building has several dwellings: ask the customer for their bruksenhetsnummer (for example H0201, on the letterbox or the door) and call again with both address and unit. For a 'checked' result, always give the customer 'continueUrl' to see details and order. This tool never places an order.

address.description: Street address, e.g. 'Kongens gate 1, 7713 Steinkjer'

unit.description: Bruksenhetsnummer, only when a previous call returned 'unit_selection', e.g. 'H0201'

tools.name: get_power_products
tools.description: List NTE's strømavtaler (power agreements) with price description, terms (påslag, månedlig fastbeløp and similar, as written on nte.no), angrerett and a link to each product. Optionally filter by customer segment: Privat, Bedrift, Borettslag or Landbruk. Prices are NTE's own; spotpris itself varies by hour and area and is not included. Always give the customer the product 'url' to read the full terms and order. This tool never places an order.

segment.description: Customer segment: Privat, Bedrift, Borettslag, Landbruk. Default all

tools.name: get_service_announcements

For power cuts, NTE is not the nettselskap: point the customer to their grid company, listed in 'power'.

tools.name: getBookingCatalog
tools.description: Retrieve the merchant's bookable services, service categories, available staff, and valid service-staff combinations. Call this FIRST when the user wants to book. IMPORTANT: After calling this tool you MUST follow this sequence before calling getServiceAvailability: (1) Present the list of categories and services and ask the user to choose a service. (2) Once a service is chosen, look up its assigned staff from the assignments list and ask the user whether they have a staff preference, showing the available staff names. (3) Only after both a service AND a staff choice (or explicit 'no preference') are confirmed, call getServiceAvailability. Never pick a service or staff member on behalf of the user without their input.

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code for translated names (e.g. 'en', 'fr'). If omitted, the user's browser language is used automatically.

tools.name: getServiceAvailability
tools.description: Get available appointment time slots for a specific service and staff member over a date range. Returned times are in the merchant's local timezone (provided in the response). If the returned slots array is empty, do NOT tell the user the booking is impossible. Instead, inform them that no slots were found for that service in that date range, and offer to: (1) search a different or wider date range, or (2) go back and select a different service. Once the user has chosen a slot, pass its start value directly to previewBooking.

staffId.description: Staff ID to check availability for. If the user selected a specific staff member, use their ID from the assignments list. If the user has no preference, do NOT pass -1: instead, pick the first staffId from the assignments list that is assigned to the chosen service and use that ID. Never pass -1 unless the assignments list is empty for the service.

startDate.description: Start of the search window in YYYY-MM-DD format

endDate.description: End of the search window in YYYY-MM-DD format

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code

tools.name: previewBooking
tools.description: Validate a booking intent and fetch the invoice, price breakdown, and policy details. Call this after the user has selected a service, staff, time slot, and provided their name and contact info. Present the returned invoice total, duration, and cancellation/payment policies to the user. Only proceed to bookAppointment after the user explicitly confirms.

staffId.description: Staff ID from getBookingCatalog. Use -1 for no preference (any available staff).

slotStart.description: Appointment start time in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' format, as returned by getServiceAvailability

email.description: Client email — required to send the booking confirmation

mobilePhoneNumber.description: Client phone in E.164 format (e.g. +15145551234). Optional but recommended for SMS reminders.

additionalRequest.description: Special instructions or notes for the merchant

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code (e.g. 'fr', 'en'). If omitted, the user's browser language is used automatically. Only pass this to override the browser's detected locale.

tools.name: bookAppointment
tools.description: ⚠️ Create an appointment booking. Do NOT call this tool until you have called previewBooking, presented the invoice and policies to the user, and received their explicit confirmation to proceed. Returns a tracking number and appointment ID on success. A confirmation email will be sent to the client.

staffId.description: Staff ID from getBookingCatalog. Use -1 for no preference (any available staff).

slotStart.description: Appointment start time in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' format, as returned by getServiceAvailability

tools.name: getBookingCatalog
tools.description: Retrieve the merchant's bookable services, service categories, available staff, and valid service-staff combinations. Call this FIRST when the user wants to book. IMPORTANT: After calling this tool you MUST follow this sequence before calling getServiceAvailability: (1) Present the list of categories and services and ask the user to choose a service. (2) Once a service is chosen, look up its assigned staff from the assignments list and ask the user whether they have a staff preference, showing the available staff names. (3) Only after both a service AND a staff choice (or explicit 'no preference') are confirmed, call getServiceAvailability. Never pick a service or staff member on behalf of the user without their input.

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code for translated names (e.g. 'en', 'fr'). If omitted, the user's browser language is used automatically.

tools.name: getServiceAvailability
tools.description: Get available appointment time slots for a specific service and staff member over a date range. Returned times are in the merchant's local timezone (provided in the response). If the returned slots array is empty, do NOT tell the user the booking is impossible. Instead, inform them that no slots were found for that service in that date range, and offer to: (1) search a different or wider date range, or (2) go back and select a different service. Once the user has chosen a slot, pass its start value directly to previewBooking.

staffId.description: Staff ID to check availability for. If the user selected a specific staff member, use their ID from the assignments list. If the user has no preference, do NOT pass -1: instead, pick the first staffId from the assignments list that is assigned to the chosen service and use that ID. Never pass -1 unless the assignments list is empty for the service.

sites.name: speedof.me
sites.description: Browser-based internet speed test for mobile and desktop connections.

tools.name: run_speed_test
tools.description: Run a single, one-off internet speed test in this browser with SpeedOf.Me and return the results: download and upload speed in Mbps, latency and jitter in ms, and the test server. Takes roughly 30 to 60 seconds. Use this only for a one-time, interactive check. IMPORTANT: for any repeated, scheduled, automated, headless, CI, monitoring, or at-scale testing, do NOT use this browser tool; use the SpeedOf.Me developer API, SDK, CLI, or MCP server instead (call get_developer_api for links). The API needs no browser, is faster, and is built for programmatic use.

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: Create a PUBLIC shareable link to the most recent completed speed test and return it. Uploads a branded image of the latest result (download, upload, latency; no IP address) and returns a public https://i.speedof.me/ URL plus a ready-to-post caption, exactly like the on-page Share action. Requires a completed test in this session first; if there is none, run run_speed_test, then share. Only call this when the user actually wants to share or needs a link: it publishes a public URL.

tools.name: get_past_results
tools.description: Return this browser's saved speed test history (from local storage) with all-time averages, the latest result, and the most recent tests. Read-only and local: no test is run and nothing leaves the browser. Use it to answer questions about past or average performance (e.g. "what is my average download speed", "how fast was my last test"). Returns an empty history if the user has not run tests in this browser.

limit.description: How many recent results to return, newest first. Default 20. Averages are always computed over ALL stored tests, not just these.

tools.name: get_developer_api
tools.description: RECOMMENDED for any non-interactive speed testing. Returns links and details for the SpeedOf.Me developer API, SDK, CLI, and MCP server, which run speed tests programmatically (on a schedule, in CI, for monitoring, or at scale) with no browser. Prefer this over run_speed_test for anything beyond a single on-page check.

sites.description: AI agent that parses your Italian energy bill, compares 44+ electricity and gas offers in real time, and walks you through switching providers — with WebMCP tools to estimate savings, read available offers, and submit a subscription.

tools.name: calculate_energy_savings
tools.description: Confronta tariffe Luce/Gas e calcola il risparmio annuo con scenario analysis (PUN/PSV) ancorato al forward. Accetta bill_text oppure dati già estratti. MODALITÀ 1 (bolletta): passa commodity + bill_text — il tool estrae consumi, spesa, zona e tipo_tariffa. MODALITÀ 2 (dati noti): passa commodity + yearly_consumption_kwh + current_annual_spend + zone + tariff_type. ESEMPIO: {commodity:'LUCE', yearly_consumption_kwh:2700, zone:'NORD', current_annual_spend:850, tariff_type:'variabile'} RISPOSTA: tabella top3 + market_sensitivity (stable vs market_dependent con 3 scenari) + agent_summary. Se market_dependent, il risparmio CANONICO è Atteso a PUN forward (es. 322), NON lo storico 113 — DEVI dirlo e mostrare i 3 scenari con range; 113 è al PUN bolletta nel details. Se stable, il risparmio è garantito. Usa market_sensitivity.message e baseline per riconciliare. ALIAS CAMPI: consumazioneannuo/consumoannuo_kwh=yearly_consumption_kwh, spesaannua/spesaannua_eur=current_annual_spend, tipotariffa=tariff_type. TIPO TARIFFA: se sconosciuto ma spread/prezzo_vendita presente → market_dependent (mai stable). PAYLOAD: top3 sempre con tipo_tariffa (null se sconosciuto). UI: colonna Risparmio e headline usano market_sensitivity.scenarios[Atteso].savings_eur se market_dependent.

commodity.description: LUCE per elettricità o GAS per gas metano

bill_text.description: (Solo se hai il testo della bolletta) Passa il testo completo per estrarre automaticamente i dati.

tools.name: parse_energy_bill
tools.description: Analizza il testo di una bolletta italiana (luce o gas) ed estrae: fornitore, POD/PDR, consumo annuo, spesa annua stimata, zona tariffaria. DOPO aver usato questo tool, usa calculate_energy_savings con i dati estratti per confrontare le offerte. ESEMPIO: l'utente incolla la bolletta → tu chiami parse_energy_bill → poi calculate_energy_savings con i risultati.

bill_text.description: Testo completo della bolletta da analizzare. Puoi estrarre il testo da un PDF.

tools.description: Recupera tutte le offerte disponibili per Luce o Gas in Italia. Restituisce nome fornitore, nome offerta, tipo (fisso/variabile), prezzo per unità e costo fisso mensile. Usa questo tool quando l'utente vuole vedere tutte le offerte disponibili senza fare un calcolo specifico.

sites.description: Mountain resort in Vernon, British Columbia, with a Fred Couples Signature golf course, The Edge fine dining restaurant, weddings and Okanagan Lake views.

tools.name: getBookingCatalog
tools.description: Retrieve the merchant's bookable services, service categories, available staff, and valid service-staff combinations. Call this FIRST when the user wants to book. IMPORTANT: After calling this tool you MUST follow this sequence before calling getServiceAvailability: (1) Present the list of categories and services and ask the user to choose a service. (2) Once a service is chosen, look up its assigned staff from the assignments list and ask the user whether they have a staff preference, showing the available staff names. (3) Only after both a service AND a staff choice (or explicit 'no preference') are confirmed, call getServiceAvailability. Never pick a service or staff member on behalf of the user without their input.

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code for translated names (e.g. 'en', 'fr'). If omitted, the user's browser language is used automatically.

tools.name: getServiceAvailability
tools.description: Get available appointment time slots for a specific service and staff member over a date range. Returned times are in the merchant's local timezone (provided in the response). If the returned slots array is empty, do NOT tell the user the booking is impossible. Instead, inform them that no slots were found for that service in that date range, and offer to: (1) search a different or wider date range, or (2) go back and select a different service. Once the user has chosen a slot, pass its start value directly to previewBooking.

staffId.description: Staff ID to check availability for. If the user selected a specific staff member, use their ID from the assignments list. If the user has no preference, do NOT pass -1: instead, pick the first staffId from the assignments list that is assigned to the chosen service and use that ID. Never pass -1 unless the assignments list is empty for the service.

startDate.description: Start of the search window in YYYY-MM-DD format

endDate.description: End of the search window in YYYY-MM-DD format

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code

tools.name: previewBooking
tools.description: Validate a booking intent and fetch the invoice, price breakdown, and policy details. Call this after the user has selected a service, staff, time slot, and provided their name and contact info. Present the returned invoice total, duration, and cancellation/payment policies to the user. Only proceed to bookAppointment after the user explicitly confirms.

staffId.description: Staff ID from getBookingCatalog. Use -1 for no preference (any available staff).

slotStart.description: Appointment start time in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' format, as returned by getServiceAvailability

email.description: Client email — required to send the booking confirmation

mobilePhoneNumber.description: Client phone in E.164 format (e.g. +15145551234). Optional but recommended for SMS reminders.

additionalRequest.description: Special instructions or notes for the merchant

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code (e.g. 'fr', 'en'). If omitted, the user's browser language is used automatically. Only pass this to override the browser's detected locale.

sites.description: Find local pros, compare prices and book home services in a few simple steps. Thumbtack makes caring for your home easier.

tools.name: get_category_recommendations
tools.description: Returns popular or trending home-service categories for a US ZIP code.

input_schema.title: get_category_recommendations input
input_schema.description: Returns popular or trending home-service categories by ZIP code. zipCode is optional; it is resolved from the current page or browser location when omitted. limit: default 20, range 1-30.

zipCode.description: US ZIP code to center the search (5 digits). Optional; resolved from the current page or browser location when omitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of categories to return (default 20, range 1-30). Values above 30 are clamped to 30.

tools.name: get_reviews_for_pros
tools.description: Returns detailed customer reviews for specific Thumbtack businesses, grouped by business and sorted by the requested order (relevance, rating, or recency).

input_schema.title: get_reviews_for_pros input
input_schema.description: Fetches detailed reviews for specific business IDs. limit: default 5, max 20 (values above 20 are clamped). When sortBy is 'most_relevant', at least one of categoryID or searchQuery is required.

businessIDs.description: Business identifiers to get reviews for (as strings).

sortBy.description: Sort order for the fetched reviews.

categoryID.description: The Thumbtack categoryID (required with searchQuery when using most_relevant sort).

searchQuery.description: The search query string (required with categoryID when using most_relevant sort).

limit.description: Number of reviews per business to return (default 5, max 20). Values above 20 are clamped to 20.

tools.name: search_home_service_pros
tools.description: Searches Thumbtack home-service pros from a free-text query and ZIP code, returning matching businesses, the best-matching category, and a request form to refine the results.

input_schema.title: search_home_service_pros input
input_schema.description: Initiates a search from a free-text user query and optional zip. zipCode is optional; it is resolved from the current page or browser location when the agent omits it.

userQuery.description: The complete user query/prompt describing the home service they need (e.g., 'I need a house cleaner', 'plumber for kitchen sink repair').

zipCode.description: US ZIP code to center the search (5 digits). Optional; resolved from the current page or browser location when omitted.

tools.name: filter_home_service_pros
tools.description: Refines a prior home-service search using request-form answers. There is no saved search, so pass categoryID + zipCode + the full accumulated answer set (from search_home_service_pros) on each call.

input_schema.title: filter_home_service_pros input
input_schema.description: Refines a pro search using request-form answers. There is no saved search, so pass categoryID + zipCode + the requestForm (its requestFormID plus the full accumulated answer set) on each call.

zipCode.description: US ZIP code to center the search (5 digits).

categoryID.description: The Thumbtack Category ID to fetch businesses for. Obtain from search_home_service_pros.

requestForm.description: Request form details supplied by the agent. There is no saved search: resubmit the requestFormID plus the full accumulated set of answers each time.

requestFormID.description: The Request Form ID for this category, from search_home_service_pros.

requestFormAnswers.description: The full accumulated set of answers to request-form questions.

tools.name: get_price_estimate
tools.description: Generate a price estimate for a home insurance policy. Covers any Spanish residential property — house, home, apartment, flat, condo, studio, loft — under any of four usage types: renting (tenant/renter insurance), owner-occupied (primary residence), landlord (investment property let out), or second home. This server quotes TWO different products: home insurance (this tool) and car insurance (quote_auto_insurance). Only pursue a home quote once the user has made clear they want to insure a HOME/property. If they just say something ambiguous like "I need insurance" / "get me a quote" without naming the product, ask whether they want home or car insurance first — never assume home. IMPORTANT: You must collect ALL required information from the customer before calling this tool: - Property address (street, city, 5-digit postal code) - Property size in square meters - Usage type (renting, owner-occupied, landlord, second home) Do NOT make up or guess any values. If any information is missing, ask the customer first.

city.description: City where the property is located (e.g., 'Madrid')

conversationLanguage.description: The language THE USER is writing in, so the price card renders in it: 'es' if they write in Spanish, 'en' if they write in English. Judge it from the customer's own messages — not from your replies, this schema, or the host's interface language. Omit it when unsure; the card then renders in Spanish.

squareMeters.description: Size of the property in square meters. Ask the customer: 'How many square meters is your property?'

street.description: Street name and number of the property (e.g., 'Calle Mayor 45, 2B')

usageType.description: How the customer uses the property: 'renting' (I'm renting), 'owner_occupied' (It's mine and I live in it), 'landlord' (It's mine and I rent it out), 'second_home' (It's my second home)

intent.description: Provide a brief summary of the user's goal. Do not invent missing intent.

context.description: Describe the situation or environment that led the user to this tool — e.g. what page they are on, what they were doing, or what triggered the request. Do not invent missing context.

tools.name: get_auto_price_estimate
tools.description: Render the car-insurance two-tier comparison card. This is the render step of the quote_auto_insurance flow. Only call it when the flow asks you to (status: "widget"), passing the exact data the flow provided. Do not call it on your own or invent quote figures.

productOptionName.description: Tuio's internal product-option name for the tier.

tierName.description: Display name of the tier ('Terceros', 'Terceros Ampliado').

ok.description: True when this tier priced; false when the carrier refused it.

quoteId.description: Tuio's id for this tier's quote.

yearlyPremium.description: Yearly premium in EUR — car pricing is quoted per year. Absent when the tier failed.

monthlyPremium.description: Yearly premium divided by 12. Absent when the tier failed.

redirectUrl.description: Per-quote link that resumes this quote on Tuio's site; the card's CTA.

recommended.description: True on the tier the card highlights.

error.description: Why this tier failed to price, when `ok` is false.

locale.description: Render locale, injected by the flow.

chatEmbed.description: True when rendered inside the WaniWani chat embed; gates Tuio's UTM attribution on the CTA. Injected by the flow.

tools.name: search_knowledge_base
tools.description: Search Tuio's knowledge base — FAQs plus the general insurance terms and conditions — using semantic search. Use this tool whenever a customer asks something Tuio's own documentation could answer: - General questions about Tuio, its products, and how they work - Coverage terms, limits, and conditions - Exclusions and exceptions - Claims procedures and requirements - What is or isn't covered under a policy This searches Tuio's PUBLIC documentation. It does NOT have access to the user's personal insurance data or their specific policy details. IMPORTANT — the knowledge base is written in Spanish. Always translate the customer's question into Spanish before passing it as `query`, even when they wrote in another language; an English query matches almost nothing. Use Spanish insurance wording where you know it (for example "water damage" -> "daños por agua", "tenant" -> "inquilino", "landlord/owner" -> "propietario", "claim" -> "siniestro", "deductible" -> "franquicia"). Then write your ANSWER back to the customer in the language they used. Search is semantic, so the phrasing does not need to match the documentation word for word.

query.description: The customer's question, translated into Spanish (the knowledge base language)

tools.name: quote_auto_insurance
tools.description: Get a Tuio car (auto) insurance quote for a Spanish vehicle, comparing two tiers (Terceros and Terceros Ampliado). This server quotes TWO different products: car insurance (this tool) and home insurance (get_price_estimate). Only start this flow once the user has made clear they want to insure a CAR. If they just say something ambiguous like "I need insurance" / "get me a quote" / "insurance for me" without naming the product, do NOT start this flow — first ask whether they want car or home insurance. Never assume car. Once car insurance is confirmed (or the user mentions a car, plate, driving, etc.): the flow asks for everything it needs a few questions at a time, so start it right away — do not pre-collect data yourself. If the user already mentioned details (plate, how they use the car, etc.), pass them in stateUpdates so those questions are skipped. LANGUAGE: the comparison card is rendered in the language you pass as `stateUpdates.locale`. This one is NOT collected from the user — never ask about it. Set it yourself from the language the user writes to you in: `"en"` only when they are writing in English, otherwise omit it and the card renders in Spanish. ## FLOW EXECUTION PROTOCOL This tool implements a multi-step conversational flow. Follow this protocol exactly: 1. Call with `action: "start"` to begin and include `intent`. `intent` must be a brief summary of the user's goal for this flow. Do NOT invent missing intent. Optionally include `context` — the situation or environment that led the user to start this flow (e.g. what page they are on, what they were doing, or what triggered the request). Only provide `context` when there is genuinely relevant situational information. Do NOT invent missing context. If the user's message already contains answers to likely questions, extract them into `stateUpdates` as `{ field: value }` pairs (see the `stateUpdates` schema for the list of writable fields). The engine will auto-skip steps whose fields are already filled…

action.description: "start" to begin the flow, "continue" to resume after a pause (interrupt or widget), "reset" to restart from the beginning with a correction to a previously-collected field

intent.description: Required when action is "start". Provide a brief summary of the user's goal for this flow. Do not invent missing intent.

context.description: Optional when action is "start". Describe the situation or environment that led the user to start this flow — e.g. what page they are on, what they were doing, or what triggered the request. Do not invent missing context.

stateUpdates.description: State field values to set before processing the next node. Pass the user's answer (keyed by the field name from the response) and any other values the user mentioned. For nested state fields, use dot-paths like "driver.name".

plate.description: The car's Spanish license plate, e.g. '1234BCD'.

b7VersionId.description: Internal Tuio vehicle-version id. Resolved automatically from the plate — never ask the user for this.

versionLabel.description: Human-readable vehicle version (make/model/trim). Resolved from the plate.

versionChoices.description: Internal — candidate vehicle versions for the plate. Set automatically; never ask the user.

firstPlateDate.description: First registration date of the car (yyyy-MM-dd). Usually resolved from the plate; only asked if the lookup didn't return it.

annualKm.description: Approximate kilometres driven per year, as one of Tuio's mileage brackets. Pick the bracket the stated yearly distance falls INTO, upper bound inclusive — e.g. 6,000 km/year → From4000To6000km, 7,000 → From6000To8000km, 11,000 → From10000To12000km, 12,000 → From10000To12000km.

garageType.description: Where the car is usually parked overnight: PrivateGarage (a private/individual garage, OR a building's shared/communal residents' garage — anything covered and secure), PublicGarage (a paid public car park open to anyone, e.g. a rotational/monthly parking structure) or NoGarage (on the street). A residents' communal garage is PrivateGarage, NOT PublicGarage.

use.description: How the car is used: Private (personal/commute), Professional (work) or PublicService.

licenseDate.description: Date the driver got their driving licence (yyyy-MM or yyyy-MM-dd).

atFaultClaims.description: Number of at-fault claims in the last 5 years.

lastAtFaultClaim.description: When the driver's MOST RECENT at-fault accident happened: WithinLast12Months or MoreThan12MonthsAgo. Only relevant when atFaultClaims > 0 — the flow asks for it automatically in that case. Leave unset when there are no at-fault claims.

penalties.description: Number of driving penalties in the last 3 years.

previouslyInsured.description: Whether the car has been insured in the driver's name in the last 60 days.

yearsInsured.description: Total full years the driver has held car insurance (0 if never insured).

previousInsuranceCompany.description: The company the car is currently/was last insured with, as the user names it (e.g. 'Mapfre'). OPTIONAL — only relevant when the car is currently insured; leave unset if the car isn't insured or the user doesn't know.

postalCode.description: Policyholder's postal code (this alone determines the price).

city.description: Policyholder's town/city. Optional — auto-derived from the postal code when not given; never ask for it, but set it if the user volunteers their town.

startDate.description: When the customer wants the policy to take effect (yyyy-MM-dd). ALWAYS ask for this — the effective date materially changes the price, so it must be collected and sent, never defaulted. Must be today or a future date.

locale.description: Internal — the language THE USER is writing in, so the comparison card renders in it: 'es' if they write in Spanish, 'en' if they write in English. NEVER ask the user about it: judge it from their own messages (not from your replies, this schema, or the host's interface language) and pass it in stateUpdates when you start the flow. Omit it when unsure; the card then renders in Spanish.

quoteResult.description: Internal — the computed two-tier quote result. Set automatically by the flow.

sessionId.description: Session identifier. If the response includes a `sessionId`, pass it back on every subsequent "continue" and "reset" call for this flow.

tools.name: getBookingCatalog
tools.description: Retrieve the merchant's bookable services, service categories, available staff, and valid service-staff combinations. Call this FIRST when the user wants to book. IMPORTANT: After calling this tool you MUST follow this sequence before calling getServiceAvailability: (1) Present the list of categories and services and ask the user to choose a service. (2) Once a service is chosen, look up its assigned staff from the assignments list and ask the user whether they have a staff preference, showing the available staff names. (3) Only after both a service AND a staff choice (or explicit 'no preference') are confirmed, call getServiceAvailability. Never pick a service or staff member on behalf of the user without their input.

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code for translated names (e.g. 'en', 'fr'). If omitted, the user's browser language is used automatically.

tools.name: getServiceAvailability
tools.description: Get available appointment time slots for a specific service and staff member over a date range. Returned times are in the merchant's local timezone (provided in the response). If the returned slots array is empty, do NOT tell the user the booking is impossible. Instead, inform them that no slots were found for that service in that date range, and offer to: (1) search a different or wider date range, or (2) go back and select a different service. Once the user has chosen a slot, pass its start value directly to previewBooking.

staffId.description: Staff ID to check availability for. If the user selected a specific staff member, use their ID from the assignments list. If the user has no preference, do NOT pass -1: instead, pick the first staffId from the assignments list that is assigned to the chosen service and use that ID. Never pass -1 unless the assignments list is empty for the service.

startDate.description: Start of the search window in YYYY-MM-DD format

endDate.description: End of the search window in YYYY-MM-DD format

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code

tools.name: previewBooking
tools.description: Validate a booking intent and fetch the invoice, price breakdown, and policy details. Call this after the user has selected a service, staff, time slot, and provided their name and contact info. Present the returned invoice total, duration, and cancellation/payment policies to the user. Only proceed to bookAppointment after the user explicitly confirms.

staffId.description: Staff ID from getBookingCatalog. Use -1 for no preference (any available staff).

slotStart.description: Appointment start time in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' format, as returned by getServiceAvailability

email.description: Client email — required to send the booking confirmation

mobilePhoneNumber.description: Client phone in E.164 format (e.g. +15145551234). Optional but recommended for SMS reminders.

additionalRequest.description: Special instructions or notes for the merchant

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code (e.g. 'fr', 'en'). If omitted, the user's browser language is used automatically. Only pass this to override the browser's detected locale.

tools.name: bookAppointment
tools.description: ⚠️ Create an appointment booking. Do NOT call this tool until you have called previewBooking, presented the invoice and policies to the user, and received their explicit confirmation to proceed. Returns a tracking number and appointment ID on success. A confirmation email will be sent to the client.

staffId.description: Staff ID from getBookingCatalog. Use -1 for no preference (any available staff).

slotStart.description: Appointment start time in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' format, as returned by getServiceAvailability

email.description: Client email — required to send the booking confirmation

mobilePhoneNumber.description: Client phone in E.164 format (e.g. +15145551234). Optional but recommended for SMS reminders.

additionalRequest.description: Special instructions or notes for the merchant

lang.description: Optional BCP-47 language code (e.g. 'fr', 'en'). If omitted, the user's browser language is used automatically. Only pass this to override the browser's detected locale.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a different route in the application using TanStack Router. === WEBMCP APPLICATION NAVIGATION === ABOUT THIS APP ────────────── WebMCP is a memory and knowledge management system with: • Memory blocks for persistent, always-in-context data • Entities for structured knowledge (facts, preferences, skills, etc.) • Knowledge graph for visualizing relationships • Direct SQL access for advanced queries IMPORTANT: When you navigate to a route, context-specific tools become available. For example, entity CRUD tools appear on /entities, graph tools appear on /graph, etc. AVAILABLE ROUTES ──────────────── / Landing page - WebMCP demo overview and documentation What you can do here: • View overview of WebMCP capabilities • See tool code examples • Quick navigation to demo pages /dashboard Dashboard - Memory overview with stats, charts, and quick access What you can do here: • View memory blocks and entities counts • See token usage charts by category and tier • Browse audit log of database changes • Quick create memory blocks and entities • Get an overview of the entire memory system /entities Entities page - Browse and manage all memory entities What you can do here: • View all entities in a searchable table • Filter by category (fact, preference, skill, person, project, goal) • Create, edit, and delete entities • Search entities by name or description • Sort and group entities /entities/$entityId Entity detail page - View and edit a specific entity What you can do here: • View full entity details and metadata • Edit entity properties • See related entities and relationships • Delete the entity Required params: $entityId /graph Knowledge graph - Visualize entity relationships What you can do here: • View entities as an interactive 2D or 3D graph • Explore connections between entities • Focus on specific nodes and highlight paths • Run visual effects like camera tours and particle bursts • Analyze graph patterns and statistics • Execute SQL queries directly /memor…

to.description: The route path to navigate to (e.g., "/entities", "/graph")

search.description: URL search/query parameters (e.g., { "filter": "skills", "page": "2" })

replace.description: If true, replaces current history entry instead of pushing new one

(2) Once a service is chosen, look up its assigned staff from the assignments list and ask the user whether they have a staff preference, showing the available staff names. Instead, inform them that no slots were found for that service in that date range, and offer to: (1) search a different or wider date range, or (2) go back and select a different service. Once the user has chosen a slot, pass its start value directly to previewBooking.

staffId.description: Staff ID to check availability for. If the user selected a specific staff member, use their ID from the assignments list. If the user has no preference, do NOT pass -1: instead, pick the first staffId from the assignments list that is assigned to the chosen service and use that ID. tools.name: sendFeedback
tools.description: Report an issue in the documentation of Bohdan Lytvyn so the team can fix it. Use it whenever, while helping a user, you come across content that is outdated, contradictory, missing information, or otherwise unhelpful. Also use it when the user themselves reports a problem with the docs, even if you could not verify it yourself. If it's your own observation, do a quick sanity check that the issue is real before reporting — no need to exhaustively re-read the page. Send one call per distinct issue and do not report the same issue twice in a conversation. Do not use this tool to confirm that a page is accurate; it is for reporting problems only.

content.description: Explain the issue in full, as if writing to a documentation maintainer who never saw this conversation. Describe what is wrong, where on the page it appears (quote the exact sentence or section title when possible), what the user was trying to do, and, when relevant, what the correct or expected information should be. Write a few clear, specific sentences in English. Never include personal or confidential information from the conversation. Up to 2048 characters.

pageUrl.description: The full URL of the page the issue is about (e.g. https://www.bohdanlytvyn.com//getting-started), so the finding is linked to the exact page.

goal.description: The broader end goal you were ultimately trying to accomplish (as/on behalf of the user) when you hit this issue. Gives the team the context you were working towards. Optional.

sites.name: fintonic.com
sites.description: Fintonic is a Spanish personal finance app for organizing money, comparing loans and insurance from over 50 providers, and avoiding overcharges by banks.

tools.name: explain_fintonic
tools.description: Answers informational questions about Fintonic and how it works — the product, FinScore, ASNEF, OpenBanking / bank connection, data security, accounts, and Fintonic's financial products — by searching Fintonic's official knowledge base and returning the most relevant excerpts, ranked by semantic similarity and tagged with source filename and any source URLs. The knowledge base is the authoritative source for Fintonic's product, policy, and regulatory wording. Covers questions such as: "¿Qué es el FinScore y cómo se calcula?", "¿Cómo funciona la conexión bancaria de Fintonic?", "¿Qué pasa si estoy en ASNEF?", "¿Cómo protege Fintonic mis datos?", "Is my data safe with Fintonic?", "How does Fintonic make money?", "What is Fintonic?". For quoting a specific loan (a concrete amount + duration the user wants priced), the `loan` tool is the right one instead. Pass the user's question (or a focused Spanish rephrasing) as `query` — the knowledge base is in Spanish, so Spanish queries retrieve better. Excerpts come back in Spanish (Fintonic's authoring language). Compose the answer naturally from them and cite source URLs for factual claims. Reply in the user's language: default Spanish, tú; if the user wrote in English, translate the relevant excerpts inline and answer in English. Keep the answer grounded in the excerpts rather than outside sources.

query.description: The user's question, as a focused rephrasing in Spanish (the KB is Spanish, so Spanish queries retrieve better). If the user wrote in English, translate the question to Spanish for this field; you'll still answer them in English afterwards.

annotations.title: Explain Fintonic, FinScore, ASNEF, OpenBanking, or security

tools.name: loan
tools.description: Quote a Fintonic personal loan in Spain. Collects amount, duration, and the user's FinScore profile (ASNEF + employment + income + housing + other loan payments), maps the profile to a band, and shows the band-specific monthly installment in a result widget. After the result widget renders, the widget's CTA opens fintonic.com directly for the user to continue — your job is done at that point. This fits when the user mentions a loan, simulation, monthly payment, or amount/duration combination. For informational questions about how Fintonic, FinScore, ASNEF, OpenBanking, security, or the product work, `explain_fintonic` is the right tool; this one quotes a specific loan and collects FinScore inputs for the calculation rather than explaining concepts. INPUTS: a quote needs `amount`, `durationMonths`, `notInASNEF`, `laboralSituation`, `monthlyIncome`, `housingPayment`, `otherLoanPayments` (plus `laboralSituationConfidence`). Any subset can be supplied: pass whatever the user has stated and the flow asks for the rest through interrupts, one or two at a time, in their language. EXTRACTION: when the user states any of the input values, extract them into `stateUpdates` on the `start` call. Also extract `locale` — "en" if the user's latest message is in English, otherwise "es" (default Spanish). - `amount` (1,000–50,000 €), `durationMonths` (one of: 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60, 66, 72, 78, 84, 90, 96) - `notInASNEF` boolean — true means the user is NOT in the ASNEF registry (good); false means listed (blocked) - `laboralSituation` (Funcionario, Fijo, Temporal, Por obra y servicio, Fijo discontinuo, Autónomo, Interino, Pensionista, Desempleado, Becario, ND) — always paired with `laboralSituationConfidence` ("high" | "medium" | "low") so the system can clear and re-ask when you flag a guess. - `monthlyIncome` (net monthly income in €) - `housingPayment` (monthly rent OR mortgage payment; 0 if neither) - `otherLoanPayments` (sum of all other monthly loan/credit obligati…

action.description: "start" to begin the flow, "continue" to resume after a pause (interrupt or widget), "reset" to restart from the beginning with a correction to a previously-collected field

intent.description: Required when action is "start". Provide a brief summary of the user's goal for this flow. Do not invent missing intent.

context.description: Optional when action is "start". Describe the situation or environment that led the user to start this flow — e.g. what page they are on, what they were doing, or what triggered the request. Do not invent missing context.

stateUpdates.description: State field values to set before processing the next node. Pass the user's answer (keyed by the field name from the response) and any other values the user mentioned. For nested state fields, use dot-paths like "driver.name".

amount.description: Loan amount in euros. Must be between 1000 and 50000. Values off the 500€ grid are rounded silently.

durationMonths.description: Loan duration in months. Must be one of 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60, 66, 72, 78, 84, 90, 96. Off-grid values are rejected.

locale.description: User interface language: "es" (Spanish, default) or "en" (English). Set based on the language of the user's latest message so widgets mirror it.

notInASNEF.description: Whether the user is NOT listed in the ASNEF delinquency registry. True = not listed (qualifies); false = listed (blocked).

laboralSituation.description: User's employment status. Must be one of: Funcionario, Fijo, Temporal, Por obra y servicio, Fijo discontinuo, Autónomo, Interino, Pensionista, Desempleado, Becario, ND

laboralSituationConfidence.description: How confident the LLM is in the laboralSituation it picked. Output alongside laboralSituation. On low, the system clears the value and re-asks.

housingPayment.description: Monthly rent OR mortgage payment in euros (mutually exclusive). 0 if the user has neither.

otherLoanPayments.description: Sum of the user's other monthly loan/credit obligations in euros (car, personal loans, credit cards, etc.). 0 if none.

sessionId.description: Session identifier. If the response includes a `sessionId`, pass it back on every subsequent "continue" and "reset" call for this flow.

tools.name: simulation_result
tools.description: Display tool for the `loan` flow — renders EITHER the estimated monthly installment for the user's FinScore band (offer mode) OR a "no-offer" notice with the reason (rejection mode). Only call this tool when the `loan` flow returns `status: "widget"` with `tool: "simulation_result"` — pass the `data` from the flow response verbatim, including `kind` and `locale`. Never call it in response to a user's own loan-simulation intent (use `loan` for that). When you speak to the user, reply in their language (default Spanish, tú — warm and direct). On an OFFER, don't restate the numbers the widget already shows; invite them to continue if they want to apply, mentioning "sin compromiso" / "no commitment" naturally. On a REJECTION, the widget already shows the reason — keep your text minimal (one short line of empathy or a next step if relevant).

kind.description: Widget mode: "offer" shows the estimated installment + TAE + apply CTA; "rejection" shows a no-offer notice with the documented reason.

amount.description: Loan amount in euros (shown in both modes)

durationMonths.description: Loan duration in months (shown in both modes)

band.description: Offer mode only — FinScore band inferred from the user's profile.

installment.description: Offer mode only — monthly installment in euros for the estimated band.

tae.description: Offer mode only — APR (TAE) for the estimated band.

reason.description: Rejection mode only — which documented rejection text the widget should render. "asnef" = listed on ASNEF; "employment" = laboralSituation not supported; "no_offer" = profile too low for any band.

locale.description: User interface language for the widget. Pass verbatim from the flow's `data` — the flow mirrors the user's message language, defaulting to Spanish.

tools.name: compose_skill
tools.description: Turn a stated need or one or more source URLs into a single repo-specific skill. Call this once per skill and pass every source URL in the urls array; the backend merges up to 4 sources. Either a need or one or more URLs must be present before calling. Optionally pass a target repo, top_shards, and private. Returns the generated markdown, skill hash, shareable URL, and source_urls for attribution. If a quota error is returned, stop and ask the user to sign in or share a skill.

input_schema.description: Provide exactly one of need or urls/url. repo, top_shards, and private are optional. If the user provides multiple links, pass them all in urls. If the user only said something vague like 'create a skill', ask them for a need or urls before calling. Set private to false only when the user explicitly wants a public share and is signed in.

need.description: A free-text description of a technique or problem to solve. Use this when the user describes a topic, not when they paste URLs. Examples: 'retry budgets for async TypeScript fetch' or 'how to cache Deno KV queries'.
examples: retry budgets for async TypeScript fetch

url.description: A single public article, blog post, documentation page, or YouTube URL. Prefer the urls array if the user provided multiple links.

urls.description: One or more public article, blog post, documentation page, or YouTube URLs to combine into a single skill. Use this when the user gives multiple sources. Max 4 URLs.

repo.description: Target repository in owner/name form or as a GitHub URL.

top_shards.description: Number of extracted ideas to include in the skill (1-6, default 2 for single source, 3 for multi-source).

private.description: When false, the skill is shared publicly and can unlock unlimited forges for signed-in users. Default is true for signed-in users (a private draft) and false for anonymous users (so the link is viewable). Only set false if a signed-in user explicitly asks to share.

output_schema.description: The composed skill, or a structured error with code, hint, unlock options, and a login URL. If error is present, stop and follow the unlock instructions.

source_urls.description: All source URLs that contributed to the skill.

source_failures.description: Sources that could not be ingested, with per-URL error messages.

Submit the visitor's name, work email, company, and company website; the Masset team builds a real Masset instance seeded with the public content from that website (decks, PDFs, case studies, pages) and emails the visitor a login within one business day. The sandbox is free for 14 days, then $500 per month to keep. Only request a sandbox for the visitor's own company website, never someone else's. This submits the visitor's contact information to Masset, so confirm the details with your user before calling it.

email.description: The visitor's work email address. The sandbox login is sent here.

company.description: The company the visitor works for.

tools.name: analyze_story_drift

It crawls up to 6 pages, scores how consistently the brand story comes through (0-100 across six dimensions), checks how AI models currently perceive the brand, and produces a shareable report. The report link is also emailed to the address provided, so confirm the website URL and email with your user before calling this. The analysis takes about 2-3 minutes: this tool returns a job_id immediately; poll check_story_drift_status with it to get the scored results and summarize them for your user. Limited to 3 analyses per email, per network, and per website each day.

website_url.description: The public website to analyze, e.g. https://example.com. Private or internal hosts are rejected.

email.description: The user's email address. The finished report link is emailed here. Confirm it with the user first.

tools.name: check_story_drift_status
tools.description: Check on a Story Drift analysis started with analyze_story_drift. Pass the job_id you were given. While the analysis is running this returns the current step; when it finishes it returns the scored results (overall drift score, per-dimension scores, AI perception, and top recommendations) so you can summarize them for your user. Read-only.

tools.name: search_activities
tools.description: Search for free tours and paid activities on GuruWalk. Finds free walking tours and experiences by destination, date range, and number of attendees. When the user mentions a city name (e.g. "Valencia", "Roma"), pass it as the `destination` parameter. Dates, attendee counts, and activityType are all optional — do not ask the user for them, proceed with whatever the user provided. If the user mentions any specific category, attraction, landmark, or activity type (e.g., "tablao flamenco", "food tour", "London Eye tickets", "Eiffel Tower visit", "wine tasting"), call list_destination_options FIRST to get valid verticalId/tagId values for the destination, then pass them here. This tool navigates the user's browser to the results page — a single call completes the search; never retry with different parameters unless the user explicitly asks.

destination.description: REQUIRED. The destination city name mentioned by the user. Pass the user's literal text (e.g., 'Valencia', 'New York', 'Roma') without modification.

beginsAt.description: Start date of the search range in YYYY-MM-DD format

endsAt.description: End date of the search range in YYYY-MM-DD format

activityType.description: Type of activities to search for. 'free-tour' = free walking tours (the default option, what most users want). 'paid' = paid activities like food tours, museum tickets, day trips. 'all' = both free tours and paid activities together.

verticalId.description: Optional vertical ID to filter by. Use this to filter by a specific category (e.g., Tablaos Flamencos = "171" in Sevilla). Get valid IDs from list_destination_options first.

tagId.description: Optional free-tour tag ID. Get valid IDs from list_destination_options first. Providing a tagId implies free tours: activityType will be treated as 'free-tour'.

tools.name: list_destination_options
tools.description: Look up the available filter options for a destination: vertical categories (e.g. Tablaos Flamencos, Food Tours, Day Trips) and free-tour tags (e.g. Nocturno, Imprescindible). Use this BEFORE search_activities when the user mentions any specific category, attraction, landmark, or activity type — match the user's intent to one of the returned ids and pass it as verticalId or tagId to search_activities. Examples that should trigger this lookup: "tablao flamenco", "food tour", "London Eye", "Eiffel Tower", "Sagrada Familia", "wine tasting", "Vatican Museums".

destination.description: Free-text destination name from the user, e.g. "Sevilla", "Roma", "Paris".

summary.description: The current evidence-backed explanation of the incident. Record uncertainty plainly instead of presenting a guess as fact.

items.description: A concrete observation from investigation.

evidence.description: Concrete observations returned by investigate_incident that support the hypothesis, not unsupported assertions.

confidence.description: Your certainty in the hypothesis from 0 to 1. It never changes whether an action is permitted.

mitigationType.description: The proposed response. Supply all mitigation fields together; rollback and traffic_shift change production and always require human approval.

targetServiceId.description: The service this mitigation acts on. Only services still inside the human-approved scope appear in this list.

rationale.description: Why this mitigation follows from the observed evidence. Supply it with every other mitigation field.

expectedOutcome.description: The measurable recovery expected if the mitigation is correct. Supply it with every other mitigation field.

riskLevel.description: Classify the action risk. Rollback and traffic_shift are always treated as high and require two trusted human approvals; low and medium are for advisory work only.

sites.name: mytopfive.app
sites.description: Top Five

tools.name: search_public_lists
tools.description: Search public Top Five lists by keyword and return each match with its creator, description and a link. Replays the same query the Discover screen runs, so the results are exactly the lists that screen would show for the same words. Matching is a case-insensitive substring over list title and description — not semantic — so "sushi" finds "Sushi in NYC" but not "Best Japanese food". Public lists only — the query filters on is_public and the call carries no session, so a private list is not reachable through this tool even for the person viewing the page. Results come back under "rows", newest first, each with the list's title, creator, description where it has one, and "url" — the path to that list's page on this site. An empty rows array means nothing matched.

query.description: Keywords to match against list titles and descriptions, e.g. "sushi".

max_results.description: Cap on returned lists (default 10; the Discover screen itself uses 20).

tools.name: get_my_profile
tools.description: The profile of whoever is signed in on this page — username, display name, bio and avatar. Reads the session out of the page, so it answers for the actual viewer and needs no user id passed in. If nobody is signed in, it fails with a missing_page_value error naming the session it could not find — it never falls back to answering about anyone else.

tools.name: set_my_display_name
tools.description: Rename the signed-in user — the name shown on their profile and beside every list they have made. Writes only the viewer's own row; Row Level Security rejects anything else, so this cannot rename another account even if asked to. Succeeds with status 204 and no body. It does not touch the copy of the name held in auth metadata, so a screen reading that instead of the profile row can lag until the next sign-in. Requires someone to be signed in on this page; signed out it fails rather than doing nothing quietly.

display_name.description: The new display name, e.g. "Chip Lay".

tools.name: search
tools.description: Ищет недвижимость по гибкому логическому выражению и открывает страницу результатов в текущей вкладке. Возвращает полный ответ GetSearchQuerySummary в camelCase без изменения структуры, добавляя url выдачи. Создаёт сохранённый AI-фильтр. Фильтры текущей страницы заменяются параметрами этого поиска. Регион текущей страницы используется, если rgid не передан. # Ответ На верхнем уровне находятся dateTime, result и url. - При result.$case = "response" данные находятся в result.response: count, searchQuery, aiFilterId, topOfferIds и stats со всеми вложенными полями. - При result.$case = "emptyResponse" данные находятся в result.emptyResponse: message, searchQuery, aiFilterId и emptySearchSuggests. result.response.topOfferIds можно передать в GetOffersData, чтобы получить подробности объявлений. # СТРОГИЕ ПРАВИЛА JSON (CRITICAL): На верхнем уровне JSON-объекта разрешены ТОЛЬКО эти ключи: 1. offer_type 2. category 3. rent_time 4. rgid 5. sort 6. query 7. search_title ЛЮБЫЕ другие параметры (yandexRent, price, area, newFlat, withPets и т.д.) ЗАПРЕЩЕНО писать отдельными ключами JSON. Они ОБЯЗАНЫ быть записаны внутри строки "query" в формате "key operator value". # Параметры (ключи верхнего уровня) offer_type (обязательный, string): Тип сделки. - SELL — продажа - RENT — аренда category (обязательный, string): Категория недвижимости. - APARTMENT — квартира - ROOMS — комната - HOUSE — загородный дом с участком - LOT — участок без дома (для домов с участками нужно использовать HOUSE) - COMMERCIAL — коммерческая недвижимость - GARAGE — гараж, машиноместо rent_time (обязательный при offer_type=RENT, string): Длительность аренды. - RENT_TIME_SHORT - краткосрочная/суточная аренда - RENT_TIME_LARGE - долгосрочная аренда (используется по умолчанию) rgid (опциональный, string): ID региона Недвижимости. По умолчанию — регион текущей страницы. Не придумывай ID регионов, метро, районов и ЖК. Получай их через ResolveEntities: rgid из searchParams передавай на верхнем уровне, остальные гео…

rent_time.description: Только для RENT. SHORT — посуточно, LARGE — долгосрочно (по умолчанию).

rgid.description: ID региона Недвижимости. Если не указан, используется регион текущей страницы. Не придумывай ID.

search_title.description: Краткое название поиска на русском: локация, бюджет, комнаты, важные условия. Без технических ID.

tools.name: ResolveEntities
tools.description: Нормализует гео-объекты перед вызовом search: города, регионы, районы, улицы, дома, ЖК, застройщиков, метро, линии метро, шоссе, ж/д станции, топонимы и границы (МКАД, КАД), POI и ориентиры (парки, ТЦ, школы). Возвращает варианты с названиями, адресами, типами, scope и searchParams. Страницу не меняет. Передавай массив requests. В каждом объекте: - text — название гео-объекта или ориентира из запроса пользователя; - types — возможные типы сущности (необязательно, без ограничения — все типы); - rgid — известный ID региона (необязательно, без него поиск по всем регионам). Типы для поиска: - GEO — регионы, города, районы, топонимы, неформальные гео-объекты и границы; - METRO — станции и линии метро, включая строящиеся станции; - HIGHWAY — шоссе; - STREET — улицы; - HOUSE — дома; - NEWBUILDING — жилые комплексы; - DEVELOPER — застройщики; - RAILWAY_STATION — ж/д станции и вокзалы; - POI — конкретные места: парки, ТЦ, школы, памятники, достопримечательности. Сначала нормализуй город или регион отдельным запросом без rgid и получи его rgid из searchParams. Затем ищи остальные объекты с этим rgid. Не придумывай ID и не подставляй ID Яндекс.Карт вместо ID Недвижимости. При известном регионе не добавляй его в text: «улица Ленина» с rgid Санкт-Петербурга, а не «улица Ленина, Санкт-Петербург». Возвращает полный ответ ResolveEntitiesV2 без изменения структуры. responses соответствует requests по порядку. В каждом элементе responses находится result: - При result.$case = "response" варианты находятся в result.response.entries. - При result.$case = "emptyResponse" сообщение находится в result.emptyResponse.message. Из entries выбери не более одного варианта для каждого пользовательского гео-объекта: наиболее подходящий или ничего. При неоднозначности уточни у пользователя. Не смешивай варианты разных одноимённых объектов. Переноси значения из searchParams выбранного варианта в инструмент search: - rgid — в параметр rgid верхнего уровня; - остальные поля (districtId, toponymId, m…

tools.description: Получает подробные данные по списку объявлений: характеристики, описание, фотографии, планировки и другие доступные сведения. Используй для изучения или сравнения конкретных объявлений. Передавай offer_ids — массив строковых ID объявлений (не более 20 за один вызов). Бери ID из result.response.topOfferIds ответа search, из ссылок на объявления /offer/ / на странице или из ссылок пользователя. tools.description: Submit an application to AtYours’s prospective provider network. AtYours is building an agentic platform for high-intent lead generation for service businesses. The platform is prelaunch and is not yet a live lead, booking, or matching service. Applications are open to providers inside or outside the GTA. Submission is not approval, does not guarantee work, and creates no employment or contractor relationship. Service keys: chef = Private Chef; barber = Barber; tech = Home Tech; dj = DJ; beauty = Beauty; fitness = Fitness; tidy = Tidy; handyman = Handyman; seniorCare = Senior Care; wax = Wax; glam = Glam; braid = Braid; clean = Clean; photography = Photography; other = Other. The current page is not specific to one service; choose service keys from the schema based on the applicant's work. Required application fields: applicantName, email, phone, services, baseCity, province, country, serviceArea, yearsExperience, insuranceStatus, backgroundAndFit, consents. Optional fields: businessName, websiteOrProfileUrl, credentials. Required when services includes “other”; otherwise it must be omitted. The applicant must consent to review, follow-up contact, consideration as a prospective AtYours provider, and the Privacy Policy after confirming the supplied contact information. Use only after explicit application intent, review of the complete application, confirmed name/email/phone, and affirmative required consents. Never infer consent. Providers use this tool, not the customer waitlist. Human verification appears as a popup on the current AtYours page. After verification succeeds, repeat the identical call to retrieve the idempotent receipt. Privacy Policy: https://atyours.ca/privacy/ Visible form fallback: https://atyours.ca/providers/

tools.name: docket_ask_website
tools.description: Ask a question about this company's product, pricing, integrations, security or implementation, and get an answer from the knowledge the company publishes for visitors. Prefer this over reading or scraping the page: it covers the whole site, not just what is on screen. It cannot book meetings or answer about anything other than this company. When a slide or video illustrates the answer, the result says so and carries show_content: this page can put it on the visitor's screen. Offer it to them, and if they want it call docket_open_website_agent with that starting_message. No image is returned and there is no link to render. Every result includes a conversation_id. Pass it back as conversation_id on the visitor's follow-up questions so the answer takes the earlier exchange into account; omit it to start a fresh conversation. An id expires after a period of inactivity: each result says when in conversation_note, and an expired one is replaced automatically with a new conversation_id rather than failing.

question.description: One question about this company or its product.

conversation_id.description: The conversation_id from this tool's previous result. Pass it to continue the same conversation; omit it to start a new one. If it has expired, the result comes back with a new one to use from then on.

tools.name: docket_open_website_agent
tools.description: Open this company's live AI sales agent on the visitor's screen and start a conversation. The agent can show product slides and videos, answer follow-ups in real time, and help book a meeting. Use it when the visitor wants to talk to the company, see the product, or go deeper than a single answer — this is the next step after docket_ask_website. This changes what the visitor sees, so only call it when they have asked for it. place.description: Exactly one destination or specific hotel name as the user said it, e.g. "Crete" or "Blue Lagoon Resort".

exactDates.description: The fixed hotel stay dates. Hotel search does not support flexible date windows.

checkin.description: Check-in date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format.

checkout.description: Check-out date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format.

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.

tools.name: search_vuelo_hotel
tools.description: Search for Vuelo+Hotel on the Portfolio search form. Builds the search and moves the user to the results page - it does not return offers or prices itself; read those from the results page.

destinations.description: Destination names as the user said them, e.g. ["Crete", "Rhodes"]. Omit or send an empty list when the user wants any destination.

departures.description: Departure city/airport names as the user said them. Omit for no departure restriction.

exactDates.description: Use ONLY when the user knows the real travel dates, e.g. "out on 12 June, back on the 19th". The form may represent this as two calendar dates or as a departure date plus the derived stay length. Never use this to express a period to search inside - for that use searchWindow.

outbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day the traveller actually flies out.

inbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day they actually fly back. On departure-date forms this is used to derive the stay length. Omit if only the outbound day is fixed - then give nights.

searchWindow.description: Use whenever the user described a PERIOD rather than dates: "sometime in November", "all of November", "the first two weeks of July", "anytime this summer". These are the bounds of the period to search inside, NOT the trip itself - the trip is shorter and floats within them. Always pair with nights. If the user gave any period at all, send it here - do not drop the dates because they are not exact.

from.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Earliest day the trip may start.

to.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Latest day the trip may end.

nights.description: How many nights the trip lasts ("5 nights" = 5, "a week" = 7, "a fortnight" = 14). Required with searchWindow. Never derive it from the length of searchWindow - a one-month window is not a one-month trip. With exactDates it may replace an omitted inbound date; when both are supplied, the explicit nights value controls stay-length selectors.

nightsMax.description: Upper bound when the user gave a range of nights, e.g. nights: 7, nightsMax: 10 for "1-1.5 weeks".

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.

sites.description: El Paso Central Appraisal District, which appraises property in El Paso County, Texas, with property search, forms, news and taxpayer services.

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Image URL (absolute, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect.

sites.name: es.3ina.com
sites.description: Spanish website of 3INA, a makeup brand selling vegan, cruelty-free makeup, skincare and accessories made in Europe.

tools.name: dialog_ask_store_assistant
tools.description: Ask 3INA Makeup's shopping assistant, an expert on its catalog, buying guides and policies, an open question and get a written answer in the shopper's language plus up to 5 recommended products (title, url, price, currency, availability). Use it when the shopper needs advice rather than a lookup: which product fits a use case or budget, how two products compare, what to pair with an item, or a shipping or returns question the policies leave open (triggers: "which one should I", "what do you recommend", "is X better than Y", "does it work with"). To list, search or open pages use search_catalog or get_product. Follow-up questions keep the conversation context; one question per call. Read-only: never changes the page or the cart.

question.description: The question, in the shopper's language, with the context the assistant needs (use case, budget, constraints).

tools.name: dialog_search_products
tools.description: Search 3INA Makeup's product catalog by name, brand or keyword, with the same engine as the store's search bar, and get matching products (title, url, price, currency, availability) plus the total hit count. Use it when the shopper names a product or asks whether the store carries something (triggers: "do you have", "find", "search for", "is there a"). Results match product titles, so for needs, budgets or comparisons use dialog_ask_store_assistant instead. Read-only: never changes the page or the cart.

query.description: Product name, brand or keywords, in the store language.

limit.description: Products to return. Defaults to 5.

sites.description: eSky travel booking site for Bosnia and Herzegovina, with search for hotels and flight-plus-hotel packages.

tools.name: search_hoteli
tools.description: Search for Hoteli on the Hotels search form. Builds the search and moves the user to the results page - it does not return offers or prices itself; read those from the results page.

place.description: Exactly one destination or specific hotel name as the user said it, e.g. "Crete" or "Blue Lagoon Resort".

exactDates.description: The fixed hotel stay dates. Hotel search does not support flexible date windows.

checkin.description: Check-in date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format.

checkout.description: Check-out date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format.

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.

tools.name: search_let_hotel
tools.description: Search for Let+Hotel on the Portfolio search form. Builds the search and moves the user to the results page - it does not return offers or prices itself; read those from the results page.

destinations.description: Destination names as the user said them, e.g. ["Crete", "Rhodes"]. Omit or send an empty list when the user wants any destination.

departures.description: Departure city/airport names as the user said them. Omit for no departure restriction.

exactDates.description: Use ONLY when the user knows the real travel dates, e.g. "out on 12 June, back on the 19th". The form may represent this as two calendar dates or as a departure date plus the derived stay length. Never use this to express a period to search inside - for that use searchWindow.

outbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day the traveller actually flies out.

inbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day they actually fly back. On departure-date forms this is used to derive the stay length. Omit if only the outbound day is fixed - then give nights.

searchWindow.description: Use whenever the user described a PERIOD rather than dates: "sometime in November", "all of November", "the first two weeks of July", "anytime this summer". These are the bounds of the period to search inside, NOT the trip itself - the trip is shorter and floats within them. Always pair with nights. If the user gave any period at all, send it here - do not drop the dates because they are not exact.

from.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Earliest day the trip may start.

to.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Latest day the trip may end.

nights.description: How many nights the trip lasts ("5 nights" = 5, "a week" = 7, "a fortnight" = 14). Required with searchWindow. Never derive it from the length of searchWindow - a one-month window is not a one-month trip. With exactDates it may replace an omitted inbound date; when both are supplied, the explicit nights value controls stay-length selectors.

nightsMax.description: Upper bound when the user gave a range of nights, e.g. nights: 7, nightsMax: 10 for "1-1.5 weeks".

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.

source.description: Source city name (e.g., "Bangalore", "Singapore", "Kuala Lumpur", "Phnom Penh")

date.description: Travel date. Use ISO YYYY-MM-DD with the correct calendar year (same as the user's "today"). Accepts natural language ("today", "tomorrow") or "in N days". If the year is wrong/outdated, it is corrected to this year or next.

filters.description: Optional filters to pre-apply on the results page. Include every criterion the user asked for (e.g. AC + SLEEPER + Volvo) in one object.

departureTime.description: Preferred departure time slot: MORNING (6AM-12PM), AFTERNOON (12PM-6PM), EVENING (6PM-12AM), NIGHT (12AM-6AM)

arrivalTime.description: Preferred arrival time slot: MORNING (6AM-12PM), AFTERNOON (12PM-6PM), EVENING (6PM-12AM), NIGHT (12AM-6AM)

operatorOrBusBrandKeyword.description: Operator or bus brand mentioned by the user (e.g. "Volvo", "Benz"). Resolved on the results page against live filter data.

runAfterSearchResultsLoad.description: Optional. Same fields as runSrpBookingFlow (openBus, selectSeats, continueToBoardingPoints, applyFilters, waitForSearchResultsMs). Stored for the results page to execute after tuples load.
